Ever play one of those games that you didn't expect to be as good as it is? That's this game. Medieval FPS 4 man coop with RPG elements. All in all, I would recommend this game.

My only problem with the PC version is that there's this weird glitch on the City Escape level where the tram train you can knock over at the end of the street boarding section will hover over you constantly and follow you around to the end of the level. I attempted to fix the patches but to no avail, and it doesn't seem to happen to my friend who owns the same version either.
Sonic Adventure 2 definitely stands as one of the last Sonic games that were 'good', though Sega have been getting better in the past few years with Sonic Generations. But if you aren't a fan of the series and haven't played it already, I'd suggest playing the original Sonic games (Sonic 1, 2 and Sonic & Knuckles) if you want your fill of 'old Sonic'. The Adventure games likely won't sit well unless you're nostalgic about them as I am.

Seriously, all I wanted to do was host a Co Op game with my friend and I spent most of my time just trying to get the server to work correctly and figure out what all the config settings meant. I had to find a damn fourm post from some random person, there isn't even a wiki or anything up.

This game is fun in its current state and has fantastic potential for its completion. It includes elements from many games which helps garner familiarity with the basic structure of the game. This game features a fully destructable environment, but not so much with weapons or explosives -- just by mining and cutting down trees. You can dig a big looping circle underground if you desire. You can open a build menu instantly and build a giant wall out of different materials specifying lengths of the x,y,z axis. This makes structure creation simple, and customization endless. The crafting system is highly intuitive, it tells you the prequisites for the object you're trying to construct.
There is creation function in this game where you can build almost anything, you choose whether it will be a vehicle (plane, car, or ship), weapon (gun, sword, etc), automated turret among many other things. The creation system has a Computer Assisted Drawing feel to it, albeit a simplistic version. You can choose a material and click to begin a rectangle and drag it out to set its x,y,z axis. You can make spheres, cylinders, triangles. It is very open ended.
Cons: This game has a bit of a learning curve, especially in the vehicle creation system. I'd recommend modifying a template first to get used to the functionality of the system. Making a vehicle from scratch is immensely rewarding, but admittedly difficult especially with an airplane (the relationship between balance, thrust, and weight can be hard)

Airstrike HD is a simple game and doesn't try to advertise itself as anything more than that - At least that's the impression I got out of it.
A few things that irritated me through playing merely half an hour into it: The take-off and landing 'cutscenes' should have some way to fast forward or skip them to get right into the game itself. Trying to tackle specific achievements, screwing up, and having to do it over again can make it get very annoying very quickly.
Another huge issue I had were the powerups. It seemed like a majority of the time, you can easily pass through levels without ever grabbing them, and in all honesty it's probably better if you don't. You rarely, if ever, will need the items that help you, but the items that hinder you are FAR more unforgiving, you can go from easily beating the level to automatically losing as soon as the item is grabbed. A good game would have some kind of insurance so challenge the player to work at completing the level, but these just seem like the developers went for more of the, "Oops you hit the box guess you lost this round ;-)" route instead.The item I seem to always hit is the pink reset item, which basically feels like the game raises a giant middle finger at you and tells you to play the entire level over again, even if you were only a few drops from completing it. Oh but don't worry - Your insignificant score will remain.
The upgrade system is also very weak. It's the same thing with each world (pass a level, get a little perk), and you don't even get the most useful ones until you face the boss (which you can destroy in one shot, without it even trying to attack you).
Why not have a system where the score is instead replaced with a currency, where we can spend this money to upgrade plane bodies, wings, bombs, etc? It's a concept we've been seeing in free flash games for years now, and a game like this underachieves in this regard?
I realize these are very nit-picky, but the bottomline I'm trying to get at is Airstrike HD is no better than your standard internet game you can find for free anywhere else. I'm not sure why this game has a price tag at all. But because it is asking money, I would imagine these little things would have been given more thought, instead of just a glorified flash game with repeated and stale levels.

I'm not exactly sure how I feel about this game. What exactly did I get for the $2 that I spent?
A "good" story, with slightly better than decent gameplay. It's only about 4 hours worth of gameplay.
The reason good is in quotations is because it was mostly based on the cliche trope of, guy gets seperated from the group and needs to find his friends, whilst also looking for his lost family. I'd hate to spoil the ending so I won't, but it does have a pretty dark theme to it.
Now the gameplay is my biggest issue with the game. Occasionally, it is unclear exactly what you are supposed to do, and there are a lot of things that are set up just to kill you. In which, say, you jump across a gap, only to be immediately met with something falling on your head. You had no way of knowing, so you just have to go back a bit and try again. It was actually pretty annoying having to start over so many times because I just didn't understand what the game wanted me to do. There was literally one time I got trapped because I didn't move fast enough to get through the area it wanted me to, which I had absolutely no way of knowing until I had killed myself and tried again.
If you are going to play this game, I would suggest having a controller for it. It seems best fit for that, because doing a sprint roll on a keyboard is nearly impossible. You literally have to hold Lshift and press Lcrt while running. It's super annoying and no there isn't an option to make it easier for keyboard users. (I checked)
For only two dollars I think it's a fantastic little game. Good enough for me to spend 4 hours of my life on at the very least. But for more than that, in my opinion, it could be a little better.
I give it a final score of 7/10!

This game has loads of issues and while it's still in beta it's been in the open for about a year now and there are still fundamental core elements missing/not functioning the way you would assume they would.
Currently my main problem is the sound issue. The weapon sounds are quite low overall (except plane bombs) but that I can tolerate, the thing that is unacceptable is that if you get hit, the weapon that hit you doesn't make a sound. So when you get shot from behind you have no idea if it was a sniper 300m away or someone right behind you.
My other main mechanical issue is character control when using toggles on aims up,prone, crouch. When you run out of ammo and start yo reload, if you were toggled in aims up you stay toggled aim's up, which affects your move speed so if you want to move normally while reloading you have to untoggle the aiming. You can't go directly to crouch from prone. Toggles here also are a bit mess since you can have crouch and prone toggled simulatenously.
Some of the ribbon unlocks (sorts of perks) are unlocked in a bit strange way, like you get the perk to hijack tanks by not unlocking bunch of tanks, but by driving one. Also as you can only have one perk selected (two if you're a subscriber) most of the perks are totally useless and would do better being passive bonuses.
Changing gear in middle of match.... you have to disconnect from the game, do your changes in the main view and then reconnect to the match. Because you can't change gear/character in the game window a slot will be reserved for you for some time to do your stuff and join back in the game. Which means that if your team has ragequitters you're not gonna get replacements for those in few mins.
Now that the negative stuff is out of the way let's get to the positives.
I like how the weapons play and the need to grind weapons and badges gives you something other to focus on than just playing the game. So much more fun aiming for those headshots with sniper to progress Recon badge for that ultimate reward of having the badge that doesn't show you on kill cam. And unlocking upgrades to your weapon to make it more powerfull. Hint when grinding for money to buy upgrades.. just go pure melee, kill someone or get team mates dropped weapon and play. No repair costs!.
The maps are mostly nice, few maps have problematic starting spawns that enemy tanks usually spam (factory).
I feel that in every other fps I've played no matter how far an enemy is they are super easy to spot from the background. Not so in this. Even an enemy right next to you in a bush is really hard to spot unless you're really searching for them.
So recommend you give it a try and see if you like it.

EDIT:  This was longer than I expected it to be. I like the game, but I also don't expect it to be more than it tries to be. Which is where most criticism comes from I think. People see a fantasy game wand assume/expect Diablo or MMO style loot and progression.
Its the same genre as L4D. A bit repetitive, doing the same levels, etc. The levels very a bit, but there are a few that get played the most if your joining randoms all the time.
I've barely played L4D at all, and if you haven't played L4D... Always 4 character co-op. (Edit: soon to chagne with free DLC patch) Either with bots or other players. Kill waves of badguys (zombies in L4D, Ratmen in Vermintide). Vermintide takes a lot from L4D, but considering that L4D is nto exactly new anymore, and no great successor has ever caught my interest, taking a lot of queues from the better game in the sub-genre isn't a bad thing.
The game it self is skill absed, not stat based.  Learning the flow of combat to avoid taking damage. Dodge and block. Heavy attack, ranged shot, aoe atacks, etc. Then mix in a special creature at random times to break up your patterns.
Not taking damage is the idea, rather than getting a high kill count. I rarely get top kills or top damage dealt.  But I do top the least damage taken score sheet, and that I think is the better thing to aim for since health is so limited and it helps you to get ready for the punishing difficulties where a single hit means a lot of life lost.  Personally I lvoe teh idea of trying to play a perfect game a bit slower, rather than sprinting through and barely finishing.
There are classes, but most don't differ too much.  Some variety is there, far mroe than L4D where your cahracter was completetly unimportant.  But it's not a totally differnt game with each class.  The flow is still mostly the same.  Just a little different timing, etc.
Bots are not great, but with some experience and luck you can eventually get through most of the game with them if you try to learn their idiosyncrasies. The game really shines though with 4 players working together properly. Witha  bad group, the game in punishing. The game really starts to feel great when you have a good group. When things just work well, it is a great feeling.  And it does happen, even with randoms.  Mostly on weekends so far for what ever reason.
I only know Warhammer Fantasy a little bit from the MMO and playing tabletop 15 years ago a little. But the lore and what there is of story (simple and limited), is interesting and I want to know more.  I usually don;t get invested into games like this.
Vermintide's take on this genre is to make melee the primary focus, instead of range. Range exists, but ammo is limited just enough to make it not a sole focus. Friendly Fire in the harder difficulties make it less a focus as well.
Loot is in the game to give a little bit of reward for that grind and to give a bit more to the replayability. Where people go wrong though, is that they think this is a loot hunt game. It's not Diablo. It's not an RPG. Loot is not the point of the game. So you see a lot of people whining about the way loot drops and that it's too hard to get the good items. Except that the entire game is perfectly beatable with white (low) quality weapons. The positive side effect of this is that experienced players and newb's can play together without feeling like you just outgear everything. Instead you outskill everything. And that can be a lot of fun.
There are levels to gain, but they are so minor in meaning that it's rarely even mentioned as a feature.
My favorite part of Vermintide though may not have been invented for this game, but it's the first time I've seen it. Partial ally clipping. Can't run through badguys of course, they stop you cold. But you can push through friends. But you both get jostled by it. You can knock each other around and push someone off a bridge if you were not careful. Choke points are very helpful, and everyone rustling around pushing each other trying to get a good angle on the small wooden no-rails-bridge and messing up your careful sniping is a LOT of fun. Really adds to the claustrophobic atmosphere. I wish more (all?) online games had this. Something like this in an MMO like WoW or Wildstar would be an absolute blast to have to deal with.
The only real issue I have with the game is there are a number of cheats/exploits taht random group members always want to use to grind things faster.  But Fat Shark is on the ball and fixing them.  Hopefully they get a little faster at the fixes for this stuff.
I've put in about 50 hours in and it has started to wane a bit (especially with FO4 now out). I'm a bit less social with randoms though, so you could easily get more out of it if you were to find some good people to play it with. But if/when anything new comes to the game, I'll be there day one to try it out, paid DLC or not.

I have many problems with Sonic Adventure 2, but my largest is that the art direction in general is much worse than most previous Sonic titles and the level variety is very weak. You have city levels, mechanical levels, forests, pyramid levels (which are very creative) and not much else, whereas Sonic Adventure 1 had a little of everything players could want. I understand why they removed the overworld from the first game as well, but I think it was a mistake abandoning the concept completely. The music is not as good as the first game's soundtrack either, but it is enjoyable enough; I especially enjoyed how each character's levels had their own genre of music too. The story is simply a mess, but is easy to ignore.
As a pure 3D platformer the game is largely mediocre. I feel the Sonic levels are more 'solid' in design than any other 3D Sonic title, but everything else feels significantly worse and less fun to me than the first Sonic Adventure. Most zones are significantly larger and infinitely more elaborate, making the scoring for the hardcore fans potentially more enjoyable, but much more frustrating and tedious for those interested in casual play.
I would recommend the game to people who are interested in revisiting levels to improve their rank and finding various secrets though. I think the scoring system in the game is brilliant and very undervalued by many. No Sonic game since has had such a balanced, thoughtful scoring system. The Chao raising is very addicting if you allow yourself to get absorbed in it too.
I do enjoy Sonic Adventure 2 and have fond memories of unlocking everything on the SEGA Dreamcast version back in the summer of 2001. I could never do it again (or would I want to), but I am very nostalgic of those times.

Planet Explorer's is a beautiful game, with interesting game mechanics but an unfinished feeling the entire gaming experience.  It's a great game if you have the patience for it-the dev's also appear to be constantly updating the game so hopefully this game will improve.
First off, the game has a steep learning curve and doesn't fully explain many mechanics in the game.  And just enough bugs and glitches to have you wondering if this is a game glitch or just a mechanic that's not fully explained.  For this game I found that google was my friend and often looked up problems I encounter in the storymode.
The building, mining, collecting resources are fun. You have a tool/weapon progress that starts at simple wooden tools and progresses up the technologicl tree as better resources become available. Although this too feels unfinished, as if they intended to release a few more higher teirs of tools and weapons but never released them.
As you can see by the pictures, you can craft some amazing things. Custom vehicles, weapons, etc except again there's a large learning curve and it's not very practical. Let me explain. So you wanted to craft a new gun, you collect the necessary parts, enter the creation system and start designing the actual lines of the gun. You make the gun look amazing, except due to the wierd rules of the creation system, your amazing looking gun does little to no damage.  After spending a good chunk of time designing a gun that looked neat but did no damage I entered the creation system. Put all the gun parts in the area and filled the entire area with diamond block. My "gun" was a big block of diamond with a barrel sticking out of it, that did 600 damage.  Vehicles also seem to full of problems. Driving cars take high amounts of durability damage along with a plague of other problem that make traveling with vehicles nto really worth it. Which sucks because the map is large and things are really spread out.
The Jetpack and glider were my bread and butter for transportation.
The storyline wasn't anything special at first, although they threw a few interesting curve balls and twists. I felt like the game ended in a satisfying way, although the overall experience felt like something was missing. Honestly I'd love to see what this game company can do with their second Planet Explorer game.
Performance. I had no problem running on max settings, although I noticed that regardless of my settings when NPC colonists would sleep for the night the game were stutter and freeze with performance issues. Upon looking online it looks like this is a fairly common problem.
The colony system is an interesting one. They are actually useful at maintaining your colony and will do a variety of tasks. Although the AI isn't very good, NPC would often hangout underwater or walk off tall buildings/cliffs. Various machines that you can build inside your colony have different functions; some of those functions are finished while other's I suspect will be changed in future patches.
Although this review is full of criticisms that game is fun, the storyline can be interesting and underneathe all the flaws the game is really amazing. But there's alot of flaws, you need patience to play this game.
At first I recommend this in the review and then after a few days comtempllation I reversed my recommendation. It's a great game at it's foundation, but it's not there yet. If the game was still in early access my review would be different. I realize that although I did have fun, it's not likely that I'll replay the game again.

This is a case where I wish the had a mixed option for reviews, cause that's what I feel about this game. Most everything works fine, no bugs (well, not performance wise) or problems to speak of, controls operate fine for an adventure game, though there are some cases where changing crawling on wolls can get annoying, though not enough to really be a problem.
The story is pretty minimal, Two roach friends go to find a flower (a rarity in a post-apocalyptic earth) and end up in a long misadventure due to the roach Bud's incredible bad luck, so his friend (the one you play as) has to save him, multiple times. Not much more than that without going into specifics, but it's a nice story.
That gameplay is where I feel less than entertained. My main problem is that, for a few of the puzzles, there isn't much to go on and the vagueness of the explanation for the puzzles and items can make the puzzles less than clear, for instance. and spoilers
At the end of the game, you need to find a replacement for a button for a crane operating machine, there's a mushroom item that, when clicked on, shows a image telling you its a toxic, psychedelic mushroom, so you might think, "Hmmm, do I have to try feeding it someone to make them do something, or distract them?" But no, it's the button you need, and completely illogical given the nature of the machine as the buttons are not mechanical, but electrical.
There's only a few other's like this (though for different reasons), but overall the puzzles feel sensible. I only had to look up answers three times. There is however an issue I take with arbitrarily limiting the player's movelent solely to make puzzles operate a certain way. You can only walk on select walls and objects to the left an right, but not everything, and walls on the background or foreground are completey unscalable. It's not technically problematic, but logically, it feels lazy. They could have at least given resoning to this.
Besides that, to me, neither the story nor gameplay were too interesting or engaging to really be fun for me. An okay game with some overly vague puzzles, hence the mixed opinion, but I'll give it a thumbs up since it is done well overall.
Also, it may say I only played a few minutes, but that's only cause I played on offline mode.
Edit: Forgot to mention, as other's have said, I would not recommend this game at full price. I got it for 1$ U.S., and that feels about a fair price given the content, length, and replayability.

Jones is an adorable game where the titular hero must rescue her favorite felines from a fiery catastrophy! (That sentence was as fun to write as it was to read). Very addictive gameplay. Love the cute blocky graphics!

Timing, timing is everything with this game. So you see a kitty hanging there? You jump to save him/her and come down. Oh no! There was a log! In this game you NEED to pay attention to where you are going and where you will land when jumping.
On the gameplay side of things it's simplistic, but has that old style level runner that a lot of us grew up with as kids. Controls are simble, jump, slide, etc. Doesn't take long to learn them. Especially if you complete the tutorial in the beginning. (I recommend this) You start at hazard level 1, 2hp (Or times you can land in fire or smash into something) before you lose a life. Not to worry! You start with 3, and they appear to regen over time provided you clear a level. When the counter reaches 0, well I'm sure you can guess what happens! It is however a bit hardcore afterward as you drop back to level 1. However, unlike most games that drop you back, you retain all your perks and or upgrades you had purchased previously. This is nice, and certainly helps you continue to climb higher and higher each time you go through runs. Your only objective is simple! You run out there and rescue kitties! And depending how many you rescue, you got it! Determines your over all score for the level and how many points you earn to spend at the actual upgrade stations.
Art style wise it's cute. It's not overly complex, but it doesn't look terrible either. I recommend playing the game to find out! (Music is pretty fun as well but gets slightly repetitive. Thats my personal opinion however!)
All in all I will give this game a 7/10, it did put a smile on my face and I will recommend it to friends and others looking for a decent level runner style of game!

quick TL;DR version:  I absolutely love this game, buy it!
Jones On Fire is somewhere between a retro platformer and an endless runner.... or... both?!  It's got tight gameplay and controls, a unique (and uniquely suiting) visual aesthetic, and a nice dose of humor and cuteness to boot.
What really makes the game great though, in my humble opinion, is that it essentially hooks you the with the same basic idea of all of the classic OG arcade games -- the game is simple enough for anyone to pick up and play, is easy to grasp, and yet... is VERY hard to play PERFECTLY.  And each time you cause poor lil Jones to be singed nearly to death, you shake your head and SWEAR you won't do that same dumb mistake next time.  I literally think anyone from kids just young enough to hold a controller or use a keyboard, to 31-year-old men (yours truly) and beyond, could enjoy this game equally fully.
Saving cats from fires is so freakin' addictive!  Who knew?!
Contagion's concept is appreciable, but the fun just isn't there.

Ylands is a brilliant game, fun for all ages, graphically impressive, fairly immersive and caters for my needs!
Specifically - I've been searching endlessly for a survival / exploration / sandbox game, that wasn't just another 'First Person Shooter', or 'Open World' game, masquerading as a survival / exploration / sandbox game for some sales.
Increasingly there has been a trend of games being released as 'sandbox' games, that really don't seem to meet what I would like a sandbox game to be - akin to playing in a sandbox, do what you want with the terrain, do what you want with building, do what you want - no set objectives or tasks.
It is for these reasons that I absolutely love this game, it is the one I had been looking for!
In the interest of a non-biased review then (as I'm clearly biased!) - I shall attempt some honest pro's and con's.
PRO'S:
- Graphically impressive utilising the latest graphics technologies.
- A true sandbox experience IMHO.
- An editor for complete creative control.
- Numerous game modes, community made, official, or your own.
- Very efficient support with issues via their forums.
- Family friendly, could be played together as a family, or someone of any age.
- Multiplayer / planned dedicated server support.
- Expansive crafting list, unlocking new inventions, tools, stations and devices, by obtaining the materials needed.
- Horse riding, ship sailing, car driving, steam and energy powered (electricity) devices and vehicles.
- Painting of objects and blocks, to suit your style... even painted animals!
- Explore mode features different biomes on different islands, each with their own kinds of flora and fauna / hazards.
- Vast underground cave systems, hidden loot and extra hard enemies for the hardened adventurer.
- Interesting 'follow the seagulls' and map + pencil + compass sailing navigation system.
- Randomly generated 'curious sites' all over the place, some of them are very interesting, and others have puzzles for rewards etc.
- Underwater exploration / loot, sunken ships, submarines and more at the bottom of the sea!
- Manage players health, hunger and warmth for survival immersion.
CON'S:
- Game Analytics / Marketing data gathered through the game client / website (efficiently helps developers but some rightfully feel this is intrusive).
- Occasional game bugs, most of which are fixed swiftly and could be somewhat expected at first release on a new platform.
- Could do with having to manage thirst and sleep deprivation as well, this would require a way to create fresh water.
- Multiplayer is currently limited to 8 consecutive players.
- Currently no dedicated server available (plans to be released).
- Not much in the way of trolling / griefing counter measures at the moment - lock your server with a password.
- No Mac or Linux support currently.
- Monetisation plans have some concerned (micro-payments for cosmetics / skins / official dedicated server slots / user made composition and game mode trading).
As far as the two seemingly biggest make-or-break factors - analytics and marketing data / monetisation plans -
While some may be tired of games harvesting information from them, one must also understand that this could efficiently assist a developer with balancing a game, correcting issues that effect large numbers of people, and making a better product in the end. Though I completely agree with people's concerns about their private data, this is one of those take a little to give a little scenarios. This feature can in-fact be switched off in the options, and the marketing data has since been entirely switched off.
As far as monetisation goes, the funding for continued game development has to come from somewhere, so what would you rather?
Purchasing the game 'as is', not paying a single cent or penny more, and in return, expecting to receive additional game content for free? (fixes and updates come free, as this is an attempt to fix something that should be working, however, new game content costs money, as you have to pay developers and artists to make it)
DLC content, costing you extra if you want to play it?
Micro-transactions on in-game items (pay-to-win)?
Or the quite reasonable plan I think - micro-transaction on non-game influencing cosmetic items. Included in the plans are ways to allow non-official content creators, to earn or trade credits without needing to pay anything - even having an official dedicated server rented via this community based economy / credits.

The first few hours on Vermintide were a little less than I'd hoped for. I had expected skill trees that would enable me to gain more moves and customize my current ones, as well as a little more complexity to the combat, instead of just a few basic swings, a charge attack, and a block. Also, I had expected to be able to sprint from target to target (which would still be nice).
All that said, now I am 16 hours in and am thoroughly addicted. I love fast classes, so I naturally settled on the Waywatcher. Combat is quick and visceral, and the dagger/sword stance I've chosen is fast and precise. It rewards you for headshots, which brings in a skill component, and the charge-up covers multiple enemies. At this point I'm infected with such bloodlust that I get on the game every chance I can to sate my addiction to dashing in and out of combat, slashing off heads and arms and cutting rodents in half. The impacts feel great, all of the rodents feel unique, and the different types keep you on your toes. I always feel like I can improve at this game (in skill, not just in damage), and the variety of weapons - and thus fighting styles - has me dying to see what's coming down the pike.
If you like fast and frantic first-person combat and feeling every single hack and slice, buy this game!
Oh, and the environment's gorgeous. :)

As I write this, I have approximately 20 hours spent on Vermintide.  Based on this admittedly light experience, the game has delivered a generally solid and fun experience that has surpassed my expectations. I recognise that it is commonly compared to Left 4 Dead, yet that was never a game I played very much; I really wanted to try this as I'm a Warhammer fan. At any rate, here are some observations and opinions:
1) Functionality - the game has received criticism for bugs and various performance issues, etc.  To be perfectly honest though, my computer is 3 years old and I have not experienced any technical difficulties whatsoever. Vermintide has been rock-solid since day one for me and I have all settings set to max levels.  I have a GTX 680 with 16GB RAM and an i7 3820CPU @ 3.6GHz.  The closest thing I have to an issue is that each time I start the game, I have to reset my display settings as they never seem to save from previous play sessions.  Annoying, but a minor inconvenience.
2)   Play experience - It's fast, furious, bloody and you are basically hard-pressed at every turn.  Some maps are more fun than others and those that require teamwork past watching each others back are decidedly less popular (ie - maps where you need to haul grain sacks or gunpowder; these have usually ended in failure for me unless I was in a group that actually made the effort to communicate and coordinate).  Maps are large and well-designed with choke points, large open areas and random terrains with lots of secret areas to explore and enjoy.  Your environment often factors into gameplay and strategy.
AI Bots are functional, but currently not great.  I have yet to actually win a match were we had more than 1 bot.  I understand they are going to be getting some work in a future patch so that's good. Play this with friends if you want to ensure at least a fun play sessison as the AI bots just aren't up to snuff yet and the community is... well, the community is good but there are some ...um... passionate people out there.
I have generally had positive experiences with the community for most of my matches (I usually play in pugs or with a friend).  However, I have also experienced more than a few instances where some people have perceived another player as a weak link and either verbally attacked them on VOIP or chewed them out or even kicked them at the end of the match. It's pathetic behaviour, but anyone considering this game should know that if you are planning on casually joining a pug, these people are out there so bring your flame suit in case you have a bad day and get singled out for a round of the Blame Game.
Also - last gameplay note - Vermintide hates failure and really does not reward it at all.  This is  why it can bring out the worst in people.  Some of these matches can take close to a half-hour to complete.  If you are defeated, you get miniscule compensation in terms of experience and nothing else. I confess it does burn when you fight like a madman through a whole city only to fail at the very end. I wish the devs at least gave you something for your time instead of a dash of experience which is actually more infuriating when you get it as opposed to assauging your ire.
3) the Hook - the hook of this game is the supposedly the loot system. (I personally think the hook is just the fun of being chased around town by giant rat people, but whatever).  The loot system is currently being revised, which I think is great since it has a lot of room for improvement. I love that there actually IS a system in place; different quality/grade weapons really do make a difference in gameplay imho - but as it is, it remains far, far too random for my liking. The game seems to think that everyone will simply want to play all of the characters. Even the forge function that lets you upgrade trash is random.  It can be frustrating when you like playing a character and all you get is the same items over and over for a character you never play.  Still though - it's SUCH a rush when you get a high-tier item that you can actually use !
Conclusion - Vermintide is worth your time. Visually, it is, in my opinion, an authentic representation of the Warhammer Fantasy world that fans have come to love over the years. The characters are great and the gameplay is intense with great voice acting, music and effects.  It's best enjoyed with friends, but pugs are totally viable and usually fun as well (just ignore the occasional jerk you are bound to run into). The devs seem keen on further optimizing the game which is good for folks having issues and more content is coming, so there is much to look forward too.  Good luck !

After having pumped 200+ hours into the game I think I should write a review to support the game, so here I go.
Mount & Blade Warband, released in 2010, a kind-of sequel to the original Mount & Blade, is a First/Third Person Action RPG/RTS set in a medieval open world. You set your own goal - live a life as a mercenary, become a Lord of one of the kingdoms, join a claimant to a throne in his battle to take, as he/she thinks, his/her rightful place as king, or go against all of the kingdoms and create your own.
You start the game completely on your own in one of the capital cities of your liking where you happen to get your first quest. You then recruit soldiers for your troop and either be a good samaritan who takes care of the bandits and helps villages, or be the feared vandal by raiding caravans and villages.
Now, putting together your troop and controlling it in battle is where the RTS part comes in.
All your soldiers can be put in groups (similar to ordinary RTS control groups which you select with the 0-9 keys) to always only select those soldiers you want, giving you a lot of control over them. In battles you can give them all sorts of commands you could think of, including, but not limited to, telling them to use only certain weapons that they possess.
Another special thing about this game is the very skill-based combat system.
The melee combat system is based on attacking from four directions and being able to block them - of course by blocking in the direction the swing comes from. This can be really tough sometimes when there's a lot of stuff going on or if your opponent has a rather fast weapon.
You can set up how you want to swing and block independently. Do you want it to work by going into the corresponding direction? Or only by mouse movement?
In singleplayer, for beginners, you can even enable automatic blocking. This will result in you only having to press the block button when a swing comes in, of course you still have to know when to block and when to swing. This setting does not apply to multiplayer though, there it is up to the server wether there's automatic blocking or not - but most likely you'll only be seeing automatic blocking in player vs bot games (there are special modules that are based on fending off enemy waves with other players).
The multiplayer mode is something that first came with Warband, and I think it's pretty solid for an indie game (except for some minor things, but later onto that).
It supports up to 250 players and several modes, including Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Capture the Flag, Last man standing Deathmatch and of course castle siege, similar to sieging a castle in singleplayer.
Apart from all that great stuff the game also has an amazing mod support. Search
for Mount & Blade mods (for both the original game and Warband) and you'll understand what I mean.
As many pros as this game has, it also has a few cons.
A big problem in multiplayer, similar to other games (like Chivalry, for example), are the trolls.
There are a lot of times when you have a lot of fun and fight a bunch of great battles, and then there's the trolls' prime time.
At that time, things are going to get messy. You randomly get hit, shot and kicked by a teammate just to annoy you and then that person just runs along as if nothing happened. When you try to take revenge, they will turn things around and make you look like the vermin, causing everyone to go at you. Classy trolls.
That's about the negatives I could think of and it isn't really the games' fault.
To round this review of, I'll give a short summary:
Pros:
-solid melee combat system
-troop management
-good graphics (remember that this was and still is an indie game - I think the graphics are absolutely fine despite what others have said. Besides, the graphics in M&BII have been improved by a lot.)
-great multiplayer with a high number of players supported and several gamemodes
-mod support
-always challenging
Cons:
-engine limitations
So I come to the conclusion that I can clearly recommend this title to others. Also keep an eye out for the upcoming sequel!

One of the better games I've played in recent years, it does however suffer from bugs and some clumsy UI elements. After a fair amount of play time I am inclined to say the developers ambition exceeded their grasp slightly, but overall they produced a fun game that is distinguished in its genre. I had a wonderful experience that was well worth the price to me.
Notable negatives:
There are bugs to be found in this game but nothing I couldn't live with. As an old school gamer I have it deeply ingrained in me to save often and that served me well for the odd instance where I encountered a bug. I knew going in the developer was a modest and unproven studio so I didn't expect otherwise, so an occassional bug which requires a reload from a prior save was fine by me. I note this however as while it may be fine for me, it may not be fine for you.
Most of my time played was single player and that was great. Online play on official servers was not nearly as great. While not terrible, overall server performance was just a lackluster experience for me causing just enough irriation with lag, etc. that it prevented me from fully enjoying myself. The greatest potential for this game is in the multiplayer which made it a bit of a shame that the offical servers just didn't quite perform well enough for me to stay interested in spending time on them. Privately hosted multiplayer I think could be great fun.
Positives to ponder and other postulations:
More than anything I love the atmosphere of this game, kind of like the equivilant of a "feel good" movie without getting overly sappy. It walks a fine line that does justice to the concept of a survival situation in a sci-fi environment while keeping the tone light hearted. In many respects it reminded me of old school sci-fi in how it lets the narrative carry its own weight in that sense. For me at least this was something I want to really applaud this game for, it's something it really got right that I think isn't easy.
Story wise, I won't tell you it's Isaac Asimov, but it's FAR better than I expected. Quite frankly my expectations here were pretty low, so I was pleasantly surprised at how well thought out and complex the story was.
I also found the audio to be better than I would have thought. While the title song is a bit cheesy for my taste, there's no denying the quality is far beyond what I would have ever expected from a small studio game like this. Likewise goes with in game ambiant sounds and music. The sound track to the game is absolutely well done, beautiful and way beyond anything I would have expected from a game of this scale.
Mechanically, the game does a whole lot of things right if a bit clumsily. Building and crafting could be a little more intuitive, but I quickly forgave that as the system is really great in allowing you to make veritably anything you can conceive. The ability to save and share creations via ISO files is a great addition that brings a lot of life into the crafting and creative aspect of the game. My criticism of any of it would be the same, execution fell a little short of the intention. It does however work well enough that despite the quirks I can easily say it's one of the best crafting systems I've ever had the pleasure to play with. I think it's absolutely underrated how forward thinking the system is, veritably everything a gamer who loves crafting could want. Again, it's clumsy at points and that's a shame, but it's still a great idea that manages to work.
Closing thoughts:
I think the bugs and clumsiness found early on turn people off before they discover the rich experience underneath. I understand where a lot of reviews are coming from and I can't really blame them, as much as I have enjoyed the game it does suffer from a lack polish. I really do believe the studio is on to something great and I hope they'll consider giving this title the polish it needs to spruce it up for DLC or a sequel.

Normally, I would write something silly, but to be honest, I actually have a strong opinion on this game.
*My opinion on the games story may not actually be what happened*
It's nowhere near as good as the first. The plotline is just that. A plotline. Filled with an unchronological set of events that don't actually mean anything at all. The only plot line that actually mattered, once more, was the phones, which I didn't like. In the first game, I loved exploring the sociopathic personality of Jacket. I loved how dangerous I felt. I just didn't get that from this game.
(Spoilers Ahead)
Once more, phones started to ring, people did bad things. This time, there was an objective: To start World War 3, Eventually succeeding in doing so. 50 Blessings being a patriotic group hated the Russian "Invasion" into their country, America. As such, they wanted people to kill the Mob. Unsatisfied, they then attempted to cause WW3 to completley irradicate Russia, assuming America was able to successfully invade.
The Jacket A.K.A "Richard" mask and it's constant appearance.
Simply put, that's actually the representation for post traumatic stress disorder. Those who see the Jacket mask or either on the brink of sociopathic insanity from the guilt of murder (that the phonecalls are making them do, hence why Pardo, or the "Miami Mutilator", kept leaving those notes saying he didn't want to do what he was doing. His mind then repressed the guilty memories, hence why he still thinks he is innocent) or were present in the battle in Hawaii (Basically this game's Vietnam) and as such are suffering from PTSD.
The remaining stories (The Son A.K.A Scarred Face Guy, The Henchman A.K.A The guy that wanted out, Richter A.K.A The Mama's boy, Pardo and The Writer.)
ALL. MEANT. NOTHING. They literally had no impact on the story, in my opinion.
The Guys With Masks.
Just a group of vigilanties, nothing more, It is important to note that they are clearly not right in the head and, as such, Mark The Bear did see the Jacket mask at one point, reinforcing my earlier statement. They are called "The Fans" because they saw what Jacket did, thought it was cool and decided to dish out a little Vigilante "Justice" themselves. That's it. They've no correlation with Jacket other than liking his "work" so to speak.
Oh and a bit of a quick clearing up for those who got confused as to the story in Hotline Miami, where the Biker killed Jacket: The Biker did not kill Jacket. I'm not sure how far along the timelime the Biker died but he was present in a few scenes in Wrong Number, though you have to look for him, don't just expect to see him plain and out in the open. In short: Jacket is alive, the Biker is dead and Jacket is in prison as he turned himself in after erradicating the Russian Mob Boss. "But you play as the mob boss in the game!" I hear you cry. No, that's his Son. "The Son". Did you really not catch on from that?
If you are expecting the game to be better than the first, don't. If you are simply reviewing it as a game then it's alright, but nothing special. Hope that this cleared up the story for those that played.

Preface: Played the original on Playstation to Platinum, and on PC (10h so far).
Hotline Miami 2 is a masterclass in tedium, analogous to waiting in line at Tesco.
The maps are overly sized, and if you value your sanity, you're left to wait for the patrol to come to you before you can dispatch them. Of course, you're free to approach them, but their field of view is a lot higher than yours, and it's close to certain that they'll tag you before they become visible.
The fast-paced play of the original is again stifled by an odd choice to move the ending of the brutal finishers to a player-controlled RMB click. I don't know why automatically completing the move has been dropped (Can I change it to automatically detach from what remains of my enemy's body? Let me know).
Weapons, while largely unchanged from its predecessor, come in a state of limbo as to whether your current character can use them, will unload them, or will either completely ignore to pick them up. (Act 2, L1. He failed to pick up butterfly knife?)
I hate that I have to leave a negative review. Seriously, HM is easily one of the greatest indie games of the 2010s, and with the developers stating that this is the last in the series, it's frustrating that it is being left in such a state.
Maybe I do just need to "git gud". Or I can just play something else, I suggest you do too.

There's a lot of terrible, low effort indie games out there.   This is not one of them.
Journey of a Roach is a hybid platformer/point and click adventure game, with novel puzzles engendered by the insect theme.
The game engine is a unique cel-shaded/hand art 3D rendered platformer.   As a "roach" you can walk on the walls, which adds another dimension to the game.   Usually hand-art is very low effort, but in this game it's sufficient that it doesn't distract from the game.   It's less noticable in the 3D engine than the cutscenes, which helps.
All in all, a lot of effort and polish went into this game, which is unusual for an indie game.  For that reason, for fans of the adventure game genre, this is completely worth considering.

This is a point and click adventure about Roaches. The name probably gave that away. It is a fun little game, a little on the short side. The humour is great,  although it ventures into the slightly lewd at times, The fun characters and puzzles are accompanied by the undertone of the world having gone through nuclear holocaust. Nothing beats Nuclear Holocaust in giving a game a dark tone. That said the game still manages to be relatively jovial and light-hearted.
The story follows two friends trying to make it in a world now ruled by militant ants. With the help of a few friends along the way they battle against the military might of ants. I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Again it was a bit short but the puzzles were varied and interesting. The characters are conveyed through their interactions as no dialogue is used. Speech/thought bubbles are used throughout to help characterize and indicate what you need to do to progress. It is really well done. The graphics and art style fit the game. Also the sounds are excellent, there is no voice acting as such but you get a real feel for the characters from the sounds, screams, etc. that they do make. The"cut scenes" come in the form of animated "comic panels" another style choice of which I approve.
If you are a fan of this kind of game I would pick this up.

Review subject to change as game is in Early Access:
With nearly 5 hours into the game after only one day, I believe this has lots of potential. From a minute to minute perspective the game is very similar to many other survival titles these days. Collect objects on the ground until you can make basic tools, then begin harvesting resources from trees/ore nodes/animals, etc.
Where the game begins to diverge, and it does this very well, is in how you learn new crafting recipies. You see in many games, you either inheritly "know" everything as long as you have the materials to craft it (ala Minecraft) or you have to spend skill points to learn new things. However, Ylands teaches you new recipies in two ways. First, having certain ingredients will allow you craft new items. But in many cases you have to craft a "key" item in a category to unlock other items in that family. With over 4000 items to use, spanning multiple centuries of history, it often feels like a Playmobil collection come to life.
For example, collecting fiber from plants allows you to craft "Yarn" and with the correct workstaions "cloth". However until you craft a needle and sewing kit, you can't craft any clothing. There is a secondary way to learn recipies, though. By collecting crafted items randomly generated in the world and discovered through exploration, you instantly learn many of the items within that subcategory without having to craft them yourself.
In addition, many items can be crafted in multiple ways. As one example a map (very important to have before leaving your first island) can be crafted either with paper and writing utensil, or via a leather hide and charcoal. Any combination of those ingredients will net you the end product, and some require significantly less work than others. It also prevents being locked in your progression because you are missing a key resource. Great idea Bohemia!
Lastly the other key differentiator, the building mechanics. We've all become a bit bored of the unreal based "snap and place" system. It can be extremely limiting and frustration inducing without heaps of mods to free up some of the rules. f Bohemia has created a building mechanic that provides the speed of snapping objects, with the versatility to free manilpulate any object in the world to place as you wish. They have even prevented builder frustration by including a built in timer on placed objects (currently 2mins) that allows you to instantly pickup any misplaced item, or break it for the full building materials cost. Once the timer is up, the item must be destroyed and for metal and stone items this can be very difficult.

This is the best and the smoothest playing of the earlier generation of Strategic Command games.   The distortion produced by the lack of hexes is not too severe, and the unit size and density is appropriate in the two main campaign scenarios (the 1914 Call to Arms from the Breakthrough game and the 1917 Fate of Nations from the Great War game).
The lack of stacking can sometimes feel a bit ludicrous in the game's WW II iterations, but isn't really a problem here.  The weakest link in the game series is the handling of naval warfare: the submarine and surface raider war is handled adequately, but the representation of big fleets leaves a lot to be desired.  But the overall naval war feels about right if you remember that you aren't really supposed to attempt a decisive fleet action, you just need to be able to threaten one.
The Breakthrough portion of the game package has some very interesting smaller scenarios, even if you aren't covinced that the game engine translates well to a smaller scale.
People tend to think of WW I as static and boring, but playing this game will show just how wrong that preconception really is.  The Western Front tends to become a static meatgrinder once the trench lines set in, but what playing the game on this scale makes you realize is just how dramatic and interesting the strategic choices were for both sides.
(And yes, I've spen less that ten minutes playing the Steam version of this game, but many, many hours playing and modding it when it lived at Battlefront before it migrated to Matrix.  Except for one scenario it's exactly the same game).

Sonic Adventure 2 is a great game. I have so many good memories playing this game, caring for my Chows and that epic music. That being said this is one of the worst ports for a game I have ever seen. Sonic Adventure 2 is a bad game. Full stop. The music is great and there's some sections, particularly the justifiably iconic City Escape level, which capture a nice since of speed that can be interesting, but the fickle camera and controls (I'm baffled by the fact that these actually got worse from Sonic Adventure rather than better), awkward character movement, complete lack of polish, repetitive Tails / Eggman levels, and outright torturous Knuckles / Rouge levels bring everything that is good about this game far, far down. Even the Sonic / Shadow levels, inarguably the game's highlight, aren't consistently enjoyable.
Stripped of the novelty, hype, and impressive graphics that Sonic Adventure 2 possessed when it first came out on the Dreamcast, it becomes obvious that this is a janky and poorly designed platformer which doesn't hold a candle to Super Mario 64 or its 2D predecessors. And despite this being a sequel to an iconic platformer, those platforming bits - which are the best parts of the game even if that isn't saying a lot - only make up less than a third of your play time. The entire rest of the game is worse and you spend far too much time doing things that have no relation to traditional Sonic gameplay. The later Knuckles levels can drag on for in excess of 35 minutes, making the game's absolute worst moments also it's most drawn out ones. At least the mech levels are marginally less glitch prone than Sonic's running ones. Not as if that's saying much. On the plus side of things, with some belated updates, the port is actually pretty solid even if it doesn't fix the game's original problems.
Nostalgia purchasers only. Grab Sonic Generations if you're looking for a modern Sonic game that is actually pretty good (and, as a bonus, doesn't feel the need to constantly force you to play as anyone but Sonic).

Insurgency is what other big budget shooters should try to be like. It's based more around strategy and good decision making than killstreaks or explosions (as it should be). This makes IMIC feel more like a classic military simulator among the likes of the original Rainbow Six or early Ghost Recon games, than Call of Duty or Battlefield. Even though death comes quickly and respawns are slow, I never felt frusturated because when I died I usually felt it was my own fault rather than cheap game design. I don't think I will be playing it for years on end like Counter Strike or TF2, mainly because there isn't a whole lot of content or support for it, but it certainly is worth playing at least a few times. While it is relatively simple (compared to most modern shooters) , it's alot of fun, especially since it's free.

This is probably a long overdue review. This game has taken the most hours from my life outside of any non-steam games. This game is playable again and again. You can pick and choose your character, how you look, your stats, your beginning equipment and stats, the difficulty is completely changeable.
For difficulty you can decrease the dmg the ai do to you as well as switch out the number of combatants per side per battle- perfect for new players to get the hang of things. For my first 100 hours of this game I was mainly getting the combat and mechanics of the game down as well as figuring out the multiplayer. Singleplayer and multiplayer are great crossovers as you learn things from both sides of this game that affect the other sides. Now with well over 200 hours I am up for more of a challenge, with 60 combatants in a battle instead of the basic 30 (the basic is great for when one is just starting and especially when one is new to the game.)
I believe the replayability is most of what keeps me coming back time and time again to this awesome game. I only play the vanilla (in general) but I also play fire and sword and Napoleon. Of them all, warband is my favorite for single player. Napoleon is my favorite for multiplayer. However fire and sword has taught me more than a few lessons that carry into warband just as well as vice versa.
As you may have guessed I am not really a mod person. That said, there are some really awesome mods for this game (youtube has pretty good videos if your on the fence about the M&B series- I do not recommend getting the original M&B as warband is better, unless you get all the M&B in a bundle).
I first was drawn to this from my TW gaming. At the time I had played over 200+ hours of RTW, and I was eager to get into an actual unit, to fight the way the men i commanded fight. M&B Warband provided that experience for me.
I have played as every faction in the game and led my side to victory. Currently I am leading the Swadians to victory- but i have a plan to consolidate my position in the north of the map and then crush the Swadians through a rebellion, effectively making myself the ruler of all Calradia.
My point is this. This game allows you to fight using authentic weaponry, develop your own skills and preferences, develop your own way of fighting, use amazing (in both look and function) equipment, AND choose how YOU want to end the game (Glorified Vassal or Emperor). This game has amazing replayability. If your on the fence after reading all these reviews, look up some campaigns on youtube. That's what helped me decide.

AirstrikeHD is one of those games that really requires no skill, no strategy or planning, just click and hope you destroy the buildings in time.  I've read a few negative reviews, and I honestly don't understand why people are being so critical. Were they expecting a significant upgrade due to it being released in 2016?  I can admit, the game is very basic, and there's really nothing to it, but it's far from being terrible.
One complaint I read that I can agree with is that there's really nothing to keep the game fresh.  The missions are the exact same thing, and while there are different planes you can fly, it's only an aesthetic.  Don't get me wrong, this is an enjoyable game, but it's not one that will be able to hold  your attention for very long due to how repetitive it is.  It would've been nice had there been some variation added.
I'm not sure if this was intended or if it's just me, but there seems to be a millisecond delay between when you press the fire button and when your rockets actually launch.  This can end up being confusing as you're right on top of a building, press the fire button, but it doesn't actually drop said rocket until you've passed it.  This is frustrating, and makes you unsure of when a good time to drop the bombs are.
This may be a stupid thing to critique, but I'm going to mention it anyway, and it sort of goes along with the above issue.  There's a power-up/negative item you get that is a magnet, and will bring your plane down in altitude.  When you try and hit a tall building but can't due to the before mentioned issue, this magnet can really screw you over.  I wish this wasn't a thing - at least until your bombs actually drop when you click.
Another complaint I read was about the game having poor graphics.  Uh....what do you want?  1080p graphics for a game where the visuals aren't even important?  Come on, people!  The graphics are mediocre, but again, this is not meant to be a visually pleasing game.  The graphics are perfect for the style of game this is.
I actually liked this game.  Basic, simple, and easy to get into. It just gets too boring after a little while.

This game turned up to be a mix bag for me, but after some thorough consideration, I decided not to recommend a purchase.
Graphically this is just about as good as a flash game, the art is neatly drawn and the animations are nice enough for what it tried to portray, though I wouldn’t agree with this as "high definition". Sure you can play this game in any screen resolution, but it’ll just stretch everything to accommodate your monitor, don’t fall for this stupid gimmick.
Presentation wise, I can see where the devs placed their efforts. You have 25 stages set in five different locales, 5 boss battles and a hidden seagull level. Almost every locale had some pop reference somewhere and every plane had their own unique take off sequence. But everything is ruined by repetition, time and again.
First of all, every plane performed the same way with the same upgrades earned by killing hidden generals. None of the bosses shoot at you ever and all of them were way too easy to beat. While you get to bomb buildings to the ground, they are always the same width of varying heights, with little variation on difficulty.
The biggest blunder must be the bonus crates, since they can punish the player by repairing buildings or "restart the stage completely". This mechanic has no design merits, and it can seriously annoy you as it did with other reviewers.
Lastly, this title can be completed within an hour, two if you go for every achievement. If you had to buy it, please do it during a sale.

At time of writing Airstrike HD has a positive review record (4/1). Three of the positive and the negative are all private reviews. I do not get it. Is this a blatant attempt to promote a game by cheating the Steam review system? I can understand that some people may actually like this game but not to the point where eighty percent of the early reviews are positive especially when three of the four are private. I’ve played much better developed and less repetitive games on Kongregate than Airstrike HD. That’s an honest assessment of the game.
The game is just too repetitive after the first level or two to keep anyone immersed in the game. Very little changes. You have slightly taller towers and you see the introduction of weather effects. To aide you you have the most basic of power ups – the plane slows down, bombs are replaced automatically, you stay on the same level twice, etc. It’s the same thing over and over again ad nauseam. The only time the game ever changes anything up is when you hit a bonus and the bonus is actually a penalty – buildings rebuild or something – and it leads to a more riskier yet higher scoring level.
It’s not as though I am demanding that developers use the latest and greatest technologies at their disposal when creating games or that some repetition cannot be a good thing because some of the games that Steamified has featured and looked upon very favorably so far this year have been repetitive and basic. But when the entire game is repeating exactly what you’ve done without sufficient change  and the core mechanics aren’t that interesting – it’s nothing more than an inverse space invaders type game where the enemies don’t attack you – it leads to tedium and boredom very quickly.
If I were to say something positive about the game is that it does indeed work as intended. It also has some pretty easily obtainable Steam achievements and has a set of Steam trading cards. In this respect the developers have done a thorough job in making their game Steamified. For this I can appreciate their game on an exterior level. Otherwise, this one is a bit of a dud I’m afraid.

Never was a fan of Left 4 Dead franchise, which is this game took inspiration and idea from, obviously, there was just not enough depth in the world and characters for me to care. Yes, levels was "somewhat" different, with varied loot and enemy positions, but there was little to no replayability in that game. In Vermintide on the other hand...
First off, graphics. What everyone cares about. Can you imagine a joy of your enemy head rolling down the stairs, and the sight of their nasty, spoiled blood on your blade? Have you ever spend minutes trying to take on every little detail, to try and shoot a candle's flame with an arrow? (I did, and even succeded)  Yet, theres not much time for you to stare and gaze around, unless you are in safe heaven of the game, tavern, because... Skaven!
Yes, Skaven, ratfolk. Half your size, ugly, stinky rats. What can this creature possibly do to you? You can kill it in one precise strike in the head! But wait, do you hear that? Its their claws, hundreds of them, and they are ALL after you. Can you hold your ground and push forward through endless waves of rats, each trying to stab you in the back, sides, face and feet!? Why don't you try out that arsenal of weapons you are offered and can add to.
Unlike L4D, in Vermintide every character is special to a degree. Each one of them have ranged and melee weapon, but each have own options for both of them. Three of them sticks to gunpowder based weapons and swords, maces, axes, shields, while elf only able to wield a bow, but with such skill, that she can easily match others! One somewhat unique character on the roaster is Bright wizard, who is able to use winds of magic and hurl fireballs at her enemies, or release a barrage of small fire missles in mere moments! Or wield a fire-infused sword. Watch out tho, as this same winds can bite you in the back, if you'll use them too much. Ever thought what would happen if you could... Explode from overusing your only ranged weapon?
Speaking about weapons. Ranged combat is somewhat basic and straightforward here. Shooting arrows, bullets, crossbow bolts and such, nothing fancy (except from fireballs and arrows that can hit up to three enemies), but the melee is the very flesh of this game. Dodging, blocking, striking back! In Vermintide you can really FEEL like you are trying to fight off waves and waves of rats, hit their small heads and pile their corpses in Sigmar's name!
Speaking about names now. Each character have a different personality, story behind their backs, their own motives. Its pretty fun to hear them blabbering to each other, even insulting sometimes or making nicknames! And its different with each(to a certain point) plays! Especially considering you are only using 4 out of 5 characters from the roaster.
Price is another matter here, usually i don't judge game by it's price, but considering all the expensive releases falling from the sky, i'm quite surprised that Vermintide is doing well with it's current price. Game might lack some features i wish to see in the future, but guys already working on first FREE DLC for the game, bringing new modes, improvements, new weapons!
My total score for this game is solid 8 out of 10. I can easily make it 9 out of 10 considering minor bugs and exploits being fixed already, and the steadiness of overall gameplay and replayability, rare thing in our days.
P.S. It was long since game really touched my feelings with its depth of gameplay, even if it (slightly) lacking story. You still can catch it up between missions if you care. I'm not a fan of Warhammer universe either, but this game i want to care about.
P.S.S. Bring friends. You will need them. Might want to gather some expendable ones first tho!

+Loot system

It’s very natural to scroll down in order to…well…scroll down the inventory. I don’t remember that being in other point and click games, so it was a nice addition.

Normally, I would write something silly, but to be honest, I actually have a strong opinion on this game.
*My opinion on the games story may not actually be what happened*
It's nowhere near as good as the first. The plotline is just that. A plotline. Filled with an unchronological set of events that don't actually mean anything at all. The only plot line that actually mattered, once more, was the phones, which I didn't like. In the first game, I loved exploring the sociopathic personality of Jacket. I loved how dangerous I felt. I just didn't get that from this game.
(Spoilers Ahead)
Once more, phones started to ring, people did bad things. This time, there was an objective: To start World War 3, Eventually succeeding in doing so. 50 Blessings being a patriotic group hated the Russian "Invasion" into their country, America. As such, they wanted people to kill the Mob. Unsatisfied, they then attempted to cause WW3 to completley irradicate Russia, assuming America was able to successfully invade.
The Jacket A.K.A "Richard" mask and it's constant appearance.
Simply put, that's actually the representation for post traumatic stress disorder. Those who see the Jacket mask or either on the brink of sociopathic insanity from the guilt of murder (that the phonecalls are making them do, hence why Pardo, or the "Miami Mutilator", kept leaving those notes saying he didn't want to do what he was doing. His mind then repressed the guilty memories, hence why he still thinks he is innocent) or were present in the battle in Hawaii (Basically this game's Vietnam) and as such are suffering from PTSD.
The remaining stories (The Son A.K.A Scarred Face Guy, The Henchman A.K.A The guy that wanted out, Richter A.K.A The Mama's boy, Pardo and The Writer.)
ALL. MEANT. NOTHING. They literally had no impact on the story, in my opinion.
The Guys With Masks.
Just a group of vigilanties, nothing more, It is important to note that they are clearly not right in the head and, as such, Mark The Bear did see the Jacket mask at one point, reinforcing my earlier statement. They are called "The Fans" because they saw what Jacket did, thought it was cool and decided to dish out a little Vigilante "Justice" themselves. That's it. They've no correlation with Jacket other than liking his "work" so to speak.
Oh and a bit of a quick clearing up for those who got confused as to the story in Hotline Miami, where the Biker killed Jacket: The Biker did not kill Jacket. I'm not sure how far along the timelime the Biker died but he was present in a few scenes in Wrong Number, though you have to look for him, don't just expect to see him plain and out in the open. In short: Jacket is alive, the Biker is dead and Jacket is in prison as he turned himself in after erradicating the Russian Mob Boss. "But you play as the mob boss in the game!" I hear you cry. No, that's his Son. "The Son". Did you really not catch on from that?
If you are expecting the game to be better than the first, don't. If you are simply reviewing it as a game then it's alright, but nothing special. Hope that this cleared up the story for those that played.

Preface: Played the original on Playstation to Platinum, and on PC (10h so far).
Hotline Miami 2 is a masterclass in tedium, analogous to waiting in line at Tesco.
The maps are overly sized, and if you value your sanity, you're left to wait for the patrol to come to you before you can dispatch them. Of course, you're free to approach them, but their field of view is a lot higher than yours, and it's close to certain that they'll tag you before they become visible.
The fast-paced play of the original is again stifled by an odd choice to move the ending of the brutal finishers to a player-controlled RMB click. I don't know why automatically completing the move has been dropped (Can I change it to automatically detach from what remains of my enemy's body? Let me know).
Weapons, while largely unchanged from its predecessor, come in a state of limbo as to whether your current character can use them, will unload them, or will either completely ignore to pick them up. (Act 2, L1. He failed to pick up butterfly knife?)
I hate that I have to leave a negative review. Seriously, HM is easily one of the greatest indie games of the 2010s, and with the developers stating that this is the last in the series, it's frustrating that it is being left in such a state.
Maybe I do just need to "git gud". Or I can just play something else, I suggest you do too.

Though Hotline Miami 2 is essentially the same in regards to gameplay, it is by far, different in comparison. It drops one my favourite elements in the first game which was the masks in favor of playing as different characters with their own perks. I reckon this worked better though and the ones where you got to further pick their playstyle felt like it had a better impact on gameplay compared to the first game.
A lot seem to complain about its difficulty, but I found it as a key highlight as it made me think on my approach every time and made finishing each level feel that much rewarding. Its difficulty will probably scare newcomers who haven't played the original, but those who loved the first one will surely have a blast with the second.
I don't think I've ever played a game that has made me so addicted and tense. The game is worth it not only because of its visuals and soundtrack, but also because it's a shooter that will actually challenge you.

Contagion is a horror survival FPS game running on the Source engine in which you play one of eight characters who have to survive in a zombie ridden world.
So what does this game offer:
- Multiple game modes, including:
• Escape: Follow 1 of 2 possible routes in zombie-infested areas to escape.
• Extraction: Find survivors and extract them.
• Hunted: Online PvP mode, at the same time survival fighting off zombies and scavenging for supplies and ammo.
• Panic: Objectives (player zombies and survivors only, like escape) and classic (1 turning into armored zombies and taking down others survivors, untill no one left or zombies life/time out).
• Flatline - coming soon.
- Multiple game-modes (including survival, survivor rescue, PvP and more)
- Offline & Online co-op multiplayer
- Encourages teamwork
- AI to play SOLO
- Atmosphere
- Long maps
- Challenging
- Good graphics
- Some paths in the level randomize with each playthrough
- Developers still updating the game with more content
- SDK
- Workshop support
This game is absolutely fantastic if you like horror zombie co-op, PvP, Difficult, SOLO Survival games.

Putting kittens into any game is going to instantly get you bonus points, but putting hundreds and hundreds of them into a game is basically a winning combination. Jones on Fire puts you in the shoes of a firefighter saving kittens from the burning blaze throughout a forest.
The gameplay itself is very simple. All you need is one button, the up key. Jones is constantly moving and you cannot stop, you must jump and slide under burning objects, if you miss the jump, the wall of fire catches up to you for a bit until you can gain some ground on it.
After each run through, you get the chance to spend your money, which is in turn granted by how many kittens you save. The rewards consist of straight upgrades, or one time abilities, such as cat nip, which basically attracts all the kittens to you without having to move to collect them.
Each run you get three lives, at the end of the three lives you have to start again, but you don't lose all of your rewards and upgrades, these are carried over. This makes it feel like every run you are improving your character in some way.
This game does the simplicity very well, there looks to be some more content on the way looking at the reward screen as there are two more sections with "Coming Soon" showing, so it will be interesting to see what else is added.
I can definitely recommend Jones on Fire for the price that is currently set at (£1,99), I have only played for half an hour and I can see myself jumping in again to save a couple hundred more kitties!
