Early Access Watcher Public Service Announcement
Game: Heavy Gear Assault
Update Version: Changelist: 12/29/16
Disclosure: This game copy was bought by the reviewer.
Game Footage:
I am going to have to disclose this despite the fact I have been dealing entirely with Early Access games the past year: I understand this game is in Early Access and I also understand it has been in the works for a long time. This is an evaluation of the present build and is entirely based on one simple principle: is it worth the current asking price. If you wish to purchase this as a means to support the developer, then it is your choice. I am simply pointing out massive issues with a game that feels like a pre-alpha as a way to provide the consumer with information. Now that this is out of the way, I will jump straight into the good qualities of the game.
The gears look wonderful (nothing special though) and the weapons have a great sound to them when fired. The few levels on offer do have a nice appearance and are varied in terrain constructions. One level in particular is simply gorgeous, especially at night when you have to deal with a raging sandstorm and the beautiful lightning streaks illuminating the sky. The Gear movement feels floaty when in run mode and husky when in standard walking mode, which really adds to the immersion of the sheer weight being thrown around. The options menu has a great selection of adjustments for visuals, sound and even UI color. That is about it in terms of the positives though.
To bluntly put it: the number of people playing is minuscule. I understand this game has been around a lot longer than its' release on December 29th, which is why I am mentioning it. The game is a multiplayer title only, so without the players to populate the servers, you essentially have a $40 ($34 at the time of release) purchase hanging out to dry. Something as simple as adding bots could have helped alleviate the issue, but for now that isn't an option.
The active player base is going to need to increase drastically to help hammer this issue out. When I was testing the servers near me earlier, the game was holding around 50-60 FPS without any players. The rest of the time, however, I was either playing on a server in Paris or over in California just so I could play the game. When this happened, the FPS decided to fling itself out the window and ranged from massive drops to 13-15 or held around 40-45. This is expected given the distance and is an issue on my end, but it is one that can only be fixed by playing on closer servers.
The control configuration options really need to be simplified from its' current system of selecting the key from a scroll list and replaced with the standard "Press key to replace." Camera controls are rather slow and could benefit from a mouse sensitivity slider (which might help with the slow weapon aiming as well). The tutorial is great for basic movements, but the rest of the commands  rely on trial and error, such as equipping weapons, capturing points and bolstering weapons (which for some reason shares the same key as drop weapon by default).
There are a couple of major bugs that start with the inability to stand up after toggling prone and end with the inability to even reload standard weaponry when you run out of rounds (it normally automatically reloads, manual reload seems to be disabled). The team member list on the top right portion of the screen fails to update so it is hard to really tell how many people are actually playing. Activating a unload when trying to grab a keg bomb or even trying to pick up a weapon can be annoying, requiring multiple key presses just to register the command. Crashes are a common issue, primarily when trying to enter a game, the tutorial or even when accessing the store (that has gears, parts and weapons for sale despite the "Coming Soon" sign meant for the images).
With all the technical issues, the low player base, the latency issues caused by the previous and the crashes hampering the overall experience, I just cannot recommend looking into this yet. If you manage to get a hold of a key, maybe, but I don't recommend paying $34 for what essentially feels like a pre-alpha stage build with a low map count.
This has been a EAW PSA.

Beautiful puzzles, beautiful music, beautiful interface.
I often find myself looking at jigsaw-style puzzle games in the Steam store, and I always end up passing on them for one reason or another.
I don't remember when I first saw Glass Masquerade, but I couldn't recall the premise when I saw it again on my wishlist. I visited the store page, took a look, and immediately bought it and played through the whole thing essentially in a sitting. It's a series of 25 puzzles of varying complexity, unlocked 1 or 2 at a time through branching paths.
Part of the game control disappointed me at first: Although yet-unused pieces freely rotate while they rest in the selection area, they automatically snap into the correct orientation as soon as they are dragged into the puzzle board area. I was expecting the pieces to require rotation, with either 4 or 8 possible orientations, but no flipping backwards. It's also a little strange to me that yet-unused pieces sitting in the selection pool are blacked out in silhouette. I guess being able to see the colors might be too much of a giveaway, even though the stained-glass aesthetic means color isn't always a good hint.
Another complaint I have is that sometimes the intended location of a given piece seems impossible or is easy to miss. Pieces held by the player are slightly larger than the space they will occupy on the board (not sure if this was meant to imply perspective relative to the puzzle board), and pieces on the board have shiny lines bordering them. If you need to place a piece with a narrow branch sticking out of it, you might not be able to see where it belongs because the "branch" portion may appear to be covered up by the overlapping borders of other pieces. I'm not sure if this is a resolution issue or what.
Even with those minor gripes in mind, I enjoyed the game and I wish there was more. I guess maybe after some time passes I can replay it as if it was new.

Wonderful, casual jigsaw puzzle game, I highly recommend it for anyone who loves doing jigsaws.
Not going to do the usual ratings scale. No point. It's a 10, for me at least. Your Mileage May Vary, depending on how you feel about jigsaw puzzle games. This one is the best one I have seen. Ever.
The art is stunning for fans of stained glass, or those who appreciate fine arts.
The music is quite relaxing, appropriate and soothing. Very nice audio here.
Runs smooth as melted butter, on an old toaster.
Puzzles are not too difficult, but not too easy either, due to the blind piece style used. You can add a touch more challenge by turning off the first piece highlighting that lets you see and snap the first pieces to predetermined dots on the puzzleboard. I did this, and played slowly, 5.7 hours for my first playthrough.
You cannot see unplaced pieces until you pick them up, which I like. The game does auto-rotate pieces to their correct orientations for placement, which some may find helpful. I would have like having this able to be turned off and manual piece orientation needed, but no gamebreaker. It was challenging enough to find the correct blank shapes to choose to flip over and fit into the open spaces. Kept my brain active while I played, and kept me engaged. The piece count per puzzle is not high, but the random shapes of the pieces along the stained glass lead-lines kept it from being too simple. Might be a bit frustrating for young kids or folks with ADHD or OCD- for real. I can see this game being either good therapy for either condition, or a potential problem for those who suffer from either.  Could go either way. I have a bit of OCD myself, and found it good therapy, for calming down and remembering not to stress out over things.
I bought this on sale, and it was more than worth the sale price of $2.99 USD. Full price of $4.99 USD is worth it, and I would have been just as happy if I had paid that amount.
Replayability? For me, yes. I feel that it has that. No time penalties, but it does record your time to complete each puzzle. And I want to go back and beat my first times. Even without the time recordingds, I know I will play this again just for the beautiful art and music, and for the stress relief and relaxation it provided.
A very nice, quality offering from an apparent first time Indie studio. I look forward to seeing what they offer next.

25 jigsaw puzzles - made as stained glass - with varying degrees of difficulty.  The game is enhanced by a pleasant soundtrack.  I've played it through a few times now, and am still enjoying the puzzles.
My only disappointment is that there isn't an option to reset the list of completed puzzles to track progress once you've completed everything the first time around - although there is a reset available using  LShift + RShift + W.

It's quite a beautiful game, but as a jigsaw puzzle it does lack in certain elements.  The scale of the pieces vs. the spaces to which they are to fit is not always clear.  As a general tip, it is better to rely on the image than the shapes.

(Puzzle)
Some of the options included are Resolution, Full-screen, Custom Cursor, Sensitivity, Hints on/off, and separate sliders for sounds and music.
Having the
on will give you help with placement of some edge pieces, giving you a good starting place, since we don't know what any of the clocks look like until we finish.  The way the hints work is that a few select pieces will glow red, and have a gold ring on them that you can match up on the clock face.  FYI, I played with hints ON.
There are 27 countries, 27 puzzles, and... wait for it... 27 Steam achievements.
As you can imagine with stained glass, these are not simple puzzles with predictable shapes and patterns.  Even when you have an idea what the image will include, you'll likely still find these to be a challenge.  For example, I was pretty sure I knew what the USA puzzle would portray, and it still took me 15.5 minutes to complete.  I somehow managed to finish one puzzle in less than two minutes, but there was also one that took me 21 minutes, so difficulty varies.
There are two things the devs did to

Sonic Adventure 2 does so many things right, but to truely enjoy the game...you have to pull through some sections that you will either LOVE or HATE. Details below
(I recommend playing this game with a Gamepad. I use this a reference when I use the terms "A", "B", and such. I am talking about a Gamepad)
SA:2s story is divided into 3 parts,
,
, and
Each story has 3 character each with their own play Style.

Continuing where Sonic Adventure 1 left off, Sonic escapes custody of the Military (CITY ESCAPE SONG PLAYS HERE), and encounters Shadow. Shadow Sends Sonic back into Military Custody and its up to Tails to break him free. Knuckles is off on his own for a majority of the game, collecting Master Emerald Pieces (Per Usual), which takes him to different parts of the map each with their own theme (I will touch on this later on)
After Sonic and Tails reunite, a series of unimportant events occur, blah blah blah, and Sonic has to go to space to destroy a Super Weapon. And go figure, the weapon is run off of the power of the Chaos Emeralds.
Eggman is infiltrating a military Top Secret base to uncover an "Ultimate Weapon", which he discovers is Shadow the Hedgehog. Shadow talks about a mission he must fullfill, and commands the Dr. around so he give the Dr. the "True Ultimate Weapon".  Shadow and Dr. Eggman team up with Rouge to recover Chaos Emeralds to power the Ultimate Weapon,  the world is about to blow up, end story.
After both campaigns are beaten, there is a secret story.
Speed sections have you running around at the speed of sound, got places to go have to follow my rainbow.
These parts of the game make everything worth while. Speed sections are fun, fair, and varied.
The only complaints I have are in the Shadow campaign, the Forest level has many glitches that it easy to die for no reason, but otherwise, I love these parts of the game.
Back in the day, having varied gameplay in your game was seen as innovative. Nowadays, going from a speedy high-octane part of the game to a slow paced "Hot and Cold Meter" style of hunting for gems is seen as a sin. If you can forgive this games age and its willingness to push these sections of the game on you then will enjoy the experience as a whole, way more...otherwise these sections of the game are hated by most of the community.
As Knuckles/Rouge, you are placed into a map with three emerald boxes on the bottom of your screen. You are challenged with exploring the area waiting for one of the gems to flash Green (Close), Yellow (Closer), or Red (Very Close) to find the pieces of the Master Emerald. Scattered throughout the levels are hint Robots, that will give you three hints as to the whereabouts of the hidden pieces.
Hold down A, move your cursor around to lock onto enemies, and release to kill them all.
This is how you kill enemies in these levels of the game. Although you CAN run up to badies and bash them (Which is a stupid idea), and you CAN manually aim at them (Easier said then done), holding down your A button and moving your laser around is the best way to kill enemies. And as far as i am concerned, it is the only way.
Here is where the problem lies: For 90% of the level, you holding down A, which causes a high pitched
sound to play non stop as long as you are holding down A. Sure the laser dies after a few seconds, but you can (AND SHOULD), hold down A again right after, just in case there are enemies off screen you dont see because the camera is trashy on these levels. Or who knows what, but holding down A gets SO ANNOYING, but is needed.
Like I stated above, the camera is trash in a mojority of these levels, and yet they require platforming on certain parts. Yuck. Levels like the Egypt and Space level as Eggman have certain angles that mess with your depth perception.
I do not enjoy these levels in the slightest.
SA:2 features a small side area of the game where you raise a Chao by giving it Power Core-ish bits you find when killing enemies, and animals. You can spend your rings in a Black market area to feed fruit or give gifts to your Chao. Each chao can be named and used to play mini-games, such as racing and fighting (But you have to pay to fight).
Show your Chao enough love, and you unlock a Chao Heaven!
Abuse your Chao and you can unlock Chao Hell...which is much cooler...
This little addition makes the game more enjoyable, and when you replay missions you are achieving something in itself when your return to your garden to upgrade your Chao.
The game is dated, we can all see that, so some courtesy is due.
+Decent Story...for a Sonic Game
+Fun Gameplay
+Chao Garden
+Good port
+Bosses are fun
-Hunting Levels can be boring.
-Shooting Levels are very bad.

It's a game you could share internationally without ever worrying about a language barrier! And the game itself is loads of fun to play! Set in a post-apocalyptic world in which things like roaches, rats, bees, spiders. etc. are the lone surviving inhabitants, players take on the role of an adorable little roach who wants to save his accident-prone friend from a series of escalating perils so that they can enjoy a beautiful flower together -- the first flower seen in a very long time. The puzzles are fun and engaging, the characters are likeable, the controls are simple and fun, and many of the adventures and puzzles you encounter take full advantage of the little roach's ability to walk up walls and along ceilings.
I really can't recommend it enough -- a truly delightful experience!

Nanbaka is a fantastic comedy anime which quite simply, is very entertaining and fun to watch.
It has a very unique and colourful art style which is very well done. The characters are all very unique and distinguishable from each other.
The show kind of takes a more serious lean part way through, and going into season 2 territory here, has some really good fight scenes. I feel that season 2 does a good job of splitting the comedy and serious narrative together whereas season 1 does either or, but is still good.
I have previously watched both seasons but have bought it on here to support it through Crunchyroll, and would reccommend anyone to try it.

I've already streamed both seasons of Nanbaka on Crunchyroll (sad that we won't see a season 3 until January or so), and I have found it both humerous and exciting. Season 1 may put people off, and for some, it may be season 2, though now it's starting to show its true colors (I've read the web comic long before its release).
Season 1 focuses more on comedy, whereas season 2 focused more on Jyugos and their past (1 of the 4 main characters, though he's the 'true' protagonist). Season 2 is probably the better of the two seasons, it maintains its humor aspect while something serious is happening (ie:
). It's moreso fun to watch because each of the characters are relateable to a a degree, some may relate to you completely, and it's hard NOT to like Hajime, the overpowered guard that no one wants to fight (except for Gokuu).
Overall, I'd say it's a good series deserving of your attention, at the least you should watch a few episodes while the series is on sale (or Stream it via Crunchyroll/VRV)

The game itself has a nice concept and is with no doubt a very fun game, though it might get grindy at times. However, whats wrong is the game engine. This game is riddled with bugs. The gameplay itself is Left4Dead-like. You've got different specials that all function like those in left4dead. The GasRat will deny an area with toxic gas, the PackRat will hook your teammate and drag them away to be hung, the GunnerRat would target 1 specific member until they are dead, the GutterRat will pounce and stab and disappear into the shadows when hit. Then theres the ogrerat which is the tank. One special thing to note is that there's these Stormvermin. Armorclad rats that are easy to take down when they're by themselves, but when they're patrolling as a group, you best avoid them. They'll surround you and push the team away from each other. Tl:dr, The game is fun, L4D players will love this. However, it's got its fair share of bugs and if you can get pass those, you will enjoy this game.

This is a pretty good jigsaw game. It has a number of oddities which will either frustrate you or add some difficulty, depending on your point of view.
First, you can't see what the pieces actually look like until you drag them around. Second, you can't fit pieces together unless you're actually placing them on the grid, so (because the pieces are hidden unless you're dragging them around), the puzzles sometimes take on a bit of a memory-game aspect. "OK, this piece is one of the bird's wings, I know I saw another one which was the mirror image of that somewhere, now where was it ..." Third, the outlines of the pieces dont always match the spaces they fit into in the puzzle very well.
I felt all of these things added difficulty, and that this was good because the puzzles are not especially hard.
One quirk of the game is that the "dials" that display the pieces don't work the way you might expect them to. Although it looks like there's an inner dial and an outer dial, the sets of pieces you're rotating through on the left and the right sides of the dial aren't the same. That is, there are actually four sets of pieces to scroll through, it's just that often two of them scroll at the same time.
The game is pretty short - I took my time, doing a couple of puzzles a night in a leisurely way, and it lasted me about four hours. If I'd done it all in a single binge it probably would have taken me two.

I love that the clocks are in different shapes, and you can spin the 'wheels' on the side with the pieces to find one you want. Also really like that the pieces are just shapes until you select them to try them, and then the color/pattern is revealed. It's a very relaxing game and I found myself just wanting to continue and put them all together. I made myself stop though, to save some for another time.
Overall the puzzes, even when ranked 'difficult' aren't terribly hard. Some def make you think longer and mess with the pieces, but they're all doable and nothing is so exasperating that you can't manage it. I also liked trying to figure out what the picture was as it was taking shape.  I really hope they come out with more like this, since it's really a very beautiful and relaxing puzle game.

Glass Masquerade (which I'm very tempted to shorten to "Glassquerade") is undeniably a gorgeous game, that much can be said without question. But underneath the spectacle of the visuals, this is a very solid game about putting together fantastical stained-glass jigsaw puzzles -- and for the TL;DR: I recommend it highly to anyone who enjoys this style of game.
The mechanics are as simple as drag and drop. One thing I appreciated about Glass Masquerade was the way in which puzzle pieces are managed. Rather than having the pieces in a jumble under the puzzle space, they're instead housed in a scrollable wheel around the puzzle -- and frankly it's the best system I've ever seen, because it negates the issue of being unable to find a piece because it's under something else and simplifies a lot of the headache that can come from trying to organize your pieces. It was a very welcome surprise!
The music is fitting and unobtrusive as well, and it complements the experience without grating on my nerves even after staring uncomprehendingly at a blank spot in the middle of the puzzle for an extended length of time. Beyond the occasional quibble of inadvertently moving the wheel of puzzle pieces instead of grabbing the one I wanted (or vice versa,) I really have no complaints with this game whatsoever. It's a joy to play.
Because the game is so simple, it needed to get all the little details right -- and in my opinion it has. It's very satisfying to play, and finally placing down that last piece to see the full artwork is always gratifying. If you like jigsaw puzzles or puzzles in general, I would recommend giving Glass Masquerade a try -- it's a feast for the eyes, a fun diversion for the mind, and overall a well-priced, welcome additon to just about anyone's library.

This is the most disempowering simulation I have played.
That is not, to say, that it isn't also an excellent simulation. It's a mediocre game, but a phenomenal simulation. Maybe not for its efficacy of allowing you to do what you want, but for its complete obstinance in making that anything other than easy. If you have fantasies of living in a medeival land and being a roamnig hero, beholden to no-one and helping the common man, prepare to be bored out of your mind. The peasants mostly want to be left alone, and when they do want things it's things like grain. Or cows. And when they actually have problems you want to help with, like bandit attacks, they don't ask you to hunt bandits for them. They ask you to teach them how to defend themselves. Everything they ask for is reasonable. That's what makes it so numbing. Eventually you abandon your desire to be a roving, solo hero. (Perhaps you are sick of being run down and gored to death by a practically untrained mercenary who just coincidentally owns a horse, which elevated him to the status of a god. So you get a few friends and wander with them instead. You do some good deeds. You train some peasants. Whatever. Your small warband starts asking for pay. You realize you can't just keep a dozen skilled warriors on retainer without producing an income. You start working for guilds. Then lords. Your warband grows.
Flash forward a bit and you're collecting taxes, refusing to give the collected taxes to the lord you're collecting them for, razing villages and selling their valuables, growing rich on your mercenary war-profits by collecting pay from a liege whose wars you never actually help with and going mad with transitory power.
I mean, if you want power. And frankly there isn't much else to aspire to, despite the level of simulation. Sure, you can romance a few noble ladies. Or men, depending on your gender, but they predictably require far less romance. But that process is ardurous and takes agonizing months if not years of letter writing and 'visits'. "I need to see you, love!" "I am here!" "Okay, later!" +3 affection.
Wow.
Maybe you want to lead a kingdom. Become a rogue power taking castles and villages and coming to lord over a vast army.
Well, your army size is limited by your Leadership. Better grind that. Not that it matters, your enemies scale so their armies are always bigger. Lords who you need to woo into your service take months if not years of letter writing and 'visits'. "My friend, we should speak!" "Okay." "We have spoken, goodbye." +1 affection (sometimes). So...you'll never in any reasonable timeframe get what you want.
So it's an excellent simulation of medeival life. You can't really get what you want. The most effective short-term gains come from screwing over peasants, and your success can be instantly destroyed at the whim of a lord that glanced at you across a field and happens to have a larger army.
Who am I kidding? The game's rigged. They -all- have larger armies.
...actually, that doesn't sound very simulationist.

I dont like the way the game looks (i prefer Sonic Adventures models) Audio-wise, On paper it stands to reason I should not like Sonic Adventure 2 within any way.
But Ill start by getting to the elephant within the room first - If you are running "Intel" of any description, you will
enjoy this title, It will run within slow-mo. I dont mean,
, I mean City Escape (first time through) took me 50 Real-Time Minutes to complete - Slow-mo.
There is currently no fix for this, And from this basis alone - I dont recommend this particular version. As I am one of the unfortunate few who run Intel. However, ignoring that and the super slow-mo gameplay. Lies what is arguably a generally mixed whether this could be considered better or worse compared to the original.
Within the original some of the levels are shared by multiple characters, accomidating for many different playstyles, with as little level alterations as possible. This lead to an issue where the levels are not talored to suit every character entirely.
Sonic Adventure 2 features character specific levels, Sonic remains within the high-speed action stages, Knuckles remains within his treasure hunting stages and tails has been religated to a mech. On the reverse side of things, the original adventure had stories talored to each character, Involving you able to choose the gameplay style that you want to play with arguably, more levels.
Meaning if you are not someone who enjoys Knuckles stages, or you just wanted to play as sonic without any other characters, Adventure 2 will annoy you - as your forced to play other characters during the storyline. But for the most part the level designs are better than the original. With one or two small gripes.
As someone who likes rock, this might sound like nick-picking, I just think sonic titles should have a good variety of music. But the music overall is alright, Dispite the lack of overall variety.
Something that could be considered to be an issue within the original was - If you wanted to beat the game, you needed to complete 6 stories, Within Adventure 2 its streamlined to two seperate stories. Hero and Dark.
Hero - Consisting of Sonic (speed), Tails (Mech) and Knuckles (hunting treasure)
Dark - Consisting of Shadow (speed) Dr Eggman (Ivo Robotnik - Mech) and Rouge (hunting treasure)
The gameplay styles are taking from the original adventure, however the levels are more focused on that particular gameplay style and overall the levels are better designed for that particular character. The only real things to mension here is If you have played Sonic adventure as sonic - Speed is exactly the same.
Mech - Basically the same, but with a number of - enemy appears before you with 1 second to react enemies which can get annoying.
Treasure hunting - they have somewhat ruined this entirely to the point I would say its almost not fun. the game selects a item for you and you have to find that particular item (out of 3) if you find either the second or third pieces, the game will not tell you your anywhere near any of the other pieces. Purely because it is not that one item it wants you to get.
Cutscenes are awkward - the storyline falls appart when you start thinking about anything, But then you dont play a sonic title for a storyline. Your in for it with the idea of speed which the game can deliver.
All things considered Adventure 2 is a title I would say, you can forget about - However if it interests you, by all means pick it up. It can be fun, Just dont expect a huge number of hours to go into this, you will either get right into it or you wont.
As for DLC - "Battle" If you skip getting it, you essentially get Sonic Adventure 2 as it was originally released and the "Battle" DLC adds multiplayer (locally) I really do not recommend this. Purely because the likely-hood of getting to play a multiplayer game is fairly slim these days, Especially considering this is DLC. Which costs money, that the game probably should have had this in the release to begin with.
My verdict, skip the Battle DLC, if you have nothing else to play or want to try and get into some older titles. Adventure 2, I would recommend after the original Adventure. Purely because it feels like sonic - But in 3D. Adventure 2, is lets try making a 3D sonic title, without trying to retain all the classic-ness the original had in relation to the original titles.

Welcome to my review of Far Cry 3.
I will discuss all the negatives and possitives you need to know,if you are interested to buy the game.
The game requires Uplay – and you have to have Steam and Uplay active to play the game.If you don't mind this,we will continue to the positives.
I will not compare this game to the others of the franchise because is different in many ways.First the story in the game is more serious and you will want to know what happens next,see how the story unfolds – but there is one big problem …
And that's that wonderful open world that they have created.You can get lost, doing side missions,activities and collectibles.You can/and will hunt animals so you can craft better gear,to expand your inventory.And most of the events get your worth of time spending passing them. For example – if you go and unlock all the Radio towers not only you will have the complete map – but also free weapons in vendors.
The gunplay is awesome,it's easy to get used to,and you will be having fun everytime you have to go to combat.
The gameplay is varied,most of the mission you can go gun-blazing but you can go stealth also.
I passed the main story + some side activities in more than 20 hours,but I kinda want to go back to finish what I have left behind.
The story is great,the voice acting and music really shines – and show how good they wanted you to immerse yourself in the role of the main character,how you want to save your friends like him,how you would want for him to finish his journey.
Far Cry 3 showed us,that not only open worlds can be immersive and fun – but also can give a good story driven experience.If you like a open world in which everything you do,you will have fun doing buy the game.If you want to play a open world game,in which not only the content is much larger and you have hours of activities to do,but also you will want to do them – you will want to finish the story.

So I played this game for 4 hours now, and I like it a lot.
The algorithm('s) should be in the brightest spotlight here:

Update 03/05/2017
Well I've racked up 141 hours now and this is the game that has come closest to getting me over my Rust/Ark jones. Key features:
• The community at the time of writing this is pretty small. It deserves more, this game is head and shoulders over all the other cheap-mid range survival games.
• There's not much pvp but you'll probably be too busy to worry about it for the first while.
• You're building a colony full of npcs and they're not too bad at their jobs.
• At the start you're very definitely in danger and will be killed.
• You will almost never lose your inventory so you can run around with everything you own on you.
• The wikia etc etc is a joke so you have to find a lot of stuff out by yourself. Leading to:
• Colony management is a bit tough but you get used to it. Its would be the first thing I'd overhaul, for example sometimes some piece of machinery or colonist refuses to work but I always found the reason or the problem seemed to go away by itself after a while.
• Crafting seems tough at first but its not bad at all.
• Good array of fancy weapons, armour and all that.
• The creation engine knocked it completely out of the park, its amazing. Hats off to whoever developed that. You can pretty much design anything out of voxels including vehicles, crazy helmets, working bladed weapons. And you can give your character a big veiny willy up to approximately one metre in length, basketball sized testicles and/or rocket knockers.
The best server to be on is one with:
All scripts unlocked, ♥♥♥♥ scripts.
Skills active, otherwise you get a pretty weak character fully dependent on his/her gear
Survival/Adventure
And although there are some outages (which can often be sorted by quitting right out to the main menu) One of the most dependable servers within the above parameters is Official Survival_Ad2
Things I'd like changed
No more bloody male or female armour. it should be unisex. There's no reason to double the list in the fartarsing replicator.
A little more pvp, it could be limited to people over a certain skill level. How cool would that be?
Just a personal niggle, I'd like to see the strength of the sliders in the character creation suite increased to about 400% of current because I'm not able to make freakish enough homunculi to suit my refined tastes. At least they let me be primary colours :)
What if there was a high level device you could build to automate all the crafting? Just click particle rifle and build and you have it  There's no reason why it wouldn't work and no reason why a high level character should have to go through all the clicking that's often involved in getting yourself simple enough (in the late game at least) items. Empyrion has it.
Are you listening Pathea? TRAINING QUEUE - MAKE IT. Training is a pain in the hole. I should not have to check it every 5-18 minutes. I want to click buttons for a few minutes and come back 3 hours later to several fully trained buttheads.
Tips/Stuff I wish I'd known
Keep plenty of healing bandages and revival shots on you. it never hurts to keep 3x antibiotics and disinfectant spray on you in case you get sick. You have about a 20% chance of that at any time, by my reckoning.
Keep some kind of bed in your inventory. Characters in PE are♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥when it comes to sleep.
You only have to mine a bit of every resource. About 1k is an ample amount. Then you can build your colony and make your colonists go get it for you.
Titanium and Lithium are the only two things your colonists can't get for you. Ti is needed for all the high end armour and weapons and its very deep so you need to scan for it when you're well below the surface. Li is nearly useless.
Build your base up high because every time you spawn in you'll be attacked by beasts or in rare cases npcs. If your base is higher than the larger beasts you'll often get away with no damage to it. At the same time you need to have some terrain inside your base's shield to grow plants on.

Hours on record at the time of reviewing - 172.5
Planet Explorers has been a ton of fun, and I have racked up 120 nerd hours since picking it up after full realease. Consistent, addictive, great map design with Maria (Main Story map). You can appreciate the detail and thought that went into making the VIP Colonists roles (Botanists, geologists, zoologists, bacteriologists, miners, security) Keeping in mind what sort of new or unknown viruses may be present in the that new planet. Seems to me pretty up to par when a real planetary colonization effort would take place in a distant future. Good variety of ISO's, the freedom to craft whenever and wherever you want and with a good and steady growing community uploading their creations if crafting is not your thing and rather spend more time playing, building and progressing.
There is enough content, gameplay hours and sandboxing in Story Mode to make up for the flaws that that need some correcting in Adventure Mode, which are the following:
• Adventure mode still feels bland, lacking content and not up to par with what is found in Story Mode, not really delivering those same dramatic landscapes and backdrops. Feels like it could be delivering a lot more, the randomly generated maps have a lot of imperfections (Terrain leveling, roads that go into the water, high-level monster spawnings where you're just starting out.
• The Dungeons in Adventure Mode feel bland, linear, lacking some polishing, same layouts often found, the monsters in there are just the same wildlife found anywhere else on the map and not even following a theme of which biomes each are found, but rather mixed in together.
On a more positive side, there are things found in adventure mode that would like to see in the other modes:
• The unique building models that would save us some time when builing a colony and placing the already built structures to house colonists and shops for vendors.
• The road network between colonies/towns.
Overall I'm looking forward to the remaining gameplay I got, taking my sweet time with progressing the story, while building and exploring along the way. I feel like my initial investment back when the game was in early alpha was a good investment in the hopes of having a good finished product delivered in full-release and with updates/builds still coming in, and will most deffinitely support Pathea in further development and future DLC/Expansions for this game, I see it as a mint product that with the right new updates and content it has the potential to go far and have a long life and growing community.
Thanks Pathea!

Contagion is a neat little game, Best described as "dayZ light". If you like the concept of dayZ pvp and loot but don't want to suffer through a "simulator" that requires large amounts of time investment and forces you to eat/drink and walk extreme distances then Contagion is worth a try.
This game also has a coop mode that is basically Left for dead but with more players. Players must get from one objective to another and find gear along the way. One cool thing about contagion is that when you die you spawn as a zombie until the next round. This means that if you are infected or die early on you don't have to be taken out of the action.
The PVP mode is basically a free for all. Everyone spawns around a pretty large map with a pistol and compete for gear. You can choose a building and board it up to create a little hideout.
Its pretty intese when dozens of zombies are trying to bust into your little fortress.
When you die you respawn as a zombie for a chance to get revenge on whoever killed you.
As a zombie you can gather hoards of NPC undead and direct them toward the survivors.
This game features a nice variety of gear. Everything from Crossbows to machine guns and plenty of melee weapons. Also the devs continue to add gear and maps for free.
Only a few nitpicks with this one: Some maps can be difficult to navigate in coop. You can sometimes get lost especially if you aren't sure what to do next. Also some servers have zombie players disabled. This means that if you die you will respawn as a cockroach until the round ends.
I suggest avoiding those servers unless you really hate those pesky player zombies.
Also the population of the game can sometimes die between steam sales and content updates.... Only a few servers to choose from in those scenarios.
Overall this game is really cool because you get the intese PVP that dayZ is known for but without the open-world grindyness or low framerates that dayZ subjects its players to. Contagion runs on the source engine so the framerates are high on a variety of system configs. The graphics aren't anything special but the game still looks great. I give it a thumbs up.

In Door Kickers, you take control of a SWAT team in a variety of different hostile situations. It is a top down, 2D realtime strategy game that allows you to make critical decisions at a moment's notice or plan entire missions from the very beginning of an operation.
After a few hours of playing the Single Missions, I fell in love with Door Kickers. The controls are simple and easy to understand, and watching your plans in action is always satisfying. The sheer amount of different scenarios, ranging from hostage situations to raiding criminal headquarters, makes each mission feel like a new tactical challenge for your SWAT team. With 6 campaigns, 70+ Official Single Missons, Level Generator, unlockable gear, and downloadable mods, Door Kickers has plenty of content to keep you busy.
Although I enjoyed Door Kickers, there are a few minor flaws. The game offers you dozens of unlockable gear such as guns and equipment, but I found myself using what I was comfortable with and had no trouble throughout the game. My only incentive to unlock and test all the guns was for the achievement. Also, there were a few situations in the Single Missions and Campaign that feel unbalanced and in favor of the AI.
Overall, Door Kickers was an addicting and enjoyable strategy game from start to finish.

I came across this beautiful little gem while I was browsing for bargains during the summer sale. I have to say, this game didn't disappoint me like a few other bargains did. Essentially, it's a glorified jigsaw puzzle game, with each country (25 countries total, I think) having a puzzle of their own you must complete. The image pertains to something about the country, such its past, tourist attractions, etc.
After you complete each artpiece you are taken back to the map to pick your next destination. The game isn't entirely linear, as you have a path you can follow, which branches off to various countries and regions. You can choose whatever direction you'd like, or even backtrack to another area. Also, each puzzle is rated in difficulty from one to five, so you'll have an idea of how long it will take.
To boot, getting the achievements is easy. You get one for each country you complete. So, if you're looking for a 'perfect' game, with all achievements completed, then this one may pique your interest.
The game has soothing music, which sometimes varies according to where you are in the world. And, the visuals are really nice. The game overall is very relaxing, even when doing the most difficult puzzles.
Really, the only con about this game, which is minor, is that the pieces are just a bit larger when you pick them up, which makes finding the right spot sometimes slightly more challenging.
Overall, I recommend this game, especially if you love beautiful visuals, art, country related themes, jigsaw puzzles, and/or something casual to unwind with.

While I'm not a fan of browser based games. I must say I am very pleased with the graphics quality of this game. It has some very annoying glitches and it seems to have an issue detecting multiple grahis cards in laptops ie it detects my integrated graphics twice as intel 4400 and intel 4400 (2) but can't see my geforce 7800 at all. Despite that the graphics run smooth on high settings but directx video driver crashes are an issue. I would like to see destructible objets in the game right now only fences seem to be destructible. You can shoot at a tree, building or even head of cabbage in a field all day with no effect I see a lot of griping on  chat about glitches but glitches do seem to be getting some attention though not as much as new content or improving eye candy. You can play free or pay for veteran status which gives bonuses towards experience allowing you to rise in rank much faster and unlock rank or skill related weapons, vehicles and skill badges. I work full time and have a family. I'm not a 13 year old who can play 24/7 so I have limited time to enjoy gaming and veteran status allows me to enjoy what game time I do get without being stuck at private forever. The paid cost is lower than most online games. I got 3 months of paid veteran status for 21.95US which is not bad at all. The ranks are not historically accurate. For instance the rank of lance corporal did not exist and technician ranks exist as subordinate ranks when in reality a technician 5th class was the same grade as a corporal and to be technical that "T" under your stripes put you in a higher pay grade so it could be argued that the tech ranks were above the standard rank. I find it irritating to have to rise in enlisted rank twice first as a tech then as the standard rank as they are the same. Game balance is an issue. A high explosive shell from a tiger tank will not damage a jeep or it's occupants yet I have had my tank fliped over useless on respawn and been killed outright by bicycles running me  down. It also seems that every infantryman has antitank mines making tanks the most vulnerable units in the game with very limited respawns a tanker lives in fear of a lone infantrman coming up behind him and planting a mine. Also a mine will destroy the tiniest tankette as well as the largest heavy tank with a sigle blast. Vision is severely restricted as well in a tank but resist opening your hatch for a better look see as snipers will take you out almost instantly. This same issue crops up for snipers as the lie prone looking for targets with their scopes it's common for an infantry unit to come up from behind and take them out with anything from a shovel to a machine gun. Infantry have a rough time as well. While it is possible to direct hit a moving infantryman in the gut with a tanks main cannon and it has happened in real life it seems much too easy in the game. I have taken out dozens of infantry in one mission from the other side of the map in this way. So every class has a balancing issue. My biggest gripe about the game is it has a multitude of weapons and vehicles yet the Panther tank is nowhere to be found. There is only 1 heavy tank for the US but the US never took armored vehicles seriously but at the same time the Russians have the same issue but had multiple tank types which are missing here no kv tanks and only 1 SU85 for the tank destroyer slot. I hope to see more varied units in the future. Despite all these issues I think this is the best WW2 mmo out there despite tank killing bicycles :) And I highly recommend giving it a try if you are a fan of ww2 era games.

3) Tanks be tanks! They can be used to make great pushes as well as a great counter vs infantry. But it's not indestructable. Other tanks and infantry with AV weapons can make quick work of them.
4) Graphics are definitly a plus, maybe not quite CoD quality (But then again, CoD is only about graphics and not story)
5) NO FACTION JUMPING! I love this feature because otherwise you have the people switching sides just because they got tired of losing, causing a landslide of no opposition to the winning side. Fight to the death or hang up your boots dammit!
Cons:
1) Can get REALLY repetitive for specific groups, i.e. tanks only really playing on one map tile (I hate that damn town map with the church and bridge!)
2) Load times with some of the more specific battle groups (i.e. Heavy tanks!) have tremendous wait times to get a game. (paratroopers are about 6-10 minutes! Heard Heavy Tanks have about 30-60 minute waits!)
3) THE EXP REQ FOR LEVELS!!!!! OMG so ♥♥♥♥ing annoying! Just to get to paratrooper level (which iirc is about 8 or 9) took me and my brother (I was playing nights while he played days so approx. 16-20 hours straight gameplay per day on one character!)  about 2 to 3 weeks to get the rank. I would love to see the general's side of things and hopefully help out with it, but as it is, it'd take me the better part of 6 months with my brother playing it hardcore to get to that level.
4) Aircraft are pretty useless! Don't get me wrong, I like that they have the aircraft in the game, but it is DAMN HARD to get bombs just right. . . then you have to wait 2-5 minutes for your next bomb. . . So unless you're a crackshot with your normal guns, you'll probably get 1-2 kills every 10 minutes, while your team may be floundering playing some infantry down due to 3-5 people flying around being nearly useless.
5) Finally, the reduced exp and money is more than ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t in this game. A lot of other games that have that sort of mechanic for rewards I can get behind because their levels and cost for items isn't so far out of wack. This is just terrible though, like i said me and my brother played together about 16-20 hours a day and barely got 8 or 9 levels. At that point we did calculations for if we added premium bonus and we still found that it'd take about 4-5 months to get to max level with hardcore play.
The money isn't much better, but it's much more managable, the guns aren't anywhere near as rediculously priced as the levels, but they are still pretty expensive. not even including the prices for addons and ammo.
Overall, I'm not sure what to rate this, it's a hit or miss imo. On the one hand you have a much more realistice war, generals basically moving player's battle groups to conflicts to start PvP matches. On the other hand, a decent number of the generals are pay to play and don't know what or where to move battle groups and sometimes mess up what might be a good defense/offense into enemy territory.
The one thing I'm incredibly sad I didn't get to test out though, was the general's version of the game. I was really wanting to get there, but the amount of exp and time required to put into it just wasn't something I was willing to pay.

By now, every modern day gamer has heard of Call of Duty. Some like it, some hate it, some are indifferent to it. Some prefer Treyarch, some prefer Infinity Ward, some don't care either way. Call of Duty: Ghosts marks the 10th installment of the series, developed by Infinity Ward and released between the Black Ops story arc. The term "ghost" was first used in the series during the Modern Warfare storyline, where a skull-branded baklava-clad soldier nicknamed Ghost appeared. Infinity Ward's last release had been Modern Warfare 3, so they decided to roll with a concept that they had already introduced briefly.
Call of Duty: Ghosts introduces some new and interesting concepts into the series, some which Infinity Ward had scrapped from their Modern Warfare trilogy. One of these scrapped concepts that has been placed into Ghosts are the outer-space missions, which have interesting mechanics to them. You can rise and descend, and propel yourself forward, all while floating in zero gravity. Except for an extremely brief stint in space during one of the Modern Warfare titles (wherein you don't even so much as move, it's more like a cutscene), this is the first time during a Call of Duty campaign where you can actually interact in space. Another series first is the ability to control Riley, the faithful German Shepherd companion of the Ghost team; it marks the first time that a non-human, non-machine becomes playable.
The story is the most linear of the franchise up to the point that it was released in 2014. Taking place in 2017, the game starts off with two brothers, Logan and Hesh, and their dad, Elias, who is telling his sons a 'creepy' story about the legend of the Ghost soldiers and the mythology that surrounds the way that they came in to existence. They begin making their way back to their home, when suddenly the Orbital Defense Initiative (ODIN) becomes hijacked and is used to destroy several cities in the southwestern United States. Needless to say, the family survives and Logan and Hesh join a special command unit led by their father, who is a U.S. Army Officer. I cannot say too much more without spoiling the entire plot, but the main goal is to find a man named Rorke, who is hellbent on killing every remaining Ghost.
With that being said, the entire plot feels like nothing more than an extensive revenge mission. There were so many bigger and better directions that Infinity Ward could've taken with Call of Duty: Ghosts, but they opted for the laziest and most simplistic plot available. There's nothing to do with saving the world, you're not on some fancy secret operative mission, you're not in some high-class undercover special ops, you're just on a standard blood-lust mission that takes you through some really unique levels. I do also believe that this title has the least amount of playable characters in the entire franchise; although I am not a Call of Duty expert, so do not quote me on that... Black Ops may have had fewer. You will primarily control Logan, occasionally Riley, Elias exactly once, and an astronaut specialist named Baker; also exactly once.
Ghosts comes with both its blessings and its curses. Compared to all of the releases that came before it, the shooting aspect of this installment is the least pleasing; the guns are boring, the bullet-to-enemy connectivity doesn't feel as solid, and its just overall lacking something that I can't quite put my finger on. Perhaps its the lack of actual shooting that takes place, as a good 90% of this game is made up of action and/or stealth scenarios, and using machines such as helicopters or remote snipers to take out foes. Most of the time, your crew will do all the heavy lifting for you as well, leaving you few kills to actually perform. On the bright side, Ghosts does feature some incredible scenery and landscapes such as humid, dense jungles, outer-space missions, and a beautiful underwater level that takes place near a coral reef and sunken ship.
Now, the multiplayer aspect in Call of Duty: Ghosts has been long deemed the worst of the series. To be quite honest, I only played a couple hours of multiplayer on this game and I was neither fascinated nor put off by it; it all just seemed rather average to me. There are some changes that have been made, including all new fully destructible environment areas. However, good luck finding someone to play with as multiplayer on this game has been dead since it began. There is also the new solo or co-op Squad Mode, which has three different play types, and also the also the new Extinction Mode, which is similar to the Zombie Mode from Black Ops, but with aliens instead. Neither of these features are exceptionally impressive, nor are they worth much more of a mention.
When it comes right down to it, Call of Duty: Ghosts is a rather lackluster experience; which is a shame, since I'm usually "Team Infinity Ward". During my first couple of hours with the game, I thought the other reviewers were crazy and just didn't know what a good game was. The truth is, while Ghosts starts out promisingly, it's really the story and lack of shooter gameplay in an FPS title that causes it to fall off the map; with the real emphasis being on the incredibly uninspired story. If there was more of a point to what is being done within the game, rather than it all being elaborately dedicated to revenge, then maybe players could've settled with the fact that there is barely any gun play involved. I'm truly torn between a thumbs up and thumbs down on this one, but I'm going to go with the thumbs up simply because Call of Duty: Ghosts does have some great, diverse levels that we haven't seen in the series before. If you can get it for less than $10, then go for it... otherwise, don't bother.

From the reviews I’ve read on the store page no one has mentioned what you actually have to do in the game. The objective is to get the blue square on to the green surface by using the red cubes to launch it and the other yellow squares into the air, if the blue square lands on and doesn’t fall off the green surface you complete the stage.
The game is mostly trial and error, the devs for about 35 out of the 40 stages have done the work for you and you can just click on the block and watch it fall in the right place without any effort. The other 5 stages or so require you to time the physics of the airborne blue square and use the red and yellow squares to guide it into the right position.
It got more interesting towards the end but there’s only 40 levels, so if you want a real challenge this game doesn’t provide it, in that way LYNE is better, and is a real puzzle game. With this one the devs did probably just make it with the intention of people buying it to use on their profile showcase, and they succeeded.
There’s no real settings options, so you can’t change the resolution manually and choose full screen mode or windowed mode, in the game you can go into a mini setting option and turn the music off, but that’s it.
Also they coulda used a better sound effect for when the red squares explode, I hope this review helps the 10% of you who actually want to play it.

The main problem of Planet Explorer is being ambitious but lacking on every aspect of the game, except the crafting system.
The developer worked hard to provide a full feature sandbox game: dozens of creatures, materials, terrain types, procedurally generated worlds, game modes including a coop story mode, a super detailed crafting system, quests, dungeons and a loot system integrated with the Steam Workshop.
What you get is all these stuff but lacking the right amount of deepness, they feels like still in prototype stage.
All served with LOADS of bug, glitches and optimization problems.
Once I started a cooperative game with a friend of mine I had a great sense of wonder... we really wanted to get sucked in this game. Sadly that feeling dropped after about 16 hours of gaming.
Everything got repetitive and pointless really fast. We found ourself stuck in repetitive tasks  (mostly mining) and playing separated.
In fact there is no reason to stick together, and even if you start playing willing to stay together, you'll end very soon wondering and doing tasks alone.
Why does it happens?
It happens for two reasons:
1) it is hard to find your mates (they are showed on the "big" map but you don't get directional clues on the minimap, so you get lost in no time)
2) it is pointless being together because every "quest" is easy enough to be accomplished alone
Even Dungeons are best in solo. They are just repetitive corridors fulfilled of monster where you get the loot just running through the enemies (ignoring them) and picking up the the loot crates  (mobs and bosses never drop useful stuffs).
There is no real boss fight and when your colony is under siege, all the defensive work is made by the turrets you've placed all around.
There is no reason to do real coop. Even the exploration.
You can craft huge vehicles to carry all your party members... but ground vehicles are useless (they got stuck in the terrain every 30 meters) and flying vehicles are boring AS HELL.
Even when  I found an entertaining way to travel (that is JetPack + glider) the exploration got boring pretty fast. You'll find soon that there is no real danger (you can overrun every creature), no real mystery and not a real rewarding aspect of exploring the world. Even the creatures are always the same. They can change shape and size but the behaviour patterns are the same used over and over.
Even death is not a big deal in this game. You can't really die. You just respawn with everything you have. Damn.. at least take out my stuff and make me get it back where I've died.
The real fun I got from this game is crafting. The shame is that your creations will be used in this doomed and boring world.
Ok maybe this review ended to be too HARSH.
Planet Explorer is NOT really THAT BAD, but the lack of deepness and polish in almost every aspect of the game is annoyingly hurting.
Planet Explorer has A LOT OF potential but the developer needs to refine it A LOT more, because it still feels like an Early Access game.
FINAL WORDS
I don't regret buying it, IF it will get improvements.
I hope I'll can give it a thumb UP as soon as possible.
PS:
I suggest the devs to focus on a single aspect of the game and heavily improve that, something that would keep up the desire of playing.
My idea is to add some unique creation scripts that you get by EXPLORING the world. You can find it by luck or by acquiring around (NPC shop or dungeon) some sort of clues about how to find them.
And creating zones that need a vehicle to be explored.

It's clear that the developers didn't just want us to give us more of the same, which personally I've never understood why that would be a bad thing but I know I'm in the minority on that one, the problem is that in trying to give us something different they changed the entire play style of the game, and to one that they don't seem to be particularly good at either. The first game was designed to encourage you to be bold take chances, and most importantly kept the flow going. This game requires a slow methodical style, lots of popping out of cover to get an enemy to charge and then killing them, which by itself doesn't feel very satisfying, but even worse is that it's very difficult to control the amount of enemies you pull at once. Often I found myself in a situation where I could either pull every enemy on the map, or just one. Your view distance is much shorter than it was in the first game, and the enemies seem to be able to see farther than you. Combine that with the larger number of windows in this game and the result is that quite often you will be shot by enemies from off screen. I'd say that it requires more careful planning but that's not true since often you can't see far enough ahead to scout a location before you charge in, so it's more about memorization. I suspect that these changes were an attempt to ramp up the difficulty for fans of the first game. It is more difficult, but not in the sort of way that encourages you to keep playing until your skill improves, but more in a way that forces you into a play style which just isn't fun. Tedious is the word, clearing a stage feels more removing weeds from a garden, or filing your taxes than playing a game. After the first three acts I found myself asking: Am I having fun? As much as a tried to deny it ultimately I had to say no.

This was my hidden gem of the 2017 Summer Sale. It gave me that Pandora's Box vibe that I've longed to feel, since that old puzzle game had a charm of relaxing discovery that no game has come close to recreating, to say nothing about surpassing it. I wish someone would make a spiritual successor already...
Still, my double thumbs-up comes with a few caveats (don't let them dissuade you from playing the game!).
First of all, the art style can sometimes be detrimental to the game. There are rare times when the sheen and colour composition can make it difficult to discern which spaces are empty and which are not. It's not bad, more like a little too much of a good thing, maybe.
Secondly, the clock-like play area wasn't such a hot idea in retrospect. Each puzzle has you place stained glass fragments within a given clock-like object - a novel idea, but it feels a bit forced and constraining. It doesn't really add anything to the game other than making the play area even more visually busy than it already is.
Finally, the puzzle mechanics don't seem to lend themselves to increased scope. I realize the puzzles were intended to be solved blind with a small number of pieces, but I imagine solving anything with more pieces could be an exercise in frustration. These stained glass puzzles lend themselves to unorthodox pieces composition, so there is some potential there for unique puzzle-solving experiences.
Despite all of the above nitpicks, I wholeheartedly recommend the game to any puzzle afficionado in search of something relaxing and a little off the beaten path. I'm looking forward to what the devs cook up next.

As in all my reviews, these are my own opinions and experiences, please check out other reviews too!
Puzzle pieces are slightly larger when you pick them up, this can result in frustration and confusion when you just can’t find the right spots. Some keys or arrows would’ve been nice to turn the piece tray without the needing to grab it. Spinning it happen often accidentally when you just want to grab a piece.
Having to pick up the pieces in order to see the colors can be a bit tiresome if you’re looking for distinct colors, an option to at least slightly see the color would be cool. The game is simply too short and can be finished in around 3-4 hours which was a bit disappointing; I was hoping for more. New puzzles as DLC or a sequel would be great. An option to show solved puzzles in fullscreen without any UI elements would’ve been a nice add to create pretty screenshots or even wallpapers.
Just what you would expect from a jigsaw puzzle game. Picking up the puzzle pieces to drop them in the right spot to complete the whole picture. There is no time or move limit so this adds to the relaxing atmosphere of the game. What makes it different is that no piece is the same, each one has a different shape and size and the overall puzzle shape varies widely as well.
While most of the game is rather easy, some specific puzzles can be quite challenging; one of them took me 20 minutes to beat it. There are 25 unique puzzles in 25 different countries related to events that happened in said countries. It was fun to guess the picture while getting closer to the reveal.
This right here is a unique mix of majestically fitting menus mixed together with beautiful stained glass artwork. The whole game is just so mysterious and colorful that it tends to mesmerize you pretty much the whole time. Artworks are based on the specific countries history and pretty much all of them are just a pleasure to look at.
A soundtrack fitting the mysterious nature of the game is also included and helps greatly with creating a relaxing atmosphere. Each section of earth has a proper song with instruments unique to that zone, doing a great job of conveying the part of earth you are currently in.

With 3-4 hours playtime, the price is justified in my opinion and this is certainly a pleasure for people who enjoy those kind of games with the added bonus of this also being very relaxing and fun. I recommend this game to anyone who is interested in the game just based on the screenshots and people who are interested in jigsaw puzzle games.
For now, it’s the the best jigsaw puzzle game I’ve ever seen. The authentic and artistic combination of instrumental music and stained glass art is just too lovely!

Some games really reach out and grab you. Others make you think the developers were drinking scorpion venom. Explosionade does both these things.
Mommy's Best Games might just be my favorite indie group out there. Anyone else's four-dollar game is, at best, a failed experiment they wanted to ship out the door to recoup on their investment. Mommy's Best Games' games might all be "experiments," but boy-howdy do they WORK. Any indie dev could come forward with "let's stack guns on top of other guns!" or "let's make a vertical shooter where you control like 30 ships!" or (as is the case with Explosionade) "let's make a game about a giant robot with infinite grenades and a rubber laser shield!" But it takes skill to craft those insane ideas into insane games, and Mommy's Best are one of the few with the skill.
It's not a long game--let's get that out in the open. It's meant to be an 'arcade' style game, where you're meant to first play on the easiest difficulty setting and feel like an invincible god of war, and then you progress to the higher difficulties and really earn that ability to curb-stomp your enemies. And earning that power is what puts this game over from "a fun time" to "LEGEND." You've got a robot with a hover boost that works like a twin stick shooter. Easy enough. And you've got infinite grenades, two types depending on when you let go of the button, one that you can use to bounce down hallways to smear some alien guts against the walls, or you can plant a sticky grenade to blow out some concrete and come crashing down on some mutant mall cop's head. And then you've got a shield which renders you invulnerable to damage as long as it's up, but it overheats quickly, so you need some True Ninja reflexes to time your shot eraser juuuust right and laugh at their puny attempts to take down your glorious golden asskicking robot. You can also use the shield to bounce against floors and walls, which, when mastered, means you can become a Cueball of Electric Death, bouncing around without touching the ground and carpet-bombing weak, ground-bound lesser creatures.
You've got all those options, and you won't grok what they mean on that first difficulty. But once you've beaten the game once, it all starts to come together, and you're using the game's systems like some sort of Computer Wizard to bend it to your will and send it home crying, and the options they give you mean you're not just "gittin' gud" at the game, you're approaching it with a certain style that'll all your own.
If you're looking for something relaxing, or if you want a video game that is an "experience" with plot and worldbuilding and an extensive cast of characters, you're going to be disappointed. If, however, you've always dreamed of becoming The Laughing God of Slaughter, playing this game is a lot cheaper than buying scorpion venom.
Oh, and check out the developer's other games on Steam. Serious Sam DD XXL may be a real game but is probably just a bad acid trip I had, people love Weapon of Choice and there's a hookah as a weapon sometimes (?), and Shoot 1up is a vertical shmup where your "extra lives" accumulate on the screen alongside you so you have a horde of ships instead of a measly one. The best thing a game can make you say is AM I ACTUALLY DOING THIS and yeah, yeah. YOU SURE ARE.

In the future, mutants and/or aliens deep below the Earth's surface, threaten everything we've ever stood for. You just might be the hero that the world needs. So hop in that conveniently-nearby protoype mech, stuff your face with cake, and get ready to make some magic. Explosionade is what I like to call a "thinking person's shooter". Yes you control a sweet mech that's loaded with fun toys, but that's just the beginning. In order to master this game you have to understand your movement, your weaponry, and most of all, your enemy. Only then can you quench your thirst for explosive goodness.
A "thinking person's shooter" is probably not the most appealing description for a game. It sounds so technical and boring that I get tired just thinking about it, but that's how the cookie crumbles. Your adversaries choose cowardice over suicide, and they will retreat to more favorable positions at every opportunity. They also don't have any problem with clogging your passage with bullets and grenades. If you want to get the most out of this game, you have to adapt. Your gun can fire in any direction, but there are walls everywhere. Your grenades can break through some of them, but you can only fire three at once. Also, while your mech is capable of jumping and hovering, its walking speed is pretty slow.
This is where you begin to appreciate your shield. While it can be used entirely for hunkering down and deflecting enemy bullets, it's most effective when your mech is in motion. While the shield is up, you can bounce off of walls. Through the usage of momentum, finding the right angle, and a grasp of physics, you can become an unstoppable force. Mowing down a handful of aliens with your machine-gun could take 10-15 seconds, or you could barrel through everything in a quarter of the time. The shield isn't always the solution, but it's your most effective tool for when everything seems hopeless.
Explosionade really comes into its own, when you get over the initial hurdles. You'll find yourself rocketing through stages, leaving no mutant alive or pile of gold un-looted. This makes the learning curve rewarding. If this was just another blastemup, there wouldn't be walls and the enemy wouldn't have anything approaching AI. There is an unexpected level of thoughtfulness that goes into each stage. You can't approach every situation in the same manner, but at the same time you're not wasting several minutes debating the pros and cons of your approach. This is a very short game, with play-throughs taking thirty minutes. Just think of it as more time to hone your ability and increase your scoring potential. Along with multiple difficulties, there are also different speed settings. If you're having trouble grasping the ins & outs, you can slow everything down. If you're looking for a real challenge, then crank everything to the max. At double speed, this game can move extremely quickly, and deaths become more common. Oh, and if you're looking for something completely different, try getting the "no-kill" bonus in each stage.

While it would be easy for me to write "HOLY SMOKES THIS GAME IS SO AWESOME!" and make a bunch of dumb jokes, the fact remains that Explosionade is cut from a different cloth. Underneath the ridiculous plot, the 80s references, and a heaping helping of kaboom, this an action-puzzle-platformer-shooter. An odd concept like this is usually a recipe for disaster. Thankfully, through solid controls, accurate mechanics, and strong game-design, Mommy's Best Games is able to deliver on their unique vision.

So you're a put-upon grunt in humanity's army, relegated to depot duty while everyone else is out exchanging laser fire with alien invaders. One fateful night, in a distant corner of home base, you stumble upon a secret prototype combat walker...whatever do you do? Oh, and did I mention there are snack cakes in the glove compartment?
These and other life-altering questions will be answered by playing Explosionade, in which your job is to, come heck or sewer water, get to the exit in one piece, one screen at a time. Of course, there are boatloads of nasty critters and obstacles between you and the "stage clear" screen, but thankfully your newly-discovered war mech is as armed to the teeth as you'd hope. While smaller ground troops can simply be squished by touching them (a guilty pleasure if there ever was one), you've also got an endless-ammo machine gun, auto-reloading grenades and a regenerating force field to ensure you're ready for anything that crosses your path. The basics aren't tough to figure out, but there are a couple of essential tricks to master: if you activate the shield just before descending from a jump it will "reflect" you higher and allow you to reach most any part of the screen, while grenades will either bounce off of or stick to walls depending on whether you hold the "launch" button as they travel, allowing you to sneak the little buggers into all manner of places with a little practice.
As you progress from room to room you are granted a small point bonus for finishing quickly, but greater rewards are obtained by taking your time, bombing walls and exploring everywhere you can reach (including those tricky areas the developer has hidden behind foreground elements) and eliminating every last Horrornym in your sights before moving on - of course, you'll want to collect all of the chunks of gold (which refill your health and eventually enhance your grenades, since your mech, naturally, is powered by it) and obligatory pies you can, too. A rather lengthy health meter and frequent pickups combined with the shield makes for fairly easy progress, at least at first, but even the lowliest of your foes can be uncharacteristically aggressive and resourceful once they've spotted you, so death can quickly make a surprise appearance if you let your guard down. Your mount also has an appropriately heavy feel to it, which can become floaty when using the "shield bounce" to get around, both of which take some getting used to, but a bit of combat experience should solve that issue fairly quickly.
Out on the periphery, the game's looks might best be summarized as "endearingly chunky", though the music is easily overpowered by the sounds of detonating grenades and death-screaming cannon fodder. My personal favorite bits are the occasional, exasperated exchanges between your in-over-his-head soldier and his chronically PO'ed commander, though they can be skipped if you prefer. While not everything comes together perfectly here, several improvements have been made since the XBLIG release (a laser sight for easier aiming, better bullet visibility, etc.), and the game still has one of my favorite taglines attached ("When life gives you explosions..."), so it's tough for me not to recommend parting with a few dollars and taking it for a spin.
Just don't mention my name if the commander yells at you.
