TL;DR: Neat! Probably worth the full price if you like rhythm games, *absolutely* worth it on sale.
-Technical Stuffses-
Had some problems getting it to run, likely due to a .NET framework issue (which also impacted Terraria, though to a smaller extent, so it wasn't the game's fault), but it works perfectly fine now. I'm not entirely sure *why*, but... it works.
Apart from that it runs perfectly fine; no lag, no framerate drops, no nothing, no crashes or bugs so far. Yay!
-Visuals-
Exactly my kind of game - sleek and stylish and pretty. The game itself looks very polished, the menus aren't quite as aesthetically pleasing... but now I'm really just nitpicking.
-Audio-
The main theme is So. Good. Seriously.
The rest of the bundled music seems fairly impressive as well, though I haven't listened to / played all of it yet.
Apart from that, the audio is obviously up to you, which is kind of the point.
-Gameplay-
Left, right, up and down can be surprisingly difficult concepts.
Apart from that - well, I mean it's a rhythm game. Some aspects kind of remind me of the field stages from Final Fantasy Theatrythm for the 3DS, so if that's your thing, you'll probably like this game as well.
On a slightly different note, using the right mouse button as 'cancel' button in menus is an awesome concept on one hand, but mightily confusing on the other hand. Still, I kind of wish more games did that - the only other ones I can recall are the Ezio-focused AssCreed games, which was ages ago.
-Additional Comments: Algorythms and Synching-
The game usually does a decent enough job analyzing songs, but it *is* occasionally less than perfect.
I've deliberately played some extremely different songs - from acoustic folksy stuff to classical music to the Portal 2 and AC:B soundtracks - and things usually worked out reasonably okay... but I really wish we had an option to synch up songs manually.
-Additional Comments: Just for Fun-
The faster parts of the various AssCreed soundtracks and this game are a match made in heaven.
I'd also like to mention how much I love how easy it is to customize things - it took me roughly 15 minutes to put together a custom hairstyle and color scheme, and I spent 12 minutes of that being indecisive*.
Generally speaking, I'm having a ton of fun so far; if that ever changes, I'll go back and edit this review.

Warhammer: End of Times - Vermintide verdict? Chaos. The vermin Skaven are all over the place. They climb from the roofs, from the sewers, every windows like the rats that they are. I thought i was to play a melee character like the Empire's Soldier, turns out that i'm more comfortable to play as a Bright Wizard. Nothing more satisfying to watch the vermin scum burn from your pyro-chaos magick but gets way too dangerous when you overused your chaos magick that it'll backfire on you. By backfire, i mean explode.
There are 5 classes to choose from, in which you can switch to whichever hero class that you want to play as, or fill in the roles as. The classes are: Witchhunter (wields multiple of flintlock guns), Waywatcher (Elven archer and uses daggers), Bright Wizard (Chaos magick caster), Dwarf Ranger (to break apart packs) and the Empire Soldier (the damage dealer).
You start off in a tavern, appropriately enough. From there, you can play solo with Bots (which is difficult as the Bots won't revive you and their AI wander off to fight Skavens by themselves if you're away from them), or start a mission and the game will find a room for you, or invite or join your friends who has the game.
The looting system is interesting. There's a vermin Skaven that carries a loot bag, kill that vermin scum to get the loot. Or treasure chests.  Sometimes you'll get "Dice-Loot" or "Tomes" to give you more dices to roll for your treasures. Dice rolls allows you to roll for your loot at the end of the mission and only AFTER you completed the mission and not if you failed. There's Grimoires to collect but at the cost of having lesser hit points for your party for more Dice loot.
Loot generated randomly. You may get other classes' weapons. But you can collect the weapons and then, fuse them at the forge to make a new weapon but as long they're the same colored weapon and same type of weapons. Otherwise, it's random. You can also upgrade the weapons as long they have the weapon slots for them. You could even salvage the weapons by smelting them to get the upgrade resource.
You gain EXP in every after mission (whether if you failed or are victorious). Gaining a new level, unlocks accessible tavern features (like the Forge or the storage box) or new weapons.
It's interesting that they put a lot of in-game chatter for the characters, they even interact with each other during in the mission, making the characters more livelier and has diverse personalities.
There are dozens of maps, but you only unlock more maps if you completed the maps.
The game plays like Left 4 Dead, but violent, gory, brutal and fun.

The only thing that may bug you is the loot system. With a grand total of seven avalible dice, randomized loot based on the difficulty, and a different hit rates on the dice it can get annoying trying to get loot.
Things to keep in mind,
All in all if you are thinking about buying the game do it.

Finally, a co-op game that relies on actual co-operation. This is on par with L4D. Great combat system, looks dark and grim, and pretty damn difficult. The "Special Enemies" are much to be feared in this one. Definately not for "casual gaming."
I will admit the RNG loot system can be dissapointing at times. There are still some bugs with the AI's pathing (I dealt with a Ogre Rat that got stuck behind a pillar, made it really easy to deal with.) The community can be a bit overzealous with new comers, but I remember L4D's community being quite similar. The best thing to do is to just tell the party your new and start on normal or easy.

So, to begin, I really wanted to like this game from the offset. I love Frozen Synapse and the idea of tactical, top down, squad shooters. I dived in with high expectations from all the praise I saw. The result of this endeavor was to be disappointed more than I have been in a long time by a game.
I will say now - the game is solid enough. However, I encountered certain aspects of the gameplay that just broke it for me. Primarily, the lack of any form of viable introduction or tutorial. I know it has some moving pictures and whatnot, but all that it covers is simple enough to figure out on your own. There is no explanation for how to time entries into a room with a flashbang properly, no explanation why equipping weapons to some of the troops just outright doesnt work. The secondary problems are... well... mentioned above. It is a massive hassle to control the squad. There are no elegant mechanics like in Frozen Synapse that allow for a time delay or no-aim movement. It also makes control difficult due to bulky command images that cross over and make clicking on them a chore. A lack of any explanation as to why upgrading your soldiers abilities doesnt seem to transfer into the tactical game also makes the game frustrating.
In short, bar the issues above, the game is spot on. Animation, sound, idea, everything. It is just a crying shame that actually playing it felt like work rather than enjoyment. Sadly I didnt enjoy the game at all and wanted to just make sure that the reason is out there.

I don't usually review games good or bad, but I had to make an exception  in  this case. First off, I have always been an adventure game lover and especially sandbox games, but in recent years I have started to enjoy exploring and survival games. After many so so games I finally ran across this one. I couldn't be more excited. I have been playing story mode for 5 days...wasting the entire 5 days off work with this game. The graphics are beautiful and unique, the story flows well and I never seem to get tired of mining and crafting. There is always something better right around the corner or from the next quest.

The battling is great too. Some animals will kill you in one or two hits and you can never carry enough ammo to kill some of them...takes turrets (of which there are plenty). The instructions aren't the best, but that is what keeps it interesting. Trying to figure things out rather than just having them outlined for you. Then there's the crafting.
This is absolutely the best crafting system I have ever used. Once you find/buy/are awarded the scripts, just click it and it cascades into everything you need, and if you don't have an item, just click it and it again tells you what you need to make that. It is totally awesome.
Now, flying machined, jeeps, boats, subs...you name it and you can create it, or just use a premade template in game. The creation system leaves a bit to be desired and has a steep learning curve, but seems rather simple once you get the hang of it. The building system on the other hand is a virtually useless. If nothing else, it makes it easy to make a wall or a floor etc, but the shapes don't seem to have much use, or at least not with any sort of effective tutorial, and that is another weak point...the tutorials.
Pro's: Great graphics. Awesome creation system. Great story line that keeps you engrossed and adds some mystery. Gathering is great. Nice mix of primitive to modern/space age tools and systems. Great upgrades for everything. Critters for days. Can't really say enough good things about it.
Con's:  Building system. Tutorials. Locked keys, can't bind tab and q for movement which SUX for me.
Over all I am 100% satisfied for the first time in a very long time.

I picked up this game early in the EA cycle and almost immeadiately put it down after playing a couple of hours since the initial release was a steaming pile of hot garbage.
So I gave it a year or two to gather some steam and put some polish, enough time to pass from alpha to beta.
And its still hot garbage.
Okay for the usual breakdown:
Visuals:
Visually Planet Explorers is pretty nice, for what it is and what cycle of development its in it accomplishes a great deal. Character customization is fine, standard fare. Building things is equally detailed and can produce some very amazing things.
Sound:
Likewise, gets the job done, it's not perfect but its still beta so a few bugs here and there is to be expected.
Gameplay:
Here is where Planet Explorers still fails.
In early alpha the 'fetch' quests had you traversing great distances for the most minor of things. At that time spawners didn't care if you were a veteran or a fresh spawn, you would likely stumble into alien creatures vastly out of your league all for pidly rewards.
Beta... they've cleaned it up but they've added more game modes and no documentation. When you now start up the game you can adjust your visuals and get thrown into a starter screen where you pick Story, Adventurer etc etc. NONE OF WHICH are explained. I *imagine* story is the original alpha experience, the crashed ship, the fetch quests etc and so forth so I thought I'd try adventure.
The first thing to fail is the fact that you can only take one quest at a time. There's half a dozen in your starter area but you can only take ONE main quest and one side quest. The main quest has you hoofing it a huge distance to a 'settlement', have fun running half an hour back and forth between HUBs to do the other STARTER quests. That's only a guess as the original beautiful world generation is utterly borked in adventure mode. Leaving the starter village required building a set of stairs to reach the floating mountain and the road onwards. Seriously... and its not the only floating mountain, I spawned on a grassy plateau surrounded by water at the bottom of a huge cliff and half a dozen floating mountains.
There's no explination of game modes, there's no tutorial to (re)familiarize yourself with how the game works. You spawn and are pretty much up to yourself to figure out how the game works.
Like alpha, I played the beta for an hour then uninstalled again.

I have to admit something, what attracted me to this game was the fact that it was made by a Spanish developer. There’s not many truly good Spanish games out there, and I wanted to check out if it was actually worth it. As usual, I’m gonna talk first about what the game doesn’t do that well.
First and foremost, the biggest issue with this game is it’s length. It’s short. Way too short. It barely lasts around 2 to 3 hours, maybe 4 if you’re having trouble with the controls (more on that later). Now sure, the game does offer an alternative ending… But it’s locked behind a crazy hard mode that I’m sure it was added just to make the game last longer. It’s a shame, really.
Second, the controls. Lots of people have problems with them, but I must admit I didn’t really have that many. Maybe I’m just used to side-scrolling Prince of Persia wannabe games, who knows. However, you should consider playing with a controller.
The difficulty is mostly okay, however the Nightmare mode is just dumb. Yeah, let’s lock an alternative ending behind a mode where you have to complete the WHOLE GAME without dying once. Who had this idea!? I wish s/he got fired for doing such a thing, specially since some parts of the game are quite trial-and-error and remembering where every damn death trap is, is just insane and borderline idiotic.
Lastly, the Director’s Cut edition. It was released time after the release, but for all I know and was able to play on a friend’s house, it really doesn’t really fix much and adds a mode that you’ll play once and forget it’s even there. It’s a dumb way to take the fan’s money, and I don’t approve of it, specially since you gotta pay for it even if you already had the game. That’s something Activision would do (remember Destiny? Because I do), make a game that costs 12€ and then charge 20€ more for a patched version that doesn’t quite fix it at all.
However, taking those things away, we got a decent 2D platformer, a weird mix between the classic 2D Prince of Persia games and a zombie apocalypse. Of all things.
The best this game has to offer is the presentation. The graphics, the lightning, the stages, they all look great. Everything actually feels alive, and even though you see everything in a 2D perspective, you can actually see things happening outside of the area you can play, something a ton of games just ignore. Further more, there's even times when things outside of the plain of 2D existence you seem to be playing on get into the play after being just a background element, and that is GREAT! More games should do that!
The sound department also did their work properly. The music, the soundtrack and the voices all fit perfectly. Maybe the main character sounds a bit clichéd at times, but that’s it.
The gameplay is also quite fun. Remember how I’ve compared this game to Prince of Persia a ton of times already? Well, it truly feels like it. You don’t really need to fight anything, what really matters is getting to the end of the stage. All of those angry zombies that want to eat you alive? You can trap them, jump over them, even tackle them and just run away if you need to, it works wonders. There’s also firearms, which will spawn a bunch of zombies offscreen and make them be aware of you to hunt you down, but at the same time can kill zombies in one well placed hit if you try to actually take aim instead of firing like Rambo on his first training course.
Lastly, the story. If you’ve read books, saw shows and played games about zombie apocalypse then it might be a little obvious how things might turn into, but it doesn’t stop from being well written and enjoyable to go through, shame it’s so short.
Do I recommend the game? Yes, and no. I do recommend buying it, and maybe even buying the soundtrack if that’s your kind of thing, but ignore the Director’s Cut thing. And if you buy it, DO WAIT for a sale. It’s 12€ for, at best 4 hour of gameplay. Sure you can replay it for the Nightmare mode, but I seriously don’t recommend even trying it. It’s like trying to play Half-Life from the beginning to the end using an Atari controller. Sure it’s possible, but you’d have to be pretty f#cking bored and dumb to try such a thing. For 6€ it could arguably be worth it, less than that is a good purchase.
TL;DR Edition: A game with insanely good presentation, sound department and gameplay that sadly, offers a really short story. However I would say it’s worth playing if you can get it really cheap. Stay away from Nightmare Mode, it’s easier to go out under a thunderstorm and dodge rain.

Played 3 hours and completed the game. I hearby dub it, "Deadlight aka Trail and Error, The Game."
A 2d puzzle platformer with some zombie killing thrown in, it has some very pretty visuals, occasionally wonky controls, interesting level design (at first) and an uninteresting story.
The first hour and chapter are the best, introducing you to a dark world and some cool puzzles. Then you get into the sewers. Oh.. those sewers. From here you'll increasingly run into frustrating instant death puzzles that you don't have enough time to respond to - you appear to be expected to die to them and do it better next time with hindsight, because many you are forced to trigger to progress. Brute forcing puzzles is not fun! Coupled with platforms that are hard to distinguish I found myself suicide sprinting into everything because upon death the contrast changes enough the platforms finally are visible.
Because the controls are not the greatest, you'll find yourself dismissing certain paths without realising they're the actual way forward. A heads up: on the roof, with the helicopter? There's a wall you climb not with the normal button but by holding up instead. It's the only time this appears in the game. Have fun with that.
All these problems - especially the instant-death puzzles that necessitate a death first, rather then letting you outwit the game and think it through lend to an infurating experience. Unlike Super Meat Boy, it doesn't seemlessly get you back into the action so these constant deaths feel disruptive. I beat this game out of sheer spite because I felt it wanted to make me quit.
The combat is interesting at least, I will give it that. Zombies are quie dangerous as axe swings rapidly deplete your stamina, so groups can quickly overwhelm you. The opening cutscene made out that shooting is a risk owing to the sound - ignore that, it's fine. Just don't run empty in case a puzzle comes up that needs bullets, but they usually resupply you in those situations.
The story is very predictible for a zombie story. One grizzled man in a zombie apocolypse trying to reunite with his family but dun-dun-DUN yawn. The biggest suspension of disbelief was that a Canadian Ranger can't swim. Only it's not a zombie story, they're Shadows. They're totally zombies, just use the word zombie, don't be ridiculous.
It is worth noting I ran into a common bug where sometimes pausing would freeze the game, and the occasional severe framerate drop moving to new areas.
Overall, any game I beat out of spite is not one I recommend.
Pros

First chapter has fun puzzle platforming
Zombies are a legitmate threat.
Achievements are song titles and lyrics. Worth a chuckle.
Cons
Puzzles become tedious and require brute force of ability to predict future.
Checkpoint spacing leaves a lot to be desired on later chapters.
Not the sharpests of controls. Reminded me a little of the first Assassin's Creed.
Gets very frustrating in certain areas because of above points.
Story is predictable at best, pure edgelord at worst.
Not brave enough / too pretentious to use the word zombie. It bothers me.
Quite short - three hours playthrough with plenty of deaths.
Beat it out of pure spite. What? It's worth repeating!
limited depth, annoying UI, better ways to spend my time even if this was free.

I have a little more than a hundred hours on this game, so I feel confident to give a complete review on it.
The cons: Although it's been released, it still feels a lot like an early access because of little bugs and weird behavior of some feature. Here some examples:
- Water behave weirdly. It is in infinite quantity (like in Minecraft) and therefore is not always very realistic. Water passes right through wall and any placed block so when it rains, it rains inside houses...
- NPC are brainless (e.g. they dive of cliffs and roofs without care), have the weird ability to pass through walls and the uncanny habits to always end up where they will most bother you.
- the world is beautiful on the surface but in adventure mode you will have things like sand on roof of caves, patiently waiting (without falling down mind you) for you to mine it. In general caves are plain unrealistic (and there is no cave-in so mad miners can feel free to dig and dig and dig)
The good:
The concept is truly great and I SO wanted a solo game like wurm or rising world where you could built towns that would not be just empty ghost towns and where NPC actually do some work in it (farming, processing)
The replicator concept is great and work really well
Overall, I do not regret buying this game because it is fun and has all the things I really was searching for. But it really feels like it needs some polish to feels less like an early access and more like a finished game (with the potential of a blockbuster). I do hope that its release doesn't mean that it will stay like that and that patches will be released to fix all that needs to be fixed. Anyway, it is already fun the way it is, so I won’t cry if there is no meaningful patches in the future.

So far I'm overall enjoying this game, but it does have problems. I'm unfinished with the storyline, but other reviewers have covered that, so I won't get too into it. I may change this review after I beat the storyline. I apologize for the fact my review seems more negative than positive, but I am enjoying it more than I'm annoyed with the issues.
Pros:
- The building system could be refined but is overall easy to work with and building nice structures isn't particularly difficult. I also really dig the custom creation, save for the armor--I would have highly preferred there was a base we could paint over, as the creation method is far too blocky to look normal as clothes. I wanted to make some skimpy armor for my guy that matched the female version, but it sure seems impossible with the tools you're given.
- Fighting is a strong point--I really like the combat system, shooting bows and guns is fun, and the difficulty is good. Hunting is enjoyable. The turrets are also nice. The swords are not as enjoyable, and I haven't used them much.
- Crafting system is solid and pretty damn expansive. No complaint at all here. Very easy to use.
- Resource gathering is painless.
- The fast travel system is pretty well done, also, but it does make the motorbikes feel pretty useless.
-  I looooove the character creation. Probably a minor detail to most people, though.
- The world is gigantic and easy to get lost in. I've spent a lot of time so far just wandering and finding different areas.
----
Cons:
- The armor creation system (mentioned above!)
- Enemy animations don't line up well sometimes. I do really enjoy fighting, don't get me wrong, but it does tend to hit you when it looks like it shouldn't and not get hit when it should have. In multiplayer, the other character model is often not where it should be, even though you're playing LAN.
- The AI is wonky, both for allies and enemies. It just acts really weird sometimes. I've sometimes fought baddies high up only for them to suddenly jump and kill themselves for no obvious reason, or had someone I was bringing somewhere just...run away, only for the quest to fail because they got attacked. This is somewhat unfrequent, but it happens.
- The person who got this for me thought it was still in early access. I didn't know it wasn't until I came to review--it feels like it is. It's clearly a good game, and like I said I am overall enjoying it, but it doesn't feel finished. I'm nervous about the reviews that say the story mode ends abruptly. It looks like they are still developing this game, so hopefully it will still reach this stage.
- The fact you have to manually close a server you're hosting with task manager is ridiculous. Not that it's hard, but it's annoying and feels very lazy.
- Movement does have some issues. The random rolls and oversteps have killed or hurt me a couple times when I was too high. The ground vehicle movement is very weird, though I have yet to try the other vehicle types. (Will update when/if I do.) The camera controls are actually very easy to control, though.
- No way to track other players, afaik :( It's really frustrating to open the map when someone is getting attacked and try to figure out how to get to them. I also really wish there were custom markers you could follow like you can with quests.

On the fence with this one, when it first came out I loved the idea of a horde game in the Warhammer universe though the more I play it, the more I find myself resenting the game. Don't get me wrong, the game looks brilliant, plays great and first person melee combat feels weighty. It's good as a time killer, has a loose story but think Left4Dead, just a series of missions you can complete at your leisure and in no particular order. Some missions are ridiculously hard even on easy, so there are some balancing issues present. The devs fixed the crashing from the beta and the game runs smoothly apart from when there are alot of enemies on-screen at any given time, as expected. Game has a good player base but you do come into contact with the general elitist every second match. There is no reward for failing before completion other than minute xp gain which gives the game a rewarding feel. You level up incredibly slow and weapons only drop upon a dice roll at the end of a completed mission or upon level up. The characters are voiced excellently and each has their own personality. All characters play different aswell, due to their varying weapon types. The game does feel good but just repetative at the moment as there aren't many unlocks and not much incentive to invest your time to level up. I would say, I wish I waited for a price drop as I paid £35 for my copy (Collector's Edition) & whilst I fully support the developers, it doesn't feel like there is much here for your investment so I would recommend picking up for no more than say £12 on sale. Good game, just nothing more.

I originally reviewed this game back in June of 2015. I did not recommend this game because of the bandwagon of people giving this game negative feedback. At the time, I did agree with them, but throughout the almost 3 years since release of this game, my opinion has changed.
Let's start of by saying that this game is by no means in the top Call of Duty games. It is probably ranked towards the bottom of that list compared to other CoD games. Even by saying that I am not saying that this game is bad, just not as great as the ones to come before it.
My original opinion of this game was accurate. When Call of Duty: Ghosts was the newest game in the series, it was absolutely terrible. I never even hit first prestige and never went back to play the campaign a second time (until now).
After suffering through the past two years with two respectively bad Call of Duty games, I have actually come back to this game to experience storyline another time. The campaign of Advanced Warfare was outstanding, but the multiplayer was disgusting. The campaign of Black Ops III was disgusting and the multiplayer was alright. Let's just say I came back to this game to relive a good campaign again. I was tired of the super futuristic garbage that the recent games have offered.
If I was reviewing this game soley on singleplayer, I would give it a 9/10, but since the multiplayer was poor and the general community disliked it, I rate the entire game a 8/10. The storyline does keep the multiplayer from sinking the game.
My original review went something like this:
Call of Duty: Ghosts is by far the worst COD in a while.
The campaign seems recycled, yet still playable and enjoyable.
The mulitplayer is just plain bad.. Like I hate it.
I cannot recommend this game to anyone.

Great FPS game. Especially online with its unlock system and coop mode.
Online PVP:
=========
First of all: I dont like games, where u need to wait for a level up to unlock your (in most cases better) weapons. Here you can create your soldier profile and unlock the weapons and items you want by the use of skillpoints from the beginning. You just need to earn skillpoints, additional to the one you got from the beginning.
Every soldier profile has to unlock it's weapons for itself. So you can create each one for individual roles - feels like RPG in a  light edition.
The devs also included destroyable environments, like a gas station, that changes the map layout.
The only big con here is the fact, the games was downhated from my point of view and therefore lacked a lot of players.
I cannot comprehend their big load of critics, I played a lot of the games, taken from this franchise and this is one of the bests online.
But suddenly the player counter online is increasing, maybe cuz of the reveal of Infinite Warfare...
Online-Coop:
==========
The coop mode with its aliens and mission driven gameplay is also good. Most of the time you have to use a drill to destroy some point of interest. But the missions and locations are great. You even have bossfights - one of the greatest can be found on MAYDAY. Each mission needs between 1/2 and 1 hour play time to finish.
You can choose between several roles, medic, engineer and two combat guys. This mode also includes an XP system, that allows you to pick up different items / skills e.g. the seeker drone, you know / have seen in Black Ops 2. Beside that, you can unlock different skills, e.g. doing more damage with sniper rifles by collecting special items (called teeths).
The mode even gives you the opportunity to pick up collectables on the maps, so you can craft own items.
This mode has a great coop experience and is very entertaininig - especially with friends.
Campaign:
========
The Singleplayer has its CoD moments, but has almost nothing you already saw in MW. The most memorable mission was the infiltration of a snow base, but this one was made really brilliant. The most annoyable part was the control of a tank - feels really crappy...

Right, I grabbed this game on a whim, thinking that it really wouldn't be a loss if I didn't like it. I thought it would just be a generic side scrolling rhythm game, and I was mostly right. In Short:
This game is great for those who want a lot more strategy in their FPSs.
Explained:
This is designed for players who want to paly something more focused on Strategy and skill instead of a total deathmatch style of gameplay (Like CoD or Battlefield).
So you cant carry every weapon to beat every other player, because if that were the case everyone would have an RPG, SMG and a sniper or Nades. The game makers did what many games should do, which is focus on team work and a collective army vice a gagle of 'swiss-army-knife'-like soldiers. An army full of Run and guns will be knocked out by snipers and a Tank army will be beat by A troop of lightfooted mine layers. You have to continuously think ahead and gauge the battle on what is needed in game and have your characters set up ahead of time so that you can support the mission depending on where the battle is going. (Example: Half the team is sniping, but you are losing ground, you probably dont want to snipe with them, so you should have a back-up 'runner', to help defend)
Creating a second or third Character is a great way of keeping players thinking ahead, instead of simply trading out weapons whenever they feel like it, makes it so that one person isnt able to do EVERYTHING. I mean the ribbon system works amazingly here and keeps people from just having everything unlocked through IRL Money or one through one character (I mean you could, but you would have to cycle through almost every weapon at half the pace) and REQUIRES players to actually play the game for those perks, hence why having to use multiple Characters is a plus, focusing your character towards a specific role vice just being 100% at everything after a few dozen hours of game play keeps you (and everyone else) from becoming these overpowered ogres.
The credit system is the one thing I gripe about, simply for the fact that no matter how well you do in a battle you still get paid less than the one guy who killed 2 guys but is a higher rank than you.
Armor is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ but well worth the grinding, much like many MMOs and FPSs You will be killed ALOT when you get your first tank, however, unlocking consecutive tanks is actually pretty easy and untaxing when it comes to time because going from Lvl 1 Light tank to Lvl 3 Light tank takes maybe 3 hours of solid tank action. Sure you cant take a heavier tank Head-on, but you can certainly level up very quickly to be able to turn around and hit back with a heavier tank in a matter of a few hours.
Map Design for this game is actually probably the best Ive seen, key locations in structures with some great defence but with exploitable positions makes every encounter with the enemy hard yet rewarding when you do it smartly.
Not to mention the Developers seem to have done the right thing by constantly listening to players, taking feedback and showing face at every chance. I have no doubt they will continue to impress us with this game.
Finally, now I havent actually played the Generals side of this game (which pretty much is a whole other game if I understand it) But this basically is the core strategy portion behind how many units are spawned in and how many respawns a team has, if you have terrible generals, you might lose a whole bunch, where if your general is a master at strategy, the war will last a couple days vice weeks.
Im seriously looking forward to what the developers have instore for us as the year(s) progress, and I will continue to play many many many hours of this game well after it is complete.

I feel this game is so genuinely good that I'll make an actual review on it.
While it does have its faults, some of which being the pathing of the Alex character or your retical being stuck to certain positions as you advance to a side of or in the corner of a map, Hotline Miami 2 is a phenomenal sequel to the first game. Plain and simple. It's different, difficult, and entertaining as long as you take it piece by piece, if you become stressed easily. Every character you play as will have a restriction or an added ability, ensuring you'll have a different experience than you did in the first game. Enemies have new variations as well. It looks and feels great. It plays fluidly and rewards you for taking a more strategic approach to certain levels rather than a reckless one. And, while I'll admit I was frustrated with the level design during my first playthrough of the game, the addition of a level editor by the developers guarantees your experience playing it will never go stale, so long as the community wants to keep the game alive.
Having kept track of this game since it's announcement and being eager for it's release in 2015, it became very apparent that Dennaton was very nervous about making it. More than anything, they wanted to make a good sequel, for their fans and for themselves alike. I couldn't argue more that they succeeded in doing so with Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. It's not just more of the same. It's a different approach to more of the same. A violent, top-down shooter/smasher/slasher still but with more emphasis on story and character rather than just gameplay. In every sense of the phrase, this game does more of the same right. Anyone who creates a sequel to anything should look to this game as an example of how things should be done.

It's only April and I can already tell this is my GOTY.  This game is just amazing.  If you haven't played the first game, pick it up when it goes on sale, see if you like it, then buy this.  More people need to expierence the Hotline Miami games.
Hotline Miami 2 is different from the first game in multiple aspects.  For starters, in HM1, there was one character (two actually) with tons of different masks with different play styles to choose from.  In HM2 however, we are introduced with many different characters, but with less playstyle choices.  I see this as a good thing.  Instead of getting use to one playstyle, such as running in a room and shooting everybody, you might have to play as someone who can't pick up weapons and can only kill with their fists.  It keeps you on your toes.
The story is expaneded on much more in HM2 than HM1 (You could make an argument that there isn't even really a story in HM1, but whatever.)  Without trying to spoil much, the background and lore behind the game is much deeper than it seems.  You can find newspapers scattered throughout the entire story explaining a lot of things.  I'll leave it at that.
The combat is amazing.  I've been farming a level to try and get the genocide achievement (kill 50,000 enemies) and being able to chop down 14 enemies without dying is satisfying.  Of course, if you do die you can get right back in extremely quickly, so that's not a problem.  There's also a lot more gunplay in HM2, which is nice since HM1 didn't see a lot of gunplay.  I've also heard people say the combat is much floatier is HM2 than HM1, but I can't confirm it.
My one gripe with this game come from level design.  Windows will be your worst enemy.  Running down a hall when suddenly, BLAM, someone with a shotgun off the screen blasts you away.  The levels are just so huge that when something like this happens, you'll have to go through that entire section again.  It's annoying, but you learn to deal with it.  Just always check for enemies before running down a hallway.
Tons of replayability.  There is a hard mode which unlocks after beating the game normally, and there is a leaderboard system.  I just went through the game a third time to get A+ and S ranks on every level (230th in the world on the final level, yeah!).  It's also fun to try and beat your friend's scores.  The level editor is coming ot soon as well so there will be no reason to stop playing this game.
The soundtrack is easily the best part of the game.  It's just amazing.  There are no words to describe it, you just have to experience it yourself.  (The music on the deathwish level is so good.)
TL;DR : Buy this game please

Quite a selection, especially gun wise but almost everything must be unlocked. Still when you find the fitting gun for all of your classes the selection will be just between classes (at least that was my case).
Good guys?
Well there are only three main stats for each officer and they are progressing without your choice but you can feel the difference between good and bad shooter especially with bad aiming gun.
Bad guys?
Enought to make it interesting but could be quite more. AI is quite good and on default missions there is several spawn points for bad guys, so it makes it more interesting.
Maps?
Plenty of different and really challenging ones.
Is it tactical?
Hell yeah it is ... but when you master most of the missions and use of pause you can kill everyone with one guy ... mostly. I had a lot of sneaky situations and they are planned to ambush you if you are not carefull. Some rage but no rage quits and that pleasant feeling when you finally do this.
Replayibilty?
With random missions and maps generator? Big. With steam workshop and plenty of maps, missions, guns, unit looks etc.? Quite bigger.
Is it worth it?
Hell yeah! I bought it for half the nominal price and I am more then satisfied of fun per eurocent ratio :-D

This game is essentially a melee oriented Left 4 Dead. There are guns, but the primary weapon is a melee weapon. Instead of zombies you fight giant humanoid rats. There are "specials", ones that highly resemble those in L4D. Missions are similar to L4D too.
With sort of a medieval feel to it, Vermintide is a 4 player co-op game where you and 3 others complete objectives on a mission and escape with your lives against a dangerous rodent race called the Skaven. There are 5 different characters you can choose from, each one having its own weapon types and play style. At the end of each mission you get a weapon drop, that you can either use to replace your current weapon, or use at the forge to help make your current weapon better.
Needless to say if you love Left 4 Dead, or games similar, you will love this game. At this point there are a few changes that could be made to the game, especially with AI and loot drops, but for the most part this is a very well done game, with beautiful graphics and a high replay ability level. I definitely recommend playing with friends, but playing online or alone is pretty fun too. Definitely a great game.

This may or may not appeal to you, depending on what sort of game you're looking for.
All told deep down it's not Left 4 Dead. This is no bad thing though: it stands on its own, it's great fun to play with a few friends, and there are Skaven!

Warhammer End Times : vermintide has all the components a co op game needs to be great. It is a lot of fun (especially when played with a group of freinds and not relying on public lobbies) with great characters who have a lot of charisma and interact between each other just as you would imagine them to do in the Warhammer world. There are 5 different characters to choose from, each with thier own playstyle and weapons. There are some cross overs in weapons and skills but this doesnt not tend to be an issue.
The enemy is called the Skaven - with your characters being rushed by dozens of the 'standard' ones and a handful of special types with different abilites. Unfortuanlty this is one of the area's where the game really lets itself down. There is almost no warning when they are going to attack (what limited audio cues there are, tend to be lost in the sheer amount of noise being made elsewhere in game). WIth some of the special attacks you can either be downed or worse still dragged into an area that will then trigger another event, means more AI. By that time you will have lost control of what has to be a carefully managed progression of the map and it will be all over. There needs to be more notice and you need to be able to stop your self being incapacitated. It is currenlty possible if you happen to noctice it coming and are skilled enouogh to get the shots / push back exaclty right. But belive me when I say it is not easy.
The AI triggers seem to be left to an RNG so you can have almost no enemies and then suddendly have so many spawn on top of each other that there  is utterly no way for you to beat them. A god example of this is the Rat Ogre - who has a smash that will hurl youir character about. Often this will mean triggering more  spawns as you try and kite to stay out of its reach (there is litterally no other option in most situations), so you will find your self with 4 specials, a rat ogre and a full horde of basic skaven. If encounted on thier own or in pairs, make a fun but challenging encounter but it will be a wipe if the RNG is not on your side.
My last major gripe is the way in which loot is handled. At the end of the mission you get to roll several dice - which can be boosted by attaining certain items in game. The better you roll the better the piece of equipment you get. Unfortuanly more often than not you will either already have it or not play the character that it is for. For example I have 100 hours or so in the game and I still do not have any of the Exotic longbows I have been religously trying to get hold of. However I have a dozen exotic swords for the witch hunter I barely play. And there is currenlty nothing that can be done with them (so even if I did play that class thee multiple dupliucates will still sit in my inventory - to the point where I hope for the lower ranked items so I can at least scrap them for use in upgrading or gamble them for a chance of a weapon I can use).
These issues could be resolved very easily - and indeed need to be as it has gotten to the point where I have lost the will to play until at least some of the bugs and odd mechanics get fixed. With these things addressed and some more content and player progression beingng added, Vermintide will do very well indeed.

Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide has proved to be as exhilerating an experience as any I have found in the hemisphere of co-op action games.
So, you've played Left 4 Dead, you've played Payday, and now you're here, ready to experience the gore-slicked depths of Vermintide.
Taking elements from two of the most successful co-op franchises in recent history syngergizing them together with a classic Warhammer veneer?  That's the ticket.
The gameplay is fine-tuned, responsive, and very technical in terms of dodging, blocking, etc.  In order to be a competent team member, it is necessary you have an understanding of these maneuvers.  This can seem daunting at first, but once you acquire the rhythm for each character and begin to understand how to time your strikes, things get very fun very fast.
The teamwork element in this game is very similar to that of Payday.  It is absolutely necessary your team stick together in order to make an effective stance against the Skaven hordes.  It takes things beyond Left 4 Dead, however, by implementing tasks in each mission that must be completed in order to advance (as opposed to simply slaying every enemy).  Some missions are more arduous than others, but they all present the the player with situations to test your ability to think on your feet and form effective, cohesive strategies at a moment's notice.
The ambiance and atmosphere of Vermintide are top-notch.  Fat Shark did a great job taking the mystique of Warhammer's lore and applying it to a co-op action game.  The music and sound effects do a stellar job immersing the player in its mire of burning rat flesh and dancing swords.
The class system offers a broad variety of playstyles to appeal to all types of players.  Moreso, each class is so customizable that it is easy to switch traditional party roles without changing characters.  As you unlock new weapons, new options open up in terms of strategy.  For example, these weapons would allow you to take your dwarf from a tank, to dps, to support, with nothing more than a simple weapon switch.  This customizaiton allows for a higher degree of player innovation, and coming to understand how different playstyles work with one another is highly engaging.
The loot system is very simple and concise.  Each class has a certain set of weapons unique to that character.  These wapons are obtained through drops received upon leveling up and completing missions.  All weapons are ranked by tier depending on rarity.  Throughout each mission, the objectives you complete and loot you pick up will affect the quality of your post-game drop.  I won't spoil the specifics, but it truly creates a sense of urgency when it comes to finishing certain tasks simply with the goal in mind of increasing your chance for a better drop.
SImilar to its predecessor, Vermintide features several special classes of Skaven with unique abilities and profiles.  They are (more or less) modeled after familiar special enemies from L4D.  These special units add a welcome variety to the chaos, and much like the rest of the game, never feel shoehorned in any way.
Yes, there are glitches.  Enemies get stuck in walls, the floor, the ceiling, and pretty much anywhere else massive hordes of Skaven manage to lodge themselves.  The Rat Ogres especially have a tendency to glitch out.  I have experienced a multitude of these malfunctions, but rarely are they game-breaking.
Overall, Vermintide is an accomlished first step for Fat Shark and Games Workshop.  Hopefully, with continued patching and updating, we will all have a polished gem of a game to enjoy for years to come (and knowing Games Workshop, lots of DLC too).

So I just finished my first run-through of the game in a little under 3 hours. I've been an avid fan of 2D platformers since way back in the day with one of my favorite series of all time being Megaman. That being said I enjoyed Deadlight quite a bit despite some of its obvious flaws. The graphics, tone and atmosphere of the game were pretty stellar to me. The borderline monochrome filter fit the bleak undertone that the game was trying to set. The story, although predictable, is still decent enough that it doesn't hinder the game progression. The platforming and combat can be really fun when everything works as it should. Now to the problem areas. The controls can be pretty finicky at times, more so due to the fact that the game forces you to play with the analogue stick. (I'm more of an old school D-Pad kinda guy when it comes to 2D platformers) The game, at times, makes it painfully tough to face the direction you want to be facing and the neutral jump can be sensitive which is a pain when your in high pressure cirumstances. The aiming system can also get in your way, especially in the latter parts of the game, since the sights wont register enemies that just come into your plane from the backdrop. (2.5-D problems) Last major issue I have with the game is the length since I was able to beat it in under 3 hours. Sure it does unlock nightmare mode and an alternate ending as well as minigames which adds to replay value but I figure they could've pushed to make the base game at least around 5-6 hours long.
All issues aside I had a lot of fun playing the game and I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoys 2/2.5D platformers or a zombie buff. 8/10 would get swarmed again by 6 zombies while trying to pick up a collectible.

In 2007, Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare was released, bringing with it sweeping changes to FPS games; Gone were the health pack pickups, the (then) overdone WWII setting and dull sprawling levels. In came tight focussed maps, peppered with jaw dropping set pieces, memorable and inventive levels to break up the pace of the game ("Death from Above", "All Ghillied Up"), all contributed to make an intense cinematic experience that was genuinely refreshing at the time and well received by the majority of gamers.
Moving onto 2013 and Call of Duty: Ghosts, the latest in a now annually released and stale franchise. Everything that made COD4 such a success is now turgidly reproduced ad nauseum in a manner that slowly renders the players brain to rancid cheese.
Linear, grey levels now inject so many set pieces that control is wrested from the player constantly so they can't possibly miss the next explosion or NPC delivering a punch to the face of the protagonist. What was once cinematic and exciting is now just a trudge through a quicktime hell interspersed with the opportunity to shoot some heads of pop up cannon fodder, enemies still using 7 year old AI routines.
COD4's NPCs were entertaining, if heavily caricatured characters, from Captain Price's tough & rough SAS leader to Gaz's amusing Jason Statham-esque Cockney sidekick. All helped drive the narrative on as you played, with minimum cut-scene intervention. Ghosts, by contrast, features a cast of cardboard cutout meatheads, who solely seem to exist as moving objective markers for the player all the while urging the player to "Check your six" apparently for Oscar Mike who I believe has yet to actually show his face in a Call of Duty game to date, despite all the rigorous checking that we're urged to participate in.
Speaking of characters, we get to the villain of the piece; All good action narrative needs a great bad guy to orchestrate the violence and COD4 provided us with two of them, Khaled Al-Asad and Imran Zakhaev, extremists forged by post-Soviet Middle Eastern and East European politics, who conspire to drag the world into global conflict, forcing the player in a race against time to save the world in spectacularly enjoyable and overblown fashion.
Ghosts' Rorke (Rourke? Rork? Zork?) is a revenge fueled berk, supposedly created by a bit of an accident and some brain washing exercise and.... yeah something and stuff happened, oooh what a nasty boy he is and no mistake.
All of this is presented by a dated graphics engine, hardly evolved from the original COD4 release. Murky, dull textures. A colour pallette that seems to consist of only brown and greys. Animation which looks clunky and unnatural, especially in contrast to the dog, Riley, which has clearly had time invested in to make it move realistically and only serves to make the human characters look even more janky. All conspire to deliver a washed out experience of a game that fails to excite or stir the player.
A by the numbers action game that delivers zero innovation, zero entertainment and the gaming equivalent of an unwelcome, beer induced turd into your Steam library, leaving a putrid smell and a stuborn stain on the side of the pan that no amount of bog brushing will remove.

The weapon mechanics are fun and diverse across the many different firearms, and playing with character voices on really gives you a more emersed feeling, as who you're playing as has much more of a personality as a human being, desperate to stay alive. The trailer makes it sound incredibly round based, but I beg to differ. Each playthrough of escape, for example, can take an average of half an hour. It's less of a "round", more of an adventurous experience, in a world that has fallen to chaos. Each map really shows how dark the apocalypse really is, with each level littered with blood pools and body bags, police cars and ambulances, death and disease. My only possible complaint is that this would be more fun if it were more of a survival experience, having to manage your own needs as a survivor, as well as defending your long-term shelter. The sound system could use some work, but something like that is hard to do.
All in all, a wonderful, yet tragic, game.

Door kickers is Awesome!
OMG they added Coop mode!
You can have a total of 10 officers. You will give each officer a class which you can change at any time before a mission starts. There are 5 classes total, 4 to unlock. You start with Pointman and unlock Assaulter, Shield, Breacher and finally Stealth. You then customize each officers class specific gear.
Each officer has his or her own rank which increases as they complete missions successfully. Their skill level increases with rank. As your officers rank up so does your overall squad rank.
Each time your squad rank increases you gain a doctrine point. These points are spent on pistol skills, long gun skills and shotgun skills. These skills are passive and improve every officer regardless of their rank.
Your officers can die permanently and will be replaced with rookie officers if you choose to continue after a  successful mission. If you restart the mission you will still have that said officer for consecutive attempts.
Each mission has a 3 star rating system. Each star awarded is currency to unlock gear. Gear is unlocked for the entire squad once you spend the stars. There are single missions, campaign missions and a mission generator for random missions. There is also the mission editor and steam workshop. You can plan a mission from beginning to end before you start. You can also pause the game anytime to plan as you go. If you are really brave you don't have to pause at all. It is very rewarding to watch your officers execute a perfect plan. You can even save replays and export videos in game.
It takes 10 minutes to plan a mission and anywhere from 5 seconds to 2 minutes to execute the takedowns. This game could probably be used as a training tool if given to the right people. Door kickers is all about tacticle planning and strategy. Very fun game to play! Easily worth the full price but if you see it on sale don't hesitate to pick this one up.

I've got a little more than an hour into this game, and I have to say, it is thrilling. It reminds me a lot of the old SWAT2 title, but far more approchable.
If you're into puzzle games, where you can pause the action to try and compose yourself, and think about your next move, than this is for you. I belive this is my favorite part. I'll use my units to clear each room, one at a time, pausing to figure out the next steps.
Does it always go to plan? Hell no, but i have a LOT of fun failing. I've had my eye on this game for a few months, and I really wish I picked it up sooner.

Probably the closest we'll ever get to another SWAT game. You get a selection of weapons and equipment to complete missions, from stun guns to stinger grenades to M4s. Then you're asked to complete levels in times that would make the SAS sweat.
Tasks can range from rescuing hostages to defusing bombs, to simply killng all enemies in the level. Intricate planning is a must - one mistake and that trooper you've been so proud of will be eating dirt in a second. You're not tougher than the enemies, so be smarter.
It's a tough, rewarding, fun strategy game with oodles of content (single levels, campaigns, and a mission generator). Well worth full price, and on sale, it's a steal.

This game has a lot of annoying UI problems - most of which are minor, but they add up - but other than that it's pretty good.
The game mechanics are solid, if a bit unrealistic in parts. For example, enemies can hit you with grenades when you're inside a house and they're outside, down the street. (The grenade appears to go over the exterior wall of a house and through the roof.) Cover isn't very consistent. Some cars give you cover; others don't. It has an iron-man mode, which I appreciate. The unit classes are a bit unbalanced in that some are much more useful than others, but it doesn't matter too much.
The game has you executing civilians without warning and without giving them a chance to surrender, so you basically play a bad cop in a police state, but then we're all used to games being murder simulators anyway. The game calls the criminals "terrorists", which is about as accurate as calling them "communists". I'm slightly bothered by the promotion of terrorist hysteria and the dilution of the word "terrorist" into meaninglessness, but oh well.
The map designs are pretty good, but it seems that you either need luck or prescience to beat some of them without casualties, which is a bit unfortunate. The game comes with an editor that lets you make your own scenarios and share them for other people to play.
The game doesn't have a manual or a decent tutorial, but you can probably figure it out.
The developer is very active in the forums and frequently responds to questions, which I greatly appreciate, but I'm not sure how good he is at fixing bugs. (I know of at least one problem that he said would be fixed "in the next update", but that was in August 2014 and it's still not fixed as of June 2015. Maybe he forgot or maybe he changed his mind. I don't know.)
The existing campaigns and missions seem like they'll provide at least 20 hours of play, and there are supposed to be more campaigns coming. I don't know whether the developer will make good on that promise, but it's nice that the game is supposed to continue to grow in the future.
Overall, the game has lots of little problems that detract from the enjoyment but even so it's still fun.

Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide has proved to be as exhilerating an experience as any I have found in the hemisphere of co-op action games.
So, you've played Left 4 Dead, you've played Payday, and now you're here, ready to experience the gore-slicked depths of Vermintide.
Taking elements from two of the most successful co-op franchises in recent history syngergizing them together with a classic Warhammer veneer?  That's the ticket.
The gameplay is fine-tuned, responsive, and very technical in terms of dodging, blocking, etc.  In order to be a competent team member, it is necessary you have an understanding of these maneuvers.  This can seem daunting at first, but once you acquire the rhythm for each character and begin to understand how to time your strikes, things get very fun very fast.
The teamwork element in this game is very similar to that of Payday.  It is absolutely necessary your team stick together in order to make an effective stance against the Skaven hordes.  It takes things beyond Left 4 Dead, however, by implementing tasks in each mission that must be completed in order to advance (as opposed to simply slaying every enemy).  Some missions are more arduous than others, but they all present the the player with situations to test your ability to think on your feet and form effective, cohesive strategies at a moment's notice.
The ambiance and atmosphere of Vermintide are top-notch.  Fat Shark did a great job taking the mystique of Warhammer's lore and applying it to a co-op action game.  The music and sound effects do a stellar job immersing the player in its mire of burning rat flesh and dancing swords.
The class system offers a broad variety of playstyles to appeal to all types of players.  Moreso, each class is so customizable that it is easy to switch traditional party roles without changing characters.  As you unlock new weapons, new options open up in terms of strategy.  For example, these weapons would allow you to take your dwarf from a tank, to dps, to support, with nothing more than a simple weapon switch.  This customizaiton allows for a higher degree of player innovation, and coming to understand how different playstyles work with one another is highly engaging.
The loot system is very simple and concise.  Each class has a certain set of weapons unique to that character.  These wapons are obtained through drops received upon leveling up and completing missions.  All weapons are ranked by tier depending on rarity.  Throughout each mission, the objectives you complete and loot you pick up will affect the quality of your post-game drop.  I won't spoil the specifics, but it truly creates a sense of urgency when it comes to finishing certain tasks simply with the goal in mind of increasing your chance for a better drop.
SImilar to its predecessor, Vermintide features several special classes of Skaven with unique abilities and profiles.  They are (more or less) modeled after familiar special enemies from L4D.  These special units add a welcome variety to the chaos, and much like the rest of the game, never feel shoehorned in any way.
Yes, there are glitches.  Enemies get stuck in walls, the floor, the ceiling, and pretty much anywhere else massive hordes of Skaven manage to lodge themselves.  The Rat Ogres especially have a tendency to glitch out.  I have experienced a multitude of these malfunctions, but rarely are they game-breaking.
Overall, Vermintide is an accomlished first step for Fat Shark and Games Workshop.  Hopefully, with continued patching and updating, we will all have a polished gem of a game to enjoy for years to come (and knowing Games Workshop, lots of DLC too).

If you're a fan of Left 4 Dead 1/2, Killing Floor, or any other wave based zombie survival, buy this. Right now. I don't care, just do it.
This game, when I first opened it up, was a bit too close to L4D for my comfort. I thought I just got ripped off, dropped 30 bucks on something that could be downloaded for free as a good mod.
Theeeeennnn I started to actually play it. The loot drops are addicting, the levels are just the right amount of action/downtime (thanks to the improved AI director over L4D), and it's not arbitrarily hard, like L4D. You actually have to be good to get away with the endgame difficulty, rather than abuse spawn points.
The movement mechanics I'm still undecided on. I really miss the ability to jump backwards (mostly to see what sort of bunny hopping shenanigans I can start), but dodging is a MASSIVE asset to your arsenal. The maps are still a bit buggy in terms of mobility, you'll get caught up on♥♥♥♥♥♥from time to time. It's interesting to see how they actively promote "parkour" throughout the maps, by hiding the Tomes and Grimoires (they give you additional loot rolls at the end, but take up inventory space, and with the Grimoires, actually reduce your health bar) throughout the map in hard to reach places.
The characters themselves are all badass, with INCREDIBLE voice acting. My favorite character is the one I thought would be the weakest, the Empire Soldier, Markus Kruber. His voice actor gives off just the right amount of biting sarcasm and dry humor, and I can't get enough of it. There is quite a bit of overlap in the character roles, most specifically with the Dwarf Ranger and the Empire Soldier, but it's not a bad thing. They all have incredibly unique loadouts and can fill just about any role you want them to.
The way the weapons feel, both ranged and melee, feel absolutely perfect. There's just the right amount of "oomph" in the heavier weapons, the lighter ones feel like extensions of your character, just slicing through everything. The bows feel appropriately elegant, the firearms brutish but effective. It's ♥♥♥♥en sweet.
The music in the game sounds like it shouldn't fit, but it strangely enough does. I love it, it fits the intensity of the game perfectly.
Have I mentioned how challenging it is? Because it's just right. Easy is exactly that, easy. Normal is a bit tougher, but still gives you that cinematic feel. Hard is actually pretty difficult, but not impossible with pubs. Nightmare is incredibly difficult with pubs, but still pretty doable with a good group. Cataclysm is just insane, it's impossible with pubs and incredibly difficult with a good group. It's not arbitrary difficulty, like with L4D, though. The inclusion of a block and dodge mechanic inherently makes it less of a pain to just ratchet up damage. The health of the enemies goes up as well, but not to the same obscene levels as L4D. On top of that, it throws ♥♥♥♥♥ier and ♥♥♥♥♥ier situations at you as time progresses, and those stages increase at an alarming rate as the difficulty goes up.
There are quite a few issues with the game, though.
The maps are buggy (Acceptable, the game's a week old after all), which rears its ugly head in the (recently fixed) Black Powder and Horn of Magnus, with multiple spots that give damn near invincibility. There is a minor bug in Enemy Underneath where, during the escape, you get stuck on rocks while going uphill, which leads to some pants ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moments.
The optimization is garbage. It's literal♥♥♥♥♥ I can run ARMA 3 on High, which is miles more taxing than this game should be (Especially on the CPU load, like this game), but on certain maps I chug down to 20-30 FPS, without big fights happening. The particle effects (Which I have set to low, for the record) tank my FPS like no other. It's a pain.
The enemy AI is... Unique.  They range from being ungodly smart (Individuals in a mob splitting one persons attention, forcing the group to dedicate two people to the same direction),  to being ungodly goddamn stupid, like kiting a Rat Ogre over the top of a fence until it dies from the ranged weapon spam.
The AI director itself ranges from being great, to being absolutely irritating. Sometimes it feels like just the right amount of challenge, other times it throws a Rat Ogre, two or three Gas Rats, a Ratling Gun, and an Assassin at you, alongside a mob, with a Stormvermin patrol coming in hot for good measure. It's odd.
The sound direction is very.. meh. While the weapons feel fantastic, they sound weaker than hell. Not much more to say here.
Altogether, if you're a fan of progressive wave-based shooters and/or L4D and L4D2, pick this game up. If you want a solid, story based hacknslash, I'd give it a pass.

Call of Duty Ghosts is an intresting game.
It has most of what made the old Call of Duty games so great. But it suffers from poor map design, a kill time which is too fast (which encourages camping with those last two combined), killstreaks which are kinda boring, and (the game itself) just not being that fun. Though overall the game (in general) plays decently, I never got too frustrated, but then again it has most of what made CoD good but has so many of it's own problems that it's not as fun to play as CoD 4 or MW2.
And (at least the last time I played it) it suffered from microstutters and texture streaming problems (exclusive to PC) on my GTX 660 (a great 2012 card which can play BF4 maxed out @1080p 60fps).
What breaks the back of this game is that nobody really plays this game that much on PC anymore.
I've payed $40 for the PC version and $14 for the Xbox One version. I don't want to shell out any more money to this game unless it's the Xbox One version (which has thousands of more players daily and I hear the DLC is better than the base game maps). And even then I'd have to have money to kill to even consider that.
I wouldn't recommend this to PC users. If you can find this for (really) cheap for one of the current gen consoles (with the season pass) then perhaps you might get something out of it, but if you're looking at the PC version, just skip it, you won't regret spending your money on something better. If you want to play a new Call of Duty game for PC, get Black Ops 3 instead.
I would not recommend you get this on PC at all. For what the game is (by itself) it's barely passable.

I played this game shortly after its initial release well before access on steam, and I can say that through all the much anticipated waiting for the servers to go back online hours after a crash, I can say the game has made some major overhauls.  First, I have not seen a "servers down for maintenance" since 2013, and the mechanics on the vehicles have since been fine tuned, although some things I feel like are historically inaccurate (e.g. the German medium armor are incapable of piercing US medium armor regardless of distance, and the Yak has four bombs when the Bf-109 can only carry one with a gold bombs away badge equipped).  The hit recognition system I feel like can be misguided at times when it pings other players asking if they were hit, but compared to what it was in the beginning is leaps and bounds better.  The grinding is a bit of an issue, but I find myself coming back again and again to play this game because of my love for WWII simulators.  Sure you might get spawn camped, but spawn in another location and flank the enemy instead of complain about it.  If you or the enemy have been pushed back to the access point, spawn camping is all you can do because the team is screwed anyway.  If a troop transport was blown up in real life, it's comparable to spawn camping, so do not let it get you down.  I rarely get spawn camped anymore, and if I do I might get annoyed for a little bit, but get revenge and kill the spawn campers multiple times to get even.
Overall, my opinion of the game is this:  I have played this game for years now and can get easily frustrated as well as easily ecstatic over a large KD spread and unlocking new items for soldiers.  You can play as any faction, which can take some time, but it's gratifying when you perform well in the battlefield.  I recommend this game for anyone who likes to use vehicles in a WWII simulator FPS.  I still play this game almost everyday and don't intend to stop anytime soon.  This game is still being worked on and i have high hopes for it in the future.

So hotline miami 2 is a game where you play as a group of people (All at different times of course) All tied to different things, the stuff after jacket is tied to stuff about jacket (The fans, manny pardo jelouse of the fans, and evan the writer writing about jackets crimes and junk), and the stuff before jacket is tied to 50 blessings. I feel this game is so genuinely good that I'll make an actual review on it.
While it does have its faults, some of which being the pathing of the Alex character or your retical being stuck to certain positions as you advance to a side of or in the corner of a map, Hotline Miami 2 is a phenomenal sequel to the first game. Plain and simple. It's different, difficult, and entertaining as long as you take it piece by piece, if you become stressed easily. Every character you play as will have a restriction or an added ability, ensuring you'll have a different experience than you did in the first game. Enemies have new variations as well. It looks and feels great. It plays fluidly and rewards you for taking a more strategic approach to certain levels rather than a reckless one. And, while I'll admit I was frustrated with the level design during my first playthrough of the game, the addition of a level editor by the developers guarantees your experience playing it will never go stale, so long as the community wants to keep the game alive.
Having kept track of this game since it's announcement and being eager for it's release in 2015, it became very apparent that Dennaton was very nervous about making it. More than anything, they wanted to make a good sequel, for their fans and for themselves alike. I couldn't argue more that they succeeded in doing so with Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. It's not just more of the same. It's a different approach to more of the same. A violent, top-down shooter/smasher/slasher still but with more emphasis on story and character rather than just gameplay. In every sense of the phrase, this game does more of the same right. Anyone who creates a sequel to anything should look to this game as an example of how things should be done.

After over 20 hours of playing the game and as a fan of rhythm/music games I continue to strongly enjoy the game.
+ You can load up your music and start playing with it!
+ Easy to learn and quickly becomes intuitive once you understand when to press keys.
+ Multiple difficulties including an option to customize the difficulty. Don't like that Overload gives you less input time? You can set it to normal (or more forgiving) if you wish.
+ Simple but nice visuals with the ability to customize Melody's appearance and colors in general.
+ Can get genuinely challenging at times.
= The music is rather inconsistent when it comes to following the rhythm of the tune you picked up. It generally does a pretty good job and at times it's spot on but don't expect it to do a perfect job most of the time.
= The input is not as it initially looks. You need to press the button a little earlier. However, once you get used to it, it is a non-issue.
- Difficulty can be pretty inconsistent at times though. Certain tunes are very easy even on overload.
- Fake difficulty. This doesn't happen all too often but there are instances where Melody will jump down and the motion will not fully catch up. This results in you landing on the ground and find yourself right in front of an input with very little time to respond.
Besides that you can't lose in this game but this is irrelevant as the game is more of a score attack to try to get better results and beat your precious score. Oh that and enjoying the game with music you like. The game might induce headaches to some because of motions and background effects. If that's a possible issue just scroll up and check the video instead of possibly end up and you'll immediately figure out if it's a problem or not.

It's a game I have enjoyed and think with continued development it could be pretty amazing. I wouldn't have described it as release quality however.
Before I say anything more I should probably say I only play offline/single player. With that said the one 'campaign' that ships with the game while not 100% bug free (And how many games are 100% bug free these days?) is pretty well done, the terrain is well made, the progression is steady and it doesn't take long to learn how to play and to reach your goals. There are one or two areas that could do with sharpening.
A large amount of work is placed on the player to create their own vehicles. Yet the tools don't take into account mass, center of gravity, etc. And yet once plaed into the world both of these are pretty essential. Furthermore when using the templates that the game gives you to - I assume - get you started, they either come with parts you have yet to unlock, or don't work as expected. Case in point: The quest was to deliver an NPC to another area, she suggests that now you have unlocked some of the boat parts that you should build a boat to take her to the place she's going.
I'm not a boat builder... so I used the templete provided within the system. The boat it produces looks amazing, however most of the parts used are still locked, having removed those parts or replaced them with the parts I can actually create, the boat will barely move without turning turtle. In the end I make a simple log raft that works pretty well instead.
Often the obvious mistakes are like this, oversights as opposed to actual bugs or poor design decisions.
The game as it stands has three 'modes'. Campaign mode (as mentioned above), Adventure Mode & Creative Mode
Adventure mode is as far as I can tell there to show you how much better campaign mode is. It's full of bugs and overall badly designed.
Creative Mode is fun for about five minutes, until you realise that while you can build anything you want, you can't interact with the world as there are no animals or NPCs.
The game is officially now a full release, but if you want to try it in it's current state just pretend it's still in beta. It's not polished enough or infact complete enough (to my mind) to be called a finished product. It's given me some good enjoyment, and the system to design & buiold vehicles and weapons while not perfect can be quite a bit of fun. So do I recommend this game? Yes but with caution. Good sandbox game it is, finished it isn't.

Note: I've only played singleplayer
The game itself is nice, the crafting aspect is deep, almost TOO deep (Not a bad thing, I just haven't gotten the hang of it)
The map seems pretty huge. but that's okay, you can build vehicles (flying, land, and sea) to get around.
The story is interesting, not like, game of the year "10/10 would bang" good, but it's interesting, you're apart of a group of people who are looking for a new home in the universe and you crash land on this planet, and now you're trying to find everyone, and it goes from there.
The voice audio for some of the characters sounds muffled, kinda weird and kills the immersion. I'm assuming they have that on the radar to work on.
The combat is cool, although (I could be wrong) but it doesn't seem like headshots matter when fighting creatures. not a big deal, but just something I noticed.
You can have followers, that's neat, and they have skills / abilities that differ from follower to follower. You can have them stay put somewhere, follow you, etc. and you can set them to defensive, aggressive, and passive.
You have to manage various types of ailments. Infection, injuries, etc. oh, and of course hunger. Don't eat too much though! there's a penalty for that. Pretty cool.
Overall I love the game, I kept telling myself that I was going to go play something else, and next thing I knew I had been playing it all day and didn't want to stop so I could build that next thing, or finish this ONE quest, etc.
I can't wait to see what they do next for this game, it's neat.
