So, I just marathoned both HM1 and 2 (as I was late to the party with 1, got intrigued by it through Payday 2 blah blah...). Anyway, after beating both and sitting on my thoughts, I felt that I had to review them. Particularly this one.
Hotline Miami 2 is trying to both emulate Hotline Miami 1's successes" while trying to be its own separate beast. Key word there is
.
First and foremost, Hotline Miami is known for unapologetic, hyper violence. The first was fast-paced and thrill seeking. The second... not so much.
As many of the reviews hovering around have mentioned, the levels are huge in comparison to HM1. The sheer size of many maps is probably an attempt to make the stakes that much higher than 1's. Throw in about triple the amount of gunners, glass windows, and fatguys compared to the first, rushing in with nothing but a baseball bat seems like an awful idea. Enemies are ready to snipe you from a good distance away from your vision, even when shift-looking. The AI is a bit more unpredictable and I've seen players restart constantly just to get the ideal set-up to get the max rank on the level.
Because of these behaviors, the challenge is ramped up yet there is more emphasis on
or
over running in like a maniac clubbing fools. It's not really a
thing, but it quite feel right when compared to 1.
As its own thing however, it is not bad in the slightest. After getting used to the new "rules" of the game, I started to adapt and find myself analyzing the situation for an ideal course of action. Then I'd apply trial and error until I got GO TO CAR.
Replacing the mask mechanic from 1, we now have multiple characters to play with that have unique abilities save for a couple of duds.
In short, the gameplay still has its ultraviolent nature from the first, it's just the approach to handling the challenge is a different experience than HM1. Beating a level is still a triumphant feeling.
Hotline Miami 1 barely had a real story to it. There were teases to background info of a narrative but it was never really the intent of 1 to tell a story. Hotline Miami 2, however, tries to tell a story... well, multiple stories to varying degrees of success.
Each character has a story arc that tells their history of what is going on in the mid 80's to early 90's. Without spoiling actual plot, some of these stories intersect to show how the events lead to the finale... as well as one or two really having no point in existing at all.
The problem with the story-telling feels like a conflict of trying to be a symbolic, interpretive art piece while also trying to be an actual narrative but never really commits to either. While there is nothing wrong with a piece that is left to interpretation... the problem is that while the lead up adheres to that rule, the climax and finale do not.
In the ways of being a narrative, we get teases of how events are set up, especially with the possible origin of 50 Blessings,the fate of Jacket, the relationship between America and Russia, etc. However, these threads go nowhere, which, ironically, is a central theme to the story lines.
Inevitability of the end is the overall theme of the story and, while the build up with scenes constructed around it are well done, the pay off is rather disappointing and almost rushed. No, really, you get to the climax and "first ending" of the game halfway through as one side of the story and then finish it up again on the other side. Shortly after that, you get the second ending to tie up the remaining loose ends, mostly poorly. At the end, you're left with literally nothing.
While I'm not asking for a full-fledged epic, the minimalist story telling HM1 did attempt worked well to get fans to think and could've continued into HM2 while building upon its twisted world. The game's environments along with the short bits of dialogue told a story. There was fun in piecing the deeper tidbits together in HM1. HM2 doesn't do that. Everything is given to you pretty much up front when dealing with the immediate plot to leave nothing to interpretation. When it comes to the burning questions of the story, they are merely brushed upon and never given satisifying payoffs, especially what, at the moment, is the last official Hotline Miami game.
To summarize: HM2 feels like it is on to something with the stronger points of the story only to just give up on it and flat out say "don't worry, there's no point, the end" at the end as some sort of deeper meaning. Granted, story is
the main appeal to the Hotline Miami series but it had the makings of something intriguing to explore.
Merging these together, there isn't much to say. You still have your colorful retro graphics and amazing soundtrack. These two followed the "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" mantra.
So, it sounds more negative here than positive. Why do I still recommend Hotline Miami 2? Because it is not a bad game when compared to the first. It's better to describe it as a game with a
meta (god, I hate that term, but it fits). I still got hours of enjoyment out of it and I am looking forward to improving my awful scores of my first run.
The game itself was an ambitious attempt to do more than HM1, but I believe the idea of finality got to deeply engrained into the development rather than work towards slowly building up to something fantastic. As of writing this review, we still wait for what the level editor will add to the experience which I do look forward to.
Hotline Miami 2 is a good game that doesn't quite match up to the original. You'll still enjoy it but don't expect it to be better than the first as many reviews state. It is the 8/10 to Hotline Miami's 9/10.

I played through Verminetide as a huge fan of the Warhammer World. It's a bit of a strange one to "Not" recommend, so I'll highlight why I feel the need to put that status there. I did play through Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide and I did briefly enjoy it. The zones are very detailed and immersive, the gameplay is hectic and fast, and the character interactions and voices are quite funny ... at first.
I haven't been able to figure out which one of the females is doing it, I suspect the Waywatcher, but everyone is constantly ripping on the dwarf. Yes he's a bit stuntie, might be an alcoholic and seems to always be the one getting tugged around the place by Vermintide's "Smoker" (Packmaster?), but does he constantly deserve the same really naff one liners that she comes out with putting him down? Leave the poor bloke alone man!
Eventually, I requested a refund for Vermintide for the time being and I think it mostly comes down to my next point. The Combat. Combat between the characters felt near enough identical and it just wasn't as fun as I thought it would be. The severing of limbs doesn't happen nearly as much as you'd want it to, playing in this grim setting and often you swing your weapon about wildly as you're struck from all over. If you've played L4D for any great period of time, you'll learn that putting your back to a wall and fending off attackers, whilst defending your flanks, generally deals with just about anything they can throw at you, that doesn't take you out of your protection zone (Gas, Rat Ogres, Fallen Allies.) I realised early on that I was doing the same thing over and over, without really ever feeling like the enemies posed a great threat, or were overly sneaky in their ambushes. I suppose it felt predictable.
I feel this is a game that I'd consider purchasing again for half the asking price (which isn't a great deal of cash, but the game just doesn't offer enough innovation for its price marker.), especially if additional races were added to give the player some relief from killing the same generic clan rats over and over again. I'm honestly not quite certain why I find these enemies incredibly dull compared to the frantic, screaming zombies of L4D, but I just didn't enjoy taking them down. Perhaps the charisma of the greenskins or the deadly diversity of the Vampire Counts could inject some additional flavour into this game, in order to help diversify it up a bit.
If you've never played either of the Left 4 Dead games, you might enjoy this as a fresh experience.
If you have a strange hatred of rodents, I'd recommend that you play this ... you strange, strange person you ...
If you're looking for something that feels really satisfying when it comes to cleaving your enemies limb from limb ... I'd recommend that you buy Chiverly. The damage of weapons + Visual carnage that follows their use Vs The amount of enemies that come at you, just lead to the bitter feeling that you're hitting an endless wave of dull target dummies. With a few minor tweaks, I think this could be a much better game.
Again, worth a go, but as someone who refunded this game, I wouldn't recommend it to my friends with confidence.

If you played this game when you were younger and you're ready for a good dose of nostalgia, buy this game. However, if you've never played this game before, this may or may not be worth your time.
I'm recommending this because, out of all the Sonic games that have been released within the last decade-and-a-half, this is still my favorite. Yes, I can attribute some of that to the nostalgic value that I'm placing on it, but it's really quite a good game in terms of gameplay. Is it the perfect Sonic title? No. Not by a long shot. But it's still fun.
You have 3 styles of gameplay in this title. First and foremost are your "Speed" levels, which you have to get through the level as fast as possible. This is the most classic gameplay of a Sonic game that many fans are familiar with. You play these levels with either Sonic or Shadow. Then you have your 3rd-person shooter levels. I feel like these levels are the most taxing and least fun in the game, but the goal is to shoot everything in your path and reach the end of the level. You play these levels with either Tails or Dr. Eggman. Lastly, we have the "treasure hunt" style of levels, which are actually pretty fun if you explore a little. You have to search for the pieces of the Master Emerald in these settings, and these are played by either Knuckles or Rouge.
The premise of the Chao Garden is to raise your own Chao by giving it animals and chaos drives to increase it's abilities, and effectively make it stronger to participate in Chao Karate and in races. Also, you get to sorta act like a parent to these things, so it's a pretty neat and fun side activity to do while reaching high scores on all of the levels in the games.
In the end, it's quite a fascinating game. The total story time amounts to maybe 4 hours if you know what you're doing and where to go, 6-7 if you're new to the game. But with all of the kart racing, chao raising, and different quests in the levels, you can keep playing the game for hours and hours and still not have done everything there is to do. If you're not a Sonic fan or didn't play this game in your childhood, then it's not for you. However, if you haven't played the game before and you enjoy Sonic games every once in awhile, this is a great title to play, and I highly recommend it.

I haven't play this game for over a year.
Bought it just for multiplayer, which unfortunately is dead and boring. Most people I've seen are 12, 1-2 scatter on official and private servers.
I played for 20 hours on an official servers.
First I tried a Official story mode server (for about an hour). I found playing on this to be completely pointless. It's still setup for single player. Meaning once a mission is completed, it's gone forever. Unfortunately learning new things are completely mission based. So all these type of servers are dependant on how many have come before you and how far they've gotten in the missions. Hence now no one plays anymore on these servers.
Per the Dev in the forums, go play on a private server. <-- I had a colorful thought to this remake.
Then I tried an official adeventure survival server (pvpve). The game still has lots of bugs and glitches. You can't destroy player built structure, and there's lots of them, usually in cities where you need to go for missions in order to be able to advance. Players log on temporarly, build something stupid (grief) and log off. Imagine that, PVP with no raiding allowed. Second I was completely bored. There's nothing to really do except some missions. some are glitched and you'll never be able to complete them, some are just plain stupid, none are level biased.
Example. I just created my character (that has no exps or skills), run thru the mission script (that you can't abort), it spawns some monsters that kill me instantly in one hit. You have the option to revive yourself, but there's no point since they are still standing where they killed you. You respawn and die immediately again.
On the adventure server I found you get skills. To get a skill to go up, you must get experience points by mining, chopping trees, or fighting.
All drops are random. I spent 20 hours to only get the knowledge to make a stone pick (after 4 hours of game play) and a copper shovel (after 17 hrs of game play). I found out I can mine ore with a shovel. A stone pick will not mine ores.
If you ask the right NPC, they will give you a mission for a MK2 laser rifle, after that you don't need anything else.
Shovels are obsoleted in this game. Best just use a pick, better reward and faster. Shovels only do a wider area, but less reward.
Ranged combat is everything in this game, you only use melee when you first start or if you absolutely have to.
They've added dungeons (adventure only). Risk vs reward just isn't there. Plus you find no scripts (to learn how to make new items) in dungeons. Just armor and weapons, mostly just junk to sell. Also the monsters tend to get stuck or they're too big to fit thru the hallways, easy pickings.
Fighting the various monster in the game is uninspiring. They run directly at you and get stuck on whatever obsticle is in the way.  And then there's the part that hardly any spawn all. I remember a year ago, I was being chased alot. Not so anymore. Most just travel in packs. Kill half of them, the rest flee. In dungeons, the harder monsters are just too big and get stuck easily. Making it easy for you to kil lthem.
To make money to buy items you have to be able to sell. Most of the time, merchants are out of money unless you purchase from them first.
They've added a comfort level to characters. Now you must either buy a comfort shot or sit in a chair/bed and wait for your comfort level to rise. Yes, this type of innovation really make me want to play this game all the more. Watch tv while waiting for your comfort level to max out, so you can play for a while to do it all over again. And the better the armor, the less comfort maximun you have, so the more you have to eat and rest, but if you eat too much then you also get penalized. So I'm starving, but since all I had was low value food, I'm also penalized for it, makes sense. Yup, they've taken all the fun right out of game play.
Was reading this game is "supposedly" schedule to leave EA on Nov 7 due to external pressure. Yeah, that's a very good reason to move a game out of EA, who cares if it's full of bugs, as long as we make everyone else happy, except the people who play it.
On the plus side you can make your own vehicles and weapons. It seems overly complicated to me as I don't play this game much. But if you're into spending hours on something like this, then this game is for you.
Got a disease, forget about getting a remedy for it, just teleport to a location to get rid of it. Kinda wondering why they even added them.
It can be fun for a while, new game nostalgia, after a while you'll start to lose interest, find out it's just repetative, and finally figure out it's just boring.

I absolutely recommend this game!
As I described it to my roommate, it's like Minecraft and Skyrim had a baby in space. And it is fantastic!
There are certainly still some bugs to work out; like written and spoken dialogue not matching up or having typos, at least one instance of a completely different character's dialogue from a completely separate mission being heard, and characters walking away while still talking to you.
But that all pales in comparision to just how great the game is as a whole. The landscapes, plants, and creatures are all exceptionally crafted, incredibly alien, yet subtly familiar, too. The creatures run the gambit from squee inducing cuteness to don't-play-alone-in-the-dark scary to I-hope-that-colossal-thing-is-friendly. The different biomes feel very different from each other, yet blend seemlessly.
Then there's what YOU can do! You can full sandbox it or follow storyline quests and sidequests. There's harvesting, learning ISO's (blueprints), crafting, and even making fully customizable weapons, vehicles, buildings, you name it. And when I say fully customizable, I don't mean you have a few skins to slap on or mods to click in place. I mean you can go as in depth as you want, from the ground up shaping or borrowing in game assets to create a wholly orginal item which is fully functional within the game.
I'm incredibly excited to see them polish this gem so it shines the way it deserves when it leaves early access to become a full release.

Contagion is a first-person, cooperative multiplayer that takes various approaches and scenarios of a zombie apocalypse into a video game. Contagion is a sequel (?) or a spiritual successor (?) to Zombie Panic: Source, which is a free multiplayer mod.  Does the game stands apart from other zombie games? Is it worth playing? What about the replay value? Let's find out.
Contagion has a problem on standing out from other zombie games. There is no uniqueness or distinct flavor for this game. Escape Mode is one of the most common gameplay feature where you (and your friends or other players) have to do objectives while trying to get to the extraction point and not being killed on the way there. Escape Mode does have a "moderate" replay value, but most of the time is wasted on backpedaling to an old area to get something or do an objective. This leads to quick boredom and it kills replay value. This mechanic seems familiar to Left 4 Dead's AI Director system in terms on what items are located (along other things), but to go back to a cleared area to do an objective is a bit, odd. In the other hand, Escape Mode can be enjoyable if you have a group of friends to play with (and if your friends
enjoy it). Escape Mode seemed to have died out very quickly and that gameplay feature is the most popular one. Try to play PVP mode? Good luck on that.
The main problem for Contagion is that the player population is very low and the daily numbers are abysmal based on Steam Charts. Contagion does have sale promotions on the Steam Store to get other gamers to buy the game (as it was shown in Summer, Halloween, Autumn, and Winter Sales), and the results varied. Overall, Contagion is typical, bland, and certainly identical to other zombie games. Contagion was in development for a good amount of years and doing a Kickstarter to help "fully" develop the game is in question that the reader or gamer would have to judge for themselves.
A summary...
1. Is the game worth $20 or regional equivalent? Definitely not.
2. Are there updates and DLCs for the game? As far as I am concerned, there was a DLC recently released as a update (and it is free). However, the time span between updates are terrible.
3. Replay value? It varies from "moderate" to downright dreadful.
4. Sale price of $5 or less (including its regional equivalence)? Your choice. For me, it is not.
I would not recommend it unless you are an avid gamer who likes zombie games. It's a buyer's beware, and take serious accounts from pros and cons for the game from different reviewers.

Music is probably the best hobby I have after gaming. I have heard several artists that I liked and disliked. Usually, almost all my favorite bands doesn’t come from the radio because most of the time the radio spews forgettable and unbelievably average music and not the kind that is laughably bad like Owl city, it’s just average. The music I usually find is on files from computers or from my mum’s collection and some from New Zealand airlines. I seem to have a fondness of weird music such as Bjork and Ben Howard some of my family members say, and sitting here right now listening to SoundCloud and other forms of casual reggae, hip-hop and Rap with my aunts and uncles on Waihiki island, makes me relax with the help of the islands beauty. It’s just good to get out of Auckland sometimes and in a situation like this reminds me of "Melody's escape".
"Melody's escape" is one of the entries of rhythm based music games on steam and just to note right now, this is the only “rhythm based game that plays your music” that I have played. I’m not quite sure what the other rhythm game are like on steam and the only indication is the reviews that make or break them. I’ll say right now that it is a good game, not a heart stopping, game that questions your psychology and tests it like 'spec: ops the line', just a calming, casual game. But that’s just not doing it justice, here’s an in-depth review on the game itself.
You play as a trim, skinny girl (obviously, melody) that looks like the thin Lizzy makeup girl’s extra details being thrown out. Your job is to get her to the other side of the level with minimal errors and to “escape” the level, hence why it’s called melody’s escape. But enough about talking to you like an idiot, the levels are designed around the music you put into the game and it works very well. The levels scenery can change from a city in the calm parts of the music to her flying her rocket boots in a forest in the intense part of the music.
There are even small details that help change the mood of the level depending on what the music does. There’s this one part when I was playing “Blue Jeans” by Lana Del Ray, the music stopped for a few seconds and saw melody falling in slow motion until it got back up to tempo and time went back to normal. I was generally impressed by this feature the developer implemented. The background can be out of sync with the music you’re playing and it only has a certain speed for certain kind of music preferably pop and indie music. The tempo in level design for “Taro”
by Alt-J was close to the same for “Windsurfing Nation”
By Broken social scene, look up the music and you’ll see what I mean.
The gameplay works with either a four or eight button control, depending on the difficulty you want. The easiest mode is that each area has one button which could be too easy and the hardest is each note must have two button consecutively pressed and throws  more orbs and lines at you. The middle ground is when you must press a button for each different orb and line which is the preferred play style, or not depending on your personality. If it sounds like it’s a recreation of Stanley's job in 'The Stanley parable', it’s more fun and difficult than it looks.
It’s the same as any other rhythm game, nothing special but the scenery and special effects makes it fun. The other mode it has is like a random generated music video, you don’t control Melody but the computer does, and you just watch her go through the level, probably not worth mentioning.
Melody’s escape is like a relaxing game you go back to once and a while, and as interesting as it looks, the novelty fades away until you find some new music. It works with any file, all you have to do is drag it to the games window and the level is generated, thanks to the developers. I’m not sure what other rhythm games are like compared to this. But it’s a nice game to come back to every few weeks when you find a good song on YouTube or an ost in a game’s file.
But not buying it isn’t going to make you miss out on anything, I recommend you get it if you want a time waster for a few minutes every once and a while, if not there are other games out there for people like you, preferably 'Manhunt' you monster.

I want to love this game! I really do, which is why I spend 60 hours hoping it was good. There are just so many small things that add up to a collected experience of "Man this game needed 1 more month in the oven". Now, some fanatic warhammer fans will downvote all these negative reviews, but believe me when I say that there is no bigger fanboy than I. This is also the reason why I'm am (and should be) the most critical reviewer I can be with games in this franchise.
I'll cut it "short" by writing the classic pros and cons
Pros-
+Melee combat is great. Weapons feel different from each other and you need to learn how to use your particular choice of weapon if you want to do well on the harder difficulties. Besides that the block and push functions work well, and you get rewarded for learning how to do this effectively. You will likewise get punished if you think that hitting is the only thing needed for success.
+Maps and graphics are amazing. I put these under the same category because I'm mostly talking about texture and feel,  and not about map-layout which is fine but negligable. The game oozes of warhammer and a dark setting where you really feel like moving through a medieval-esque city. I love it and the immersion is super strong.
+Left for dead with loot! This is a great way to add longevity to a game, and I like getting that shiny new item to try out on the next run. This has its drawbacks too which I'm going to talk about in the cons.
Cons-
-Let's start with the loot. Loot is great and all, but why do so many people have hundreds and hundreds of hours played in L4D if there is none. It simply comes down to a question of wether the game is fun or not. And boy is L4D fun. Same could be said for counter-strike. These games get played because they are fun and no other reason. So why does vermintide have loot and what does it contribute? As I said it feels great to earn a new piece of loot.
The problem with this is that loot has become the central point of the game to a point where exploit after exploit is being found and used to get that slight edge over the game. Alot of people would much rather play the same map over and over again rather than do a slightly harder map with a chance to fail and not get those shinies! This tells us a few things about the game. 1. alot of people play to get loot instead of getting loot for playing. And 2. the games maps are badly balanced loot-wise. The harder maps won't give you better loot, they just cost you more time with a higher chance to fail (and get zero loot). You are basicly not awarded proportionally with your effort. I could write page after page on how this could be fixed, and alot of people on the official forums are already doing just that.
I will however add another little note to the loot system -  The better the loot is, the more stats it has. Most stats are percentagebased (like 3-10% chance of healing you on a hit) and undetermined until you spend resouces to upgrade them at which point the stat percentage is determined. So sometimes you get a great item and roll the worst possible stats. I have a sword with 1% chance to heal you on a hit which is just the worst possible thing in the univers to see on an exotic item. What I'm trying to say with this rant is that in order to get the items you really want, you need to play several hundred hours. I have about 60 hours played right now, and I have only rolled terrible stats on my 25+ exotic items (exotic is the highest tier of non-cosmetic item in the game). That is an incredible amount of sub-par weapons.
The loot system needs to be reworked if the game wants to survive a few months into the future.
-Optimization is just god aweful. Seriously, this game is terribly optimized to a point where some newer computers need to run it on lowest settings to get 40+ FPS. The developers are constantly telling us that the sheer amount of skaven is taking alot of CPU power, which is why we are experiencing lag. Problem is that L4D has the same if not more enemies with similar if not better AI, and everyone and their dog can run L4D. Besides that the graphics are much better than L4D, but not on potato settings and resolution, where you can still experience terrible frame-drops. This might actually be my main complaint. It feels like a beautiful painting with stickfigures instead of people. Sad but true.
- So many bugs. Seriously, this game has not been tested enough. The developers are working hard and somewhat responsive on the forums, but damn did they do a bad job of playtesting this before release. It is a mess sometimes with skave clipping through the floor and specials teleporting or shooting through the roof and whatnot. Just plain bad.
-No dedicated servers (Yet). It is peer to peer which means that the whole game comes down to the connection to the host pc. And even worse, there are no save points in the game, so if the host has a DC of any kind, you will have to start ALL OVER. This is just plain bad design. When testing the game, the developers were all planted in the same building and probably playing over LAN at which point they thought - "Well this is a perfectly good way to handle multiplayer". Problem is.... It isn't. I haven't met a single person ingame who hasn't experience at least a couple of these, and most of us has had it happen in the last minutes of a map. You just want to punch something when a 30-40 minute playsession gets terminated.
+-There are alot more to say about this game, but I won't do it. I have said what is most crucial to know for whoever wants to buy this game. I have played 60 hours and will likely play 60 more. But I won't do it because I think the game deserves it. I do it because I'm a loot-♥♥♥♥♥, and I am repulsed by the notion that this possibly amazing game has made me one. You can do better, and for that I advice you to not buy this game yet. Buy it when the developers fix these things.
I promise to revise this review when/if things get better.

This is a great game, and it doesn't have a difficult learning curve to the play style.  First, you take over a SWAT team that consists of ten members with varying attributes in marksmanship, assault shooting(close quarters), and field skills(a skill that speeds up the ability to disarm bombs for instance).
Since the game is in the top down mode, you are able to script out the directions you want your team members to move, provide covering fire, which doors to breach etc...  This is done before the match, and if you realize you made a mistake during the fight, you're able to pause, and re-adjust your routes, and covering fire; or you can make adjustments in real time.  As I said earlier, it's not a difficult learning curve, once you realize it's about applying covering fire for teams moving in open areas, or stacking alongside a room you're about to throw a flash bang in.  There is limitless possibilities you can create within the scenarios.
The game offers 80 missions(and often, when updates happen, more missions appear).  You can also create your own quick missions with varying styles.  Which means you can go in just to kill the enemies, capture and arrest individuals without lethal harm, disarm bombs and rescue hostages.  The game offers 5 campaigns at the time of this review, and they each have an additional 5-6 missions of varying difficulty.  This is not to forget that Steam Workshop is enabled for this game, and you're honestly left with so many choices that just about everyone can find something they're comfortable with(ie: you can apply mods for military type actions, with military weapons , or extra police type actions for instance).
The game progresses your characters by the number of missions that they accomplish, and the skills being applied are done for you.  It's up to you, and the mission to decide which of your team members gets placed in the action(for instance if you're disarming a bomb, you'll want someone with high field skills).  You'll also get experience to level up, which then you can unlock perks from a tree of skills to enhance skills with firearms(pistols, shotguns and rifles/carbines).  The game unlocks after certain levels as you can get different character sets, like breachers(shotguns), stealth(silenced weapons and movement), and using police shields to add extra defense to your team members.  Yet there is even more, you gain stars by completing missions(1 to 3 stars depending on what conditions are met), which the stars can be turned into buying upgraded weapons, body armor, accessories(tazer, breaching kit for example.  You basically have full control on what your team needs to complete the mission.
This game doesn't have too many flaws(at least when I've played), and the developers are still really active in producing content for the game.  What I do find enjoyable about this game is that it feels satisfying every time I play.  I don't feel like I have to commit 2 to 3 hours a day to enjoy the game.  I can honestly play a single mission, or 30 minutes and I won't feel disappointed in what I've accomplished; and certainly there is enough it do in this game to have you lose track of time and play hours at a time if you wish.
I highly recommend this game if you enjoy a tactical game where you're able to do all the planning and adjusting real time.  You won't be disappointed.

Incredible game, just incredible. I am currently as of writing this only six hours into the story mode, but wow. The graphics are great, it is very well optimized(at least SP, again have not tried online at all),the combat isnt amazing but is still fun,there are ALOT of creatures/aliens that all have different behavioral patterns(i.e. there is a stegosaurous looking guy that travels in packs)that mesh very well togther. The colony feature is also something to shout about. It basically allows you to recruit your fellow colonists once you do some quests for them. This makes hunting in single player much more entertaining and immersive, while adding more strategy as your colonists will only have what you equip them with, including healing items and ammo.Last but certainly not least is the crafting system. On its surface, it appears much like anyother survival crafting(using resources harvested from the world) to create things like wood pickaxe,copper pickaxe ect. However, there is a crafting editor where you can make literally anything you want. For example, I saw a guy that made a laser pistol that looked just like a X-wing,again that was a hand held laser pistol. Anything from weapons, armor, robots, vehicles(land, air and sea) and more.Not only that but you can choose any kind of resource to make any of the parts from, changing the stats of whatever for example a gun made from refined steel will probally do more damage than wood or normal steel.
So bottom line, if you are looking for a game that offers you the choice between complete freedom or more structured play style, do yourself a favor and pick this up.
p.s.- do yourself a favor and watch a youtube video and not the store page ones, they honestly downplay how great this game really is.

I cannot reccomend a game with a cancerous community. But I do reccomend a good game. This is a good game, not a good community.
With a HEAVY (and I mean 3.5 metric♥♥♥♥tons) focus on teamplay and cooperation. This game is golden for friends and players who ENJOY working together. Unlike most of the playerbase who rather exploit and try to solo this game to get loot. (They have fixed an exploit and over a week 50% of the playerbase droppped. Shows something) But instead of a long rant about this game heres a simple list of pros and cons since you prefer those better
Pros:
+(Personal Pro) Warhammer universe shown all in its glorious splender. Not a colorful bloody world but, dark dingy and +dank, with some colorful missions.
+Some well done (but still needs tweaking) melee combat (This is a melee focused game, Guns are more situational than a main weapon even for the Elf and her bow)
+Great atmosphere, Characters talk and bicker with one another, get to see some cool city scapes
+Enemies, most enemies vary and show off a distinct look like the Gutter Runner (Akin to L4D Hunter), Ogre (tank) +Packmaster, (Smoker/jockey), Poison Thrower (Spitter/smoker), and Ratling Gunner. And each one is equally deadly
+Lobby, now this was interesting to me but could still use more work. You start off inside a safehouse/inn working with other players to survive the Vermintide, more or so an interactive UI where you can choose your mission, customize and upgrade weapons.
Cons
-Toxic community, most of the games you will join it will be silent no one wants to chat with one another. From time to time you get a "GG", or "Halp me!" but apart from those no one likes to talk. People seem to be reluctant to help you and more inclined to insult you for going down. In fact the player base dropped from 25k to 11k after the devs fixed an exploit on a certain mission.
-Lootbags, idk what to call these players but this ties into the con above. The reason why players left was because the said fixed exploit gave players loot, whether it be good or bad.
-Difficulty, personally I like the difficulty. Hard is MEANT to be hard, Nightmare is well. A NIGHTMARE. Starting off at level 1-2 then trying to play on nightmare you are gonna have a bad time. The range of the Skaven are ridiculously long in melee, and most newbies dont know that you CAN dodge in this game. (hold down ASD and space and you will slide left right or back) But with a heavy focus on teamwork and noone working as a team. Players will have a bad time.
-Bugs there are still many bugs that were said to have been "fixed" Like when the orge attacks a downed player. That still happens or when the pack master grabbing someone from 2 stories up or through the floor.
Overall I CAN say this is a good game. But I cant reccomend it for people who play solo or matchmaking.

The storyline and voice acting are pretty good, and the concept of gameplay is sound. However, the tremendously unresponsive controls just end up being too frustating deal with. Things like, you can't hit zombies while they're standing up,  (you have to wait for them to finish their animation), taking a long time to swing backwards, etc.

Zombie scenarios don’t require much depth or story to be effective. But what they have needs to work coherently as a whole. Deadlight launches into its story without giving you much time to know the characters or invest in their situation. It tells a story that seems cobbled together out of loose ends, held together by irritating dialogue. Combined with often-frustrating platforming, this results in a game that isn’t terrible, but was a struggle to want to finish.
You play a character who sounds like a gritty film noir detective, constantly surprised to find himself in a zombie apocalypse. He’s prone to stating the obvious, like “The city isn’t a safe place anymore” as you run through a zombie-infested burning city, and, when zombies are clamouring outside the door, “I don’t think I’m alone.”
You will try to help some of the most annoying survivors of the disaster. One runs away each time you find him. “He’ll never make it alone,” your detective insists, even though he seems to be managing fine. The detective handled so badly in this chase section it seems like he’s puffing and wheezing after too many years at a desk job.
Another survivor wants to “help” you, by trapping you in his underground obstacle course of deadly traps, which he thought was a useful way to prepare for the zombie outbreak. He utters cryptic nothings like “There’s no time for questions, or answers.” But there’s time for his obstacle course? Like the detective, this section of the game doesn’t seem to know what genre it is in, and it ruins a lot of the effective atmosphere of the previous level.
Humans are the biggest threat, of course, which is why the military spend ammunition and fuel pursuing you, only turning their weaponry on the zombies when they stumble between the guns and your character. Logic is one of the first casualties of a zombie apocalypse, and their motive is never made clear. Fortunately, they are the kind of bad guys who announce their plans over loudspeakers, so you can stay one step ahead.
If Deadlight had followed Limbo’s lead and made the character mute and the story vague and implied, I could’ve enjoyed it more. Instead, the emotional payoff it aims for is meaningless if you don’t care about or believe in the characters. The story is too disjointed to pull you through some difficult platforming. It’s not a bad game technically, but for me the irritations outweighed the enjoyment.

One of the greatest Multiplayer experiences I have ever had. The singleplayer isn't that bad either! I've just been too hooked with M&B MP that I have given M&B SP zero time. I hear nothing but great things from my singleplaying friends though. If you buy this game, I recommend getting the Napoleonic Wars expansion. It's multiplayer only, but that is where I have had the most fun. There are several different game modes. The first is called Siege. In where a defending team must protect their castle from Enemy advancement until the timer has run out, however, keep your head well hidden from them Snipers. As defending team lives are limited to just five. Or less, depending on the time you joined the map. The attackers however, they have unlimited lives but in order to get to you, they must breach a hole in your wall with cannons and then storm the breach; which normally results in your bayonet stuck in their chests as you sing Rule Britannia; or mention the Kaiser if you're playing as Prussia/Austria.
The next gamemode in M&B MP is Battle. In Battle, both teams have just one life. And there is no respawning until the round is complete, so if you charge ahead early on and get mowed down by 6 Cavalry who have joined together and created a small posse, then you're going to be waiting 5-6 minutes for the round to end probably. That can be frustrating so I recommend teaming up with your teammates, rather than go lone wolf assasin style. The game also features TDM and DM gamemodes, I don't need to explain these. As they feature heavily in pretty much every game with a gun or sword and has multiplayer.
Overall, I recommend M&B to anybody if you're a fan of the era it's set in, and are war crazy. Or if you like the RPG and open world elements of the singleplayer. The game also has a VERY strong modding community. And you should try out some of the awesome mods. This was a fantastic experience.

I really liked Far Cry 3. For a while, I didn't think it would be better than Far Cry 2, which I thought was better than the first one. And I think some aspects of Far Cry 3 are better, specifically the crafting, the strongholds you can take over, and some of the characters. But what separates the two is the fact that this story centers on Jason Brody and his friends as he tries to save them, while Far Cry 2 is about accepting a job to assassinate someone whom you basically play cat and mouse with. And the cat and mouse aspect allured me in. While Jason Brody and his friends made the mistake of trusting someone who tricked them in to sky diving to Rook Islands, in terms of real life, the whole thing could have been avoided.
Still, the game has a strong story and strong character development for the protagonist. Jason Brody starts the game as an innocent (maybe not innocent, but not violent) 24 year old from California, and after he escapes from Vaas, a drug runner and slave trader, after watching his older brother get murdered, Brody ends up becoming a warrior of the Rakyat. The game plays like the first two Far Cry games in terms of the driving and shooting. But the mission layouts are different in that you take missions from a few different main characters that direct you to your friends as you try to rescue them. And as you eventually do, they take notice to the changes that Jason is going through. They can tell he's become a killer, but still human. Anyway, the game has a strong story and without going into details, it can be pretty surreal, especially when you meet Citra.
There are plenty of side missions that involve turning on radio towers that'll unlock more content on the map, hunting animals, killing specific people, random NPC story missions, poker games, races, basically Ubisoft made this into a big action adventure open world game while keeping it a solid first person shooter. It works well.

First of all, this game is amazing. It's a classic, and even though it is getting old now, it still holds up well.
HOWEVER: In my opinion, this game is awful on PC unless you have a gamepad (I'm using an Xbox 360 controller) and are willing to use some third party software like Xpadder to map the controller to the keyboard. This game really should have come with controller support, and it was obviously just laziness on the part of whoever ported the game to PC that it doesn't.
For instance, even in the in-game manual, the explanation of the controls has a picture of an Xbox 360 controller, telling you what buttons do what. There is absolutely no explanation of what the keyboard controls are, and I finally had to press random buttons until I discovered which buttons they'd made the equivalents of each Xbox 360 gamepad button.
Even after discovering what the keyboard buttons were, this game played horribly on a keyboard. I put this game away until recently, when I got a gamepad and was able to map the buttons correctly using Xpadder. Now the game feels comfortable and correct.
TL:DR - The keyboard controls are terrible. Only buy if you have a gamepad and are okay with using Xpadder or similar.

As fantastic as it was on the Dreamcast and GameCube. Although there are some flaws.
- Audio isn't bad, but sometimes the audio comes in too early or late. And sometimes it just outright cuts out (Ex: The police at the end of the cutscene after Sonic's first boss battle) There are also times where the speaking has little feeling or feels unnatural. I know it's a game about a super-fast blue hedgehog, but the audio could be a LITTLE better (even if is one of the first fully voiced Sonic games).
- The controls for the PC could be a bit better. I understand that you can map the controls; that's what I did. Still, the PC controls don't work as well for certain aspects. For example, although it isn't terrible, Sonic and Shadow's homing attacks are a bit hard to control. You have to have almost exact aiming with WASD keys (if that's what feels natural for you; otherwise, it's whatever keys you mapped moving to) to be able to hit the target you want. Also, I feel the movement of the mouse could've been utilized for Tails/Eggman missions for aiming their laser.
- While the Knuckles/Rouge missions aren't the worst levels in gaming, I'm going to be blunt: I hated them. They were too repetitive and annoying. I feel a better concept for these missions could've been created other than "the emeralds are lost, use your radar to track them down in the least time possible". Maybe they could use their respective punch/kick attacks to actually, you know, destroy enemies (which were actually kind of rare to find in these missions) and use their glide abilities to get to other platforms to reach the end of the level? Maybe not that, but something more engaging than a boring treasure hunt mission.
- Multiplayer being DLC. Need I say more? Crappy decision, Sega. Same goes for the PS3/360 versions.
Other than these, the game was great. Decent story, fun gameplay (most of the time), unique bosses, and AWESOME music.

Imagine a small, family-run restaurant tucked behind a butcher's shop on some little-known street in some no-name Italian village. Somehow, you come across it anyways as you travel through the countryside while backpacking through Europe, and decide to sit down and have a meal. What follows is the most ♥♥♥♥♥♥ic meal of your life.
Well, Vermintide is like that. Except, in place of a kindly Italian family serving you your meal, is a horde of giant, murderous rats hell-bent on splitting you open with a wide array of pointy objects. And, instead of meatballs and pasta, you feast on the blood of these creatures as you slaughter them in the thousands, each slice of your sword, blow of your hammer, or explosion of your fireballs more satisfying than the last. The sound their heads make as they pop open from an overhead blow, or their screams as they burn to a crisp, is only topped by the glorious sight of a head flying through the air, sliced clean off their body by your giant two-hander.
Vermintide is an adrenaline-fuelled bloodbath. Limbs, organs, blood spatter, you name it, it'll be flying across or onto your screen at one point or another. You'll undoubtedly have more than one heart-pounding ecounter through each level, and the suspense and tension is palpable throughout each map. Each weapon is fun and unique, with unparalleled visuals and sound effects. This game is a true work of art, and the effort and attention to detail the developers have put into it really shows.
Beyond the gore and amazing gameplay, the lore of the Warhammer universe brings the experience to a whole new level. The little tidbits of story and lore you pick up on via the banter between the heroes can be both hilarious and intriguing, and before you know it, you find yourself seeking out more of it on Google as you are sucked into the world that Fatshark has made come to life. The voice acting is exceptional, as is the sound design, music and overall "feel" of the game.
Do yourself a favor: buy this game. Buy this game and experience it, because it truly is something special.

At the time of writing I have about 30 hours clocked so I'm no veteran by any means, but I just wanted to write and say that anyone new to this game should strongly consider modding it from the start; I played about 5 hours of vanilla and found myself getting sucked in, but also wishing certain things were different and less frustrating (e.g. not having to wander the streets every time I wanted to speak to a guild master). To this end, the Floris mod stays faithful to the vanilla game's spirit and setting but makes really intelligent changes and tweaks. It is also compatible with Steam achievements. I normally advise people to play a game in its vanilla form for a while before modding, but in this instance it's a no-brainer. If you have a powerful machine, also consider the battle size extender mod. 500 vs 500 pitched battles are really epic!
Modding aside, this game has a massively steep learning curve but it is really addictive. It's brutally unforgiving at first, but hugely rewarding once you find your feet and understand it, particularly the unique combat mechanics. There's no rush quite like riding full tilt at the head of a cavalry wedge, smashing home into an enemy infantry formation and watching the bodies fly and the chaos ensue.

The game is a 2.5D action platformer with some shooting and light puzzle solving. The art style is the strongest thing about this whilst I feel the length, voice acting and story could have been much better.
I completed this within 3 hours. A lot of that time was replaying parts with cheap deaths (falling buildings, sizeable hordes) as some scenes need to do remember how you died to avoid it, only to die again at the next jump, it can be frustrating at time. My major gripe with the mechanics is if you're too close to a wall, you cannot walljump and this caused me to die more than I'd like to admit. Also, jumping on to something directly above you can be quite clunky as you need to be super precise. The melee weapon and shooting feels quite good though with plenty of weight behind hits. The voice acting is sub-par all over but the main character got on my nerves and made me cringe constantly, he just did not suit the part and a lot of his acting seemed forced.
If you're into 2.5D action platformers, you will probably enjoy this and for that reason I recommend it. If you're interested due to the theme alone, I would say avoid this unless the price is right (as of writing it is £9.99). I believe I got it in a bundle, so it was a good buy for me. I would not have bought it was full price.

Same siht as Audiosurf, except it's sidescroller now. And spaceship is replaced with a girl with headphones.
Here you have to guide the heroine through the track by mashing the buttons, a la parkour: evading some obstacles and crashing the others. But it's not as easy as it sounds.
This game is hard as balls. Forget about slow and pleasant rides on slow songs you could do in Audiosurf - you won't see it here. Even not the fastest song will be made into something really painful to play, unless your reaction time is top-notch. In other words, you have to possess some inhuman reflexes in order to make it to finish line. And the difficulty level you chose doesn't affect the gameplay speed - only the number of keys in use. Lowest difficulty - almost PRESS X TO WIN, highest difficiculty - get ready to perform keyboard solo. Good news though! You're not restricted with given difficulties and can set up your own. But after all, both length and difficulty ultimately depend on your musical tastes.
Mods! Lots and lots! Ingame color palette, heroine's haircut, her outfit - you can change everithing!  If you're not okay with default models or just want MOAR - welcome to workshop! 2B from Nier:Automata and Tohru the dragon are at your service!
Oh, almost forgot, you can use here gamepad too! But not all models are supported.
In the end I'd like to add it all looks darn gorgeous and totally impressive! The game is one big color show! Level background, hair, and sheakers - everything flashes and changes color. Even jetstreams emitted by sneakers do it! Yeah, right, when running is not enough, Melody takes off.
So, if you are really into:
Say no word! Here's all of it!
P.S.: How to add your music folder to favorites? Mark any track from that folder as favorite - the folder will be added automatically.

If you like tactical games, or even have a passing interested in strategy games, I highly recommend picking this one up. If you are like me and played and loved old school SWAT/Rainbow Six games, then you owe it to yourself to buy this right now.
Cons:
- A bit pricey compared to other indie games of similar (high) quality
- Some difficulty spikes: the progression of difficulty in both campaigns and separate maps could be smoother, though it never feels impossible
Pros:
- Great music
- Amazingly simple yet effective controls
- Overall wonderful atmosphere for such simple graphics
- Nice sense of progression (even with failed missions) with both individual team member and squad leveling without it entirely revolving around power gained from leveling up
- Lots of content, with multiple campaigns, individual maps with rankings, a random mission generator, a mission builder, and plenty more to download on steam workshop
Meh:
- Sound effects are merely ok
- Some odd bugs here and there that take you out of the experience, but aren't game-breaking
- Destructible environments would've been nice
TLDR: Well worth your time and effort as a strategy gamer.

EVERYTHING IM REVIEWING HERE IS MY PERSONAL OPINION.
So please stay open minded!
so as of recently gaining interest in the game once again, i decided to give it another shot!
and while the game is fantastic in certian areas it has flaws. some extreme that need addressed and some minior that you can make do with on whatever mode you are playing. first let me just get straight to the point on a issue that needs to be resolved as of now, and il go into the pro's and cons of the game :)
The game has moved from a 32bit version to 64bit only version (for now - 32bit will follow but with severly reduced features). the developers are extremely active on the discussions page on steam for the game, so if any questions or concerns with the game that need to be addressed you can post there knowing that a dev will reply in that very day you posted the thread.
for anyone interested in the game that has a somewhat mid range PC,
the game is still in beta and optimzation is still a high priority for the devs (judging by comments left on discussions) however.. if you are just slightly above the "Minimal System Requirements" chances are you wont get that great of a gaming experience.
the game is primarily GPU intesive and RAM instesive, IMHO the min specs need to be adjusted because a 460 wont even net you a stable 30FPS with the lowest settings (Fastest). im going to give a personal thought on what the min specs should be, just to serve as a guide line for for new purchasers and also to serve as what would be acceptable in terms of FPS!
Win 7/ 8 / 8.1/ 10 - 64bit
Quad Core - i5 2600k or better - 3.2GHz or better
8+ GB RAM
GTX 580 or better (dunno about AMD but look up the equivelent)
Version 10 / 11
Broadband Internet connection
10+ GB available space (SSD Recommend)
Must have OpenCL compatible CPU or GPU (DX10.1)
32bit can run, but will experience - Extremely bad frame rate / Slow load times for both 32/64bit (devs know about this issue and working on it) and the game has alot of crashes!
i say these should be the new min specs because a dual core just simply wont cut it when you get to a certian stage in the game that requires you to make a colony. as soon as you start filling your colony, Your FPS will plummit... HARD! people have said they play fine at 50-60 or even 80-90FPS but when they start filling their colony and hit max population. they say their game hangs around the 18-26FPS / 24-33FPS range!
now that the rambling is all done, onto the pro's and cons
- Fantastic Huge world to explore (in Single player)
- Adventure offers unbound freedom (Randomly generated worlds)
- Great World Editor
- Amazing creation system (build miscellaneous objects / funriture / guns / cars / planes / heli's / boats / shields etc)
- Great in world building
- Decent colony managment
- Good survival aspects
- Story line is meh (not that appealing)
- Voice acting could be better
- Some aspects not really that well explained
- Clunky camera positioning
- very bad mouse options (using anything that requires aiming like bows and guns etc has a crap ton of mouse acceleration, not options displayed in settings)
if your PC can handle the game, it serves as a very fun and entertaining game that allows people to build in some ways whatever they like.
7/10

One of the greatest Multiplayer experiences I have ever had. The singleplayer isn't that bad either! I've just been too hooked with M&B MP that I have given M&B SP zero time. I hear nothing but great things from my singleplaying friends though. If you buy this game, I recommend getting the Napoleonic Wars expansion. It's multiplayer only, but that is where I have had the most fun. There are several different game modes. The first is called Siege. In where a defending team must protect their castle from Enemy advancement until the timer has run out, however, keep your head well hidden from them Snipers. As defending team lives are limited to just five. Or less, depending on the time you joined the map. The attackers however, they have unlimited lives but in order to get to you, they must breach a hole in your wall with cannons and then storm the breach; which normally results in your bayonet stuck in their chests as you sing Rule Britannia; or mention the Kaiser if you're playing as Prussia/Austria.
The next gamemode in M&B MP is Battle. In Battle, both teams have just one life. And there is no respawning until the round is complete, so if you charge ahead early on and get mowed down by 6 Cavalry who have joined together and created a small posse, then you're going to be waiting 5-6 minutes for the round to end probably. That can be frustrating so I recommend teaming up with your teammates, rather than go lone wolf assasin style. The game also features TDM and DM gamemodes, I don't need to explain these. As they feature heavily in pretty much every game with a gun or sword and has multiplayer.
Overall, I recommend M&B to anybody if you're a fan of the era it's set in, and are war crazy. Or if you like the RPG and open world elements of the singleplayer. The game also has a VERY strong modding community. And you should try out some of the awesome mods. This was a fantastic experience.

Are you one of those players that spend hours and hours playing Company of Heroes and always wished you could play this as one of the squad members you where sending into battle?
Or, where you always looking for a bicycle simulator that not only allowed you to go cross country between enemy lines while having your buddy muttering behind you what a bad driver you are? Even being able to take out that evil enemy with the bike when your mood is seriously down the drain because of a stupid camper?
But, perhaps you love the WWII scenario, with the possibilities to become an ace tanker, sniper, decorated infantry guy that saved the day with his actions in the last minute.
If any of that applies to you then this game certainly is worth a test drive.
Lets get down to the essentials.
H&G is a FPS and also includes RTS. Ok, for those not into the elite geekology sprech, its a first person shoot combined with real time strategy.
Uhm, ok so that means... you can play classically as a fps and later in the game when you get into the higher rank buy your own units that you can place on the european war theatre, which then can be played in battles a an fps.
(If your still confused, just play it and you'll see)
The game is still in beta alot still is changing and added (like maps, units and skins) making it interesting over the long run. If you don't like changes and you always think the enemy is overpowered and all is biased this game might not be for you.
The developers have a weekly twitch stream in which they show you the future builds and things their working on, answer questions they gathered from the forums and also answer questions from the live chat.  Since they have a beer during the stream and this might offend you, as a milititant anti-alcoholic that you are, then this might be something to avoid. Also they give you insight on the developers side of the game and the making of the game making it interesting to watch.
So what are you in for?
1. 3 nationalities (at the moment) smashing their heads in to win the war over europe.
2. Any class to pick of such as a Tanker, Infantry (Anti tank, Rifleman, Shocktrooper), Recon (Sniper), Pilot or a Paratrooper.
3. Later in the game (or, if you chose to pay, right away) your own units depending on the classes you play.
You can have endless characters from each nation for no extra fees, giving you the possibility to play all whenever you want.
4. A constantly updated game with new maps and features (not a dead game where developers left you to pay as long as it lasts)
5. An active interaction with the developers in weekly Q&A giving you the possibility to offer your input and help build the game.
6. Different weather and day times changing the fight on the war map
7. Many different weapons to pick from and moddable.
8. Also a game where you can give one of the developer team a headshot because of the balancing issues you think the game has (most of them play the game)!
But (and here it comes), one problem the game does have is the updates do often carry server downs with them meaning you better have another game to play (or a r/l) in the meantime. It is in beta so that is something you have to "live" with.
I might add more about the game play itself and how avoid possible mishapes when you start as a new player.

is the tenth primary installment in the Call of Duty series and is the sixth game developed by Infinity Ward.
Would I recommend this game?
I cannot definitively say "yes" or "no", but rather "meh".
One of the most appaling things about this game is that Steam still charges around $40-$60 on this game in spite of its small community and the fact that it is more than 2 years old. Don't buy this game on Steam. Do what I did and purchase it off of a discount game website. I cannot post any links or names because Steam automatically censors them... Go figure. When I did buy Ghosts off of said un-named website, I got it for around $5.
Now for the actual review.
If you are looking for mindless fun (note the word
), then you probably wouldn't mind this game. The active community of this game is about the size of Modern Warfare 2's (approximately 700-800 people at certain times of day). It offers you the standard Call of Duty fare; run around, shoot things, get points, prestige, repeat. It offers a decent, semi-balanced selection of weapons/perks,  and slightly interesting killstreaks. The default maps aren't too bad, either.
But here's where we get to the bad part.
I could swear that Harry Houdini and Neo both had a hand with developing the game's netcode, because I have forgotten how many instances I've shot someone, only for the game to fail to register the bullets,
. Shoot someone with a shotgun at point blank range, chances are your shot may not even register, no matter how straight your shot or how true your aim. Never before in the Call of Duty games have I run into an issue this bad. While not necessarily Battlefield 4 post-launch disastrous, the occasional failure of the game to register your bullets does dampen the fun factor a bit. Also, it seems that its much easier to be put into a lobby where the people live in other continents, giving them higher ping, and giving you more frustration as the failure of a hit detection system fails even harder as they lag through your field of fire
style.
Do you enjoy spawning, only to find that you're staring down the barrel of an enemy's weapon, or get stabbed as soon as you start moving? Well, get ready for that to happen in this game a lot, too. The severity of this issue seems to vary map-to-map, but there are plenty of moments where this does happen, especially on the map Strikezone. Granted, previous Call of Duty games have had this issue (Rust with more than 6 players was a huge spawntrap), but none as recurring as this.
Do you like turning a corner only to be killed by something you could not see? Well, there's plenty of that in this game for you. The I.E.D. is an explosive device that the player can throw on the ground, and it can be hard to notice unless the enemy has SitRep equipped. When an enemy player gets too close to it, it beeps for about a second and a half, then explodes. Now, imagine an enemy team camping in one location with several of these devices planted in major entrances and hallways. Now imagine that you are the one that keeps tripping said devices. These rage-inducing explosive devices are the camper's first choice when it comes to defense.
Speaking of camping, I've noticed that although camping is all too-often a black sheep staple of certain FPS games, it seems to be more prevalent in
. Partially due to the ease of defending your own position that the I.E.D. offers, as well as certain other devices/killstreaks, campers can feel especially at home in this game.
Would I play this game seriously? Probably not. Again, it is a good game for some mindless fun, especially if you get some friends together in a lobby. However, I can't help but feel that this game is missing a certain amount of polish like the original Black Ops, or Modern Warfare 2 had. As a matter of fact, sometimes I can't help but shake the feeling that
isn't even completely finished.
All in all, its a good time-wasting game, and if you're looking for the typical, albeit slightly unfinished
experience, this game is for you.

Melody's Escape is probably the best music-generated game I have played. One, it reads all of my music files (unlike BeatHazard, Audiosurf, or Crypt of the Necrodancer that can't read those with complex characters). Second, their audio detection algorithm is literally magic. Like, wow. Smooth transitions, obstacles and orbs in sync with an ever changing beat which gives variety within a song, and adapting visual speed show just how magical and amazing their algorithm is. And third, I am not getting tired of it. The gameplay is simple, really; you press buttons for the corresponding orb/obstacle. Melody's Escape...
Boy what a game. In all honesty if my playtime has nothing to show for it, this game is very, VERY fun. I purchased this on February of this year. So far I am glad I did. This game is a simple rhythm-based side scrolling runner that requires you to input button presses to avoid tripping up, pun intended. It plays much like rhythm games like guitar hero or dance dance revolution, except you don't use your feet and uses wasd or directionals for input. Unlike guitar hero or dance dance revolution, this game can use ANY music audio file (wav, flac, mp3, wma, ogg, mp4 and so on), barring DRM protected formats. It will read the file and construct an obstacle course for Melody to run through based on the music you choose. The obstacle course is also not randomized; you will get the same obstacle course if you play the same audio file. However things might change if you use lossy file formats. I'll explain this later. Melody's Escape has 4 difficulty settings + a custom difficulty to change things up. This means the difficulty of this game varies wildly by the music you choose and the difficulty you set the game at. Finally Melody, the girl running through the obstacle courses, is customizeable. She comes with 4 or so presets you can use with various hair styles, or you can design your own skins and hairstyles if you so wish. For the otakus out there, that means you can have your favorite waifu run through the course of your favorite music. ;)
The biggest complain you will see coming from people playing this game is that this game will not sync up music well or the beat detection is off. Trust me that is not true. This game has one of the best beat detection algorithms of any steam game I've played. It's debatable that Audiosurf has better note detection, but in terms of beat detection, Melody's Escape is better hands down (I have tried them both). Anyways the thing about Melody's Escape is that it is very sensitive to audio quality; So sensitive in fact that It will pick up differences between a 248kbps mp3 and a 320 kbps mp3 file of the same audio. That's impressive considering the average human will not pick up these differences. Anyways this game is also not perfect. It will struggle with genres that have no apparent beat, have multiple changes in beat, or are just plain noisy. This is not to say the game will not try to produce an obstacle course, but it will probably be less accurate than the obstacle courses whos beats were successfully detected. That being said no procedural beat detection system is perfect and all struggle with certain genres regardless of how sophisticated the algorithms are. Even Audiosurf suffers from this.
Anyways to conclude, do I recommend Melody's Escape? Definitely yes. This game is very fun. If you enjoy rhythm games, this is a definite must play. If you enjoy games you can pick up for five minutes, this game is also recommended for you. If you're an otaku audiophile who loves rhythm games like me...what the hell are you waiting for?! Buy it now!...Else try it, see if you like and decide from there.  This game is only $10. However it is worth every penny. ;)

Gives the same feeling as L4D2. I would not call it a clone though, does some things differently.
-Melee Focus-
The melee combat is probably some of the best first person combat I have ever played. There is also the capacity to go full shooter if you would rather avoid such combat, as all characters have an assortment of ranged weapons, some of which you are capable of using as your primary. Importantly though being right in the thick of it created more tension for this than I felt in L4D2.
-Loot-
A fair loot system. I think some people might find it a bit too punishing, but I think its just about right. The loot system is such that it provides something for you if you want to dump a lot of time into this game, which I know people have done with L4D2. The ability to increase the rarity of drops by making the game harder for you is great. Also that if you die you get nothing, no matter how far through the level you are makes some of the latter parts of levels very tense. Finally the ability to take 5 crappy handguns and make a 1 good handgun makes it possible to get to tier loot simply with time.
-Maps-
Thought the variety of maps were good. From sunny farmsteads to dark city streats to underground rat holes. Some of the levels though did seem much more complex than others. One is simply a courtyard in which you defend some wells, while another is a phenomely well done wizards tower with Escher like rooms that were quick stunning.
WHAT IS MISSING
Well compared to L4D2 it is missing some things at launch, which there is only vague rumours about being added.
-Verses-
There is no Verses option. Wouldnt mind being able to control some Gutter Runners or Rate Ogres. It was a very fun mode in L4D2 which it is sad to see is not here. That being said if it was added it would d open up the capacity for loot drops for the Skaven which would be sweet.
-Mutations-
The mutations in L4D2 offered some fun twists on the game that kept it fresh. Would love to see some interesting mechanics abused in Vermintide.
Sadly though I think what I have enjoyed most about this game is its potential. The DLC I am imagining for this game would be great. So many avenues to go down, more characters, more items, more maps, more special skaven, more enemies.
[if you add the ability to switch out the skaven for undead/chaos/orc, it would make every map play different and really up the replayability. ALSO you could make loot tied to the enemies you killed.]
-Final thought-
If you liked L4D2 the worst thing this game could make you do is reinvigorate you into going back and playing more of that, and is that the worst thing? at a best you just found a new love.

Great game if you like to RP or just be a warlord or a trader. Not only does the game offer huge RPG elements but also it offers a huge veriety of roles for a player to choose. For exemple in Vanilla MB:warband you can trade between city:s and village:s while being a faction warlord or you could just be a huge trader and buy everything and have a own privet army. The trading system is based on demand and production aka things that are produced at one place can be sold for a higher price at another place.
There are alot of work spent on the trading system where you even can produce your own items such as silk,wool,hide etc. MB also has a political system built around reputation and honor,people with power are more easily sided with you if you are liked by them,if you have alot of honor by helping pesents etc. you have an eaiser time being liked by kings and lords that holds honor valued.
It also matters with background your character has and also what gender your character has to some extent. The combat system is built around a class and  faction system,each faction and its soldiers has an easier time against certain types of enemies, the veigers are very good with crossbows and has some good infantry core:s,while being at a disadvantage against Cavalry because they dont have a polearm core.
This all balances out nicely and creates a smooth and fun combat system. Character custumization is on the normal side with no massive amount of choices,you can choose some presets and then adjust their facial features and hair + name. There alot of replay value as there are alot of factions and a giant sandbox where alot happens. But if you want more there are always ALOT of functioning mods for this game,my personal choice being Floris mod for MB:Warband. Making it possible o fight as a normal soldier in a king:s or lord:s army,this is one feature of many including epanded troop tree:s and lots more.
Have fun,easily worht the buy.

Quite the short game, I finished it in around 4.5 hours.  The game has two unforgivable flaws that are related to each other:
1. This is a platformer with essentially running and singe hop wall jumps. The levels are handcrafted for specific jumping sequences, with very few instances having multiple paths . All those could be overlooked if the controls were tight, but unfortunately they are anything but. Thus, it takes away a lot of the fun and even causes frustration not due to difficulty but unresponsiveness.
2. This is related to the previous point. I guess the developers knew their game was short, so at the latest half of the game, especially chapter 3, there are some situations that require millisecond precision. This would be fine if not for the unreliable controls. The biggest sins are the first collapsing building sequence in chapter 3, where rolling sometimes registers as a crouch and sometimes you're too near the wall to jump. Furthermore, although early on essentially every screen or room has its own checkpoint, towards the ending scene which involves you helping a team member through some jumps while fighting off soldiers, there's only a couple of checkpoints, breaking the game's own convention. In that way, artificial difficulty is introduced in an effort to make the game a little bit longer, but most experienced players will see through it and almost anyone will get frustrated anyway.
Although I am a completionist, I didn't bother with this one. After reading a little bit online, I specifically stayed away from nightmare mode, since it would add very little to the experience and it would be an exercise in frustration with these controls.
The atmosphere was nice, although the story was overall generic and voice-acting was at best mediocre. I played with a controller and from my experience it is a must, since I expect keyboard controsl to be even more frustrating in a platformer. There are myriads of platformers out there, some much more difficult but with tight controls you can rely on, others with much more developed stories and a few gems that have both. So, my final recommendation is to get this either in a bundle, for free or deeply discounted (less than 1 euro or dollar).

I loved the first Hotline Miami, and was excited to get my hands on its sequel. I can say I was not at all disappointed.
This game is extremely unique; you won't ever play anything quite like it. It has great storytelling, entrancing visuals, graphic depictions of extreme gang violence, one of my favorite game soundtracks of all time, and is just dang fun to play.
I would like to say it was better than 1, and in many aspects it is, but 2 has a few flaws. In the first game, you could beat levels with either stealth or recklessness, but in this game I feel the level design at times only accommodated the latter. Also the levels are very open, and it is hard to see what is ahead of you. As a result, I certainly used a lot more guns, which I suppose isn't necessarily a bad thing, but I prefer melee. It's also worth mentioning that there are windows everywhere. And I mean FRICKIN' EVERYWHERE.
Despite all the aforementioned issues, Hotline Miami 2 is a spectacular game. It is well worth its price, and surpasses the first one in most aspects. Buy this game and get ready for the ride of your life.
