This recommendation comes with a warning: Buy this game during a sale for the best value for money. Otherwise, you may regret it.
Overall, Contagion is a great game and a great zombie experience, but there are issues that keep it from being REALLY worthwhile.
From atmosphere, to the weapons, to the level of intimate detail in everything from picking up keys, to stabbing a knife at head-height, to debating a "quiet manuevers" style vs "bury-the-trigger" style approach, the game feels serious, dire and your tasks feels important, and tasks are interesting enough to keep you playing for hours. But some things REALLY detract from the game experience: hit-detection and instruction.
Sometimes you'll be in close with a zombie - a sure hit - and you'll fire at the head, looking down the sights and... nothing? Seriously...? And now, the zombie is close enough to hit you - a game issue has cost you health, my friend, which would be a big deal in this game even if health packs WEREN'T few and far between. Other times you will hipfire several shots to the head, at near point-blank range... and ...nothing, again?! Spraying at a distance is sure to be inaccurate, and anyone who is familiar with first-person-shooters knows this, but at close range the idea of the bullets missing doesn't make sense.
Now, couple this with directions which are regularly unclear and you have a recipe for a frustrating game experience, spent running back and forth trying to figure out exactly where you need to be and, since gunshots attract zombies, you can quickly get overrun. If you are lucky enough to find a melee weapon and smart enough to pick it up, you can keep your kills quiet and save ammunition, but when several zombies move together, the only thing you CAN do is shoot, causing you to regularly call zombies to refill the areas you just cleared, as you move on.

In the main game mode, the phone you carry receives the messages that direct you from objective to objective. Now the phone is a novel idea, but when you get messages in tense situations, you are left with the knowledge that the objective has changed BUT you have no idea what you need to do next since pulling the phone up to find out could cost you dearly. In other game modes, the phone's display changes to a GPS map (something that might have been helpful in ALL game modes), but even then you have to struggle with lifting your phone and obscuring part of your vision in order to reorient yourself and find the character you have to escort to safety.
But even when you have the time and are given clear street addresses to look for, you will regularly have no choice but to wander madly about until you randomly find what you are looking for or are lucky enough to find a tourist street map, since streets are often not clearly marked. This can make the game interesting and tense, you are even more on edge than normal because this is no spray-and-run zombie game. You have to think and be tactical but in the end it causes problems.

When you are running from an endless horde (not an exaggeration, they just keep spawning depending on how close to the end of the map you are) and the phone says something like: "the truck's outside, let's get out of here!" The last thing you want to be doing is running out of every door the building has to offer, one after another, and combing the surrounding streets looking for your escape vehicle. Is it directly outside the building they told you to go to? Is it back by the CB radio? Have you experienced a glitch and you just can't see it? Is it clearly marked or is it some innocuous vehicle that you've maybe run past once or twice already? Are you aware that the horde is just growing and growing in your wake and if you have to go back the way you came, cause you didn't find what you were looking for, you will have to go through THEM?!
To be fair, overall the game is good, but when you are combing the walls and desks and tables for a small bundle of keys, in the dark, to the point where you have backtracked half-a-dozen times or more, you have a problem. If you can't progress in the game then it's not worth playing. And if you frequently find yourself in trouble because you have no real idea of what you are supposed to be doing, because the phone messages aren't clear, it's only going to cause frustation. The best suggestion I can give is to buy the game when it is on sale, that way if you take to the game, great! If you can get past these issues then you WILL enjoy it. It can be a great experience. What it gets right, it REALLY gets right. And, if you don't take to it, you will have lost very little since it was on sale.

I love these sorts of music games that creat levels based on your music. I can heartily recommend this game with a couple caveats. The game works really well with music that it can find the beat/tempo to. This works great for electronic music, or rock music that doesn't have much going on. Once you start using music that has a lot going on like metal or orchestral music, the algorithms start having some trouble find the beat as well. While still playable, songs where no beat/tempo is detected are not as fun to play. Another issue I have had is when I play on a controller, if the vibration setting is on, the game lags anytime there is vibration. With the vibration off, i have no frame dips or lag spikes at all. It's just a little weird. The vibration isn't necessary, so it is an easy fix.
Overall, though, if you like games like Audiosurf or Beat Hazard, you should give this game a go. You won't be disappointed.

Sonic Adventure 2 was the game that got me into Sonic. So when I found out it was on Steam I was excited. And it did not disappoint me. The game is an older game, so some things still persist like incomplete lip syncing in cutscenes or the music being louder than the dialogue at times. But there are subtitles to read if you can not fully hear the dialogue. There are added sound effects during the beginning of boss fights or when throwing switches, like in Crazy Gadget where there are far more sound effects for various panels than back in 2001. Now as a game itself, for me it plays well, even the hard mode is challenging but not unbeatable, the plot is the same of course but you will know pain, thy name Biolizard, and has replay value in the Chao Garden, Kart Racing, Boss Attack, and five modes per stage. And the unlockable if you get 180 emblems. Multiplayer is just as fun as before too with multiple modes and the almighty Grind Race. Curse you Metal Sonic. There are a variety of characters to play as, rather deep story, and multiple modes to play, something some in the fandom complain current games lack, making this game a plus. This game comes from an era where complaining was not as critical. So if you are looking to get into Sonic games, and want a somewhat straight forward but challenging game to play, this is definitely a game you'd need in your collection.

If you love the game and are tired of having to rebuy it on every friggin' console from here on out, buy this. Its HD, its Sonic, and its on the PC. Hell, theres a patch out that makes it so every stage is a Sonic stage; the way the game was supposed to be.

Quite the short game, I finished it in around 4.5 hours.  The game has two unforgivable flaws that are related to each other:
1. This is a platformer with essentially running and singe hop wall jumps. The levels are handcrafted for specific jumping sequences, with very few instances having multiple paths . All those could be overlooked if the controls were tight, but unfortunately they are anything but. Thus, it takes away a lot of the fun and even causes frustration not due to difficulty but unresponsiveness.
2. This is related to the previous point. I guess the developers knew their game was short, so at the latest half of the game, especially chapter 3, there are some situations that require millisecond precision. This would be fine if not for the unreliable controls. The biggest sins are the first collapsing building sequence in chapter 3, where rolling sometimes registers as a crouch and sometimes you're too near the wall to jump. Furthermore, although early on essentially every screen or room has its own checkpoint, towards the ending scene which involves you helping a team member through some jumps while fighting off soldiers, there's only a couple of checkpoints, breaking the game's own convention. In that way, artificial difficulty is introduced in an effort to make the game a little bit longer, but most experienced players will see through it and almost anyone will get frustrated anyway.
Although I am a completionist, I didn't bother with this one. After reading a little bit online, I specifically stayed away from nightmare mode, since it would add very little to the experience and it would be an exercise in frustration with these controls.
The atmosphere was nice, although the story was overall generic and voice-acting was at best mediocre. I played with a controller and from my experience it is a must, since I expect keyboard controsl to be even more frustrating in a platformer. There are myriads of platformers out there, some much more difficult but with tight controls you can rely on, others with much more developed stories and a few gems that have both. So, my final recommendation is to get this either in a bundle, for free or deeply discounted (less than 1 euro or dollar).

After playing this game for currently a little north of 30 hours  at the time of this review, I can definitely reccomend this game. Virtually all of my time has been spent playing with other people and utilizing bots as little as humanly possible. With that said as a lifelong Warhammer Fantasy & 40k fan this game is tailored to all my nerdy needs and wishes. I am incredibly baised towards Warhammer games but lets be honest....... Most Warhammer games are mediocre at best. Is this one different? Totally, not even in the same tier. The game is far from perfect, and many nagging issues and strange design choices remain but the devs seem incredibly involved and active in pleasing the playbase.
Pros:
*Decently Optimized, even on my 970 with everything on max/ultra I can pull around 90 fps anywhere but the level 'Gardens Of Morr' where the common rates flucuate from around 40-70fps.
*Fluid animations, combat is simple and generic. But incredibly satisfying thanks to good audio SFX
*Extreme class diversity, each class excels in a few areas and is terrible at others
*Amazing playbase / Team interaction, I know this is purely from my experiences but the community as of the moment is the polar opposite of toxic.
*Replayability, the combat is so intense you rarely focus on the levels itself and even playing the same levels over and over seems like a new experience many times over
Cons:
*Terrible loot system / Rewards. Even when collecting 3 tomes, 2 Grimores, a Loot Die, etc on Hard mode you will most likely get a Green weapon.
*Rewards upon death are virtually nil. Died after 35 minutes of intense fighting? Heres 50xp, only 40,000k more to the next level!
*Strange Matchmaking system, expect to see Found Game, Joining, Searching, Found Game, Joining, Searching, Cannot Find Game, Found Game    exactly in this order, usual wait times are only 1-2 minutes though.
*Broken 'Special' Skavens. Gutter Runners that teleport through walls and floors. Rat Ogres who are easily beaten but are basically damage sponges. Pack Masters who can move through walls and pull you through walls which are total game wrecking moments.
*Odd disconnects, this is a more seldom issue but I've had quite a handful of matches that have loaded me back into the starting Inn. No host has disconnected, no votekicked, nothing. Weird.
*No sidestepping dodge? You can dodge front and back but not side to side? Unearthly!
*Bots, almost absurd in how bad they react and play. It's a step backwards. Significantly worse than L4D2 bots.
All in all, as a biased Warhammer nerd who loves this game I'd rate it a 7/10. The game does feel a little on the Beta side still, but I'm happy with my purchase.

Call of Duty Ghosts é o meu primeiro jogo da série Call of Duty.
Enquanto a história Call of Duty Ghosts decorre numa cronologia alternativa e segue os eventos de uma destruição nuclear do Médio Oriente. As nações produtoras de petróleo da América do Sul criam Federation, como resposta à crise econômica global.
Em 2013, San Diego, na Califórnia é bombardeada por uma super arma norte americana Orbital Defense Initiative, após um ataque desencadeado por Federation, resultando naquilo que ficou conhecido como "O Evento". Dez anos depois, em 2023, a Federation emerge como a superpotência dominante e invade os Estados Unidos.
Assim nasce Ghosts nas cinzas do inimigo.
Multiplayer esta repleto de ação, tens vários mapas e extensos modos de jogo, mapas são enormes aonde permite fazer uma pausa para criar as tuas armadilhas para surpreenderes o próximo inimigo. Modo Extinction aonde o objetivo é destruir uma espécie letal de Aliens que invadiram o planeta, no que começa por ser uma ameaça desconhecida. Neste modo Extinction temos um universo fantástico para explorar.
Call of Duty Ghosts tem boa jogabilidade é fluida, os gráficos são razoáveis, banda sonora e cutscenes excelente. Infelizmente existem pontos negativos o jogo acaba por ser pesado, não existe justificação para tal.Nota-se que ao longo da série Call of Duty não existem grande evolução que acaba por ser um dos aspetos negativos na série.
Recomendo sem dúvida.

Like Watership Down and Animal Farm before it, Sonic Adventure 2 employs the use of human-like animals as a means of analysing and critiquing our societal structures within a kind of allegorical microcosm.
The dark horrors reflected back at us in this metaphorical mirror are enough to sicken even the most hardy of folk! Take, for instance, the lyrics of the butt-rock tune players first hear at the start of the game - within just four lines of prose, the hyper goal-driven, ADHD nature of modern life is deconstructed and damned, the fear of the great unknown is recognised and embraced, and reference is even made to the importance of furthering and developing LGBTQ rights.

I got this game during Alpha near the release date. There were a lot of bugs and the game was limited, but I held onto it because it looked like it had a lot of potential.
This latest update to Beta was actually pretty good.  I have only played some of the singleplayer so far and it's already leaps and bounds above what it was in alpha.  It feels very much like an RPG mixed with minecraft but with better graphics.
Pros:
- Making vehicles and houses is a challenge in itself, as the building function is very detailed.  You can make anything from the millenium falcon to a motorcycle.  It also has a modular building feature which is similar to minecraft.
- Visuals look nice, plant life looks un-earthly but still appealing.
- From what I remember in alpha, there will be large bosses that you can only really fight using really god vehicles, and they bosses looked very cool.
- Going through the singleplayer will teach almost everything you need to know in the game, so multiplayer will be a breeze.
Cons:

Door Kickers. Tactical, top down simulation game in which you are in full control of a highly trained SWAT team. Oh yeah, it's brilliant.
The objectives are usually very straight-forward: eliminate all hostiles (or tangos, as they call them), save the captives and/or apprehend the suspects(s). However, every level offers a new location, with unpredictable enemy spawns and new tactics to be developed. Over time and the completion of missions four new classes will be unlocked: Pointman (the starter  class), Assualter (essentially a Pointman with an assualt rifle), Shield (carries a tactical shield which takes most damage), Breacher (shotgun wielding units for close quarters combat and making dramatic entrances) and Stealth (probably the most dynamic, effective classes, although more difficult to design practical tactics for). Stars earned in finishing levels quickly and with minimal casualties can be spent on new weapons and tools.
The main thing to know is the freedom that this game offers. There are so many ways to fulfil objectives that it is unlikely that in a group of 100 people (maybe even more), one person will use the same tactics and methods of completing the mission. You can choose what units you use, where to put them, where to move them from there, how to enter a building, when to enter a building, and many more.
There are, however, a few cons to this game. For instance, it is very common for the game to quit responding while launching for the first time in a while. After quiting and relaunching all is normally resolved, though it is worth mentioning. Also, unit control occasionally will act up, allowing me to only control one officer at once. A simple quit of the level will normally fix the issue though. I am fully aware of how unimportant these are, and in turn will note these are not significant enough to be a reason to not purchase the game.
All in all, Door Kickers is a marvelous example of how games of the genre should be, and deserves more attention. I would give it 9/10. Well done, Killhouse.

Mount & Blade: Warband is what I wish Wars of the Roses, Viking Age, and Chivalry might grow into someday.
I keep waiting for a newer game that even comes close to M&B:Warband, but nothing comes close.
This one has it all, weapons physics (attacks actually do different damage based on direction of swing and your velocity relative to the target), RPG-style skill improvement, a colorful cast of NPCs, an (admittedly rudimentary) trade economy, an interesting setting with multiple factions, diverse troop-types, and a completely open-ended sandbox world. Do you want to earn glory and lands serving a noble liege? Become kingmaker in a bloody civil war? Declare your own claim to the throne and conquer the world? Just ride around plundering caravans? All of the above are possible.
The only downsides are the graphics (not bad when the game came out but a bit dated now), the rather weak AI (pitched battles tend to have the tactical depth of a soccer game with 5-year-old kids where everyone converges on the same point and starts hitting each other), and a repetitive late-game (the early game is very fun and interesting, the late game is still challenging but you end up fighting a plethora of siege battles on the same castle map again and again).

I haven't found a wargame more enjoyable than this. Mount and Blade trully delivers in epic battles.

One-line review: Highly recommended. Planet Explorers is a remarkably good game, once you've learned the controls and UI.
More in-depth version:
I bought this game ages ago, and it's come a long way since I first tried it. The more I play the current version of Planet Explorers with my friends, the more impressed I am. It just clicks with me, in a way ARK did not for many reasons.
Here's a real story from last night's gaming session with my friend Bandito. He and I went to the beach in search of petroleum (I have to say, that scanner tool is AWESOME). Finding some about 100 feet from the surfline, we started digging. I wasn't sure how the game would handle a hole in the sand, so close to the ocean; my best guess is I'd hit the water surface when I dug down to sea level, or maybe no water at all. As it turned out, we dug below the waterline without a problem, and after a few minutes we had joined our two tunnels and met back up, underground. A few minutes later, Bandito said, "Oh no, water incoming!" He'd dug too close to the actual shore and now seawater was filling our mine at a rather troubling rate. I frantically dug myself an exit and barely avoided drowning underground. When we were both safe, the entire excavation was filled to sealevel with water. It's impressive that the game actually modeled fluid water voxels filling up a cavity once it was connected to the ocean.
There are so many things I like about this game.
The world feels vast. You can see for miles, and somehow the distances feel more impressive than they do in ARK. While ARK is graphically amazing, it also gave me a curious feeling of confinement which I didn't realize until I played PE.
The game is suffused with a sense of discovery and strangeness. I really feel as if I'm exploring an exotic alien world.
There's an actual story to the game, and it's interesting.
The crafting system (indeed the whole UI) is remarkably good, far better (in my opinion) than ARK's. For example, your replicator shows the items needed to make a thing right on the creation panel, and you can click directly on the sub-ingredents and go to their own production screen. Thus if you are lacking a sub-sub-sub-ingredient it takes only three simple clicks to drill down to the thing you need. It's astonishingly well designed and should be the gold standard for any game that does crafting.
The Inventory is similarly well-handled, with subtabs for the various types of stuff. They also include a "Reorder Items" button that does an awesome job of tidying up your inventory and putting things in an order that makes sense. One-click magic!
I haven't dived into the voxel-based builder yet, but the tutorial videos I've seen are amazing. You can make weapons, vehicles, all sorts of things.
Planet Explorers has just the exact proportion of danger/sightseeing I like, whereas ARK was far too brutal for my taste. I can roam much more freely in PE, and mostly avoid (or successfully flee from) the really dangerous predators. Mishaps do occur, but they feel fair rather than punishing.
The game handles co-op story quests better than any other game I've played. If one player takes a quest, all of them have it. Everyone gets the rewards, too. And if one player does quests alone on the server, while others are offline, her companions will have the rewards also when they log on. It just feels right, and works perfectly.
If you want to host a game, you need to set up port forwarding on your router for UDP ports 9900-9915. But that's not necessary to just join a game. My friends and I have been very impressed with the smoothness of connection, and only occasionally saw rubberbanding...but then we're playing in Canada, the US, and Chile. Quite a lot of internet between all of us!
Because this game is still in Beta, the game has some unfinished animations and outright bugs, but they're not too bad and Pathea has a good track record of fixing those that crop up.
My least favorite thing about the game is the horrible music which plays at the multiplayer server screen. It's pretty enough the first time you hear it, but it can't be shut off and loops endlessly. It's also far too loud, I can't even hear my friends over Teamspeak while it plays. Please, please, Pathea, give me at least a volume control for that music.

I've had PE for quite a while, since about two years ago. It was not very polished then, it had a fair clout of content but it was clearly very early. Years fly by and the game seems to be in development hell. Fortunately for this indie gem, it clawed it's way back thanks to a remarkably dedicated dev team, so kudos to them for that. The game itself has improved in leaps and bounds, since the long awaited v 0.14, to the current 0.4, to become much the same game but so much more polished and rounded. Truly, it has been improved to the point of becoming a good game in its own right, which sets it apart from the rest of the herd (The title screen song is a real masterstroke showing the effort and attention of the devs, again, kudos). Not only becoming a good game but really becoming fun.
With a fair bit more polish, optimization, content and general improvements, this game really shows a lot of promise, rocketing past it's slow period. The real only things that let it down are twofold:
One downside I can complain about (and complain I most certainly will) is the camera control. Make no mistake, things are definitely getting better, but it's still definitely a pain having to switch control methods just to talk to a character, or having to hold tab to use a cursor. This is the main irritation most of the time, which slows the pace down to a crawl unnecessarily, especially when coupled with infuriatingly limiting keybinds! (TAB REBINDABLE FOR INVENTORY PLEASE!!)
The second thing I would like to quibble about is the blizzard of menus and interfaces that all do different things, with different modes of access. At least now they are all in one list but I feel a lot more work needs to be done on the GUI usability before the game will flow appropriately. While gorgeous to look at, the user interface being all over the place is becoming somewhat archaic, especially when compared to more polished/larger budget titles which, if possible, would definitely make interfaces much more enjoyable to use. (Perhaps something more like a single master interface, with tabs for inventory, character, replication, map, etc.)
TLDR:
This game is FANTASTIC, in so many regards, having crawled out of a period of inactivity to rise to become magnificent. If you can get past the maddening difficult-to-use blizzard of GUI, and the camera controls from the black lagoon, there is a simply stunning game there, and it is meteorically improving.

Amazing game, and without a doubt, one of my all-time favorites.  A loot-shooter with TONS of things to do, and a huge island to explore.  I probably did 2 or 3 playthroughs on console, and after recently building a new gaming PC, I decided I wanted to raise hell on Rook Island once more.
My only knock (and a big one) on the PC version of this game is that it crashes without warning CONSTANTLY, and I have no idea why just yet.  When the game was released, Windows 10 was obviously not in existence yet so there is some sort of issue having to do with the operating system.  I've researced some boards in an effort to troubleshoot, and from what I can gather there is something with Windows 10 that isn't playing nicely with FC3.  The problem is that people have suggested about 100 different ways to pinpoint and ultimately fix the issue.  Whatever the reason, it's pretty frustrating and I don't feel like spending hours troubleshooting this when I could spend what little spare time I have to play something else.  As great as this game is and as much as I love it, I'm kind of regretting the purchase and thinking of abandoning it altogether.
If you choose to purchase the game, I'd recommend looking into these issues first to spare yourself a TON of frustration and wasted time.  I've lost track how many times I've completed a mission or liberated an outpost only to have the game crash immediatley afterwards without saving my progress.  Unless you know for certain you can pinpoint and resolve whatever is causing the game to crash, I'd probably recommend that you pass on this game for PC.  If you have a legacy console (PS3 or XB360) you'd be much better off playing it on one of those.  I've been hoping that this game would be made backward compatible for XB1, but sadly that hasn't happened yet.

Hotline Miami 2 takes a big step from the original with larger scale of level, characters, and storyline.
The gameplay is a biggest change compared to the original. It’s bigger, longer, and full of enemies to beat. The change of level and gameplay offer you harder challenge to play smart and prepare for each section. However, the larger level design and loads of armed enemies lead up to some frustrations such as off-screen killed and inconsistent field of view of enemies. The mirror and big guy also force you to hold gun all the time. These factors make most character execution and melee weapon feel less potential compare to the first game. The game forces you to learn mistake from each level and the design tends to break the flow of gameplay which is the fun core of the first game.
The story has quite good script and narrative. It fulfills some questions from previous game, but also leaves theories for fans to discuss. Even, some characters feel unpolished for the story and it’s quite awkward to end the series in that way.

Hotline Miami 2 is still a fun game, gorgeous and memorable soundtracks, and very satisfied massacre. If you’re looking for tougher challenge from first game, Hotline Miami 2 is your best choice. But if you’re looking for more fun-flow gameplay, I recommend you to stick with first game.

Mount & Blade: Warband is what I wish Wars of the Roses, Viking Age, and Chivalry might grow into someday.
I keep waiting for a newer game that even comes close to M&B:Warband, but nothing comes close.
This one has it all, weapons physics (attacks actually do different damage based on direction of swing and your velocity relative to the target), RPG-style skill improvement, a colorful cast of NPCs, an (admittedly rudimentary) trade economy, an interesting setting with multiple factions, diverse troop-types, and a completely open-ended sandbox world. Do you want to earn glory and lands serving a noble liege? Become kingmaker in a bloody civil war? Declare your own claim to the throne and conquer the world? Just ride around plundering caravans? All of the above are possible.
The only downsides are the graphics (not bad when the game came out but a bit dated now), the rather weak AI (pitched battles tend to have the tactical depth of a soccer game with 5-year-old kids where everyone converges on the same point and starts hitting each other), and a repetitive late-game (the early game is very fun and interesting, the late game is still challenging but you end up fighting a plethora of siege battles on the same castle map again and again).

Sonic Adventure 2 is one of my favorite Sonic games up to date. It was first released fot the Dreamcast on the 1st June 2001. Since then it has been a fans favorite.
Pros:
- Overall nice plot
- Long playtime
- Chao garden
- Smooth controlls
- Great soundtrack
- New likeable characters
Cons:
- Side character stages are only average
- Clunky camera
- Not well ageing graphics
- No online multiplayer or chao trade
Story:
This game takes place after Sonic Adventure. Eggman releases the ultimate lifeform "Shadow" to help him steal all the seven Chaos Emeralds. Of course it is up to Sonic and his friends again to stop Eggman and save the world.
The story is seperated into the "Hero" and "Dark" side.
In this game Shadow the Hedgehog and Rouge the Bat were first introduced. In each one of these you will play three diffrent characters who each have their own little story that ties into the overal plot of the game.
Playstyles:
Unlike in Sonic Adventure, SA2 does not have a world hub but a world map where you can choose which stage you want to play next or revisit.
All 6 characters are split into three diffrent play styles.
Speed stages are avaiable for Sonic and Shadow, Shoot 'em up stages for Tails and Eggman and the Treasure Hunt stages for Knuckles and Rouge. After each stage you complete you get rewarded with an rank and the rings you collected in the level.
For me the best stages are the speed stages. Sonic and Shadow feel very natural while playing and they are nicely designed with great music and a very fast pace. Then there are the Shoot 'em up ones wich I don't like as much. They break the fast pace of the game similar to the Werehog in Unleashed.
I do like the Treasure Hunting stages. They are huge and I spend a long time exploring all of them. Also these stages have some of my favorite songs.
Only problem with the Treasure Hunting is that they changed the radar system from SA and you can only search one shard of the Chaos Emerald. It's pretty frustrating to back track through whole levels to get all three of them and sometimes levels can take ages since some of them are huge and they tale ages to get an A-Rank. (*sigh* Meteor Herd)
Also you have the Chao Garden and the racing minigames.
Controls:
I would reccomend playing with a controller.
I would say that SA2 has the best controls of every 3D Sonic game right now.
The camera can be a bit clunky but overall okay and even if you play the speed sections you never feel like you are not in control of Sonic or Shadow.
The controls for the Shoot 'em up and Treasure Hunting sections are are very diffrent. Of course you have to walk around but you will have much more jumping and hovering and many enemys you have to clear out of the way.
Treasure Hunting doesn't have a linear design. You can fly around and explore and dig for treasures and the missing shards of the Chaos Emerald. You have a radar to help you locate all pieces hidden in the level and tips you can get from various flying TV's all around the level.
Sound:
The voice acting is average but the music is one of the best Sonic soundtracks.
Each song fits it's level perfectly. There is a huge variety in genres too. Knuckles has many Rap songs where as Rouge has soft RnB like songs. Sonic, Tales and Eggman got rock songs while Shadow has some a bit darker rock songs with electronic influences.
Chao Garden:
One of my favorite parts of the game is the Chao Garden. Here you can raise little creatures called the Chaos. Each level you will play will have little animals running around or hidden somewhere. You can collect these and give them to your chao o alter their appearance and increase thir stats. Also enemys drop "drives" which also increase Chaos attributes.
Chaos can also compete in mini games such as Chao Racing and Chao Karate.
I spend hours into leveling and breeding them and raising them and mastering all mini games.
Multiplayer:
The multiplayer in Sonic Adventure 2 has been always one of my favorites.
You can play almost all the levels of the main game together with a friend. Some are shorter than the ingame one but there are many that are full lenght. You can play the speed stages as well as the treausre hunting and shoot ' em up as well as the car racing minigames.
Also you can trade Chaos or let them compete against each other in a race or karate.
Sadly this is not online on the PC version. You have to have a friend next to you to play the multiplayer. Sadly it's a missed opportunity.

Door Kickers is the best top down tactical simulator in the world in my opinion, and I have played a lot of top down simulators. Door Kickers has very rich components, from its music to its tactics. The music is extremely atmospheric, making it feel like Payday 2, except you're the tactical advisor. The tactics are extremely rich, giving you so much space to establish the best path and tactic to get the mission done. And you have a lot of customization for the SWAT Officers on your team, whether he/she would be a pointman or breacher, wielding a shotgun or rifle.
The client is also very smooth and slick, allowing for uninterrupted and smooth gameplay. And with randomly generated doors to kickdown, the game is endless and can be educational. Making sure your officers never forget to check their corners and always stop before entering a room when your fellow officer hasn't caught up with you. This is a very realistic tactical simulator and is an essential game to stratagy lovers.

A great Pausable Real Time Squad Based Tactics game! From a top down view, you click and drag your SWAT Team members, drawing a path for them to follow, in which they'll shoot anyone they see, though later on you can tell them to hold their fire. You can have them breach doors through a variety of ways, such as lock picks, kicking, big hammer, small hammer, and bolt cutters for padlocked gates.
There's a large selection of guns, ranging from pistols, Shotgun, SMG's, and Rifle. I especially like the P90 POW when raiding houses, and the M4 for more open maps, since the M4's Accuracy and Stopping Power is maxed out, or very close to it. The tradeoff is that they have
low maneuverability.

What "SWAT 2" should have been, and what we all longed for it to be. A top-down/isometric strategic version of "SWAT", not the RPG/Action-based first game, but the squad-based TPS/FPS versions that followed. Unfortunately, "SWAT 2" was a critical and popular failure. Still, the promise of it kept many of us coming back to it, despite it's inherant design flaws, and managing SWAT vehicles was always fun.
Fresh from the fields of "Breach & Clear", a top-down & isometric military CQB mobile port (clear and away better than most AAA titles) I'm pleasanlty surpsied this takes that concept, though admittedly without trying to, and brings it to the real time confines of SWAT CQB situations.
Placed squarley between the simplistic, but involving "Breach & Clear"and the sophistication and complexity of (some might say, overly difficult) "Frozen Synapse", "Door Kickers" is "SWAT 2 - Re-Imagained" (without the vehicles, of course).
As "Breach & Clear 2" is going to ramp up the looks and gameplay for it's PC base, built upon it's on it's sales so far (taking it to preactically AAA standards), I have high, very high hopes that "Door Kickers 2" will finally be the ultimate "SWAT" tactical game we strategy nuts have always wanted.
Unitl then. I have Tangos to take down, hsotages to rescue, and sitruations to control without being remonstrated by Samuel S. Jackson. Many, many challenges yet to face with my team of gungho "Cold Zero" sharpshooters.
Honestly: 8.5/10, even though my time-in-game does not reflect just how enamoured I am with this gem.

Game needs some serious tweaking before full release.
Physics for jumping is a bit off, fall is quite slow.  You can't fire while you're in mid air, but if you step off a rock you're pretty much floating for a half second and unable to defend yourself.
You can only play with friends in a squad if they all have the same soldier type as you.  You want to be a pilot and your buddy a tanker?  Nope, can't play together.
Finding and  adding friends needs some work.
Cannot change equipment loadout while in a match.  You have to quit the match, change loadout, then rejoin.
Advanced war has long queue times, even during "peak hours".
German armor is underpowered in staged battle, versus Soviets and US.
Game has good concept, with the RTS portion, but from some posts on the forum, it seems fewer and fewer people are actually playing the RTS portion, because of the Assault Teams being attacked while the player who owns them is offline, low level and new players wasting the resources of the assault team, among other things.
Many of the newer players don't understand that vehicles are a limited resource in advanced war, and they cost the CO who is deploying them funds everytime they get destroyed.
Large disconnect between new players and veteran players.
Gameplay also tends to lean more towards arcade; think CoD or MW.
TL;DR  Cool game, but enough issues that it's a novelty and not worth dedicating tremendous hours in.

Sonic Adventure 2 is fun. Very fun. But not perfect. The story is meh with really only one thing that bothered me. Sonic pulling off chaos control for the first time. Don't know why, but sure. The speed levels are by far the best in my opinion with their nice rock music and fun level design. They have the occasional puzzle thrown in there to stop you for a second, but it's mainly just speed. Oh and Sonic's in that, so automatic win. The mech shooters are kinda boring and control like a tank. You also have a health bar instead of rings, but rings help fill up the bar. You can lock on to multiple targets and shoot a ton of missles everywhere too. These are alright, but get repetetive. The treasure hunting stages are by far, my least favorite. I don't hate then, but I don't like them either (except for Rouge's security hall which can go screw itself). You're collecting three emeralds in a stage and that's it. The big problem here is how big the levels are. Especially the later space levels. You also have a radar that tells you close you are to the next emerald (gray is nowhere near, green is in the area, yellow is closer, red is very close, and the exclamation mark means you're within 2 feet of it). The problem with this is it only tells you the next emerald it wants you to find. So you could walk right by an emerald and not know because that's not the one it wanted you to find. Security Hall also has a time limit of 5 minutes to collect the emeralds. This level's fairly small, but that time limit is pressuring. The Chao Garden. I love this place. You start out with two eggs and hatch them with 3 methods. Throwing it, shaking it, and just letting it hatch. You get a hero or dark chao by raising it with one of the respective characters or beating it up with the opposite ones, but why would you wanna do that? :c After getting a hero or dark chao, you obtain the hero and dark gardens respectively. You also have a daycare where they can learn different things such as drawing, singing, playing an intrument, etc. A doctor who can tell you what your chaos' weaknesses and strengths are, what they like to eat, and other info. The principal gives you some tips on how to raise your chao and there's a black market where you can buy fruit, seeds, and other goodies for your chao. There's also a fortune teller who can name your chao or (by decling all her names) you can name it yourself! There's chao racing and chao karate is you got the DLC. I could go into even more detail, but that'd take way too long (possible guide?). There are also 2P battles you can have! Races, mech fights, and race to emeralds are all things you can do! Locally. Unless you got a certain mod. *cough*
*cough* All in all this game is great, but the chao garden and speed levels are all I 100% enjoyed. If you're getting into Sonic, pick it up. I'm sure you'll like it. Not into Sonic? Get a demo, then see what ya think. Diehard fan? How have you not played it once? For real though. I love dis game. c:

What I can say is that Deadlight is a beautifully presented platformer experience that tells a good (albeit cliche) story that starts off strong and ends too abruptly.  The game moves at a very brisk pace that wraps itself up perhaps a bit too early for my taste, though with the essential questions more or less wrapped up.  The story had a very comic book way of presenting itself, often doing its exposition through hand-drawn stills and primitive motion-graphic animations.
This is a quintessential "Snow Day Game" for me: fun gameplay, interesting characters and story, and finishes in mere hours (I went from start to finish in a single five hour play through, and the only reason it reached that long is because the controls regularly hampered me).
One thing I will say is that if you play this game, for the love of God, DO NOT USE THE KEYBOARD CONTROLS! Whomever mapped them must have been able to dislocate their fingers on command for all the sense used in mapping the controls.  In my first playthrough, I got about half-way through the game until I found a section nearly impossible to complete with keyboard controls.  At the advice of my girlfriend, I switched to a controller and got through the challenging portion in a single pass.

Deadlight is a 2.5D side-scrolling action-platformer survival horror zombie game.
You and some fellow survivors have been searching for a place called “Safe Point” and also for your wife and daughter who went missing in the past. As Randall Wayne, you have at your disposal the standard free-running mechanics of running, jumping, wall-jumping, rolling, and climbing, all of which help you traverse post-apocalyptic Seattle.
While doing so, you will come across zombie hordes that have infested it, and so you will need to fight them with weapons like axe, revolver or shotgun.
Artistic design of the game consists of beautiful yet post-apocaliptic sceneries; abandoned traffic jams, rain-specked neon motel signs, dark fire escapes - never has a 2.5D world felt so believable.
Deadlight's best moments are its intense chases: be that a gauntlet run through a street that's crowded with zombies, or a game of hide-and-seek with a military helicopter in deserted office blocks.
Overall rating: Highly recommended
Similar games: Prince of Persia, Another World and Flashback.

I am not sure what all the bad reviews are about.  I will review the game, not the attitude of the developer.  Developers have lives and sometimes don't get around to doing everything on time.  How would you feel if you spend all of your time developing a game and then all you get in return is complaining and nasty reactions by entitled children who don't have the ability to make games themselves?  You would get pretty upset pretty quickly, and thats a fact (four years of customer service taught me that).  Besides, its under new management now.
Anyway, I bought Contagion while it was still in Alpha and I have always had a great experience with it.  Multiplayer escape maps can be challenging, as good communication amongst your squad members is a definite necessity.  This is also the case for extraction, but less so as there are far fewer goals to achieve other than rescuing survivors.  The hunted maps are a lot of fun on full servers, and the enjoyment almost increases with fewer players as it becomes a game of cat and mouse.
I have had hours of fun on LAN or over skype calls with my friends and have never regretted buying this game.  Sure, there are a few bugs occasionally, the hitboxes can be a bit sketchy sometimes, but that comes with the territory of designing a game that relies on headshots for kills (i.e. its not easy).  Its a good buy full price but a real steal on sale.  I am looking forward to the continued updates.

I hate the RNG but I love the game.
The combat system feels great. Every blow you land feels like you're hitting something. It's very satisfying to grab a great hammer and pop rat heads or slice through a horde of vermin.
The different classes/characters are great, but some do tend to feel samey. The dwarf and imperial soldier tend to be a bit similar, etc. But each class feels different enough to be interesting with the bright wizard probably being the most unique.
There are also more powerful items you can strive for, but they're accessed through an ofen-times frustrating RNG. You roll dice and your odds of success are determined by how many bonus dice you find and at what difficulty you completed the stage at. Sometimes it's a let down to finish an epic run only to have all of your rolls fail. Also, if you favor a certain character don't plan on getting a lot of gear for them without a bit of a grind. There's an item combination system that helps alleviate that, but unless you have a lot of similar items you're at the mercy of the RNG.
The loot system is even more brutal considering if you fail a level at any point, you get nothing but XP.
Despite the RNG the game is insanely fun, especially with friends. It takes the Left 4 Dead formula and greatly improves on it. The "special" rat variants have similarities to, but are often more interesting than the special infected in Left 4 Dead.
This game is definitely my sleeper hit of 2015.

5/10  (+3) if you have a regular premade group to play with  (-3) if you mostly want a viable single player game
This is a solid, and sometimes enjoyable, four person first person coop game.   However, the limited amount of content, repetetive gameplay, heavy reliance on randomness to drive (slow)progression, and unforgiving game play may be (very)off putting to some.
===PROS/CONS/CONCLUSION===
==PROS==
+L4D CooP alike in many ways
+There are five different characters, with 3 that play differently and 2 that play similiarly to each other.
+Itemization with Progression (mostly through items)
+Well realized grim-dark Warhammer atmosphere
+Well done weapons and animiations give the combat a visceral appeal.   The visceral combat where you slay hordes of Skaven can be especially apealing.
==CONS==
-It is very easy to fail & a failure nets next to nothing as far as progression goes (no loot,  very low experience)
-A failed missions resets you to the very start of long missions.  There are no safe houses as restart points like l4d2.
-If the host crashes/disconnects mid-mission, you lose all progress.  No dedicated servers (yet).
-Rewards are completely random.  The RNG for loot after a mission often results in a very poor reward or rewards for toons you aren't interested in playing.
-You can't trade items with other players.   Items can't be chosen using in game currency.
-Only one game mode, albiet with several difficulty levels i.e.,No survival mode or versus mode
-Repetetive gameplay/limited content: You can play through all the levels at least once in a dozen or so hours of play.  Most people play the same 2 or 3 levels over and over again.   What fun(not!).
-Due to many of the above CONs, this game has the worst PUG experience I have experienced in any game, ever.  This game isn't like killing floor 1/2 where random matches will be fun and provide progression most of the time.
-Poor bot AI.  Don't think you can play this solo to get around the PUG problem.
-No steam integration to see who you recently played with.  If you get DC'ed before the end, have fun trying to find the game you were just in.
==Conclusion==
In the end, while the game is compared to l4d, it isn't anywhere as near as fun to play

In short: It's Left4Dead in the Warhammer fantasy setting with giant rats (Skaven) instead of zombies. For an independent studio and considering some of their past flops, Fatshark has outdone themselves this time. The level designs are fantastic and beautifully crafted. They have also been very active in patching out bugs and exploits.
Unlike Left4Dead, playing different characters completely changes how you play. There are two primarily melee classes and two primarily ranged classes. Each class has unique weapons that can be upgraded and each plays in a very different way than the others.
With 13 levels, the game got stale fast and left me wanting more variety, so hopefully there will be some more in future updates. The loot system is a bit awkward. You could spend days grinding to get that one special weapon you want, or you might get lucky and get it after a couple levels. There are really divided opinions on this among the community, some saying they like it, some saying it needs changed. Fatshark has yet to say anything about the topic.
There are lots of bugs and exploits still abound in this game, which aren't game breaking, but game ruining. People kick you from groups because you don't want to cheat. The community is turning toxic and it's just no fun to play anymore. Playing alone is also terrible because the bot AI for the other characters is just stupid as hell.
If you have a group of friends, it's worth buying to play with them. I'll still recommend it for that. However, if you're looking to play it alone or with random people online, don't bother. Left4Dead 2 is still a better game for that.

Sonic Adventure 2 is fun. Very fun. But not perfect. The story is meh with really only one thing that bothered me. Sonic pulling off chaos control for the first time. Don't know why, but sure. The speed levels are by far the best in my opinion with their nice rock music and fun level design. They have the occasional puzzle thrown in there to stop you for a second, but it's mainly just speed. Oh and Sonic's in that, so automatic win. The mech shooters are kinda boring and control like a tank. You also have a health bar instead of rings, but rings help fill up the bar. You can lock on to multiple targets and shoot a ton of missles everywhere too. These are alright, but get repetetive. The treasure hunting stages are by far, my least favorite. I don't hate then, but I don't like them either (except for Rouge's security hall which can go screw itself). You're collecting three emeralds in a stage and that's it. The big problem here is how big the levels are. Especially the later space levels. You also have a radar that tells you close you are to the next emerald (gray is nowhere near, green is in the area, yellow is closer, red is very close, and the exclamation mark means you're within 2 feet of it). The problem with this is it only tells you the next emerald it wants you to find. So you could walk right by an emerald and not know because that's not the one it wanted you to find. Security Hall also has a time limit of 5 minutes to collect the emeralds. This level's fairly small, but that time limit is pressuring. The Chao Garden. I love this place. You start out with two eggs and hatch them with 3 methods. Throwing it, shaking it, and just letting it hatch. You get a hero or dark chao by raising it with one of the respective characters or beating it up with the opposite ones, but why would you wanna do that? :c After getting a hero or dark chao, you obtain the hero and dark gardens respectively. You also have a daycare where they can learn different things such as drawing, singing, playing an intrument, etc. A doctor who can tell you what your chaos' weaknesses and strengths are, what they like to eat, and other info. The principal gives you some tips on how to raise your chao and there's a black market where you can buy fruit, seeds, and other goodies for your chao. There's also a fortune teller who can name your chao or (by decling all her names) you can name it yourself! There's chao racing and chao karate is you got the DLC. I could go into even more detail, but that'd take way too long (possible guide?). There are also 2P battles you can have! Races, mech fights, and race to emeralds are all things you can do! Locally. Unless you got a certain mod. *cough*
*cough* All in all this game is great, but the chao garden and speed levels are all I 100% enjoyed. If you're getting into Sonic, pick it up. I'm sure you'll like it. Not into Sonic? Get a demo, then see what ya think. Diehard fan? How have you not played it once? For real though. I love dis game. c:

With almost 400 hours of gameplay under my belt, I think it is safe to say that this game is one of the greatest games of all time. Within my first hour of playing it I fell in love with the single player experience (This will not be a review on multiplayer, as I have not played it, as it is not what I enjoy in the game). It allows you to amass hundreds of soldiers; powerful Nord Huscarls with their large shields and an axe, deadly Rhodok Sharpshooters with their siege crossbows and giant pavises on their back, and destructed Swadian Knights, armed with morningstars and powerful warhorses. This game gives you the sense of a General on a battlefield, as you are actually on the battlefield, riding in on your horse and armed with whatever equipment you have sacked off dead enemies, or bought in the cities, issuing orders to your men to hold their position at the base of a hill, while the archers stay at the top, killing enemies in masses. This game's strongest suit is not in graphics or animations, but gameplay. It looks atrocious when outside of battle, and amazing while in it. The fighting is easy to learn, and almost impossible to master, with 4 attack directions that you can control with your mouse to try to outsmart your opponent's blocking, which, unlike in many popular games such as Skyrim, will actually block attacks thrown at you, shields catching arrows when they are fired at you, instead of just negating damage a little. This would be overpowered, if not your shield breaks after hard wear, becoming fixed if only for your next battle. This game is entirely open world, with a tutorial that only teaches you the basics of the game, or, to put it bluntly, how to not get slaughtered. You can be a bandit, stealing from caravans and villages, or you can be a lord, working to put your king on top of all, and slaughter all other kings, you could work for a claimant, and overthrow a current king. Or, if you want, you can become the king, destroy all lands who oppose you, and rule over Calradia with an iron fist. This game, however, will make you hate stairs. Despite that, it gets a perfect score of 10/10, highly reccomended for anyone who likes Simulations of medieval combat, RTS' or even Skyrim-style adventure games.

Though it has level design by Lucifer and more guns than a russian child's christmas list, Hotline Miami 2 is still an amazing game.
The story is great, using a Pulp Fiction-style narrative that connects different characters (all with their own hidden motives and secrets). It made me sympathise with (almost) everyone, while hating most of them at the same time. The Pulp Fiction aproach allows the game to show different motives and viewpoints, expanding your understanding of the good and the evil of the world. I will divide this review into technical and gameplay sections.
Technical:
Ghosts is poorly optimized for PC - whether or not a PC can run it is extremely unpredictable. Two identical PCs may not be equal in the ability to run it; and also a cheap non-gaming office laptop like mine can run it well enough to be playable (and has never crashed since purchased in February 2014), while the game may fail miserably on a good gaming rig which runs other demanding games well.
Gameplay:
Multiplayer: at the time of writing, number of players online is fluctuating approximately between 200-800. If you play popular game modes like TDM, for me, I have never had any problems finding a game. Other game modes or DLC maps is difficult to impossible.
Ghosts is probably the most different COD since COD4MW - bigger maps, map layout not typical of other CODs, and the weapons and movement physics have more inertia/weight to it, thus a very slight slant towards the BF3/BF4 feel. You either love it or hate it. I have 6 CODS since COD4MW, and 8 BF games - being also a BF fan, I happen to like these characteristics of Ghosts, while most COD fans really hate it for these same reasons.
AI emulating 'multiplayer' matches: A significant number of players play and enjoy Ghosts for these feature - setting up private matches with AI (or bots), or playing the 'Squads' mode - where you can configure in detail your whole AI squad and challenge other players' squads. While this is essentially you and a bunch of bots in your team and the other, you can still rank up via this method. While any idiot knows that playing with bots will NEVER be the same with multiplayer with human players, Ghosts bots are among the best out there (comparable to CSGO bots or maybe better? You be the judge) and these bot matches can be fun.
Should you buy it? Due to its unpredictability as mentioned above, you are taking a risk. I managed to test it during a free weekend, and spent many hours to finally be sure I can make it work on my very humble PC before buying it. Apart from trying on a free weekend (which won’t happen anymore for Ghosts), no matter how powerful your PC is, there is a big enough risk that it may be problematic - so its a gamble purchase technical-wise.
Gameplay: if you want classic COD, this is not it. But if you want something different than the rest of the CODs, this may be fun for you. I am in the minority who likes the gameplay - but at the same time, I already have another 5 COD titles to play with for classic COD gameplay).
Campaign: I can't comment on this since I never play any games' campaign.
So, technical wise, buying Ghosts is a gamble because how powerful your PC is may not be the only factor which decides whether or not it will run well.
Gameplay wise, Ghosts is not the typical classic COD, and most people hate it. The question is whether you belong in the majority or the minority - which will end with you hating or loving it.
I belong to the minority, and my preference is purely personal taste of course. And I am the lucky ones who got Ghosts to run well enough on my potato for me to have fun.

When I first bought this game I was disapointed. I paid full price for it and I felt confused and annoyed by almost everthing I tried to do. After investing a reasonable amount of playtime into this game, I am happy to say now that I thoroughly enjoy this game. That is why I would really like for more people to buy this game and play it. This game deserves to be more popular. Furthermore, the game is on sale right now so people will be checking it out and there has never been a better time to join if you have considered it. For those reasons I have decided to provide what I think is a good recipe for getting started in Contagion.
1. The first thing you should do is go to start game and select the hunted game mode on any map. Choose solo play, turn infection off, and put the difficulty on easy. You will be dropped into a map with randomly generated zombies and a decent amount of weapons and ammo laying around for you to pick up. Hunted is a pvp game mode and since you are playing solo, this will be a good way for you to just run around aimlessly killing zombies and familiarizing yourself with the gameplay and the maps. Do this until you get tired of it and feel ready for the game to get more intense.
2. Now that you have gotten a feel for the game, go to find game, select hunted as the game mode, and join the first server that pops up. From here you will be looking to find and kill the other living characters (not zombies). This is a lot of fun, for beginners and vets alilke. Since your new, you may or may not get killed early, but thats ok since you get to come back from the dead to seek retribution against the living. Basically you get to play the entire time without having to sit and wait just because you died,
3. Have you made any friends yet? If so, check out some of the escape maps and see if they want to play. If not, check out some escape maps anyway, pay attention to your phone, but dont expect it to spell out all the information you need, your gonna need to figure things out on your own.
4. After logging some time in the game, now you are ready to try your skills at extraction. Try to find and save the survivors, but be warned, it gets intense. Just remember to wait for other players before entering the extraction points, as you will need their help when the hoards start to arrive. Not to mention if you go running straight into the houses without waiting for the others, it kinda ruins the game for everyone.
5. Have nothing to note on the panic game modes since it's pvp and I've never found a server playing them, looks like it might be fun though. Check this game out!! Happy gaming everyone!

I played this game and enjoyed it.
If you liked the old SWAT tactical shooter, here's something you will enjoy.
The good thing about this is that there's actual planning invovled - ypou don't just send your men in guns blazing, cause that way most or all of them will go back in bodybags. Here you have to plan ahead and every room you clear matters. One unexpected event will often demand of you to re-think your strategy. This is NOT a game wher eyou plan, then hit "execute" and forget about the whole thing. Far from what it may seem from screenshots or short videos, this is a thinking man's game.
Another good part of it is that there's more replayability than meets the eye. The same scenario will vary from one playthrough to the next. You may encounter different number of foes, in diffrent places, with different behaviour, armament and patrol patterns than you seen in your last playthrough of a given scenario. There are a lot of scenarios on tp of it all.
There is also an RPG-style mechanic - your SWAT agents will rise in skill after participating in missions, you will also get access to more armor types, weapon and doctrines as you complete more missions. Doctrines act much as passive bonuses in mmorpgs. This works pretty well, although it is primarily a tactical game and the rpg elements are not as deep as in complex mmos.
Only two downsides I can think of are two elements from the SWAT games taht I miss here - there's no tear gas and there's little in the way of opponent morale - 99% of foes will fight to the death and not surrender.

Mount & Blade: Warband is a game that has such a wide variety of experiences among those that play it. I honestly can only speak for my experiences in the game and highly recomened you look at other reviews to see how they went about playing the game. The game drops you into the middle of a country torn by war among 6 factions. You create your character, their background and jump into the middle of a capital of one of the factions while being assaulted by bandits. The game can actually be played many ways with the overal goal being living your character's life the way you want to live it. At it's heart it is an RPG but it does have economy simulator, RTS, and even political simulator elements in the game. The goal of the game is...there isn't one. You can become the ruler of a trade empire, the ruler of a kingdom, the marshall of the armies of your liege, a ruthless bandit or anything you set your mind to. The game has a companion system with enough variety for any playstyle/morality to work. The companions even have dialogue with each other and develop friendships/rivalries depending on who else is in the party. The game has a wide variety of options and paths to pursue. Combat can be either as simple as charing your men at the enemy or forming up on the flanks with cavalry while infintry hold the line in sheild wall formation. The game actually centers itself around combat and even if you decide to be a trader you are going to need some bodyguards to defend yourself from bandits. The game promotes building your character to do whatever you feel like doing. Fighting off bandits, enemy nations, and trade caravans at your pleasure feels good with your troops. Your troops are recruited as the greenest of soldiers and have to work their way up through the trees to receive veteran unit status. Each unit receives xp individually so you know the soldiers that are getting stuck in are the ones leveling up. The game has a nice political and trade system as impoverished cities are the ones that are being constantly seiged/raided and are having their caravans and peasants slaughtered while the wealthy ones are receiving protection from enemy nations and bandits. Politically the game holds grudges and wars can be incited by the simplest bandit attacks on caravans, mistreatment of poor citizens, and trespassing. The fact that the kings are constantly declaring war, fighting, then taking their losses and leaving make for an always evolving map as towns and cities become destitute due to the heavy fighting. The system of marriage and lordship, including owning your own kingdom, is fun despite some issues and actually adds depth to simple things like feasts and tournaments as you fight for the love of lords and ladies, the wealth of the city, and a chance to place yourself higher in the realm. There are, sadly, plenty of issues in the game due to basically being abandoned by it's developer. There are a plethora of bugs that can ruin a game experience. For a game with a big focus on combat horse units are just some of the best in existence. The thing everyone knows is the heavily armored Swadian Knight which rides in on horseback slaughtering scores of men then if you manage to dismount the unit they are still a heavily armored infantry unit capable of fighting with sword and sheild and two handers. An army of all cavalry is quite honestly one of the best in the game as it is capable of outfighting a majority of units just due to the bonuses (Extra hp, damage etc) that riding a horse provides. The political system has it's flaws as you are not capable of directing the king to declare war, frame a nation for something without getting in trouble, and various other things. Following a marshall is fine until you realize the AI is derping around refusing to fight anything and you have to leave the Marshall's side to attack things or hope he likes you enough to trust you when you say that city over there only has 50 men in it.  Managing your towns basically  comes down to running fetch quests all over the region just to make your village/city wealthy enough to actually give you money. The game iteself does require the same thing over and over again due to the lack of a semi-competent AI. You have to fight many battles so you can win them as the auto-resolve will not actually work and will make you lose a good portion of your force. Even fighting your way though the entire enemy nation means nothing unless you leave 80+ men at each location you take due to the inability of your nation to capitalize on the death of the entire standing army of the enemy nation. It is also to be noted that the game will take forever to make meaningful progress as anytime your host nation gets any amount of pull in the world ALL other nations will declare war to curb it's power regardles of how much land they lose to their other enemies. The game itself has issues with even making your own kingdom. It trys to justify it by saying you need "Right to rule" but never really explains what that is or how to aquire it. It also doens't seem to matter as even with a large amount of it you will be beset by every neighboring faction as soon as you decide to make your own kingdom. The issues with owning your own kingdom are plenty with you being genreally unable to control your lords even in times of war. You basically have to pray that they are following the marshall/you around in times of war and are not just wasting their own time outside of the wars.  Fighting long wars doesn't seem to have  a lasting affect unless you take land as you can never truely get rid of a lord. Merely imprison him until the peace treaty. This means that although you can try as hard as you might the game is designed to drag itself out to absorb as much of your time as possible while still remaining just entertaining enough to keep you playing. Most mods for the game are complete overhauls turning the game into a Warhammer, Warcraft, LotR, or GoT version of itself all with their own problems and bugs. Although these mods typically vastly improve the gameplay of the vanilla version they are too varied to give a concrete rating. I rate Vanilla a 6.2/10

It's not that the game is bad but rather it's simply bland.   As I type this it's on sale for $5  and it has been cheaper  even here on Steam when I bought it for $3.74   it's also been similary priced on the humble store for $4.    So know that the game has and no doubt will be again cheaper if you're on a tight budget.   The standard asking price of $20 is absurd though and is clearly priced high soley to make it appealing during large Steam sales.
The game has two major modes.  One being a Co-op where you have to advance through the map doing objectives while trying to not become zombie lunch.  This mode is the best the game has to offer but it's not great.   The generic gameplay  gets old quite fast so hopefully whomeever you are playing with (and god help you if you actually bother to play alone) better be a rather amusing friends.   Otherwise once you play a map once there is little reason to ever play it again even though objectives are  somewhat randomized each time.     The game is terribly easy except if one of you actually manages to die.   If that occurs they get a few zombie lives and  this is where diffaculty steps up, player zombies are a actual threat and likely your team will be wiped out due to them in many cases.   This also causes trolls to get themselves killed to disrupt the game as early as possible.  These types of players are not overly common but do exist.
Then there is the PVP mode which is just god awful.  It mostly consists of players trying to camp  and a few being brave enough to hunt the others down.  The phone can be used as a method of  playing hot and cold  which will give away other players positions.  Why do you have the numbers of everyone you are trying to hunt? Who knows, but while this may sound like a neat feature it also serves as a warning to the camper that the threat is coming.    Again with the majority of players prefering to camp this causes the brave hunters to often die because killing 4 campers one after enough tends to get you shot a few times during the fire fights.  It's a terrible game design.   Likewise however if you die you become a zombie and can try to get some  brain flavored revenge.... or cheat...  You see the game has another issue when friends play together it doesn't take long before they realize the zombie can help their buddy human.   So lets say the human is camping in a room with 1 entrance  the zombie can sit just outside and call NPC zombies to gather keep calling them keeps the zombies with him making  a zombie protective shield  for thier friend and attacking any player that comes and you'll know their coming because they will no doubt be using the noisy phone.
Beyond game-play  the sound is generic, and the graphics are heavily aged because they decided to go with the Source engine.  A great engine sure even more so in its prime but we see other indie games looking better or having unique art styles to comensate this just once again decides to be bland.    There are just too many games today to choose from that do this genre better, some of them even free like No More Room in Hell.   So there's no reason to buy this game at the end of the day.   You're reading this review during a sale right?  You can do better for your $5.

So I put a decent amount of time into this game and these are my thoughts on the game.
- The ISO system
The ISO system is easy to use you pick some base parts (like gun barrels and handles.) and put the materials you pull out of the ground onto them to create new and personalised weapons vehicles and aircraft.
- Adventure Mode
The Adventure Mode is the sandbox mode essentially and you get dropped onto a randomly generated world that can be fairly large with just the basics and you can do anything from there.
-Story Mode
From what I played they have an interesting allbeit cliche story. The background information and the landmass you play on are both plentiful and interesting. They added a lot more since the last time i played and I am genuinely excited to play it.
-Build mode
This mode gives you all the equipment all the materials and is just for testing ISOs. No AI spawn which is unfortunate because i would like to test my weaponry to see if they work well or not and build a huge colony.
-Multiplayer
I have only played Multiplayer a handful of times it seems pretty well fleshed out it plays like Adventure mode but has other players in it.
All in all I enjoy the game and will continue to play it in the coming years. This game is still in early access and still needs work done so while playing I recommend not looking at the bugs to hard and to make note of them and let the Devs know.

Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number is interesting. Compared with the first game, there are many notable improvements such as storytelling, soundtrack and presentation. However, it takes a couple steps back in gameplay, which sucks because well...the fast paced gameplay makes up 90% of the game. I found myself dying waaaay too many times from enemies off screen, or random enemy movements. I thought the first game had wonky A.I. here and there, but not as bad as this game. One of the things that made the first game great was the ability to learn levels, and maneuver them to your bidding. What helped in that too was the fact that you had such an array of masks to choose from for every single level. In the sequel, you are severely limited to gameplay styles. I think it’s a clear example of how a hard game shouldn’t be frustrating, it should encourage the player to think, adapt and overcome the difficulty.
All that being said, the story in this game is ♥♥♥♥ing insane and will make you want to keep playing. The diverse array of characters, themes, and shifts in storytelling make for one of the most unique story experiences I've had in a long time. The expanded soundtrack is also fantastic. In the first game, several tracks were repeated for multiple levels. Not that there was a problem with that as the original soundtrack was incredible, (and I would say overall was more cohesive than Wrong Number's soundtrack) but it's really nice and fresh to have individual songs back every level in the game. It makes certain levels really memorable.
Unless you try for all achievements and A+ like me, then you really shouldn't have a problem progressing level to level, as it's only reeaally when you challenge yourself to get a high score that the flaws in gameplay show. But that being said, even taking my time on some levels in hard mode made me want to bash my head against a wall. Overall, I'd give it a flat 8.0/10. The level design in the original is leagues better, however I think Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number is still a great game, and a worthy sequel, even if the progression and tediousness in the gameplay becomes apparent.

Gameplay is quick, bloody, and fun. Graphics are haunting, grim, and forboding, all good things for this game. In game voice is good. Stability is good. Of course a few bugs persist, but very few compared to other modern day new releases. Active studio is listening to feedback and pushing out fixes. Thats a good sign for continued support as well as future content.
4 player coop can always be dependent on the quality of the party. The matchmaking is purely random, so newbies and vets are matched alike, which is good for introducing new players to the maps. Learning new levels can be tough, not super clear mission objectives with guided waypoints. However the map design is superb and will naturally guide the players towards their intended destination, while allowing some free exploration in route.
Replayability is high, if you enjoy gear hunting. The crafting of new weapons is random and has high costs, additionally random drops at the end of matches requires victory and is dependent on difficulty for weapon quality potiental. There certainly is an element of "gah, why can't I find that 2 hander!?!?!?" that may frustrate some players. If you are turned off to gear grinds, you may not enjoy the longevity of this game, but there are still plenty of levels to master that I feel most people would get their monies worth with just playing each level to mastery.
Great investment for the price.
