Im a pretty big fan of most co op horde survival games. I initially thought I missed the boat for Left 4 Dead, had to play mostly solo and it simply was not fun for me. The level direction was non existent and the AI would maybe come save me as I get wrecked in a corner by a Hunter.
Vermintide seems like an exact copy of Left 4 Dead, but in a good way, although Im still not much of a fan.  Level direction and objetives seem pretty straightforward, didn't find myself getting lost like I did in L4D.
The main thing obviously is the combat. Personally I felt L4D did it better, at least melee wise. For whatever reason, enemies have an invisible box in front of them at any given time that just throws me off whenever I try and rush in and kill rats. Sweep attacks that look like they should hit multiple targets dont because Im on some box being pushed away. Attacks that should land and interupt an incomming attack miss because of said box. Not a fan of that whatsoever. I shouldnt be forced to use a ranged character to avoid that.
At the end of every mission you get a dice roll for equipment drops. I feel pretty split on this. On one hand, every mission you manage to complete guarantees you some item or another. What isnt guaranteed is whether or not the item is better than what you have, though I assume thats what the forge is for in fusing 4 less than stellar items together to improve another one. Another thing is that apparently you can get items that arent even for your current character. Really not a fan of that, I dont understand the logic of getting an axe while playing as a dual wielding rogue.
All in all it simply isnt for me. Would I recommend though? Sure, especially if you are a Left 4 Dead fan in any way shape or form. Maybe if Vermintide ever goes on sale I will get it again but right now Im just not feeling it.

EDIT: This game is meant to work more like Diablo 3 than left 4 dead.  If you're not farming better loot, and upgrading all your items, then you're not getting the entire experience.  The goal is to beat all levels on the maximum difficulty level.  If you played through this game once, on 1 or 2 characters, on normal difficulty, you basically just played the tutorial/story.

My favorite game of all time, which I only installed on Steam to get my best times screenshotted to crush a friend's dreams.
SA2 is by no means perfect. The Tails/Eggman levels are a chore, and there are a lot of bugs. Luckily the port negates many of the control-related bugs found in the original Dreamcast version. Spinning to win through particular areas that would make you fall (such as the last loop-de-loop in Green Forest) no longer do so, and walls as a whole are a bit less likely to act like glue to the Blue Blur.
I'll be honest: I'm really biased toward this game, as it and its predecessor are probably the only games I'll never get tired of playing and trying to hone my skills at. Let me start out by saying some good things about this game. I really enjoyed the graphic style, the really cool sound design and during the first chapter of the game, I also enjoyed the gameplay mechanics.
Now let's talk about the rest. Story-wise this game is atrocious. I won't spoil anything, but the writing is really clichéed. Strong man that doesn't talk much and mourns his family. The real enemy is not a zombie, but the human itself. And it is a human that attempts to♥♥♥♥♥♥a woman at the point, where the story almost falls apart, just to create some suspense. Not really imaginative.
The gameplay turns into a catastrophy while playing the last chapter. From timed jumps, to bullsh*t hitboxes that will make you die over and over again - everything is in there. Phrases like "The Safe Point is no more than a trap used to hunt the survivors." will make the replaying of those little parts even worse. The worst part are the checkpoints. You think that you will only have to replay that one jump, but you start out at the beginning of a long and unrewarding section that will take you approximately 30 minutes to finish. The game design in the last chapter is just really, really bad.
Another minor quirk is the overlapping of audio. Since recordings that can be found throughout the game world do not have subtitles, you will have to crank the volume up in order to understand them. Of course, they are a bit distorted, to make it even harder to understand.
The collectibles are also very, very unrewarding. There are hints at the government using leftover missiles from the Cold War, but as a whole the plotholes are very big. Furthermore, the ID's of strangers do not make any sense. I do not know if they are a reference to something, but they are in no way motivating collectibles.
As a whole, I do not recommend this game. The first part was very enjoyable and the game could have been a lot more. Nevertheless, because of the unprofessional writing and the rushed game-design towards the end, it is a tedious experience. If you really want to experience the (bad) story, you should rather watch a playthrough.

Deadlight is a puzzle platformer game with light action elements that tries and fails to be an atmospheric horror experience.  I really enjoyed the art style and the attempt at a 2.5 D environment. It could have been an atmospheric horror game or a creepy adventure game based just on the presentation.  Unfortunately the platforming is inconsistent, the objective of each section not always clear, and the combat laggy and unresponsive.  For me this resulted in lots of deaths.  There is no punishment for this as you start over at the last checkpoint which is usually a few seconds from where you died, but for a game who’s art style and audio went to a lot of trouble to create a sense of immersion constantly retrying a check point because I didn’t understand what to do and got swarmed by the undead really takes you out of the story.  There are three chapters to this relatively short game.  I started in on chapter 3 and after dying a handful of times decided to move on to other things, not so much because the game was too hard to complete, I could have forced my way through, but I totally lost interest in the world the game was trying to create.

Planet Explorers stands proud as having the most creative freedom of any fleshed sandbox/survival game I've ever seen. From mining the terrain to collect resources, to crafting, colony creation and NPC recruitment, to being able to build your structures, weapons, armor, helicopters, jets, motorcycles and tanks, and even your very own Kitchen sink how you wish.
PE utilizes a fully minable voxel world, along with a building and creation system that lets you bring your imagination to life.
You can build weapons, vehicles, and even armor through a voxel creation system that let's you shape, color, and even texturize. Not only create them, but use them ingame for their determined roles.
While there are plenty of games out there that have colony management, It's noteworthy to mention that recruiment in PE is about finding randomly generated npcs (aswell as pre-made npcs if you're playing story mode), that you can recruit into your colony for different roles. You can have them farm, gather resources, upgrade equipment, or patrol your colony to protect it from assailants. You may equip them as you wish, and even recruit them as followers to acompany on your journey. They all have unique appearences along with names (The names list is a bit short at the moment though..). They also come with their own sets of skills that you can have them train other colonists to have aswell.
This is a big one.. Pathea has created a sandbox creation game that includes a storymode, without any cut functionality from adventure mode. Not only have they done this, but they've also gone and made it multiplayer. You can either play this on a public server, or host a private game with friends only!
Monsters have been programmed to act according to what they are, rather than a default all-round AI slapped onto everything.. One creature will not engage the same as any other. Birds will keep distance, and swoop at their pray, or come in close temporary for a close range attack before swooping away..  Different bird creatures will even do this differently than others.. Not only do they have their own AI packages, but they also have their own animations specifically designed around them.
Humanoid NPC's, followers and colonists, utilize the different tools and weapons you give them based on situation. For example, you can give a follower a sword and shield, and they will engage into melee, until their hp gets low, in which they will withdraw a distance from the enemy. If you've given them a ranged weapon aswell, they will draw their bow or gun and continue firing at the enemy from a distance, while they heal. If they have an axe in their inventory, they will aid you in cutting down trees.
If you have an inkling for design, and would love to see your very own creations have a purpose and use in a sandbox world, Planet Explorers is a must!

Warhammer Vermintide doesn't even attempts to hide its roots. It's very clear that it is Left 4 Dead but in the Warhammer Fantasy setting, with a some spice over it. However, instead of rats, the common enemy, by that I mean every enemy, is a man sized anthropomorphic rats that WILL swarm you in large numbers, along with special infect- I mean rats, whom share many similarities with their L4D counterparts, but with some original ones and different behavior overall.
The game also features Classes, in a somewhat "classical" RPG manner, as each character is a different Class, and each have their own exclusive weapons, but still with some overlap between them. There are 5 as of the time of this "review", and they're all enjoyable to play, however some are trickier than others to get used to.
Gameplay is somewhat simple but functional and, in my opinion, fun. It is much more melee focused than L4D is, but you have your light attack and strong attack, with each weapon having their respective attacks being different some way or another. Everyone also gets a secondary ranged weapon, but they have limited resources and ammo is not nearly as plentiful as in L4D. Like I said, every class has their own loadout that you have to choose before the map starts, or at the chest at the spawn point. The weapons can vary from a Two Handed Hammer to a Sword and Dagger, or even from a Crossbow to a Revolver (that is called pistol for some reason).
The AI for the Skaven (enemy rats) is impressively competent, which makes the higher difficulties truly a challenge.  The special infected will often work together, and wait more often than not, go for the lone player who wandered off.  Common Skaven are also notorious for swarming you, but with a few actually taking the time to go around you, rendering you surrounded and pounded from every angle. Game is not easy, and requires competent team work even for the normal difficulty. However, the ally BOT AI is stupid. Just absolutely scatterbrained and unreliable. Prefer humans, as dumb as they can be.
Another really neat thing is the number and variety of maps. There are more than enough here to render you amused for quite the while. Wizard's Tower is really really cool.
However, the game is a mixed bag. And you MUST be aware of that before making the dicision to purchase this game.
Let's start with the -oh so important- graphics: They look fine. Models and textures look okay, even in Medium quality. It's no Crysis, but it shouldn't bother anyone. Asthetics are closer to realism than fantastical. But the real problem here is with performance. This game, when no enemies are afoot and just the map and my comrades are about, can run at a smooth 60 fps with everything on max on my GTX 970 and i7. But the moment a few skaven show up, the game takes a hard slowdown to around 15-ish frames. And THIS also happens when everything is on Low, but instead of 15 is around 30. That's just poor optimization and, according to the devs, this problem, that affects most but not all, is related to CPU usage of the game. Still, it is something the potential consumer needs to be aware of.
Another problem is with Online connectivity. If the host disconnects for whatever reason, you're ♥♥♥♥ed. The map will reset to the start instead migrating to another host on the fly. That can be very VERY frustrating, specially when playing with ragequitters or just hosts with bad connectivity. So be advised.
And now the very controversial Loot system. Look, it's cool that after every mission complete you get to roll 7 dices and, depending on success, you'll get a specific weapon that varies on rarity depending on your roll. And you can also stack dices in your favor with modifiers that are items you find and need to carry throughout the map. That is all fine, but it currently is very much potentially frustrating. You can play your favorite class for hours on, and not get a single drop for said class, because it's random the ones that show up at the reward table at the end of the match. Sure, you can fuse 5 weapons you wish to make a new one, but the result can only be one of the type of weapons you used to fuse in the first place. So you can actually have NOTHING of worth to use for your favorite class after countless hours of play (much like me). It needs some refining and rebalancing.
If any of those problems vehemently put you off, I recommend you to wait off a few months and see if any of that is changed. For those who can manage, do play it. But play smart. Please.
tl;dr
Game is good. It's L4D + Fantasy Warhammer (not 40k) with some spice over it and melee focused. But it still is very much flawed with its host connectivity, loot system and poor performance issues
Cautious recommendation.

My favorite game of all time, which I only installed on Steam to get my best times screenshotted to crush a friend's dreams.
SA2 is by no means perfect. The Tails/Eggman levels are a chore, and there are a lot of bugs. Luckily the port negates many of the control-related bugs found in the original Dreamcast version. Spinning to win through particular areas that would make you fall (such as the last loop-de-loop in Green Forest) no longer do so, and walls as a whole are a bit less likely to act like glue to the Blue Blur.
I'll be honest: I'm really biased toward this game, as it and its predecessor are probably the only games I'll never get tired of playing and trying to hone my skills at. I originally played SA2 in 2001, and have pumped about 300 hours in spurts over the past 13 years. It's fun, soulful, and has an amazing soundtrack.
Whether a classic or modern Sonic fan, this and its predecessor are important games to play to see how the series evolved. Whether or not you consider the transition to 3D smooth or worth the effort is up to you, but I honestly could not ask for anything more.

This game feels like hard work.
Once you finally get an army together after many days (in game) and you try a new mission type. Bam! You get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by wandering units.
If you are looking for a relaxing and entertaining game, which gives you some satisfactory feeling on a day-to-day basis. Then this is not for you. You will spend hours on hours trying and trying to survive and level up your soldiers to some useful degree and maybe end up as level 8 yourself. Just to have it all taken away from you and you are back to square on. You may still have your money, but your units are gone. Start over training new ones.
The game has good ideas and a good setup, but to me it is not relaxing.
It feels like a job, where your boss continuously gives you new tasks, which ends up kicking you back to square one. Keeping you down. I had expected this game to provide me with a good amount of hours enjoying it, but in the end, no. A challenge is good, but there is no challenge if the game rapes you just as you get a little bit of the way. It is time consuming and not in a good way.
The settings are very different from what you would normally see in a game of this genre. The combat system is very demanding, like nightmare difficulty demanding. It is far from out of the box user-friendly.
In most cases it is just guess work as to, where you hit when you strike, mounted on a horse. The shooting is better, but still feel not as certain as you would normally do with other bow and arrow games. The bow acts weird with its crosshair, leaving you wildly guessing, where in the large circle your arrow might hit, even when standing still. Crossbows are better, the crosshair feels like it works as it should, but it still requires some skill to master. It is the only weapon which feels useable out of the box.
I have tried the fighting style of this game in other games, but at least they did give you some indication as to, where you would hit and it was easier to control, which direction you would hit from. At times it feels like the NPC you are fighting, are reacting ninja fast and to talk about stray arrows, yeah right stray from miles away, headshot.
That you can lose a battle if you fall, even if the enemy is 2 left and your army still have around 20 men fit for fight, is a total joke. The battlefield system could learn something from Total War games. They are easier to handle.
This game lacks many details, but if you put in days and hours to learn it, then maybe you will be one of those, who praise this game for being what it is.
As a casual gamer who likes an entertaining challenge, achieving goals and not feeling like normal is really hard+ difficulty, I cannot recommend this game. This game does not feel satisfying in any way, mainly because as you get close to just doing well in the game, you risk getting♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by the game. One 0.nano wrong step, and you are toast.
Basically it is not fun sitting and watching your 2nd to 3rd level captives drag you around the map after they defeated your 3rd to 4th level soldiers, while being ½ your army size.
If I have to say three things, which describes the feelings I have mostly felt playing this game. They would be:
Start over, Start over, Start over!
In the end the game is good and maybe after months of spending hours daily, you will get close to master this game.
The combat system will be your greatest challange, unless you are used to the freeform-feeling-your-way-combat, that is Mount & Blade. Second is the battlefield and your troops often weak state, until you get the much spoken of "Swadian Knights".
In any case good luck if you buy this game.
Final words on this game after 100+ hours.
It can be very addictive and will be rewarding in the end.
Just be aware that you may experience FTG moments.

Just picture a vast continent filled with 22 cities and 48 castles each with several villages split amongst 6 factions constantly at war fighting for control and it's all your playground.
Do you play the noble knight, swearing homage to a lord and defending the poor peasants? How about a bandit pillaging the villages and raiding trade caravans to line your pockets? Or maybe you have aspirations for the throne. Build an army and carve out an empire under your own banner. These are but a few options that you can take.
There are a sizeable amount of skill options that allow the creation of many types of characters from the heavily armoured knight to the swift horse archer.
The game has a rather steep learning curve however practice and patience will give results.
The difficulty is easily customised to your preference from the options menu.
The graphics are dated by today's standards and there are still some bugs.
The multiplayer is still active at the time of writing with many dedicated players.
It offers multiple game modes / Deathmatch(free for all) / Team Deathmatch / Siege (teams attack and defend castles) / Capture the Flag / Battle (no respawns).
The community is a mixed bunch, with about an equal split between friendly and ill mannered players.
There is a vast active modding community that offers players the ability to change the settings and mechanics of the game. Genkokujo(Sengoku jidai era of Japan), A Clash of Kings(Game of Thrones) Anno Domini(13th Century Europe), Just to name a few.
~Vast Customisation
~Re-playability
~Modding
~Skill based Gameplay
~Learning Curve
~Hit and Miss Community
~Dated Graphics

I'll say it up front -- I hate side scrollers.  The reason I hate side scrollers:  It's not 1984, my computer isn't a Commodore-64, and I'm not 15 years old.  I had PLENTY of my fill of side scrollers in my day.
I took a chance on this one,  This is one of the few games (not just on Steam -- but PERIOD) that I would play full price for.  $14.99 for this game is a bargain.  It has been on Steam for three years and it does not appear dated AT ALL.
The graphics are beautiful -- they are so beautiful and realistic that at times I wished I could have explored the environment more.  It didn't bother me that I couldn't interact with stuff like in Half Life 2 (which this game reminded me of).  Sometimes I just wanted to be able to hang around and check out the scenery.
But, like all side scrollers, you gotta keep moving.  And so I could see the replay value of this game being very high as you check out various scenes and settings.
A negative (which wasn't a tremendous negative for me) was that the plot of the game is pretty cliched.  How original can the plot of a zombie apocalypse be?  In this game, I didn't care so much.  The storyline I'll go back for.  But my OCD tendencies make me want to race through to the end as quickly as I can.
Another positive -- there is a lot of content in this game.  This is part of the way I judge games.  When I read a review that says the game is too short, I get wary.  At 3.7 hours played, I can tell you that I am satisfied with the content.
Again, as in every game I comment on -- you need to read this through the lens of a casual gamer.  I have a life, a career, a family, and soul-crushing student loan debt.  I need my games to allow me to escape for a while.  This game is one of those that does.
If you can even tolerate side scrollers, you are doing yourself a tremendous disservice by not playing this game.  Would purchase again, no questions asked.

I got this game on a steam sale for a couple of bucks. I started playing it after "This war of mine", I figured I could transition from one side scroller to another. I love zombie games, and survival games. So I thought I'd give it a go.
So let me just rant, because I cant really pinpoint this game without disliking it, which makes me sad:
It's a true classic platform game hailing to the days of original platforms. The puzzles are not difficult to solve, and you'll feel like Mario, jumping from platform to breaking platform to floating platform, and switching sides on ladders. I completed 96% of the first act and 66% of the second. I had to write this review because I'm getting tired after putting 6 hours of my day into this game. I hope I can pick it up tomorrow, but the truth is it's frustrating.
It plays like a classic, and I was never good at the exact timing and unforgivingness of their playability. This game at least loads you almost immediatly before the obstacles you die upon. If your not a quick thinker you will die a lot. I'm not insulting myself, rather I find the fault to be in the controls and character movements of the game. You see this game suffers from classic platform problems and thats the issue. Time and time again I was dying not because I couldnt solve a puzzle or get to a secret (Another tribute to classics, they are fairly well done but not impossible to find), I died time and time again from overjumping, underjumping, not jumping at that exact second your at the edge of the platform. I almost stopped playing it, the controls are 'sticky', your character wants to keep moving. You have to gently tab back and forth to hit a mechanism, you will accidently hit the wrong key and die.
This is meant for the console, and its almost a bad port. The WASD is a bit tricky to get used to, I dont think it works very well, and now I'm just complaining.. I cant really put a delicate touch to this review. I appreciate everything they did in this game, but the autmosphere isnt landed, theres not much character development (besides a little for Rat and Randal), you have enemies wasting helicopter fuel to kill humans during the zombie apocalypse? Cheeky comicbook type cutscenes to bring it along with a loose story about finding friends and family we dont know except for diary entries. I could hardly read them I was busy jumping around and avoiding getting bit.
I'm sorry but it just didnt do anything well. With how linear it plays, and how simple it all is, I was almost seeing pixels as a helicopter shot a straight line of bullets as I was trying to run ahead of them. I thought I was playing the original Castlevania, or Turok.. I wish they had shot for a solid goal, if it was to be like a classic platformer, well then they nailed it. The bad and the good. But personally, I mostly played with my sister when we were 8, I was never that into them after graphics started to change, ideas were hatched, and we got more dimensions. I would have appreciated it more if it had some diversity, or survival elements, like 'This war of mine', but it felt too much like a Super Nintendo zombie version of 'prince of persia' to me. Like I said, I hope I can finish it tomorrow so it wont sit in my library for eternity. Seeing as I have work to do, and it's the weekend after that.. This game will be lucky if it sees the light of day sunday.
If you love classic platformers, then pick it up on sale. But other than that, I would'nt recommend it.
I havent wrote a review in a long time, and I'm sorry it had to be to pinpoint the negatives of a game I'm sure some people worked hard to make.

I wasn't really sure if I should vote thumbs up or thumbs down on this... So I went with positive.
Why? Well hang out for a sec and I'll explain.
What is Vermintide?
Well it's basically a rip off of a few different games but mostly a rip off of Left 4 Dead, but... It's a rip off done right.
In Vermintide you can chose from one of five different characters, you level up but this seems to have no real effect on your toon besides unlocking slots to equip trinkets that have zero effect in game...
You can loot, and craft, kind of. You get loot at the end of a round if you complete the round, if not you just get xp.
So a slight rpg mechanic is in place thought the results of leveling up are unsatasfying because you don't really gain anything.
Crafting is designed to take a fair amount of materials to make anything good, which keeps you farming, er I mean playing.
The combat is Mele, and well. They got it right, in fact it's the best FPS style game that has been able to nail down combat with a swung weapon. Sure L4D2 tried, but they failed miserably at it. In Vermintide it just feels right, the distances, the reaction times, how I don't feel like I have to get so close to something that I've almost walked past it in order to strike it where it seems the enemies could strike me from almost out of site. That's right, none of that. It's balanced in the reach and you can actually block, push, and attack effectively.
More good,
It's Hard.
Why is that good? Because it actually presents a challenge and all team members must not only stay together but work together and have some skills to survive.
The playable toons are different, not only in looks and animation but different skill sets, and abilities.
So how is this a Left 4 Dead rip off you might ask?
Well the special mobs. All do basically what the L4D mobs do. You have a tank/oger, Jocky/Task master, boomer, smoker hybrid being a /glober in this game tossing smoke bombs then charging at you to explode if it's near death, hunter/gut runner, The waves of enemies come in as hords, and they have patrols which are arguably different but it's basically a random mechanic designed to take you out or cause you greef if you get slopy, much the way the car alarms are in L4D.
That being said, this re-skinned Left 4 Dead game with a few inventive twists is fun to play, it's challenging, and can even be a little aggrivating if you are matched up with people who don't get the idea of working together. The enviornents are fantastic, the animations are great, the game play is fun, and really what more do you want.
The game does have some opt issues and drops frames once and a while, usually just before an "event" which can ruin the suprise... and no, it's not my computer. Check my specs on my page and or note that I can run the Witcher 3 on this thing at 4k with no issues.
So what's the verdict? Would I recomend buying it or not?
That's a hard one, it's a good game and fun, but it seems like Valve diserves the money for the blatent plagerism commited by this game more than that dev's deserve the money for only half♥♥♥♥♥optimizing it.
I bought it, I play it.. so figured that would be the tipping point in giving it a positive review.

You command a SWAT Team in different scenarios, be it simply eliminating all the terrorists or missions that include hostages or bombs to defuse.
The level variety is great, the different types of mission always make the game seem fresh and provide a challenge.
One mission might be a rather simple (but still demanding) run-and-gun assault on a hideout with not much pressure, another one might give you a small 20second window to eliminate a terrorist threatening a hostage.
The levels can be approached rather casual if you don't mind casualties, but they are still challenging.
Most players will rather take a more tactical approach where you minimize the collateral damage and have a "more elite" execution of your plan.
The tactical possibilities for each mission seem endless with the variety of weapons and classes.
Every mission can be completed with 0 (failed) to 3 stars depending on your performance with additional challenges that add replay value such as "Only use real time combat" or "Only use one plan to finish the mission", as well as the classic "Beat this time".
The AI is good and always makes you think twice about your next move, their position also varies from try to try.
A really engaging, challenging game that always leaves you satisfied after a mission. Quite some customization (weapons), leveling (different classes, experience, small "perks") options and enough missions to keep you busy for a while.
Last but not least a small video that showcases how a mission works out after a few hours into the game (created with the ingame replay-to-video function)

GREAT game that was well worth the price (woo holiday sale!)
Planning out your unit's movements and facings is surprisingly intuitive, and the go-code mechanic helps keep your guys coordinated. Your units feel competently trained but not godlike, and the enemies are challenging without being frustrating. Pretty much every time one of my units dies, it's immediately apparent it's because I forgot to plan for some variable/check that corner/messed up my pathing/some other personal error rather than my units not shooting straight.
Each officer can be customized with different class, weapons, support options, armor, and a tool, and each choice feels meaningful. For example, if I want the officer to stay in the back of an open area and provide cover, I'll make him an assault and give him a carbine for range and stopping power and heavy armor since he won't have to move as much. If I want to run the same officer through a drug bust, I'll change him to a pointman (stealth once I've unlocked it), give him a silenced pistol and light armor so he can quickly and quietly run through the hideout and secure the evidence before it's destroyed.
The game almost feels puzzle like, in that it encourages players to find the optimum route through each map to guarantee success no matter enemy placement (something the game tests by mixing up where the enemies are on each map) with a well though out plan, rather than simply winging it on the fly (although that is possible, especially if you want to make effective use of the spy cam). Notably, the player is rewarded on some maps for executing the perfect plan by planning everything once, then hitting go and doing nothing but watch the action. It maintains a good balance in difficulty as well. The game rarely feels too easy, but it also rarely feels frustrating or overwhelming in difficulty.
Progression is surprisngly well thought out, starting players on a simple kill house with a handful of badguys and a pair of officers, cutting their teeth in before introducing door entry, different classes, hostage rescue, and arresting/escorting mechanics.
I haven't messed with the ingame editor yet, but its very presence almost guarantees near infinite replayability. Currently, there is a wide selection of challenging single missions, and four campaigns (a string of 5 or 6 missions), with a 5th having a confirmed release date and more being promised.

Mount & Blade: Warband is by far the best medieval battle simulator. It is not like other battle simulators where you command a bunch of minions to attack eachother and watch closely how your troops die. No, it is not. You will actually be fighting yourself. Take a bow, sword, pike, crossbow; mount yourself to a horse or fight on foot; command your troops to attack with you or stay back while you will be the hero. All of this is possible in this wonderful game. But that's not all; it is not just about fighting. You can recruit your own swordsmen, mercenaries, archers, pikemen - level them up, garrison them into your freshly won castle, or even a town. To explain why I love this game I must compare it to a game that really annoyed me: BIT.TRIP.RUNNER. That game, like this one, requires you you press buttons in time with music but it was just so unforgiving it was tortuous to play. I was so frustrated by it as the concept was brilliant but the execution was terrible. So when I saw Melody’s Escape on Steam I was extremely excited as it looked like it was the game BIT.TRIP.RUNNER could have been. However at that point it was still in early access and I’m not interested in playing a half finished game so I waited until it was finished.
When I finally bought the game I was not disappointed, it was everything I expected. The gameplay is rather reminiscent of Guitar Hero. It is immensely fun with varying difficulties to fit exactly how casual or challenging experience you want. It has the perfect sound track i.e. whatever music you want. The graphics are simple but appealing. Being able to create your own custom character was an unexpected bonus too.

Of all the "Music Player" games, Melody's Escape is my favorite because it's actually a rhythm game like Dance Dance Revolution or Guitar Hero, rather than just a non-rhythm game that spawns enemies and items in time to the music like Beat Hazard or Audiosurf.
The beat detection is not perfect, but is immensely satisfying when it does work. I personally found that songs that had "Energy Peaks" instead of a normal BPM matched the music more closely, which is strange since I thought Energy Peaks was meant to be a back-up plan in case the tempo detection didn't work. So if there was a way to always use Energy Peaks, that would be an improvement.
For the downsides, as I mentioned the BPM detection-based algorithm is not perfect. To elaborate, the patterns often consist of one arrow and one button, alternating for a while, which makes it feel like you're playing alongside the song's metronome rather than the song itself. Additionally, the sections where Melody is walking are frustrating since she moves so slowly that visually, a note that's too far and a note that's in reach look too similar.
However, if you play this game to listen to your favorite music first and to test your skill second, it is great fun. I recommend it if you have a lot of music you like to listen to.

After Melody's Escape leaving Early Access, I decided to give the game a second try - seeing as during the first months of its release it gave me eye sores worse than any other game predictable. It definitely helps to have a 120+hz monitor or to enable/disable any sort of vsync features possible. Other features such as slow-mo and other eyecandy visuals have also been added since!
Anyway onto the real part of my review - Melody's Escape is a fantastic DDR alternative for your computer with the incredible ability to use your own songs! There are a few different difficulties you can choose when opening the game so you can play a super relaxing game to just enjoy the visuals and hit one button, or go full intense mode and hit more than one key at the same time! Overall for the price you're paying, Melody's Escape is a fantastic game if you're into DDR-related games, and has incredible modability, to the extent of being able to use a whole different mascot if you wanted! Worth a buy - highly recommended!

I don't usually write reviews because i feel it is unnecessary; But this time i felt i just had too due to the really undeserved bad feedback this game is getting from people who haven't even played it for a couple of hours.
Planet Explorer is a free-roam, open-world, voxel-based sci-fi RPG game.
You're free to roam and explore a huge procedurally generated world filled with different and colorful flora and fauna, gather resources to survive and have NPC characters join your colonization efforts, and fight off various creatures who'd have you for dinner or as a doormat.
The game has a story mode with a really interesting quest-driven plotline in which you explore the world after a crash landing and eventually gather the survivors for a colonization effort, while facing off with an unexcepted native threat.
The gameplay is somewhat articulate to grasp and isn't all that easy early on - which is why so many people tend to leave the game in the first hour of playing. However, after you get into the kiting and dodging mindset and start getting confidence with the commands and the somewhat wacky interface the door opens for a whole lot of fun.
The game world offers lots of fighting opportunities, but the main treat of the game is undoubtely resource gathering and crafting.
Aside from the standard RUST-like crafting system with which you can craft various basic parts, armors or food, players have acces to a voxel-based editor under which you can create your very own weapons and vehicles. This is probably the funniest part of the game and you're given complete freedom over choice of shape, materials, mechanics and so on. The game then calculates the weight in each resource you've created your item/vehicle out of and prepares a crafting recipe.
I said resource gathering: The totality of the game world can be harvested, broken, dug, chopped down - thanks to the dynamic voxel engine.
Additionally, players can create a colony -think of Terraria NPC hosting mechanics, but much deeper- which will require food, for which you have to hunt or farm, protection, and so on.
Overall the gameplay is vast, rich and addicting.
The main downside is the uncompleted state of the game, which is however kept under a continous updating regibe my dedicated developers. Aside from that, the animations and graphics are kind of wacky, but the gameplay strongly makes up for it.

Pros:
-Solid Zombie Atmosphere
-Great visual storytelling within the environment. This could have been a simple flash game, but instead they put a lot of 3D art into work here.
-Gameplay stays fresh enough to keep you interested throughout.
-An alright story with a plot twist that I half expected.
-'Mostly' good voice acting.
Cons:
-Riddled with unfair difficulty. There's a lot of on-the-spot reaction required of you, and many of these obstacles can only be passed via trial and error. Had to reload a lot, which is fine and all, but I just didn't feel like most of my deaths were fair.
-Despite having an alright story, the plot is often contrived and very formulaic.
-Still PLAYS completely like a flash game from 2004.
-Vevry clunky controls. Wall jumping is less effective if you don't run up into it from afar, but you wouldn't think it. Also, there's many doors locked with a padlocked chain. You have to either hit it with your axe, shoot it with a gun or just press the interact button to remove it - but only ONE of these work for each lock, and which one you have to do changes at random. It's very inconsistent and there's no real difference being made by any on-screen prompts. It's like 3 different mappers have worked on the game and didn't come to a consensus on how to script it. Stuff like this is really frustrating to me. Theres a host of other small issues that make the game feel clunky like this. At least three times I've got stuck in this game for 10+ minutes, having tried and failed specific stuff, only to retry the same actions and finding that it randomly worked that time, such as wall jumping, shooting something specific or jumping to avoid an obstacle.
-The main character has one of the worst voice actor I've ever heard. If you take a piece of solid wood and gave it voice, you'd get the voice actor of this game's protagonist. Everyone else has quality voice acting, so it's weird.

Far Cry 3 is a first person shooter that takes place on a lawless island ruled by pirates. You play as Jason Brody, a spoiled rich kid who has to learn how to survive in order to save his friends who were captured by the pirates.
Gameplay consists of typical FPS elements, but with lots of added new mechanics, like stealth killing and chaining kills together. Completing missions and killing enemies rewards XP to use in unlocking these new skills, and definitly adds more enjoyment in combat. The crafting system is simple, hunt animals, loot pelts, craft ammo pouches, bigger inventory, etc. Along with survival, you have to take on pirate outposts to create fast travel points across the map, while disabling radio towers reveals more of the map to you. Overall, combat feels good and enjoyable watching Jason basically go on massive murder spree.
Story is definitely a strong point in Far Cry 3. Jason is given a tattoo, symbolizing his status as a warrior. As you become more powerful, you add more to the tattoo, eventually becoming the ultimate warrior. The game provides one of the best villains in gaming history, taunting you and making you question your own sanity. The game does well in showing Jason maturing and realizing who he's meant to be.
Graphics in Far Cry 3 feel as if I'm really trapped on an island. The first person experince is excellent, and the island design is great. Lots of variety despite being a typical hot island. The environment feels living and interactable. Character design is also excellent, creating memorable faces as you experience variety of people.
Overall, Far Cry 3 is probably the best in the series with an intriguing story and enjoyable gameplay along with likeable characters and very impressive graphics system. Definitly reccommend picking up this game, especially on a sale.

Cons - you do tend to see the same layouts over and over again - even with random missions, troopers aren't radically different from one another in their personalities.
I also wish that there was some form of negotiation option to try to talk to folks while also inserting your SWAT team and performing recon or stealth takedowns - something approaching aspects of SWAT 2 with occasional non-violent resolutions. I do wish that more missions featured 4 man teams.

Great game, graphically wise i'd say the best of any FPS with zombies involved. You won't find these graphics in any other zombie game. The gore is great, and the whole atmosphere with the classic zombies is great. The game modes are great, even the Hunted game mode imo. Many complain about this game mode that there's just people walking around trying to kill each other but that's the whole point of this game mode! It's Deathmatch, in the survival world of Contagion.
But don't think it's easy just to shoot someone you wander in to, the gameplay mechanics still force you to actually aim and control your shots, instead of just spraying n' praying.
I came across this moment I once had in Hunted which reminded me of movie-like scenes, where this stranger came spraying at me with his AK 74U around 20 meters in front of me behind a fence, while I gave surpressing fire and we both walked sideways firing shots at each other, with me having a 9 mm pistol and obviously having a disadvantage weapon-wise. And at this one moment I decided to calmly aim for his head as I crouched, zombies around him, with my pistol while he just kept spraying like a maniac, and I ended up shooting him in the head. With zombies between us, in the dark city, this was one of the most epic moments I had so far in this game. The overall scenery in this game is somehow amazing and really hits the nail on the head for those of you who truly love zombie survival games and things alike.
With that, it's epic as a zombie genre lover to actually decide to wander off while in a gunfight with a stranger, hiding in the bushes  and wandering off the city blocks, the house blocks, the piled abandoned cars, the government barricades etc etc hoping that stranger gets noticed by zombies and perhaps other strangers around, which will happen frequently, give you an advantage into getting away and finding new supplies again, and surviving. What this game is really about!!
People who can't seem to get the hang out of this should rely more on actual tactics, like the one I just told you about.
Really, people whining about the Hunted game mode should concentrate more on their own path while continuously watching their backs, then they will get much further and actually become able to be one of the last 3 players alive, and win the round. It's all about the TACTICS, which makes this game great as itself, because it's not just a simple shooter.
All the other game modes are great too, and I've had tons of fun playthroughs on Escape for example, deciding where to hide out until extraction, while fighting off hordes of incoming zombies. And those zombies are aggressive even though they don't run! Some somehow still limb in quite a fast pace towards ya, so good aiming is a must. They're far more of a threat than the zombies in other known co-op zombie games. which really nails the pace the whole zombie genre is about. Slow zombies, yet the whole sphere is action paced.
And those zombie hordes keep coming, so you better off sparing your ammo for the right heads to shoot, while scavenging for more.
This game gives you movie-like experiences, and is a piece of art in itself. It reminds me a lot of all of those classic Romero zombie movies!

Just picture a vast continent filled with 22 cities and 48 castles each with several villages split amongst 6 factions constantly at war fighting for control and it's all your playground.
Do you play the noble knight, swearing homage to a lord and defending the poor peasants? How about a bandit pillaging the villages and raiding trade caravans to line your pockets? Or maybe you have aspirations for the throne. Build an army and carve out an empire under your own banner. These are but a few options that you can take.
There are a sizeable amount of skill options that allow the creation of many types of characters from the heavily armoured knight to the swift horse archer.
The game has a rather steep learning curve however practice and patience will give results.
The difficulty is easily customised to your preference from the options menu.
The graphics are dated by today's standards and there are still some bugs.
The multiplayer is still active at the time of writing with many dedicated players.
It offers multiple game modes / Deathmatch(free for all) / Team Deathmatch / Siege (teams attack and defend castles) / Capture the Flag / Battle (no respawns).
The community is a mixed bunch, with about an equal split between friendly and ill mannered players.
There is a vast active modding community that offers players the ability to change the settings and mechanics of the game. Genkokujo(Sengoku jidai era of Japan), A Clash of Kings(Game of Thrones) Anno Domini(13th Century Europe), Just to name a few.
~Vast Customisation
~Re-playability
~Modding
~Skill based Gameplay
~Learning Curve
~Hit and Miss Community
~Dated Graphics

Warband is a very frustrating game for me as it offers something that intrigues me: it merges a roleplay game with a strategy game while at the same time implementing them so weakly.
Take the roleplay aspect
You play a character that  levels and has skills that you can develop. You can also equip that character with weapons, armor and such that you find in the loot of defeated enemy armies or that you can buy in one of the towns.  Eventually you can even recruit other characters and level and equip them too.
But what lacks is actually a good story line with an captivating background and good dialogues. In fact there is not much roleplay to be done.  There are lords and kings.. but they are all faceless ententies and limited to a set of basic quests.
Take warfare
At first the battles are fascinating. You don't look down up them as in most games, but are actually there down on the ground among your troops thanks to the 1st/3rd person look. And that gives you more of a feeling that you are actually there.
But when you start to get more troops you want to be able use tactics, but there is hardly any tool to control your armies properly. In fact because battles are limited you won't have all troops on the battlefield and you have a limited control over them. Most battles thus are nothing more than masses of men hacking away at eachother.
Recruting of troops is nice until you are somewhat further into the game. Than you find you have to harvest the villages for recruits on a permanent basis. You find out that you spend a lot of time running around the map recruiting troops and training them. Interesting at first, but when the game progresses and you need more of them this harvesting and recruiting becomes tedious. In many games this process is automated.. but not in this game.
Take diplomacy, trade and economy
Diplomacy comes down to just four options: declare war, end war, submit to an adversary and say hello. There are no such things like making trade agreements, alliances, sending gifts or threathen.
Trade can be done by buying items in one town and selling them in another town. Given the fact that you have a limited inventory, most towns have only a few items and a profitable town is usually at the other side of the map, trade is too time intensive, especially as compared to the option selling loot and captured troops.
Economy consists of taxing your lands and buying a factory, one per town at the max. You have almost no control over taxing or over your factories.
Take the relations you with your lords
Eventually when you establish your own empire, you will need some lords to help you out. These lords have likes and dislikes. You have a very limited control over that. You can give them a fief, which makes them more happy with you, but makes all the others less happy with you. Given the fact that when you give a lord a fief his happiness will increase with say 10 while those of the others will decrease with 1 or 2 you know that you are limited to ten lords at the most as they will all overall decrease more than you can increase them by given each of them a fief.
Take the sieges
Sieges are terrible boring affairs after a while. You can try to leave sieges to the AI, which results in tremendous losses. So you are forced to organise them yourself..which generally comes down to having your missle troops kill all their troops until you can either assault them or until they have nobody left.
And on goes the list of weakly implemented things.
I am surely amazed that people find it a good game.. and if so I am happy for them, but you must have a lot of stamina to go through having to besiege each and every castle and town, some of them twice, just to beat the game.  At some point the game should end.. if you have like 75% of the map.. or are so powerful that others should submit to you. But you have to defeat them all by conquering the whole map. It is tedious and boring and when achieved you get a simple message. I therefore won't play it again. Nor am I enticed to play sequels.
However... I have seen that there is an expansion called with fire and sword..and it seems to have improved on some aspect of the game. Perhaps improved enough to make it interesting.

I absolutely love Hotline Miami 1. Nailed it on all accounts and a perfect balance of unforgiveable gameplay and high speed action. How they managed to ♥♥♥♥ this up in a sequel, I don't seem to understand.
To me, it all has to do with a couple of gameplay choices the developers made that don't add up:
1) The difficulty is higher by a mile. This could be a good thing, except the difficulty is harder simply because of small errors. The feeling of being cheated arises when you die again because one of the many bugs still left in the game. It doesn't feel like an honest and deserved death, because of many instances.
2) One of those reasons, by far, is the fact that enemies recently inhabit bigger maps. Bigger than your SHIFT-view allows you to look around. This wouldn't be a problem if the enemies wouldn't be able to detect you on a distance greater than your view. This creates angsty gameplay where just popping out of the corner to look around can get you killed. I would go into smaller rooms more up north and push through just to see more of the map, which kills the pace and also idea of the gameplay. Only one scared tactic remains and that is to lure enemies to your hideout. Only way to survive.
3) The many bugs in the walls, the doors and enemies are killing it. Cheating is an easy option, when you can go out of the levels and walk around them, and as you can read from the other two options, sometimes feels like the only way.
4) The options of characters and including different playing styles forces the player instead of, like HM1, offering you to play the way you like. One newly found playing style that plays horribly bad is the dual team where melee and shooting is brought together. As the second character is not aiming from the same spot as your meleecharacter, shooting is a nightmare.
These things all could be forgiven if it wasn't for the fact that it sucks out so much fun and speed out of the game. I'm trying to plow through one level at a time, just to get it over with.

Far Cry 3 is a first person shooter that takes place on a lawless island ruled by pirates. You play as Jason Brody, a spoiled rich kid who has to learn how to survive in order to save his friends who were captured by the pirates.
Gameplay consists of typical FPS elements, but with lots of added new mechanics, like stealth killing and chaining kills together. Completing missions and killing enemies rewards XP to use in unlocking these new skills, and definitly adds more enjoyment in combat. The crafting system is simple, hunt animals, loot pelts, craft ammo pouches, bigger inventory, etc. Along with survival, you have to take on pirate outposts to create fast travel points across the map, while disabling radio towers reveals more of the map to you. Overall, combat feels good and enjoyable watching Jason basically go on massive murder spree.
Story is definitely a strong point in Far Cry 3. Jason is given a tattoo, symbolizing his status as a warrior. As you become more powerful, you add more to the tattoo, eventually becoming the ultimate warrior. The game provides one of the best villains in gaming history, taunting you and making you question your own sanity. The game does well in showing Jason maturing and realizing who he's meant to be.
Graphics in Far Cry 3 feel as if I'm really trapped on an island. The first person experince is excellent, and the island design is great. Lots of variety despite being a typical hot island. The environment feels living and interactable. Character design is also excellent, creating memorable faces as you experience variety of people.
Overall, Far Cry 3 is probably the best in the series with an intriguing story and enjoyable gameplay along with likeable characters and very impressive graphics system. Definitly reccommend picking up this game, especially on a sale.

You also have a weird fetish for radio towers, but people give you free stuff for going to the top of them, so why not? Oh yeah there are a bunch of bad guys constantly trying to kill you too.
Yup, just another day in paradise.
The good:
+ A shooter pretty much anyone can pick up and play. The easiest difficulty I didn’t have a problem playing with a steam controller.
+ Impressive visuals. Can still challenge even a GTX 1080.
+ A sizable world that I never really felt bored in.
+ Decent story, but the game is not that story heavy. Think GTA V not the Witcher 3.
+ Great voice acting with very interesting characters.
+ A decent mix of missions.
+ A satisfying kind of bad♥♥♥♥♥ending.
+ Trippy drug induced sequences add some artistic flair.
The bad:
- Weird technical glitches, at least 2 missions I had to replay because I was unable to loot an important body.
- Crappy save system. Can only save outside of mission. Event then some times when you save you don’t end up where you think you will on load.
- Occasional crash, this will cost you some time because of the save system.
- Weird performance deterioration between save points / transitions.
- Bad driving controls. Driving is overly challenging on a controller.
- Couldn’t get it to recognize the steam controller. There is a controller mode but had to map controller to keyboard / mouse. Less desirable because you have to remember what everything is mapped to.
-Uplay. Need I say more?
TLDR;
A pretty good looking shooting romp around a paradise island that I think most people would be able to play. Story is OK if not a little weird. A few technical glitches hold this game back from being highly recommend, but if you can overlook that it’s still a decent game. I’ve played much worse so I say give it a shot.

As much as want to enjoy Door Kickers, as I am a big fan of Tactic RTS's , this one has given me the most frustation yet, and not in a good, challenging way either. Although my hours spent on this game at the time of this review is few, the movement mechanics have already hindered a positive impression from me. Often times, the fault in my plans is not in my ability, but in the broken mechanics of the game.
When things work out and bugs such as shooting at the wall because the target is to my characters adjacent isn't a problem, the game is fun. Watching my team swiftly move in and clearing the area under a designated time feel rewarding and I can see what the dev's envision. But, having a constant struggle with things like redoing my carefully laid out plan because adding a step would somehow erase the previous ones, or, being unable to peak around the corner of a doorway because the action menu of breaching methods block my cursor from selecting my move node, breaks the experience for me.
Among all my concerns however, the two big annoyances are when my team disregards the assigned command call (ex. Alpha, Bravo), and moves in on their own, and, when the units move before clearing a newly breached room. The work around for for the first issue is to redo my whole plan which, as mentioned before, is a chore that takes away from the fun.
Although my review has mostly been negative, this is not a bad game at all. In fact, I would recommend you to give it as try as this review is soley based on my own critique. You may overlook these minor flaws and thoroughly enjoy this game. But for me, these minor issues were little details that became a major hassle as I played on.

The developers have put a lot of work into this game and that has come a long way since when I picked this game up a few years ago.
The ability to create new weapons, armor, vehicles, and items to place around your colony is taken to new heights in this game. There is a built in modeling program to design things to make your gameplay one-of-a-kind for you.

Planet explorers is the best open world sand box game that I have everr played. The combat is excellent with many different types of weapons to use and a wide variety of animals and aliens to hunt and all of them give some type of resource upon killing them, usually meat or some item that can be sold to vendors for currency. The crafting system is excellent and has many armor pieces that can be crafted out of differnt level resources from wood to diamonds. The crafting system also allows you to design and build custom armor, weapons, and aircraft/vehicles/boats all with their own individual stats based on what material you used and how much of that material is in the design. You can also manage a colony and build many useful buildings in the colony such as replicator, training station, repair facilities and more. You can build a tram in the game world and then ride in that tram. There are many quests to do in the story mode. There is a good farming system once you have a colony set up. There is a lot of things to do in this game. I highly recommend it.

Sometimes a game is made that hasn't got the highest grade graphics, seems a bit simple and perhaps might be considered 'limited', but then that game is actually incredibly fantastic and you can easily play it for hours. Mount and Blade: Warband is a example of such a game. It is essentially a rpg strategy game which allows you to command epic armies into battle, as well as manage your fiefs (villages), castles and towns for your money. You create your character, give him a character background and lead him onto the battlefield.
As if management and battle wasn't enough for your medieval tastes, there is the option to marry noble ladies, get in good with local lords and even (if you work hard at it) work your way to becoming king of a land. Going over all these little details will quickly see you playing the game for whole days at a time. Most importantly however, it is just very fun! If the graphics hold up at one point it is during the most important part of the game...battle! Slashing your way through the ranks of the enemy has never felt so satisfying. So basically if you haven't got this game already, you better buy it!

Melody’s Escape is a great game for relaxing and unwinding. It’s not a game that you can play for hours straight usually, for it would get boring then, but I would highly recommend it because of how calming it is. You can even choose how hard/easy to make the game, and different modes are better for your different moods.
The game allows you to listen to any song you have saved on your computer and create a specialized obstacle course based upon the game’s analysis of that song. It is like Guitar Hero except that you can choose any song you want. Sometimes the analysis of the song is not perfect and the beats are not perfectly coordinated, but there have been other times that the created “obstacle course” fits the song amazingly well. A song that changes tempo will have the runner Melody speed up and slow down. You will push buttons that coordinate with the main beats of the song or the notes of the melody. How Melody navigates her obstacles may change when the song transitions to a new section that has a different tempo, intensity, or mood. Sometimes you might hold down the buttons for long notes. It’s really quite cool when the game gets it down cold and you feel like you’re watching a music video of yourself playing.
(The best song I’ve ever seen in Melody’s Escape thus far is XOXO by Secret and Whisper. WOW).
Even when Melody’s Escape does not get the rhythm down completely correctly (and it’s a hard algorithm to do… I’ve seen my professional music composition software programs fail on this front) (and frankly Melody’s Escape does PRETTY WELL), it’s always visually stunning. The game is beautiful. The design is artistic and engaging. However, I do warn people who have challenges with fast motion or flashing lights that this might be too visually intense for you. That is the only visual negative of this game that I can think of.
For people who like to unwind listening to music but want a little extra to do with their hands, Melody’s Escape is perfect.

The game could easily be descibed as Left 4 Dead in a Warhammer setting.
To me that is a good thing because I'm a huge fan of both, but it is so much more.
I've played quite some Skaven in the tabletop, this game absolutely nails the atmosphere!
Extreme attention to detail for the lore and the sound effects/music are spot on.
There are some bugs that need fixing, but overall I love every second of it.
At first I was afraid that the hack and slash would get repetitive soon, but the combat sytem itself and general tactics go deeper than you'd think at first glance.
Because of the higher than average difficulty you're always on your toes.
Even with more experienced players on voice chat there is always a chance to get wiped the second you get cocky (or unlucky with specials).
The campaign is relatively short with 13 maps (Skaven lore strikes again), after that you repeat maps to get better loot for your favourite characters. For now this is still nonstop fun and excitement, but that will only last till you get good stuff for all characters.
So on the part where this game will fail or succeed in the long run: MORE CONTENT!
I'll turn to CapsLock once more when I say: VERSUS!
Will need some heavy tweaking on certain specials, but it could be awesome.
Extra maps/enemies/characters/loot are always nice.
The enemies atm are almost all straight copies from Left 4 Dead, not a bad thing because they work.
Looking at the lore though, there are interesting options to try some original units like the Ratling Gunner (once again lore love for letting it jam from time to time).
For example: Jezzails (snipers), Verminlord (bossfight), Hellpit Abomination (bossfight), Plague Censer Bearers (I know Pestilens is on vacation, but they're just too awesome)
But before I get to fullblown rambling, if you like co-op games and even remotely like the fantasy setting, get this now!

Hotline Miami 2 is a good game that would be better if the first one wasn't around
More specifically, it's a lot messier and less polished than HM1. The story lacks the intense intruigue and mystery the first one had and instead ops to tell a massive, epic story about everyone on the face of the earth going nuts after some nobody in a letterman jacked killed a bunch of mobsters in the first game, and how it all ends up for them. The story has a lot of cool MOMENTS, but is overarchingly hard to follow and all over the place, like a painting cut up into a jigsaw puzzle.
The gameplay is a lot dodgier, the level design in particular feels very... malicious. The game can get very frustrating, due to levels designed not to be cleared in a variety of different ways but to punish players who aren't on their A-Game. On a second or third run-through, you will eventually get the hang of some of the levels and start having some honest to goodness knock-your-socks-off fun, but first time through you will probably just be stuck baiting enemies around corners and spraying down hallways too far to see down because you either can't see the whole level or you overlooked a window or patrolling fat guy.
The core of the game isn't as good, but everything else blows the first game out of the water. The sound track especially is probably the best I've ever heard, and has pretty much taken over my music library.
Basically, if the first game was a small but lovely and inventive flat that did wonders with an unimpressive plot of land and budget, then the second game is a bigger, better house that looks awesome and has all sorts of cool little features but the floor is squeaky, the foundation is just 1 or 2 degrees crooked and people keep shooting you through the windows.

Mount and Blade, the first game, was brilliant and new thinking. It felt like the Total War games, but in first person. The graphics wasn't that good, I can tell you that, but everything else was perfect. Balanced gameplay, good soundtracks, detailed history and background, smart battle system and total freedom to do what you want. It had everything except graphics. But that was part of the charm. Then there was Warband. The developers managed to make a nearly perfect game even better.
Warband, unlike the first game, have a more up-to-date graphic. Still not Total War beautiful, but it's better than before. But there's more content, more freedom. When I first sat down and played Warband, I was struck by the in-game depth. You really feel the control and freedom. You want to be a leader of a band of mercenaries? Well, be that then. You want to be an succesfull merchant? Be that. You want to be an outlaw king, in a castle up north? What are you waiting for? The choice is yours. You decide what you want to be or do.
The strategy and battle gameplay is like the first game. At the start of the battle you begin with your army and you at one side, and the enemy at the oppsite side. You can give orders like: infantry in the front forming a shield wall, with archers in the back, and cavalry protecting the flanks. As the battle progresses, you will probably change orders to your tropps. Maybe you see that they lack cavalry, so while your infantry holds their infantry in check, you ride up behind them and crush them from behind with a mighty cavalry charge. You have total control and it's a really easy system to use. You'll figure it out quickly.
There is no real story or questline in this game, you just play and decide what your story is. Like I said before, this game is all about freedom. There are too many features for me to cover here in one review, but if your interested you can find all of them really easy with just one google search.That's it. Have fun doing whatever you want.

So I had this game gifted to me as soon as it came on steam early access on sale for $5 around December 2013 played it for an hour before giving up and uninstalling. Recently I got a week ban on CSGO and was looking for something to kill time until my ban ended. I played this game again for about 7 hours of May 2015 and there were plenty that has changed.
Improvements From Early Access:
Loading Times:
When this game first came out, the load times were absolutely horrendous. Taking 2-3 minutes to even load a map and 30-45 seconds to load the opening menu. Now using the same computer at launch, it takes 10-15 to load the menu and a minute at the most to load the server.
Improved AI:
The ai survivors in the extraction mode at launch were basically potatoes. They would follow on command but were unarmed and didn't react to zombies. Now survivors are armed with basics weapons, usually a pistol but I have seen them armed with a shotgun and now react to the zombies.
Cons From Early Access:
Community:
Originally this game and all it's servers were packed from its kick starter hype, finding around a 100 people on 15 servers just on the first tab while I was browsing. Now in May 2015, I can find around 10-20 total in all the occupied servers. What I've seen through steam forums is that monochrome has lost most of its original team, and that promised DLC and kick starter backer bonuses were never delivered. Currently at the moment this community is so small I practically play with tr same guys every night and I practically know everyone's first name and basic information.
Regular Review:
Just playing as if I had no knowledge of before.
So loading this game for the first time again in a year I decided to run a game of Hunted, a game mode of up to 16 people surviving in an open arena until there is one. Unfortunately there was only one occupied server with around 10 people playing on the same map (Aurora States). So I spawn in, the map is a dark zombie overrun surburban neighborhood, and I start with a pistol a baseball bat, and some ammo. I hear the moans of zombies and gunshots in the distance, and quickly run to a nearby house and hide in the garage. I think some of the zombies on the street heard me as I hear the front door starting to break, suddenly machine gun fire breaks out and I hear someone enter the house. Suddenly I hear a player enter the house, because it has irregular footsteps and I hear their flashlight flick back and forth. Paralyzed I aim my gun at the door waiting, as the man is going door to door looking for supplies. Then I hear a crash of the window glass breaking and a hail of gun fire and the screams of a man dying. Probably unaware that anyone else was in the house, he opens the garage door where I immediately pump his body with lead. There I stood, looking at the loot of the two men, with an ar15, a revolver, grenade, and around 80 rounds of ammo. This was the most heart pounding zombie experience I've experienced in a zombie game, including DAyZ Standalone and No More Room In Hell
Pros:
Sound:
The guns in this game sound fast, and powerful but not too much where it overdoes it. The rhythmic beat of the small caliber mp5, to the thundering sound of the remington sniper, sound responsive and fluid.
Controls:
Controls feel semi-realistic blending the arcade like movement of hl2 and the movement of Insurgency is the best way I can describe it. However you can see your ammo count, see a stamina bar, and see your health which makes it more of an arcade kind of feel.
Infected:
Zombies react to noise and sight very well in this game. Run across a street into a home spraying an ar15, and you'll get a horde surrounding you within minutes. Also a very cool element is that everytime a zombie hits you, you have a chance of getting infected, where your screen and sound will blur and turn muffled until you turn. However I wish there was a way to revert it or slow it down like the pills in No More In Hell
Cons:
Characters:
There is no story in contagion per say, but all of your selectable characters have a "backstory" which consists of a paragraph description in the selection menu. How am I supposed to even care about these characters when there's no reason to. Also they have no personalities whatsoever and all have the same 18 or so lines in the quick command bar and don't even seem to know each other. Overall worst cast of chaarcters in a video game, don't even know their names to criticize them individually.
Weapon Balance:
The weapons in contagion especially the melee weapons are extremely unbalanced. How can a zombie take a full swing from a fireaxe, and live but die from 1 hit on a Kabar Knife. Melee weapons are a joke, and if you find one you should immediately drop it. Okay now you might say, balancing melee weapons is difficult. Well look at No More Room In Hell, a similar game also based on the source engine. In that game, there are heavy swings, which take time to load up and can decapitate zombies, and fast swings which usually don't do anything, both are dependent on the weapon you're using and how much stamina you have left.
Melee weapons aside, the main weapon you'll be using are the guns. However these are horribly unbalanced especially against zombies. I haven't played enough to see of it makes a difference against players in hunted, but here every gun can one tap a zombie with one well placed headshot. Whether it's a high powered sniper, or your 9mm starting handgun, it all feels the same. Also there doesn't seem to be a bullet dropoff damage, as I can get kills with a colt from about 30 meters away with a headshot. Compared to no more room in hell, .22 or 9mm ammo takes 2 headshots to connect, meaning you'll need to use .45 or higher to get a 1 hit headshot.
Music:
Bland, forgettable, don't even remember how it sounded most of the time. No contrast either? Always stays at the same volume except in a loading screen when it starts to fade out.
Lack of Maps:
Maps are very limited, and the community is fairly dead, so no new maps are coming out to play on via modding workshop
Lack Of Map Change or Vote Kick:
Servers seem to be stuck playing the same map over and over with no way to change the map,meaning once you beat a map, you just play it again. So that means everyone is stuck playing one extraction server on Aurora Estates, and escape on Roanake PD. Also we can't vote kick any trolls, and with a severe lack of community, I've never seen a server admin who could help
Level Progression:
Playing a coop map such as Escape on Roanake PD is especially unfriendly for new spawns. Instead of placing a checkpoint t to spawn new players, they spawn right at the beggining, leaving them up to 3-9 objectives behind everyone else which is something that should've been fixed a long time ago
Overall:
Pretty average zombie FPS with some cool ideas but poor execution, and the community has suffered from it in terms of number, and overall support for this game.
Score 6/10
