This game is amazing. If you want a FPS that is open world, this is a great one to jump into since there is a ton of nice gameplay and a good lot of things to do.
Despite being a total blast, honestly, the story irks me in more ways than one.
It swapped a "save your friends and escape pirates" thriller to become what the game truly is: Massacring evil pirates that deserve it in the most bad-*** ways possible.
Not that the second part of that is even bad, it's just that the game blatantly lies to you about what it is when you jump into it. (Spoilers ahead, but as I said the story isn't worth much anyways).
Let me give it to you this way. You are a socialite college kid on a trip with your best friends. You've never killed in your life. You worry about relationships and normal people things. You go to bars and party. You get kidnapped by pirates. These pirates scare you, keeping you for ransom, generally making you pee your pants. Not knowing what to do, your older military(?) brother leads you to an escape, and after the head "I am de capitan naow" kills your sibling, you get chased through the jungle while your flight instinct kicks into overdrive. You lose everything. You escape the prison camp, get rescued, and not even 2 seconds later you are leading a charge into an enemy outpost and gutting people with machetes. That's not an exaggeration, it's the next thing you do and the first thing you learn. Not even that long later, you find all of your conviniently alive friends... and then don't leave the island, because the game just switched antagonists and now you are psychotic warrior with a bloodlust. Talk about pacing.
Had it just presented it like that from the beginning I still would have enjoyed the game, but it threw probably one of the most suspenseful taglines down the drain to become one of those games where you remove the criminal scum from a potentially nice place and save the values of the free world in the process.
It's not boring, it's not a grind, but the story is a lie, and the character development of the protagonist from a college kid into a warlord is just putrid and rushed. And the worst part is that Vaas, that guy in the red tank on the cover - he's only your enemy for not even half of the game. Despite being a very believable crazy warlord character that is perfect for this flavor of game, he hardly lasts long. You know what I mean. Don't pretend you don't. And the guy they replace him with is just generic to the point of being laughable.
There was so much potential with drawing out the "saving your friends" arch but most of your pals that you are lead to believe are important hardly have any lines or much of a personality beyond what you see in the first few hours. Had they just made it about your friends (and actually gave them character development) this might have been my favorite shooter. Like... they don't even help you. It's not even a team effort once you "liberate" everyone. That's how much they messed it up. You switch friends and the story continues on, with resident batman Jason Brozinsky, taking down all who share one of under 10 reused pirate models. Seriously. You go from some kid to Rambo in not even an hour after you finish the prologue. What are your friend's names again?
So don't buy it for the story, instead, buy it for the beautiful map with a ton of lore, the fact that you can drop onto an enemy from the sky and then in one fell swoop take all of his buddies with him, and the fact that you can take down entire strongholds without being seen due to a great stealth system.

Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, much like its predecessor, is an ambiguous, interesting, yet very flawed game.
One of the big things that Hotline Miami 2 does that is interesting is that it splits the story up between multiple characters, rather than just 2.
It runs off of a similar system to its predecessor, a top-down view, with heavy focus on twitch reaction times and awareness.
First the pros:
The multiple characters with their intertwining stories are incredibly neat - one of the characters is a writer who does not like to kill, which leads to missions centered around nonlethal takedowns. That was fun and interesring!
The mask mechanic has been ramped up. And by that, I mean, the mask effects ('mask'. Not all the characters wear masks.) are so absolutely diverse, and it's excellent.
The combat, like the first game, is satisfying and fun. The weapons are more diverse, and it's fun.
The cons:
The game is janky as hell in many ways. For one, AI jumps between being hyperaware to the point of being superhuman, and between being so unaware that they must have brain damage. This makes planning ahead very difficult, not fully knowing how quickly the AI will react.
A big issue I had is that, although the doors appear to be wood, thay seem to function as pure durasteel, seeing as they are utterly inpenetrable. This wouldn't be a problem so much if some of the AI (namely the attack dogs) weren't able to attack through doors. This gave me a whole lot of grief and I ended up being frustrated more often than not.
The AI also have hawkeyes, and they'll often bullseye you from the other side of the level. This is alleviated somewhat by the ability to 'aim', which allows you to look farther. Not far enough, though, most of the time.
Also, you don't add pseudo boss fights where you need to run in circles until something happens that allows you to fight the boss some time after running in circle, but you still don't know how, and you die in one hit. THIS IS NOT FUN. This is just frustrating.
In a nutshell, I would say that overall, I enjoyed this game. There's just a lot to be frustrated over. There's a large portion of the game that I still look at and thing: 'Did I have fun?'   I really cannot tell.
It's worth its price though. I'd give it a buy. If you enjoy it, great. If not-... It didn't cost you all that much. If it's on sale, even better!

It's Call of Duty... don't be surprised.  Many have begun ripping into the Call of Duty franchise for their lack of originality.  I suppose one could make that argument, but I think they would be missing the point.
I've never looked upon the Call of Duty franchise as a game, at least not a regular FPS.  I enjoy Call of Duty for one simple reason, it's an experience.  Period.  It's about 6 to 8 hours of interactive movie making whereby you are along for the ride in typically fantastic, far from reality, scenes of epics battles where even the action will slow down and wait for you should you decide to stroll off to the side somewhere.  Not to worry, they'll call you back soon enough.
I had some optimisation issues, but my rig has begun showing its age, so maybe just me.  Otherwise, graphics - solid, controls - solid, sound - fantastic, voice - good.
In the end, if you're in the mood for an intereactive cinematic gameplay rush.  This game is for you.  If you're looking for a cutting edge FPS, keep on walkin' soldier.  I liked it for what it is, an experience!

This game is crazy fun, even in it's beta stage. The environments are gorgeous (I LOVE the bioluminescent trees and flowers), the light level at night is reasonably realistic (if you don't have light sources on you, it's really hard to see - which is as it should be imo), and the tools you use to modify the world around you work well also - shovels clear more land than picks, but yeild fewer usable resources; and unlike many fantasy games there is a good amount of medeival-style feel that for me, really accents the sci-fi nature of the game *very* well.  Swords and Guns (including Flare and Rope guns) in the same game at base? YES!
It's not the kind of game that's going to give you a ton of objectives and tedious grinding to do - there is a bit of that in story mode, but it strikes me more like a long tutorial.  I haven't yet finished Story Mode, though - I spend waaay too much time just exploring the beautiful environment and running the hell away from giant flying stingrays with lazer beams on their frickin' foreheads.
The best part, in my opinion, is the ability to start a colony and build it up from scratch, from the buildings to who gets to live there, and gardening/farming in addition to building your own guns and vehicles.  I'm a huge Harvest Moon, Sims and Dwarf Fortress fan, and this game seems to take the things I liked the best about each of those and rolls it into one lovely app. The monsters you fight will even destroy your constructed buildings so you have to be strategic when fighting on your home turf!
I like how there isn't any money/gold in the game, either.  The closest thing that passes for currency is the Meat (the same kind you find on animals), and credits you get once you start a colony.
The only real gripes I have about this game is the lack of detail on the overworld map (Not so bad in Story Mode, but Adventure and Build modes appear to not have any automated mapping ability, it's just a solid blue background with icons on it.  Though you *can* automatically fast travel to your colony and other landmarks the game creates, but at this time you can't fast travel to map markers you place yourself. The other thing I get a little annoyed by is that the buildings in pre-established villages in Adventure mode can't have objects placed on them unless you've built overtop of a space with the Build tools - for example, if you want to decorate a room on the second floor of the default Hotel building, you have to use the Build tools to overlap the flooring and walls, otherwise your lamps and chairs and stuff will go straight through it.
I wish it wasn't such a RAM hog, but it does perform very well aside from that, and the graphics settings actually seem to make a difference.  Very very few crashes.  Overall it's one of my favorites - been following it almost since the beginning, v 0.3x.  It's come a LONG way since then, and the devs are super dedicated.  You can tell this game is a labor of love - it shows!

There's always the impulse to compare it to certain other sandbox games... but I don't know how. Planet Explorers plays like an RPG, crafting game, exploration, adventure, even a 3D modelling program!
* It's like Elements: You start with initial resources like plants and minerals, and can craft new technologies & accessories.
* It's like an RPG: Beautiful open world, small & large enemies, Obtain missions by talking to NPC's, some of which can join your party and eventually your colony (city)! They will fight with you & you can equip them with weapons, armors, items, or just give them stuff to carry.
* It's a sandbox: make tools to help you dig out the world. Search for ore deposits using your 3D scanner then use them to construct just about anything! (not player-designed clothing)
* It's 3D modelling software: Construct swords, shields, guns, land/sea/air vehicles, or just decoration objects like stairs, utilities, household, really anything you can think of!
Custom models are inserted into the game like this: If you have the resources required to build it, they will automatically be removed from your inventory and the object will appear. You can interact with it or pick it up anytime that you are next to it. An 'approved' build that has been picked up may be reused until it is destroyed; once it's built, it's built.
I have spent over 10 hours on Story mode so far and I have only just built my first car. I have leather armor, sword & shield, bow & rifle. My 2 followers have Steel armor & swords; they 'tank' while I shoot. I have barely explored the south-central part of the island. There are videos of immense constructs and firepower, enemies and adventure. I have only barely begun, and I am very much addicted :).

What I like: It's not all about the money.  Some people may have commented that it is all about micro-transactions, but it really is not.  Everything is earnable at some point in the game.  Also, even if people decide to spend money to get things faster, the weapons really aren't unbalanced.  Also, I've noticed many people have complained about the matching system.  But to be honest, I kill higher ranks all the time.  It really isn't that hard.  Also, three sticky grenades can blow up the Tiger 4, which is one of the if not the most powerful German tank.  So infantry are not push-overs nor any player for that matter.  I also like that you can modify many weapons in many ways. You can also steal vehicles, quite an interesting thing.   All of the upgrades have pros and cons as well (with a few exceptions).  Another interesting mechanic is being able to ride on tanks so if the tank is full you can still get somewhere fast.  I also like that vehicles can flip (more on the realism side).
What I Dislike: The game can be a bit laggy at some points.  Also, whenever you exit a jeep or motorcycle in kills you at a certain speed.   Making it impossible to avoid death if you have an imbecile for a driver.  Not to mention the ragdolls are pretty unrealistic (which doesn't really matter gameplay-wise).  I usually don't care about silly things like this, but I just find it weird that when a car hits into me my dead body flies up 20 ft in the air.  Now there is one more thing, which is that Russia (I believe) was referred to as an ally on the description of one of the SMGs.  But when the Soviet Union was added, they fight Americans.  Now I do realize it just makes it fair to Germany, but why can't they add Japan and call it even?   Or will they ...
Overall:  I enjoy this game very much.  Fun and addicting.  I'd give it 8/10 stars.  It just lacks a bit of realism in some areas and can randomly lag.

Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide is a game that shares many similarities with the Left4Dead series, with the main difference being the removal of PvP modes and a heavy focus on aquiring better equipment for your character(s), of which there are 5. Each Character feels very unique from the others, and has an impressive array of primary and secondary weapon varients to unlock. (Gear is unlocked by a single drop at the end of each mission, regardless of length.)
Unfortunately, the same loot system that offers such a wide variety of playstyles and customization also drags the game down into what is essentially a grind for the best gear. Bonus objectives (tomes and grimoires) can be picked up throughout the level, and improve your chance at better rewards if carried to the end of the level, while the difficulty chosen decides what loot can be dropped at the end of the mission.
Because of this design, players often run short, high difficulty missions repeatedly with the same bonus objectives each time. Adding to the monotony is the lack of randomization in each level that Left4Dead showed with it's Director system. It often feels that player skill and game knowlage takes a backseat to your equipment and knowlage of cheese strategies for the level, which feels even worse without PvP.
TL:DR It's a co-op survival with well made combat and classes but suffers from grindy progression and over-reliance on equipment rather than player skill. Reccomended for Warhammer fans or fans of Borderlands, Warframe, etc.

The singleplayer portion is open roam, scattered with collectibles and enemy outposts. Every enemy outpost is unique and can be captured by defeating all enemies within. The enemy outposts act like a puzzle, as there are different ways to tackle the situation as well as different enemies that change the usual dynamic such as armored personnel or sharpshooters. The game allows the player in the freeroam sections to either approach combat in complete stealth, broken stealth, or alerted; Players are free to choose whichever way they want however a certain skill is unlocked with successful complete stealth takeovers. Completing each outpost in complete stealth rewards the player with extra currency, however the Player will have no trouble purchasing everything in the game without using stealth at all.
The storyline, however, forces the player to play in open combat. The characters are generally unlikeable, and the Main Character may not be relatable or even likeable to the Player. The first half of the game is dramatically more interesting than the second half.
The multiplayer is divided into standard PvP and Co-op play. The standard PvP fails to compete with the Battlefield and Call of Duty offerings. L4D with action game elements and a fantasy theme.
Pros:
Animations are well done for a western fantasy game and enemy attacks are easy to see coming in order to dodge or block. Makes for a fun combat experience.
Character progression. Not so much through levels, but in the variety of gear you accrue through completing levels/leveling up. The gear comes with random stats, some more coveted than others, and you upgrade them with random proc rates. RNG can be frustrating, but honestly even a well rolled weapon is nothing game changing over a mediocre one. You really only want the damage breakpoints from the color of the item + the specific weapon you're looking for. Plus these are equipped on your bots if they are equipped on that hero on your account, so you'll find plenty of use for them.
Level design is great on the bigger levels, still good on most of the smaller ones it's just harder to appreciate. For the mechanics of a L4D game I'd say it's mostly spot on.
Dialogue and acting is well done and always appreciated to hear.
Cons:
Some maps are pretty damn small, and considering there are only 13 I hope we get to see custom content support or some fairly priced dlc's.
Bots are just as bad here as they are in L4D, they definitely at least need an option to tell them to prioritize various loot modifiers you may find throughout the level instead of the healing items they rabidly dash for. And they definitely need to be told to healing draught earlier.
All in all, done well enough, only 30$ with some replayability already, but could definitely benefit a lot from custom content and some deeper expansions on the L4D formula. There are some bugs to fix, but they are still continuing to work those out at a good pace. Honestly the game is very playable as it is, I really don't understand some of these negative reviews that say getting hit through a wall in some random spot on a level just breaks the entire game. Hopefully we'll continue to see development beyond bugfixing, but I'd still recommend it as it is right now.

First off I like some platform games but don't usually love them... this game is an exception! GOOD
+ great atmosphere
+ moves along at a quick pace for the most part
+ good length
+ deaths can be fun and rarely require much back-tracking
+ most areas you can take some time to figure out (some not so much)
+ ability to kill, kill, kill or avoid, avoid, avoid...
+ nice voice-overs (see exception below)
NOT SO GOOD
-  there are a few sections that require some pretty perfect timing (and might be much better with a game-pad but I don't know for sure)
-  there were a couple sections that were fairly long and hard (I nearly gave up a couple times, but didn't)

Overall a very enjoyable experience that I highly recommend.

This game definitely has potential, in addition to being fun to play in it's current state. The devs are pretty transparent with their goals and timeline.
There's certainly a few things that are lacking (am I the only one who thinks rotocopters should be able to strafe instead of just yaw?)

The iso creation system is, in my opinion, what really sets this apart from other sandboxes. Not only can you create your own things out of blocks, but you can create your own useable items - vehicles, weapons, objects. The interface is a little intimidating at first, and isn't the most intuitive or user friendly, but once you get the hang of it, you can do some pretty amazing things! Overall, it's a beautiful game with some very innovative ideas. I can't wait to see where it goes, and I'm having lots of fun playing it as is.

I really enjoy this game;  I've put almost 900 hours into it at this point;  The game is worth it, even if they never finish it, it is very fun.
FOR REVIEW OF CURRENT BETA GO TO BOTTOM.
Current form:
32-bit, memory threshold limit is 3.6 gig; game locks up if your system memory allocates 3.5 gig of active memory to the client; does not affect the server.  Game has some story bugs that can crash or ruin a game save; always save your game in multiple slots and often!!  The interfaces are not scalable; that is being fixed.
Multiplayer:
You can create your own server or join others; you will have to open ports on your router and direct that port traffic to your computer; as such, you need to set a static local IP for your server within your router (lock your IP to your mac address), so that if you reboot your computer it will retain the same IP.  Take that IP and now open the ports that the game tells you to in your router, directing that traffic to your server only.   MP servers can be set to allow pvp, or simply cooperative.  The creator of the server can set people to be admins, unable to build, or kick/ban people from the server.  Once you start the server, you do not need to join the game for it to run.  At a certain point your digging will cause some parts of the map to not load (due to the 32-bit veersion and 3.5 gig memory threshold),  when this happens, you cannot log in.  To fix this, stop the server, and delete the files in the voxel folder of your server, located in your steam folder.   Multiplayer is being worked on too, and will hopefully have the ability to capture the flag soon.
The Workshop:
The game workshop only allows you to share your items after you start the game; choose to play multiplayer; select or craft a character; and then open the workshop to upload your item.  Sometimes it is difficult to upload, just keep trying.  The only way to find items however, is to select a category and then page through all the items under that category.  Search by name is ridiculously bad.  Icons of your items are super lo-res and blurry, unless you load a picture of something you made, then people won't know what the item really looks like.  The Workshop on steam makes it so you can easily find stuff, but you cannot download the item when you subscribe.  So the in-game workshop is hard to use and has blurry pics, and the steam version is easy to use but you cannot import from there
The ISO creator (voxel crafter)
This creation system is awesome;  There are pre-crafted parts for:
sword handles; gun and barrel handles for single shot and multi shot, rifle and barrel handles for single shot and multi shot, laser blaster tubes and handles, vehicle tires (multiple types), vehicle engines(multiple types), vehicle batteries (multiple types), vehicle lights(multiple types), vehicle exhaust, vehicle Cannon, vehicle tank cannon, vehicle machine guns, vehicle gatling guns, vehicle laser guns,  vehicle  missile tubes, motorcycle seats, vehicle cockpit, aircraft cockpit, boat wheel or cockpit, boat scews, boat rudder, VTOL engine, jet thruster, helicopter rotor, and some I probably missed.  These pre-fab items can be scaled in size in any or all of three dimensions (changing size modify's the item ability), made invisible.  The material editor allows you to craft voxel creations, in solid forms, paint by single voxel, extrude from voxel, a single voxel can have its volume changed and that single voxel used to make very thin walled items, swords, etc.
The creation system currently allows you to make static items from the size of a toothbrush to a one-room schoolhouse, it allows you to make swords, hammers, maces, axes, rapiers, a pistol with up to 4 barrels, which shoots one shot per barrel or multi, a rifle that allows the same, a laser pistol, a 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, or 8 wheeled vehicle such as a motorcycle, car, truck, tank, any of these vehicles can be made small (volkswagon) to super large (stretch hummer), you can make a boat, a raft, a submarine, any large ship from a battleship to an aircraft carrier.  You can make hovercraft, helicopters, jet aircraft, flying platforms such as dirigibles, air carriers, air battleships.
In game Crafting with BLOCKS:
Like minecraft, you can take blocks of material which you have mmined or crafted, and build shapes suh as buildings, walls, platforms, houses, castles, forts, and other mega structures out of multiples (10+) material types including diamonds and glass. Once you make the house or building, etc, you then can selct a box around the house and SAVE that structure to memory.  If you ever need that structure built again, you can select that recorded item from your memory and drop down as many copies as you want (so long as you have the proper materials).
The Storyline:
Its unfinished and needs some serious polish.  Adventure mode is super boring.  Much of it can hang/crash the game.  Make sure you save often and in different save slots every time you save.  Since the story is so unfinished, I can't fairly critique it.
Game Physics:
Currently its Unity four, so physics are standard;  the new version will radically change physics, wheel collision, weather activity, material reflection, water movement and reflection.  The combat engine is weak and is being worked on at this time.
Game UI:
Too busy, unscalable, and seems like placeholder;  This is true because the UI has been completely overhauled and we will see many complaints about the UI to be resolved in the next update.  UI is standard from inventory sort, split, multiplayer drop, discard, to the standard row of hotkeys, and a minimap.  Once the new version is released all of these UI elements will be changed to be a blue interface which will be scalable.
World Editor:
This editor works on its own, but will not allow import into the current game build.  There are many more ores which can be mined in the world editor which are not in the current game build.
Future versions:
Currently the game is still Early Access, and the version .90 64-bit version has not yet been released.  It is approx. 1 month late at this time; 5/17/2015 10:00 MST  This is still an alpha build.
A cool item that will be released before beta:  armor designing in the editor.
I recommend that you buy this game.

BETA .88 & .881 of Alpha .90 review:
The new beta is much more visually stunning.  The shadows and light attentuate over distance, giving real world lighting.  The character's hari animates when moving, and the body muscle groups shift as the player is animated.  This also occurs on creatures that spawn.
Creature AI is much better than previous versions.  Creatures seem better able to dodge and run if they are in flight.  Be ready to have to run downsome creatures when you are on a quest.
The rope gun is currently not in the game as it causes major issues that the programmers are unsure they can overcome.
The game is now GPU intensive and I can hear my video cards rev up when I am in the game, and instantly slow down the moment I go to main menu or alt-tab out of the game.
Creatures actually seem to be walking on the ground, and when on inclines, they match the incline.
Wheeled vehicles now shift their tires according to the ground elevation, so a car sitting on a hump near one tire will elevate that tire into the car body to simulate real world suspension.
Guns have been weakened and they only allow one barrel now.  I am unsure if I agree with this as some bosses are overpowered and a supped up gun is almost always your best bet.

We have played some four or five missions, and it is incredibly fun. The base game is a lot like Left4Dead. Four character co-op, hordes of infected/scaven, with special scaven appearing from time to time. There's more emphasis on staying together, as the specials can come out of nowhere, and many times you have almost no time to react before you're incapacitated and need to be helped. The melee combat feels a lot more solid than L4D2, you can block or dodge attacks, and every class has their unique ranged weapons. It's very fun to gain new equipment and play around until you find the weapons that fit your playstyle best. As all five classes are different there's a lot more variation than L4D, and unlocking weapons and leveling means there's a goal to strive towards, leading to an intrinsic replayability. It's also very difficult. We're struggling with normal difficulty, and there are three(?) difficulty levels more.
Pros (+):
Very fun co-op
Lot of variations in equipment and playstyles. Some weapons are better for hordes, while other are better for armored enemies.
Many different special scaven
A lot of maps on launch
The characters have a lot of amusing quips and banter between each other
Cons (-):
Haven't played with randoms, but can imagine the experience wouldn't be as great. Find three friends optimally
Maps are very dark and gloomy. Too dark sometimes.
Sometimes hard to see if people are downed, as they don't glow if you're close to them, and can be buried under a lot of scaven corpses.
A bit glitchy. It crashed on me once, and there are a gameplay bugs, such as people shooting up high if pounced by a gutter runner.

If you're played Hotline Miami you know what you're in for with the sequel, sadly, most of the ambitious changes won't work for the better. The gameplay remains the same, gotta act fast to kill enemies unless you want to get killed yourself. It still rewards reactions over luck but the problem is you're severely limited in how you get to play the game.
Characters:
The first game you were presented with a variety of masks, each with a different perk to suit any playstyle. There was a mask for everything. Not so much in this one. You play through several different stories and only a couple of them allow you to play as "The Fans" which are the mask wielding characters of this game. There's other characters that just don't really work such as a soldier that's limited to a machine/knife combo but you can't pick up any other guns from the ground, you need to find ammo caches to replenish your supply, this forces you to approach the level in a linear fashion so you can get to the ammo crates. Another character gets a dodge roll that allows you to duck under enemy fire it isn't all too useful. One character's gimmick is "non-lethal" takedowns, in which you have to knock out enemies rather than kill them (though pipes and bats are a OHKO) and picking up guns causes you to dump the clip so no other enemy can use it. I feel it works pretty well though, so no complaints there.
The Fans are pretty great, when you get to use them, and I think Ash and Alex are my favorite between both games: You control two characters, you directly control Alex who weilds a chainsaw for really quick and brutal melee kills while Ash is constantly in tow weilding guns. You control their acts individually with the different mouse buttons and it feels really good when you're finishing off an enemy with the chainsaw and holding back others with bullets to defend yourself. The problem is the AI for Ash is absolutely awful, he'll get stuck stop following you or just play run in another direction from where you're heading. I've even seen him clip through walls. Other characters are mostly hand-me-downs from the first title such as Tony, but only this time he's limited to melee punches and cannot use guns.
I would of preferred if there was a singular character with a bunch of different masks rather than several characters who seem to only be in for the sake of driving the game's convoluted story that you probably won't even care for.
Levels:
This is the biggest issue with the game, the levels. Some are just WAY too big for their own good. You'll find yourself being shot from off screen often, windows plague a lot of the levels in abundance and open areas leave guns as the only option to get through. Melee attacks are seldom useful and some maps are neigh impossible if you play mostly relying on them. The game is too focused on firearms. Also some areas are swarming with huge amounts of enemies usually leading to you forgetting about one at the very end only to have him take you out with an off-screen gunshot. The big levels and large amounts of enemies force you to play very caustiously because trying to go gung-ho never works now. That was the beauty of the first game, it wanted you to run and gun and take enemies as fast as you could and a death meant you had to rethink your strategy, you were were going for the perfect run. That's not really applicable due to the size of the levels, amounts of enemies and the RNG factor in some of their pathing. Death in this game is a frustration and you feel like you wasted your time after several seemingly good runs.
Visuals and Audio:
This is where the game shines bright, the neon 80s look is in top shape and the soundtrack matches it perfectly. The soundtrack is also large than the previous game while over-all being much better. I'd say the price of the game and soundtrack are worth it for the music alone.
Overall, it's more of the same with some really poor design decisions that hinder the experience. If you're a fan of the first game, I recommend it, if you're never played the first game start there because it provides a better gameplay experience. Your enjoyment of the first game should be the determining factor in picking up the sequel.

Left 4 Dead had a baby with Chivalry: Medieval Warfare, and they raised it in the Warhammer Fantasy universe. All the best parts from these games thrown together with a unique loot system. If you're looking for a cool co-op game to play with some friends, this is worth the money.
Pros:
+Gothic architecture that rewards exploration = Great level design.
+Each character is fun and unique to play.
+Missions don't follow the typical formula of "hit the switch, survive the horde."
+Loot system is engaging without forcing you to drop old gear like a rotten tomato a la every Diablo Clone Ever.
Cons:
-Not very original. Basically Left 4 Dead with melee combat.
-Loot system feels entirely random. You get gear for characters you don't want to play.
-Some people are having trouble running it.
-No tutorial or moves list. I had to look up a guide on how to dodge.

You fail missions often because of precedent randomness and so get 0 loot and when you get it can be very random like giving you a weapon for a char you never use. I mean seriously, when we all have full slots, it won’t pick up books, when we’re all low hp it will throw itself at the healing stuff and keep it selfishly in its inventory while the rest of the team dies, when we decide to hide form a patrol it just throws itself at some random mobs and pulls the patrol, it tries to “save” you by charging a strangler rat with melee (needless to say that’s suicide since that mob has a range of like 3 meters) and there is absolutely no way to give orders to it. I'll just start off by saying this game has an excellent concept of the Heroes and Generals aspect (One being a foot soldier another being in charge of a War Map) but it was executed pretty poorly. Gameplay is more or less a chore when you die --especially when you can only spawn on a vehicle or a taken outpost. I understand it makes for a pretty slow pace of a game but this is a WW2 game -- there was way too much room for enemies to spawn camp or just for you to get to the next objective will take a while each time you die, especially if you just rush in there to try and take it. I understand that last part shouldn't be the point of the game, but there's no other way to approach the objective other than to just rush in there, there's way too much room for the enemy to sit and wait at each objective.
The weapon variety is another issue, there's essentially none. The only thing you can get after your submachine gun is your standard rifle you first get and it's usually a piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥ I'll give an instance of when it can't be a piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥-- yesterday I was playing and I would try and take the objective but everytime I did I got sniped by someone with a kar98. Totally unbalanced since the guy is using starter weapon, just fully upgraded. So I'll end this review with this: Great concept, poorly executed, almost no balance for this blatant P2W

I've played a lot of zombie games, some good, some not so good.  Contagion ranks near the top of the stack of the great pile with it's great visuals, ambiance and pulse pounding intensity.  The multiple maps that change each time you play make this a fantastic experience in FPS's.  Playing alone is VERY difficult, so be sure to have a good group of friends to help you fight your way through many of the maps.  Barlowe Square is especially difficult, as is extraction.  Be careful not to get yourself trapped in a house while being swarmed by zombies.  You can't push your way through and ammunition resources are limited.  Speaking of ammo, head shots are the only thing that take down the shambling dead, so pick your shots carefully.  You don't necessarily have to wipe out an entire level of zombies (not nearly enough ammo for that) and sneaking is helpful.
Things I would personally like to see improved is more variety in the zombie skins, more melee weapons and more health kits, even if they were just bandages giving you partial health.  However, my critiques are small, and overall this is a great game.

'Deadlight' is a visually stunning, wonderfully atmospheric, survival horror 2.5-D Platformer which raises the bar for the genre in some respects, but then also stumbles in others – resulting in a generally fun, if confoundingly uneven escape from reality.
Developed by Tequila Works | Microsoft Studios and released in late-2012, the game drops you into the shoes of Randall Wayne, a US Park Ranger on a desperate search for his missing family in the aftermath of a zombie apocalypse. Each level takes you across a fantastic imagining of a post-apocalyptic Seattle (circa 1986), featuring both indoor, outdoor and underground elements, with hauntingly beautiful backdrops making for some of the best visuals, atmosphere and tone in recent gaming memory.
Gameplay is focused heavily on platforming and solving puzzles to help your character circumnavigate an increasing number of obstacles. Several sections also feature a timed element that naturally increase player stress-levels as you scramble to get to the end - heightening the immersion element of actually ‘running for your life’. Importantly, frequent checkpoints are well spaced throughout to ensure frustration is kept to a minimum. Your character will discover a few weapons - an axe, revolver etc - along the way, but ammunition is severely limited to reinforce the point that confrontation with the hordes of undead is generally discouraged. Sound Design is excellent and immersive overall, and controls are well optimized for both K&M and Controller.
Unfortunately, the game is not without some major missteps – Gameplay is restrictively linear – and the lack of any real challenge or even variation in puzzles, ‘enemy AI’, weapons or fighting elements make the game highly predictable and repetitive about a third of the way through. Additionally, a shallow plotline, lack of sidequests, no customization options, and relatively few collectibles make for low replayability overall as well. Finally, the game also tends to be buggy in spots (with sound randomly cutting out during cutscenes), no ‘Restart | New Game’ option, and if all of the above weren’t enough, it’s terribly short as well with average playtimes running between 3-5 hours.
‘Deadlight’ is a gorgeous looking game no doubt – but look under the hood and many inherent issues become quickly apparent, leaving the gamer feeling like they are just going through the motions without much of a plot or challenge to distract from proceedings. While extremely hard to justify at full price, On Sale (at $2.99) it’s worth a casual playthrough if largely for the visual experience alone. Recommended on Sale! – Rated (7.9/10)

I like Melody's Escape. It's cute and unassuming. The game's reminiscent of Audiosurf in concept: you plug in your music and the game generates a track for you to try and score the best you can on. You have four buttons and four directions you can press to respond to events on the track. There are four difficulties. Easy only requires one command pressed in rhythm with the song. Medium requires you to press only the buttons. Intense uses the full control scheme. Overload goes more into hard DDR song territory, heavily increasing the number of notes. There's also a custom difficulty that you can adjust the individual elements of to your liking. In other words, there's something for everyone.
If you're coming in expecting a story or anything, go find something else to play. If you want an arcadey rhythm game though, casual or difficult, check this game out. I enjoyed it a lot.

The system requirements are low enough that even if you don't have a computer nearly powerful enough to play a game like GTA 5, you can have a smooth, input-accurate, 60 fps experience. The music analysis that generates the levels is pretty good. Some songs will create better levels than others. A regular tempo or beat helps. When it does generate a good level, it is damn good. My favorite thing in the game is when the character dives off a ledge and the music slows down at the same time. She dives in slow motion and it looks so cool. A song that a lot of Steam users probably have access to that does that is Nuclear Mission Jam/Lambda Core from Half-Life and Half-Life 2 respectively. The Half-Life music in general creates pretty good levels.

Fills the L4D void better than any other game in the genre. Five heroes to choose from, each with different playstyles, with 12 maps each with five difficulty settings, throw in the loot system and the Forge system (used for breaking down duplicate or unused weapons/trinkets etc to create new items, and upgrading existing ones) and you have a game with immense reply value.
Pros:
+ Fantastic gameplay
+ Great atmosphere
+ Clever hub setting functioning as a lobby and main menu
+ Swift matchmaking
+ Variation in characters and playstyles
+ Even more team based than L4D (a pro and...)
Cons:
- (a con) Even more team based than L4D - pubbies can let the side down with a single action of selfishness or lack of consideration.
- Good loot can be difficult to come by due to the loot system, which is very much risk and reward with a massive RNG element thrown in
- Host migration can occasionally destroy progress on a map
Almost all cons can be tackled by playing with a group of friends.
Be aware though, Packmasters can ruin your day if you aren't quick to deal with them. Your team may be transformed into a grotesque art display if you aren't careful!
Overall, 8/10. Essential if you like L4D-style co-operative games. Would be brutally murdered by vermin again.

I got this game as part of a Humble Bundle, and boy oh boy do I recommend steering clear of it. I'm forcing myself to finish it out of some misplaced desire to complete it, but I wish I had never started.
First, the good: the game looks nice. It has a good aesthetic, and the backgrounds and environments make this 2.5D sidescroller pretty to look at. This is where my praise ends.
Despite how polished and professional the game LOOKS, nearly everything else is crap. The gameplay is a rather tired form of puzzle platformer that's been done time and time again by games like Limbo and the original Prince of Persia. However, the "Puzzles" are mediocre, usually involving activating whatever highlighted item happens to be in the room with you. Similarly, the "Platformer" is just frustrating, due to sloppy controls, and frankly bad design. "Trial and error" gameplay is particularly heavy In the later levels, often times with the character dying for no particular reason.
Then there's the "story." The plot is yet another cookie-cutter zombie-apocalypse story, a genre which is so played out by now that I almost expected this game to be a parody. Deadlight adds nothing new to the genre whatsoever. It's full of a million tired tropes, the voiceacting is subpar, the script is bad, and it's not even fun to play.

If you're an L4D/L4D2 fan, you should definitely get this! I bought this game for RM19 on Xmas sales, but a few days later it only costs RM9.50, really?? Despite that, I'm gonna give a good review about this game.
Pros
* This is a REAL zombie survival game! You need to learn how to SURVIVE as a team!
* Nice graphics, FPS is around 60 on my machine
* Headshot to the zombies is a must or you'll be wasting ammo
* You can play this for hours with your friends and never got bored of it
* If you're thinking of playing this solo, be prepared for getting creeped out or overwhelmed
Cons
* For first timers, there are no tips on what to do at all, it is up to you to find out
* You can only scroll me messages all the way back to the first one, but you can't scroll back to the latest message
* There is a bug where some zombies would get stuck on the ground
* On the options menu, the description on the lower right gets extended out of the screen, limiting visibility (is it just me?)
* Hiccups in the game even when my connection is good and FPS around 60
* The phone in-game could be better than just viewing messages
* Sometimes when I shot a zombie in the head accurately, the system didn't register it, causing me to fire multiple shots, wasting my ammo (I'm certain I hit the zombie in the head!)
* Riot police zombie, ammo is already scarce. Best option is to run away from him
* This game needs more people playing it
I totally recommend this game if you're looking for a challenge, people who love L4D/L4D2 would definitely love this. Let's hope the devs will put more effort in improving the game.

A good sequel uses the original game as a springboard, taking the concepts and ideas and evolving them naturally, taking the good parts and improving on them, and trimming the misused or outright bad aspects down to manageable levels, or removing them entirely if possible. Hotline Miami 2 is not a good sequel.  The core gameplay, that of chaotic violence to the tune of a fantastic soundtrack, is relatively intact. Everything else, however, has changed, in my opinoin, for the worse.
Hotline Miami was not an easy game by any means, but the gameplay revolved around that. It accounted for that. Death was cheap, and respawning was instant, your player character going from a bloody stain on the floor right back to the front door in a second flat, ready to try murdering an entire building one more time. The levels were mostly compact and there were plenty of separated rooms for you to take advantage of, the formula changing slightly as the game went on to add organic challenge and force you to adapt to situations you can't prevent. Due to the game's top down nature, the entire level was not always in frame, especially as the game went on, but you didn't typically have to worry about someone off screen killing you from across the stage because there were rooms between you and them, not one long hallway that you can't see down.
Hotline Miami 2, on the other hand, makes death feel absolutely annoying. Levels are significantly larger, the enemy population growing accordingly. And there's a lot of empty space to traverse. Ordinarily, this wouldn't be too much of a problem, were it not for the greatly emphasized focus on guns. Half of your deaths will absolutely come from off screen because a goon saw you and blasted you from an angle you couldn't account for. You respawn just as fast, of course, but instead of getting right back into the flow without a care, you feel the loss of progress. There's a lot of guys to kill, and if the last ones get the better of you, you are going to feel the pain. The gameplay itself becomes a chore, and the most successful way to get through stages goes against the entire point of the game: taking it slow and steady, holding down the shift key the entire time to make sure the big area you're traversing doesn't have a guy with a gun who'll pop you the second you enter his line of sight. The basic game design has remained the same, while the scale of the actual game has outgrown it and taken things in a different direction that the design wasn't built to handle.
Another factor that Hotline Miami 2 boasts is several different characters. There's actually a ton. And in my opinion, that makes things less compelling. Especially because at least half of them don't even wear masks, and as an effect, don't have special abilities beyond two that specifically come to mind, both with glaring downsides and with no sizeable buff to compensate. One of them is "nonlethal", the air quotes being present because you can be lethal, but only with downed enemies. He refuses to use bladed weapons or guns, choosing to unload picked up firearms and make it so enemies can't use them instead of using them himself. It makes sense in character, of course, but adjusting to his gameplay takes time, especially because, again, a lot of enemies use guns. The other character starts with a gun you choose at the beginning of his segments. That gun sticks with you. You can never drop it, only switch to your knife. You can reload it at ammo boxes, but confusingly, he doesn't fully restock, even though the ammo boxes can be used forever. Dropped enemy guns taunt you, because as that character, you cannot pick up any weapons.
The story has expanded accordingly, aiming to expand on how the events of Hotline Miami started, and conclude them. Taking the Pulp Fiction approach of presenting events in anachronic order, the story jumps from character to character at various points in time, not too much of a far cry from how the first game was handled. However, because there is now an overarching story that isn't laid out piece by piece for you to put together, and is instead thrown directly at you, there is dialogue everywhere. Characters talk, and talk, and for some reason, that doesn't feel too "in the spirt" of Hotline Miami, the expanded roster making the experience less of an utter mind screw and more of a crime thriller with the chapters all mixed up. Not a bad thing ordinarily, but because it is a direct sequel, it does need to be compared to the original.
Thankfully, the soundtrack remains one of the defining aspects of the game. It was always good in Hotline Miami, and it's thankfully unchanged here. It's one of the unquestionably best parts of the game, and I recommend getting the soundtrack and looking into the various artists that contributed, Perturbator being my personal favorite.
Occasionally there's a level where you get into the groove. You tune out everything but the music, and just jump right in, going right in and playing the game the way it was meant to be played, never stopping, every second punctuated by the death of a pastel suited goon, grabbing his weapon and using it on his buddy in the next instant, the way the game wants you to play it. Unfortunately, those levels seem to be few and far between, most of them throwing guns at you and expecting you to wade in amidst a wall of instant death. Curiously, every character seems to have a degree of resistance to bullets, able to take maybe one or two before dying. However, you won't notice that unless you're lucky. Shotguns kill you instantly, and the ability to take one hit doesn't matter when a thug with an automatic rifle sends several rounds your way. And amidst my major issues, there's a bevy of errors and glitches, the masked twins act as one character, yet the partner AI gets frequently stuck on walls and often fails to give you back up when you storm a room. Some levels have a strangely bright filter thrown over them, which makes your cursor hard to see. On the upside, I haven't seen a single boss encounter or stealth section. That's...about it.
It's strange to see a game functionally unchanged, but feel wholly different. It's a sequel that aims to expand, but does so ungracefully and with surprisingly short sight. At the time of writing (March 21st, 2015), I cannot recommend it at full price. If you must play another Hotline Miami, wait til it's on sale. One of the few redeeming aspects of the game is its cross promotional deal with Payday 2, making Jacket a playable character in that game if you buy the special edition of Hotline Miami 2.
All in all, 5/10. The end result has changed while keeping the basic formula intact, but the game expects you to play it like the first one when doing it in such a way will get you killed more often than not and just lead to frustration. It's a sequel that aims high, but performs worse than its predecessor and falls short of the mark.

I followed Vermintide's development from afar. On the one hand, I'm in the minority, and am not particularly fond of FPS games. I far prefer the TPS type view, especially in games where melee is involved. I also have an odd relatshionship with Left 4 Dead. I loved the first, and hated the second, in no small part because the content promised for the first one was never delivered, L4D2 being released a short time afterwards.
So in short, Vermintide wasn't the type of game that seemed particularly appealing. However, I should also mention I'm quite a big fan of Warhammer, Warhammer Fantasy in particular. I don't play the tabletop game, nor have any interest in it, but love the lore, and enjoy the novels very much, for whatever reason. That is what kept me following Vermintide, until I finally pulled the trigger.
This is, in my opinion, a fantastic game, and one I truly enjoy. For warhammer fans, the atmosphere is very, very well made. The architecture and grim ambiance provide a lot to make you feel this is, unmistakably, the warhammer universe.   The music - courtesy of Jesper Kyd - adds to that. And the skaven are true to themselves, their models being quite varied, the sounds they make similar to what I imagine they'd sound like.
The characters are well designed, and all of them play very differently. This adds a layer to the game, for those who might be worried that this is a mere L4D clone. To me, it's just not. Aside from the setting being unique, character progression, items, and character classes add a lot to the game. Then there are more subtle differences. Some of the special rats bring a real challenge. A sense of dread fills you when hearing a pack of Stormvermin marching your way. These things can be a real challenge, and certain death to unprepared groups.
The game plays well, and looks good. It's a joy to hack through the rodent tide, and pinning a rat to a wall with a well placed arrow is equally enjoyable.
The game is not without it's faults, of course. There are occasional bugs, though they're being worked over. Some people complained about the game being way too dark. Though I didn't feel that was the case, a gamma tweaker was added for release. Fatshark seems to be on top of things. Now let's hope they can keep adding to the game. Some more classes perhaps? A versus mode would be sweet for sure.
If you enjoy the warhammer universe, and are tired of all the run of the mill, post apocalyptic zombie games, you might want to give Vermintide a try. I highly recommend it. It's a blast, especially if you've got a few friends to enjoy it with.

This game is absolutely awesome. Not only can you build and sculpt your environment to your likings, you can design and build your own weapons, modes of transport (air, water and land) and armor.... The only limit you have is your own imagination!

When you first start this game and go in build mode things can become a bit overwhelming because of all the materials, options etc... I only have 30ish hours so far in this game, but i am definately falling in love with this game and would reccommend it to everybody that is looking for a fresh, original, modern voxel based game!

Devs, Keep up the amazing work and as for the community, please do the same :D

Pros:
+Songs are tracked within seconds
+Each song delivers a different and unique track (endless replayablity)

+Very slick, sweet art style and effects
Cons:
-Some songs do not track as well as others. This is saddening if you're a big fan of death metal such as myself since most of these songs track poorly, except Rings of Saturn for some odd reason... (If a song says it has no steady tempo detected, the track quality is not that great)
-An option to edit and upload tracks would be nice, especially for the afformentioned poorly tracked songs that could potentially be made into really good tracks.
There is a lot of fun to be had here and I would recommend you pick this game up if you are a fan of rythm games like I am.

Sonic Adventure 2 was one of the best games of its time in my opinion. To this day, it's still a pretty solid game. It receives a lot of flak for its plot holes, cheap enemy placement, and poorly done camera, but I don't think that stops it from being fantastic. I haven't seen a lot of games that execute a fast paced 3d platformer as well as this one. There's a pretty decent amount of content. There's a lot of variety between the levels, especially with the 3 different types of stages. One of these stage types, treasure hunt, is commonly looked down upon. Some of the stages are frustrating, but I actually found it to be a really enjoyable mode. As long as you aren't going for speed, hunting around is a really nice change of pace that still works within the scope of the game. Adding to the content is a slew of minigames and activities. The game features a Chao Garden which allows you to raise Chao with drives and animals you receive from playing the main game. The integration with the normal levels is done very well, as it doesn't force you to grind a poorly done minigame. There is a lot to do with Chao, and they serve as a pretty great distraction from the main game, which can easily slow down once you've beaten all the levels multiple times. All things considered, it's a great game with plenty to do, but whether or not it still is a great investment in 2015 is something you'll have to find out for yourself.

That's my nerdgasm speaking. Now for my english review, this game is definetly NOT WITH OUT IMPURITY, meaning it's got quite a few glitchy, frusterating or unsatisfactory qualities, but ultimately this is one of my most favorite games in history. Sound-wise, It has AMAZING music, interesting sound effects, slightly embarrasing voice acting for some characters, and sometimes tacky dialog in some scenes. Graphically it's very vivid - I like the art style, but youcan obviously tell this is a very old game. It's physics are as unrealistic as you'd expect from any Sonic game, but it's passable.
It's story is in some ways goofy (again, it's a Sonic game) but you can get very attached to the characters - more so than in most sonic games and it has an usually decent ending for a kid's game with...dramatic elements you don't normally expect. Many people hate this game because it and it's predecessor were the first time Sega tried to make Sonic into a 3D-game. Many people didn't like the switch of gameplay style, but I love this, and this right here is the only time for a very long time (until Sonic Generations) they got it (almost) perfect. Many other bad sonic games spawned from this (such as Sonic Unleashed) - but please, despite what you may have heard, give this game a chance. It may♥♥♥♥♥♥you off sometimes, it may make you laugh sometimes, but when you really get down with this, you'll cherish it. This game is a true gem from the ancient past reformatted for modern platforms and given a mild HD retexture.

An excellent L4D clone. While it lacks the VS. mode that is the essence of L4D, it makes up for it by having a significantly more challenging and engaging Co-op Vs. CPU experience. Player Heroes all differ in weapons and strengths, making each own feel unique and fun to play as. The added layer of gear and gear drops (with varying rarity and extra traits) also help differentiate one Dwarf Ranger from another and so on. The drawback here is the very likely need to grind in order to get better gear, though higher difficulty modes and other in game items can increase the chances of useful item drops. Also note that the Hero A.I. is at often times absolutely abysmal and has extremely poor priority logic, so be sure to play with actual people online.

This game is an exact clone of Left 4 Dead 2, reskinned in the Warhammer Universe. Even the music sounds the same. Combat is boring. Someone described it as "Chivalry crossed with L4D2"--except in Chivalry there are directional, overhand, and thrusting attacks for different situations and to get around enemy defenses. Vermintide, you literally just hack at packs of enemies with swiping attacks. Left, right, overhand. Left, right, overhand. Until there are no more faces looking at you. They advertise each class plays completely differentlly, which is also a vague lie. The archer shoots arrows and can zoom, the witch hunter has two pistols and can either quick-shot one with his rapier or pull them both for rapid fire, the soldier has a shotgun, the dwarf has a gun... the only one that is kind of different is the bright wizard who can shoot different staffs shoot different kinds of fire based on what staff you have equipped, whether lobbing a fireball that AoEs, a cone attack, sustained fire stream. It's all the same, though, just if you want to shoot one target from far away, several targets up close, or spray fire. The various rat enemies are about the only genuinely interesting aspect, but they are literally carbon copies of L4D(2). Assassin rat pounces on you exactly like the hunter, packmaster drags you away exactly like the jockey, poison rat is just a ranged boomer, rat ogre is a tank - special slams and all. The loot system -- honestly, who cares? Seriously. This one swings faster, this one does more damage... ok, terriffic, I'm still just hacking at packs of rat faces until no more are looking at me.

Although I don't recommend this game, I feel that the game could be enjoyed by a niche audiece, who can tolerate the many flaws. Thus I can't guarantee that you'll enjoy it even if you are a platformer fan and like the Zombie Theme.
Let's start with the good things, the developers did a good job in making a zombie-apocalypse atmosphere, and especially in the beginning you feel like a lone survivor, just barely escaping the horde, with your Ezio-Like Climb skills.
You have very low health and run fast out of stamina (used for climbing and mainly fighting), making combat challenging and because if you mess up the horde will get you and just makes sense in these kind of games.
A big point about positives is the graphics, the game looks nice and the 2.5 D style makes this game feel more alive, defintly adds up to the atmosphere and seems to be what took most of the budged than developing this game sadly.

Not to mention the game can crash a few times, but due to the checkpoints, it is for most people irrelevant.
On certain level I want to comment on is the rat’s labyrinth, it's a fairly long level, without the great atmosphere and with generic platforming the rest of the game has and completely unreliable to the rest of the game, in case you come past this level don't be discouraged if you enjoyed the zombie-apocalypse atmosphere, it will come back
Again, it's very niche and only few playres will enjoy this. Well I found it ok and a bit enjoyable, but there are a lot of problems this game has and if you aren't willing to except these problems and want to some zombie-apocalypse atmosphere, than don't get it.

You can see i am playing this game for quiet some time now; why do i have so many hours into the game? it's because i am working on cars and ships in the ISO editor most of the time, then go into build or story mode (where i mined enough items and build a colony that works pretty well) and test those creations. At the moment PE is a great construction platform where you can test your creations inside the game environment.
That said i am missing alot of tools to be able to make better shapes then you can create right now, or only in very difficult and complicated/timeconsuming ways. While i have alot of time and patience myself, i can see why many players don't really try to make nice looking creations, but only stuff 'to get the job done'. Physics are off too in the game, so that makes it even more complicated, for example leveling a ship so it doesn't tilt, or a car getting stuck on every little bump in-world ect. pp.
I get more to the physics later on.
The Storymode is fun, because it shows you the mechanics of the game, and introduces you to the basics (and more). At first it can be a little bit confusing when you start in the ship over the planet, but with a little patience you can overcome that.
I didn't play multiplayer very long, because it crashed all the time with memory overflow errors. guess i bought it at a time where they just updated the game from 0.86 to 0.87 and a major bug or bugs kept the game crashing for me. I don't want to get too much into detail what it was, but they fixed that pretty fast in 0.871 so it was playable again. That said, you will run out of memory in adventure mode fast when you travel around alot because the game is still 32-bit, which means that you only have about 3 GB of memory for the game, which is not enough for a long playtime, specially when traveling around alot. (The Textures don't  seem to be updated, they just get added until you crash when you run out of memory space.) I can play story mode in nearly best quality for a long time before things go wrong though.
The developers are working on a version they call 0.9 which has 64-bit and the new Unity 5 engine, which hopefully solves that memory problem.
Gameplay: (i am talking about story mode now, because that is what i usually play:)
Although it is alot of fun to play the story, you can see and feel that there is still a lot of work to be done to get the game into more then an alpha stage. i don't really need perfect combat animations, ( they promise to change the combat in 0.9, we'll see), but the world, as pretty as it looks at first glance, becomes pretty uninteresting after a couple hours of gameplay. it just lacks a certain... detail here and there. I think i can explain that to myself reading from others that it's a small team programming the game. How much more detail there will be later on nobody can predict at this point. I also have to put in the fact that the game came out 2 years ago, but they are still working on it, so i see that actually as a positive aspect, keeping a small team in mind.
However, there are huge differences in graphics quality that i cannot explain: The animals look GREAT, i mean GREAT GREAT... the area around them for now is more like average compared to them. The animations could be better, but for my taste are more then good enough to make them feel very much alive. The plants, trees and so on on the other hand don't move at all, they are like statues, and if you hit a smaller tree with your ride, it gets damaged and that small tree doesnt move at all getting hit by a 50 t  4x4 tank ;-) .
Physics are still lacking here big time, and that is only one example of the physics not really working right atm. I hope they fixe those things later on.
The currency in story mode is 'meat', which is... something getting used to. I suggested 'protein' for a supplement, and i got a response they consider it. We'll see :-)  (this is another indicator they take your input seriously)
From what i hear they use cash or credit for multiplayer, which is something people just are more accustomed to in games... why just not keep it that way? I never played a game before that uses 2 different currencys in different game modes, and it just complicates things...
I understand they want to make the story mode more like a survival game mode, but just using a currency that sort of suggests that isn't enough imho. Don't make currency you can eat... no other food at home? just eat some dollar bills! :-)
That gets me to the fact that i never really feel it being a struggle to survive. At all. You must be pretty dumb or very unlucky to die in story mode. (Running into animals you don't know if they attack or not for example... You can avoid those animals quiet easily.) You cannot starve to death, you just run out of stamina and you get slower. That's it. You cannot dehydrate, you don't need to drink. For me those are basics for a survival game, aren't they?
I don't really see that myself as a big disatvantage, because i like to play in easy mode(s), so it's more of a relaxed gameplay rather then hectic fighting. Getting old.... ;-) But i am sure it will bother other people. Games like "7 days to die" do a better job on that: you take damage if you run out of food and/or water plus you run out of stamina while using tools, even more so when you are out of food.

Melody's Escape is a rhythm game that let's you play your own music while capturing the emotion of a song on the screen all while keeping you pretty dang engaged in the game.
(Positives)
The game uses an audio detection program/algorthim to turn your songs into a track on the game, and it does a fantastic job for the most part. The detection can pick up pretty much all the genre's of music. No matter your taste in music, this game can deliever to you an experience (depending on the song..,. more later) that you'll never have in any rhythm game ever made. This game can enhance the emotion in a song incredibly by the actions of Melody on screen. When she kicks down a brick wall at that perfect time, it can send a shiver down your spine if you love the song being played. The best example I can give is the song "I need a doctor". This game enhances that song much much more. When the game jumps from walking, to jogging, running and flying (and every combination of them) it can make you feel a song that much more.
Artistically, the game is phenomenal. The color changes, the background scenery, the animations all are incredibly well done and suck you into the song. The only complaint in this department, is that it can mess with your eyes as another review has pointed out, but you can adapt to it after a bit.
Gameplay wise, the hit detection is spot on. Very, very, VERY tight. You WILL get frustrated if you've never played a Guitar Hero game before (depending on the song of course.) Plus, every song is unique. I know I only have a couple hours in the game, but I've played enough songs to get a general idea of the differences, and it is quite nice.
I shouldn't have to talk about sound...
On to the (Negatives):
The music detection is absolutely incredible for sure... However, it could be better. I feel as though it doesn't differentiate genre's well enough. An example would be an older Metallica song (Say.. The Four Horsemen) and a 2Pac song being played very much alike. The detection seems to be all over the place or only focus on 1 or 2 things. A metal song should pick up drastically when a guitar solo comes around, just as a rap song should pick up when a rapper starts to go H.A.M on the mic. Instead? Melody just tends to run at the same speed during those times/songs.
The game could also be a bit harder in terms of the amount of beats/nodes/whatever to hit. It kind of goes with the genre thing, as I think you should be frantically hitting buttons with a guitar solo or if a rapper starts to go absolutely nuts with speed (Rap God anyone?) This can ruin the game for some people as it can lose the challange and lose your interest.
The only suggestions to the Developers I can offer, would be to 1) Somehow make the rhythm detection software be able to be set to a specific genre of music so it can better capture that genre overall, rather than a relatively large minority of a genre and 2) To add in more nodes/strikes/whatever when the first suggestion is implemented. Some songs can just be a bore when they're some really upbeat/in-your-face songs.
(3) This gets its own seperate paragraph... A storyline possibly. I can see a story popping up right in front of me if this algorthim gets complex/flexible enough. That might already be in the game, since the artistic style suggests someone just getting lost in the emotion of a song. However, this game just seems to have that many possibilities. A story mode that can match a number of songs in a genre together (or several genres together) to make it have a begginning, meat, climax, and end would make this THE music/rhythm game.
OVERALL: This game is worth the 10 USD (5USD as of the winter/holiday sale). Whether you're a music lover looking to get more emotion/interactivity from a song or a musician trying to gauge where your song's emotion comes through, it's worth it. The potential here is absolutely as high as the stars. Sure it has it's quirks with detecting songs, but, you can very easily have at least 40 songs on your computer/ipod/phone/mp3/whatevertheheckyouusenow that'll take full advantage of the engine/algorthim in place right now. Plus, with it being early access, this can very well be the beginning of an amazing game and I wouldn't want to miss out on the chance to get it now to see it evolve into something incredible. Optimistic? Yes. I can't see the developers being able to screw up a creation like this.
If you love music, get this game. If you have a crap ton of music on your computer that you never listened to after downloading it to your iPod/phone in 200X, get this game so you can put that music to good use!
