Vermintide is a fun game that puts 4 players up against swarms of Ratmen itching to kill you.
The game seems in some ways heavily influenced by Left4Dead.
You can expect, Swarms, Special Ratmen and Crescendo's... and yes, they have a Rat TANK! :)
*There is no Versus though, this is purely a PvE/Coop game.
The game plays good, feels meaty and is aesthetically done really well.
There is currently 5 classes in the game, each have their own unique gameplay mechanics and can be further customised through end of level loot drops of different items.
Loot is handed out at the end should you complete your objective(s).
Failing will only reward you a small amount of XP.
Successfully completing a level will award you more XP, and add additional dices(If you got bonus loot dice, or are carrying books)
Loot is handled via dice rolls.
You roll some dice, the value of the dice raises the loot ladder level.
A perfect roll will get you the top item, while a crap roll will net you a crappy low level item.
Items are coloured in general RPG style, with white being basic, and orange being top quality.
The game also has a crafting system of sorts, where you can fuse and break down items to unlock abilities and or just take a chance at a better item.
This game is very Team orientated especially in the harder game skill levels.
This is due to the numbers that the Rats attack in, you must work together and take advantage of bottlenecks.
One person running off too far can be the catalyst for a team wipe quite easily especially if they are dragged away by a packmaster(think jockey).
All in all, I think the game is great but it is a game you need to play with a good team to excel in as it is not as forgiving as other games.

Remember the two bonus levels ("Highball" and "Exposed") from the end of Hotline Miami? The poorly-designed, wide-open levels that nobody particularly liked but played anyway? That is basically every level in Hotline Miami 2.
After you finish the introductory mission designed to help familiarize you with the controls again, the missions are very hard. Not challenging, just hard. With enough repetition, you will memorize where the enemies hide off-screen and the best corners to hide in, but it doesn't feel like the same controlled chaos of the first game. Hotline Miami rewarded you for the creativity, variety and speed with which you dispatched enemies, but HL2 never quite gives you the same autonomy; you basically have to stick to one particular path in order to complete a mission and stay alive.
The new character abilities feel more like gimmicks than helpful tools. I never found a practical use for shooting two guns in two directions. The combat roll is bound to the same key you use to execute downed enemies; it got me killed more than it saved me. The twins (which you control at the same time, similiar to the Ice Climbers) don't work well together, either. The secondary character follows you around and can use a gun, but it's not possible to peek corners with her or effectively mow people down. I used her as an attention-getter for luring people into the primary character's melee weapon around the corner more than anything else.
I have high-hopes for the user-created content, but between the poor level design and half-baked masks and weapons, the campaign felt very forced compared to the first game. All that said, it's hard to say this is a "bad" game. It just doesn't seem like it builds on what Hotline Miami created; it's just more of the same but with longer, more frustrating missions.
If you enjoyed the first one, it's worth playing. Just don't expect much.

A fantastic game which, despite one or two flaws, does justice to its famous predecessor and delivers an improved and more enjoyable game experience.
Characters
------------
There are significantly more characters this time than in the first one, which only let you play as 2 different ones. In this installment, there are 12 characters with various skills and abilities which change the way you approach levels. Examples include a maniac in a Zebra mask who can roll and dodge bullets, and a grizzled detective who can wield his shotgun one-handed. They also possess a voice and personality, unlike Jacket in HM1, leading you to have a better understanding of the characters and their differing motivations.
There is also a larger variety of enemies and NPCs, leading to a more immersive experience as you constantly encounter new and interesting people throughout the game. The number of boss battles has also increased, and there's nothing more satisfying than taking down one of these unique enemies in a violent way.
Levels
--------
The levels are far larger to an almost overwhelming scale sometimes, which can ramp up the difficulty because of the increased enemy count. Maps still possess the same features, such as doors and windows, but there is not really any need for anything new anyway as it would just feel 'gimmicky'.
Weapons
-------------
There is an increased number of weapons- all of the old ones make a magnificent comeback, but there are also exciting new kill machines such as a flamethrower and a sniper rifle.
Story
--------
The story, although confusing at first, ends up being a fascinating novel full of plot twists and developments. Although the ending feels slightly adrupt and out of place, you are left with a feeling of satisfaction and conclusion after you fully grasp the meaning of it.
Negatives
------------
The game possesses a few irritating bugs, such as enemies sometimes sticking in doorways and abnormal movement patterns. However, on the whole it is a smooth experience and I did not experience a single game-breaking bug or crash in my gameplay.

First off, I reccomend this game to anyone who even slightly enjoyed Minecraft or Terraria, espescially if you enjoyed the building aspect of the games. So what makes this game different?
You create your own weapons, shields, vehicles, and decorations. I dont mean MMO-style crafting either, you literally build them from the ground up, voxel by voxel.
A few quick warnings; This game does have bugs and glitches (ie, can't currently explore the northern half or so of the map without it crashing). As a side note, monsters and terrain have a bad habit of destroying your favorite vehicles. To solve both problems, save often.
Lastly, I wanted to provide a few tips that I wish someone had shared with me.
-There is a meteorite crater just north of where you start in story mode, It is full of Iron and Copper and is great for making money.
-Almost straight west of the meteorite crater is a "Rock Formation" the vendors there sell you the scripts (crafting recipes) for a better pickaxe as well as the parts to make a land vehicle.
-To the west of where you spawn (Past where the river forks along the coast) There is a vendor, he sells the items you need to make aircrafts.
-Don't try hunting (for currency anyways) with bullets. With a few exceptions, you lose around the same amount you gain. Instead, try building up a vehicle with lots of firepower. As long as you have coal from mining, there really isn't any cost to refill the batteries on said vehicle.
-(IMO) Build your vehicles out of Marble. It is easily the most abundant of the resources, making upgrades/repairs cheap. Also, my Marble helicopter currently has 55,000 durability after two upgrades. I will die before it does every time.
tl;dr? Yes this game is amazing, no it isn't perfect. There are a few bugs that really need to get fixed, but the game is in alpha. Save often and I would easily give this game a 9/10.

It's like if Left 4 Dead and the old warhammer game Mordhiem had a very angry baby.... then that baby grew up with a backass beard and a hatred for rodents!
Edit: I felt the review was lacking so i though i should go into further detail.
The characters are very close to the lore of the source material, While the game is similar to left 4 dead in alot of respects the melee combat is vastly superior with the weapons having varity and viewable statistics to them, a better blocking mechanic and even a dodge move that can help you jump to either side or back to avoid incomming strikes.
The only downsides with this game compaired to its predecessor would be the lack of a vs mode though the Co-op side of the game stands on its own just fine, i also hope additional characters are added to the roster and the few bugs the game has is adressed and ironed out, still for a game that is not AAA it certainly had alot of polish and atmosphere to it, even if it does make my CPU boil!
I will recommend you keep an eye open on the system requirements, this one is a bit of a glutton though even at its lowest setting the game is still appealing to look at (bare a few low ress wound textures on the skaven when you kill them)
Best of all its not set in Age of Sigmar! :D
